Affairs Bureau; Vice-Min. of Agrl. & Com.; attended World Postal Conf. at Wien. Address: 5 Mita Koyamacho, Shibaku, Tokyo.

Vice-Admiral (Reserve); b. Oct., 1872 in Saga-ken; s. of Eizo Fujiwara. Career: grad., Naval Coll., 1894; apptd. Sub.-Lieut., 1895; Vice-Admiral, 1923; during the service, grad., Naval Staff Coll.; Sec. Gen., Naval Construction Dept.; Chief, Yokosuka Naval Arsenal; Head, Naval Munitions Bureau; Comdr., Makun Naval Port; enrolled on Reserve, 1926; at present, Pres., Sagami Transportation Co.; Dir., Yashima Shokai, Ltd. Address: 23 Shirokane-Imazatocho, Shibaku, Tokyo.

Mem., House of Peers; Pres., Oji Paper Mfg. Co.; same, S. Saghalien Ry. Co.; same, Kyodo Yoshi, Oyodogawa Hydro-Elec., Karafuto Elec., Kyoei Kigyo, Uryo Elec. Power, Kyushu Soden, Hokkai Hydro-Elec. Cos., Ltd.; Chairman, Board of Directors, Denki Kagaku Kogyo K. K.; Dir., Kyodo Pulp, Hakodate Hydro-Elec., Miike Nitrogen Ind., Karafuto Ry. Co., Ltd.; Aud.; Fuji Paper Mfg. Co., Ltd.; Councillor, Nakai Yoshiten; b. June, 1869 in Nagano-ken; s. of late Mohei Fujiwara. Career: grad., Keio Univ., 1891; founded Matsue Nippo; joined Mitsui Bank; transferred to Mitsui Bussan Kaisha, serving as Mgr., Shanghai, Amoi, Taihoku Branches and as Mgr., Timber Dept. of same; nominated Mem., House of Peers, 1929. Address: 16 Shin-Amicho Nichome, Azabuku, Tokyo.

Trader; b. July, 1881 in Okayama-ken; s. of late Shinjiro Fujiwara. Career: Mem., Kobe Chamber of Com. & Ind.; Dir., America-Japan Society, Kobe. Address: Fujiwara Bros., 160 Sannomiyacho-Itchome, Kobe.

Rigakuhakushi, (D. Sc.); Meteorologist Central Meteorological Observatory; Prof., Meteorology, Tokyo Imperial Univ.; b. Oct., 1884 in Naganoken; s. of Mitsuzo Fujiwara, county official. Career: Engaged in present profession since graduation. Address: Chuo Kishyodai, (The Central Meteorological Observatory) Kojimachi, Tokyo.

Dir., Postal Affairs Bureau, Manchoukuo; b. Mar., 1889 in Kumamoto-ken; s. of Chujiro Fujiwara. Career: grad., Law Coll., Tokyo Imp. Univ., 1915; entered Communications Office; sent to Europe and America for study; attended World Postal Conference, 1924; Chief, Foreign Mail Section; Dir., Telegraphic Affairs Bureau; Sec., Communications Office; apptd. present post, June, 1932. Address: 303 Ichinokuramachi, Omoriku, Tokyo.
Chief, Gen. Affairs Section, Supervisory Council, Manchoukuo; b. in Yamaguchi-ken. Career: grad., Econ. Coll., Tokyo Imp. Univ.; present post since 1932. Address: Hsinking.

Mem., House of Peers; Pres., Dai Nippon Sugar Mfg. Co., Niitaka Sugar Mfg. Co., Musashi Central Elec. Ry. Co.; Chairman, Board of Directors, Chiyoda Trust Co.; Dir., Mitsui Trust Co., Japan Dyestuff Mfg. Co., Tokyo Printing Co., Imperial Theater, Japan Fire Ins. Co., Yasuda Trust Co., Dai Nippon Celluloid Co., Toyo Steel Works, Dai San Bank, San-a Paper Mfg. Co., Shuseisha; Aud. 34th Bank; Councillor, Mitsukoshi, Ltd., China-Japan Ind. Co., Kyodo Trust Co.; b. Aug., 1863 in Saga-ken; s. of Kakuzaemon Fujiyama. Career: studied at Keio Univ.; Mem. and later Pres., Pref. Assembly; Pres., Shibaura Engrg. Works; Mng. Dir., Oji Paper Mfg. Co.; same, Tokyo Street Ry. Co.; Pres., Tokyo Chamber of Com. & Ind. Address: 14 Shirokane Imazatocho, Shibaku, Tokyo.

Vice-Pres., Bank of Japan; b. Nov., 1871 in Gumma-ken. Career: grad., Doshisha Univ., 1891; entered present bank, gradually promoted present post; attended Paris Peace Conference, 1919; Washington Disarm. Conf. and Geneva Int'l Econ. Conf., 1921. Address: 51 Hikawacho, Akasakaku, Tokyo.

Dir. and Business Mgr., Japan Elec. Power Co.; b. Sept., 1889 in Tokyo; s. of late Hanzo Fukano, business man. Career: grad., German Law Course, Tokyo Imp. Univ. Address: 79 Kishinoshita, Ashiya, Hyogo-ken.

Baron; Mem., House of Peers; Pres., Nisshin Steamship Co., Ltd.; b. Jan., 1877 in Osaka; s. of Motomu Fukao, clansman. Career: grad., Tokyo Univ. of Com.; joined Osaka Shosen Kaisha, 1899; Mng. Dir. of same, 1920; Vice-Pres., 1924; resigned from same, 1927. Address: 30 Ichigaya-Nakanocho, Ushigome, Tokyo.

Bungakuhakushi (D. Litt.); Prof., Tokyo Imp. Univ.; b. Sept., 1874 in Ibaragi-ken; s. of late Tamegoro Fukasaku, clansman. Career: grad., Litt. Dept. Tokyo Imp. Univ., 1900; apptd. Asst. Prof. of same, 1912; sent abroad for study, 1916; received degree, 1912. Address: 902, 5-chome, Sendagaya, Shibuyaku, Tokyo.

Pres., Shiseido; Dir., Tateyama Hospital; Dir., Teikoku Life Ins. Co., Ltd.; Aud., Goto Fuundo; b. July, 1883 in Tokyo-fu; s. of Arinobu Fukuhara. Career: grad., Chiba Medical Coll.; 1907 studied at Colombia Univ., 1908; in U. S. 8 yrs. to study pharmacy and beauty treatment; returned home, via Europe, 1913; founded Shiseido which became Ofuna Garden City, K. K. 1914. Address: 278 Chojamaru Kami-Osaki, Shinagawaku, Tokyo.

Dir., Sankyo Co., Ltd., same, Harley-Davidson Motorcycle Sales Co., Ltd.; same, Koto Trading Co., Ltd.; Aud., Torii & Co., Ltd.; b. Sept., 1874 in Yokohama; s. of late Genjiro Fukui, merchant. Career: grad., Yokohama Commercial Coll.; succeeded father's business in 1898; has been connected with Sankyo Co. since 1919; travelled abroad twice for studies and on business. Address: 14 Hikawamachi, Nakanoku, Tokyo.

Mgr., Supplies Dept., Oji Paper Mfg. Co., Ltd.; Dir., Japan Wire Netting Co., Ltd.; b. Mar., 1874 in Miye-ken; s. of Hedahei Fukukita. Career: grad., Higher Sch. Dept., Doshisha, 1898; Stanford Univ., 1904; Non-Official Staff, American Embassy in Tokyo, 1906; joined present firm, 1912; present post since 1918. Address: 48 Hommuracho, Azabuku, Tokyo.

Custom Dir., Dairen, Manchoukuo; b. July, 1892 in Hyogo-ken; s. of Kosaku Fukumoto, Dr. Career: grad., Tokyo Higher Com. Sch., 1905; joined Chinese Customs Service, same year; present post since June, 1932. Address: 3 Iki-machi, Dairen.

Mng. Dir., Yamashita Steamship Co., Ltd.; b. Aug., 1888 in Kumamoto-ken. Career: grad., Nagasaki Higher Com. Sch. joined present firm, 1910; Dir., Yamashita Gomei Kaisha; Aud., Yamashita Mining Co.; Mng.-Dir., Hanshin Harbor Co., Ltd. Address: Kishimoto, Mikagemachi, Hyogo-ken.

Pres., Boring Co.; Aud., Toshima-gumi, Ltd.; b. June, 1866 in Hiroshima-ken; s. of Kei Miyata. Career: grad., Keio Univ.; Head., Polit. Dept., Hochi Shimbun; Pres., Tokyo Taisei Shimbun; same, Japan Steel Pipe & Shaft Co.; Dir., Tokyo Kogyo K. K., Taiwan Sulphur Co.; Auditor, Toa Shokufu K. K.; Pres., Kogyo-no-Nippon-Sha. Address: 548 Okusawa, Tamagawa, Setagayaku, Tokyo.

Mgr., Tokyo Branch, Sumitomo Trust Co., Ltd.; b. Oct., 1890 in Fukui-ken; s. of Kumezo Fukuyama, farmer. Career: grad., Law Coll., Tokyo Imp. Univ.; upon graduation joined Sumitomo Bank, 1916; Asst. Mgr., Shanghai Branch of same, 1927; Sub-Mgr., Business Dept., Head Office of same; Sub-Mgr., Sumitomo Trust Co., Ltd.; present post since 1931. Address: 10 Nishikatamachi, Hongoku, Tokyo.

Baron; Mem., House of Peers; Dir., Daito Cultural Society; b. Feb., 1866 in Hiroshima-ken; s. of late Baron Mamoru Funakoshi. Career: passed Diplomatic & Consular Service Exam., 1894; Eleve-Consul; Consul at Fusan, San Francisco; Acting Ambassador, Germany; attached to Tsingtao Garrison Headquarters; Minister to Mexico. Address: 22 Ichigaya-Kagamachi Nichome, Ushigomeku, Tokyo.

Dir.-Gen., Japanese Cotton Millowners' Assn., Shanghai; b. Aug., 1873 in Saga-ken; s. of Saikichi Funatsu, farmer. Career: in 1894, as Student Interpreter of Foreign Office; sent to Peiping, China; served in Russo-Japanese War; apptd. Chancellor, Foreign Office, serving at Chefoo, Tientsin, Shanghai, Yingkow, Chicago, New York; Vice-Consul at Nanking, 1905; Consul, Hongkong, 1908; same, Nanking; Sec., Legation at Peiping, 1914; Consul-General, Tientsin, 1919; same, Shanghai, 1923; resigning from same, apptd. present post 1926. Address: 610 Kinutamura, Tokyo-fu.

Mgr., Bank of Chosen, Dairen; b. 1875 in Okayama-ken; s. of Hiroshi Murayama, Govt. Official. Career: Ex-official, Okayama-ken; Okayama Agricultural and Industrial Bank; Konoike Bank; later held posts as Mgr., Wonsang and Liaoyang Branches and Head Office; Chief, Adjustment Section, Keijo; present post since 1932. Address: 2, Yamashiro-cho, Dairen.

Dir., General Affaires Bureau, Justice Dept., Manchoukuo; b. in Gifu-ken. Career: grad., German Law Coll., Tokyo Imp. Univ., 1914; Procurator, Tokyo Local Court.; Sec., Justice Office; Procurator next in rank, Tokyo Local Court 1931; Procurator, Supreme Court 1932; Present post since Oct., 1933. Address: Hsinking.

Ins. Agent & Broker; Prop., Fuji Co.; b. Jan., 1881 in Oita-ken; s. of Yasujiro Furutono, farmer. Career: grad., Law Dept., Waseda Univ., 1906; founded Fuji Co. Recreation: golf. Address: 36 Kami-Nibancho, Kojimachiku, Tokyo. Tel.: Kudan (33) 181. Marunouchi (23) 2291–3, 3094. Clubs: Japan Industrial Club, Marunouchi Club, Eiraku Club, Japan Trades Assn.

M. D.; Swiss and Japanese Diploma; Medical Practitioner; b. Mar., 1896 in Zurich, Switzerland; n. Swiss; s. of Robert Furtwaengler, business man; m. Margot Anne-Marie Beck, of Arnstadt, 1929. Career: studied at Univs. of Zurich, Lausanne and Munich; received degree, 1920; apptd. Asst., Clinics and Hospitals in Lucerne, Aarau, Winterthur (Switzerland) and Innsbruck (Austria); 1st Asst., Clinic of Surgery, Zurich Univ.; P. G. work in Vienna, London and Paris; in 1928, took over Dr. Paravicini's practice in Tokyo; Medical Officer, British Embassy in Tokyo; Surgeon, General Hospital, Yokohama: same, Kokusai Seibo Byoin, Tokyo. Recreations: walking, swimming, music. Address: 26 Ichibeicho-Nichome, Azabuku, Tokyo. Tel.: Akasaka (48) 1909. Clubs: Tokyo Club, German Asiatic Society, Tokyo; German Society of Surgery.

Mem., House of Peers; Chief Sec., Privy Council; b. Feb., 1878 in Toyama-ken; s. of Hyotaro Futagami. Career: grad., Law Coll., Tokyo Imp. Univ., 1904; passed Higher Civil Exam., same year; Councillor, Communications Office; Sec., Communications Minister; Sec., Privy Council; Sec. to Pres., Privy Council; Judge, Court of Administrative Litigation; then present post; attended World Telegraphic Conference. Address: 253 Chojamaru, Kami-Osaki, Shinagawaku, Tokyo.

Pres., Taiwan Fertilizer Co., Ltd.; Mng.-Dir., Dai-Nippon Artificial Fertilizer Co., Ltd., (since 1921); Nitto Sulphuric Fertilizer Co., Ltd.; Godo Yushi Co., Ltd.; Osaka Alkali Soil Co., Ltd., etc.; b. June, 1868 in Ehime-ken; s. of Shinzo Futagami, Pref. Assembly Member. Career: grad., English Law Dept., Chuo Univ., 1895; founded and became Mgr., Tokyo Mousseline-de-Laine Spinning Co., Ltd. 1897; joined Mitsui Bussan Kaisha in 1901, successively served as Mgr., Nagoya and Moji Branches, Asst.-Mgr., Coal Dept.; Acting Pres., Super Phosphate Industry Assn.; elected M. P. from Ehime-ken. 1928. Address: 41 Yaraimachi, Ushigomeku, Tokyo.

American Consul-General at Tokyo; b. Jan., 1873 in St. Louis; s. William and Antonie (Wiebe) Garrels; m. Elinor McEwen Norfleet, Nov., 1923. Career: grad., Smith Acad., St. Louis, Missouri; employed in banking and mfg. business, 1890–98; connected with theatrical and amusement enterprises in U. S. and Far East, 1898–1903; in bond and stock brokerage business, 1903–08; apptd. Consul to Zanzibar, June, 1908; Consul at Catania, 1910–12, Alexandria, Egypt, Aug. 1912-Dec. 1919; Consul-General, Near East and Africa, 1919–22; Mexico and West Indies, 1922–24; Athens, Greece, 1924–26; Melbourne, Austria, 1926–30; present post since 1930. Address: American Consulate-General, Tokyo, Japan.

Italian Consul-General at Kobe; b. Dec., 1867 in Florence; n. Italian. Career: grad., Rome Univ.; Interpreter to Italian Embassy; Consul at Yokohama; High Commr., Interallied Committee in Vladivostok, 1916–18; Chargè d'Affaires, Italian Embassy in Tokyo; present post since 1923. Address: 27 Yamamotodori Nichome, Kobe.

Mng.-Dir., Industrial Welfare Assn.; Commr., Social Welfare Bureau; Lecturer, Meiji Univ.; b. Apr., 1883 in Tochigi-ken; s. of Toshitaka Gamo, judge and later became lawyers. Career: grad., Law Coll., Tokyo Imp. Univ.; General Office Mgr., Tokyo Elec. Co., Ltd.; while in service promoted “Safety Movement” in Japan; leader of industrial safety movement in Japan and knowledge of new system of labor management; attended 12th Int'l Labor Conference and Annual Safety Congress, Chicago, 1929. Address: 9 Mabashi Itchome, Suginamiku, Tokyo.

Teacher; b. 1894, Oil City, Pa., U. S. A.; n. American; s. of William Jefferson Gealy, Private Sec. to the Chambers' Trust Estate, Oil City, Pa. Career: grad., Allegheny College, A. B.; Boston Univ. School of Theology, S. T. B.; Graduate study in Harvard Univ.; Univ. of Basel, Univ. of Berlin; Union Theological Seminary, S. T. M., Boston University, Ph. D.; was Minister to Townville, Pa., in the Methodist Episcopal Church, 1921–23; Prof., New Testament, Aoyama Gakuin, since 1923. Address: 3 Aoyama Gakuin, Midori-ga-oka, Shibuyaku, Tokyo.

Financier and Executive: b. 1872 in Albany, New York; n. American: Career: Dir., Tokyo Elec. Co.; Nipponophone Co.; Columbia Gramophone Co.; Shibaura Engrg. Works; Japan Steel Products Co.; Corn Products Refining Co. Address: 3 Mitsui Bldg., Nihonbashi, Tokyo.

Chief, Customs Bureau, Ministry of Finance, Manchoukuo; b. Oct., 1899 in Shimane-ken; s. of Harushichi Genda. Career: grad., Law Coll., Tokyo Imp. Univ., 1923; entered Finance Office; Supt., Sapporo Revenue Office; Chief, Financial Section, Kwantung Govt.-General, 1927–1932; apptd. present post, Mar., 1932. Address: care Ministry of Finance, Changchun, Manchoukuo.

Exchange Broker; b. May, 1876 in Malmö, Sweden; n. Swedish. Career: grad., Malmö Högre Almänna Läroverk; after 4 years' com. training in Hamburg, Germany, came Japan and joined A. Meier & Co., 1896; Partner, same firm, 1910–17; Swedish Vice-Consul, Yokohama, 1906–16; Consul, Same, 1919; Dir., Winkel & Gedde, Ltd., Kobe & Yokohama, 1918–22. Address: c.o. Elked & Gerdts, 14 Marunouchi-Nichome, Kojimachiku, Tokyo.

Kogakuhakushi (D. E.); Ordnance Vice-Admiral; Pres., Showa Steel Works; Dir., South Manchuria Ry. Co.; Gen. Mgr., Anshan Iron Works and Fushun Colliery Office; b. Oct., 1877 in Kanazawa; s. of late Takuji Godo. Career: grad., Engr. Coll., Tokyo Imp. Univ., 1901; entered naval service; Chief, Ordnance Dept., Kure Naval Arsenal; same, Steel Mfg. Dept. of same; same, Ordnance Testing Dept. of same; Chief, Aviation Dept., Hiro Arsenal; sent to Europe and America 4 times; apptd. Chief, Kure Naval Arsenal, 1924; attached to Naval Construction Dept., 1927; retired, 1928. Address: 36 Kikuicho, Ushigomeku, Tokyo.

Baron; Mem., House of Peers; Pres., Tokyo Chamber of Com. & Industry; same, Japan Chamber of Com. & Industry; Chairman, Board of Directors, Tokyo Elec. Co.; Pres., Toyo Steel Works and Japan Lead Tube Mfg. Co.; Dir., 3rd Bank; Councillor, Chujitsu Jitsugyo K. K., Nippon Yusen Kaisha, Tokyo Stock Exchange, Int'l Transportation Co., Toyo Seishi Boseki Kaisha; b. Jan., 1865 in Tokyo; s. of late Baron Junzo Goh. Career: went to Germany for study of economics, 1884; received Ph. D. degree, 1890; entered business, 1895; Mem., House of Peers since 1911; high taxpayer in Tokyo-fu. Address: 28 Kami-Nibancho, Kojimachiku, Tokyo.

Mng.-Dir., Mitsubishi Aircraft Co.; Dir., Mitsubishi Ship Bld. & Engrg. Co.; b. Nov., 1880 in Iwate-ken; s. of Tamasaburo Goko. Career: grad. Law Coll., Tokyo Imp. Univ. Address: 2 Minamicho, Ushigomeku, Tokyo.

Rear-Adm.; Dir., Naval Education Bureau; b. Jan., 1881 in Miyazaki-ken; s. of Chuzo Goto. Career: grad., Naval Academy, 1903; served Russo-Japanese War; Comdr., 1st Destroyer Flotilla; attached to Yokosuka Naval Station, then Naval General Staff Office; Comdr., H. M. S. Kako; same, Defence Corps, Yokosuka; Mem., Tech. Assembly, Naval Construction Dept.; Comdr., H. H. S. Haruna; Comdr., Makun Naval Station, Jan., 1932; present post, July, same year. Address: Navy Office, Kasumigaseki, Tokyo.

Agr. & Forestry Minister; b. Mar., 1884 in Oita-ken; s. of late Yoshitomo Goto, official. Career: grad., Law Coll., Tokyo Imp. Univ., 1908; Dir., Police Bureau; Sec.-Gen., Taiwan Govt.; Pres., Japan Young Men's Assn.; toured Europe and America for inspection; nominated Mem., House of Peers, 1930; upon formation of Saito Cabinet, apptd. present post, May, 1932. Address: 29 Konno, Shibuyaku, Tokyo.

Chief, Central Meteological Observatory, Manchoukuo; b. in Gifu-ken. Career: grad., Science Coll., Tokyo Imp. Univ.; Chief, Chosen Govt. Observatory and Engr., Central Meteorological Observatory, Tokyo; present post since Oct., 1933. Address: Hsinking.

Mng.-Dir., Meguro-Kamata Elec. Ry. Co., Tokyo-Yokohama Elec. Ry. Co.; Pres. Tamagawaen, Tokyo-Yokohama Bus & Taxi Co.; Vice-Pres., Bantan Ry. Co.; Dir., Osaka Elec. Ry. Co.; Auditor, Sangu Kyuko Elec. Ry. Co.; b. Apr., 1882 in Nagano-ken; s. of Kikuemon Kobayashi. Career: grad., Law Coll., Tokyo Imp. Univ.; resigned as Chief, Supervision Bureau, Ry. Dept., 1920, and entered business; Dir., Imp. Ry. Assn. and Tetsudo Doshikai. Address: 49 Hasedo, Shibuyaku, Tokyo.

Former Dir., Post Office Ins. Bureau, Communication Dept.; former Mng.-Dir., Japan Wireless Telegram Co., Ltd.; b. Aug., 1882 in Tokyo; s. of Takatsugu Goto, official. Career: grad., Law Dept., Tokyo Imp. Univ., 1907; upon grad., entered Communication Dept.; apptd. Dir., Local Communication Bureau; same, Post Office Ins. Bureau; same, Mail Affairs Dept.; sent to Europe and America for inspection of communication business. Address: 127 Hakusan Gotenmachi, Koishikawaku, Tokyo.

Mem., Tokyo Chamber of Com. & Industry; Dir., Nippon Girls' Higher Com. School and Nippon Girls' Com. Sch.; b. Aug., 1889 in Kumamoto-ken; s. of Mankichi Goto, rice-merchant. Career: grad., Polit. Dept., Hosei Univ.; Dir., of several concerns: for years engaged in fishing business and reclamation work. Address: 203 Mita, Meguroku, Tokyo.

Mng.-Dir., L. J. Healing & Co., Ltd., Tokyo; b. Feb., 1885 in Yokohama; n. British; s. of William Graham, engr. m. Mae Whymark. Career: studied at Winton House, Yokohama; entered present concern, 1901. Recreations: golf, swimming, tennis. Address: 13-F Reinanzaka, Akasakaku, Tokyo. Clubs: Tokyo Club, Yokohama United Club, Kobe Club.

Diplomat; American Ambassador to Japan; A. B. (Harvard Univ., 1902); LL. D. (George Washington Univ., 1926); b. May, 1880 in Boston; n. American; s. of Edward Sturgis Grew. Career: grad., Groton School, 1898; Harvard Univ., 1902; travelled extensively in Europe and the East; Clerk in Consulate-General, Cairo, 1904; Deputy Consul, Cairo, 1904-06; 3rd Secretary, American Embassy, Mexico City, 1906-07; St. Petersburg, 1907-08; 2nd Sec., Embassy, Berlin, 1908-11; Sec., Embassy, Vienna, 1911-12; Sec., Embassy, Berlin, 1912-16; Counselor of same, 1917; Counselor Embassy and Charge d'Affairs at time of break of diplomatic relations with Austria-Hungary, Vienna, 1917; assigned to Dept. of State, Washington, May, 1917; Acting Chief, Western European Affairs Division, Mar., 1918; attended Pre-Armistice Negotiations, Versailles as Sec. American Delegation, Oct.-Nov., 1918; Sec.-Gen., Am. Commission to negotiate Peace, with rank of E. E. & M. P., Paris, Nov., 1918; assignd as Am. Sec. on Int'l Secretariat of Peace Conference, Jan., 1919; apptd. E. E. & M. P. to Denmark, 1920; same to Switzerland, 1921; Am. Rep., Conference on Near Eastern Affairs, Lausanne, 1922-23; negotiated and signed Treaty with Turkey, 1923; Am. Unofficial Rep. with Temporary Mixed Commn. of League of Nations for control of Traffic in Arms, Geneva and Paris, 1924; Under Sec. of State, 1924-27; served as Chairman Personnel, Examining and School Boards of Foreign Service and as Mem., Central Comm. Am. Red Cross; Ambassador to Turkey, 1927-32; present post since Feb., 1932. Address: American Embassy, Tokyo.

Accountant; b. June, 1888 in Hackettstown, New Jersey, U. S.; n. American. Career: grad., New York Univ., (B. C. S.); joined Standard Oil Co., New York; Socony-Vacuum Corporation. Address: 250 Bluff, Yokohama.

German Secretary, Japanese-German Cultural Institute; b. Apr., 1880 in Stuttgart; n. German; s. of D. Gundert, publisher. Career: grad., Univs., Tubingen, Halle and Hamburg; served German Lutheran Church, 1902-1906; Prof., Dai-ichi Koto Gakko, Tokyo, 1906-1909; engaged in missionary work in Tokyo-fu and Niigata-ken, 1909-15; Prof., Dai-go Koto Gakko, Kumamoto, 1915-20; research work in Germany, 1920-22; Prof., Mito Koto Gakko, Mito, 1922-27; appointed present post, 1927. Address: Nichidoku Bunka Kyokai, Shisei-Kaikan, Hibiya Park, Tokyo.

Marquis; Naturalist; b. Feb., 1903 in Tokyo; s. of Marquis Masaaki Hachisuka. Career: grad., Magdalene Coll., Cambridge; went on expeditions to Egypt, 1923-24; Arctic Region in Iceland, 1925; Corcica Island, 1925 & 1926; French North Africa, 1927; Philippine Island, 1929; Belgian Congo, Africa, 1931; etc. Address: 9 Mita-Tsunamachi, Shibaku, Tokyo.
Sub-Chief, Heilungkiang Revenue Supt. Office, Manchoukuo. Career: present post since 1932. Address: Tsitsihar.

Chief, Industrial Dep't., Heilungkiang Province; same, Revenue Supt. Office, Lungkiang-fu; b. 1893 in Kin-chow, Kwantung Prov. Career: grad., Nagoya Higher Technical Sch. in Japan, 1917; Pres., Eastern Asia Industrial Co.; Pres., Asia Flour Mill Co.; Pres., Harbin Clearing House; Pres. Harbin Trust Co.; exerted in reconcilliation between Japanese Army and Ha-Chen-Shan; Councillor, Heilungkiang in 1931; after rebellion of Ma, assisted Cheng Chih-yuan in maintaining order in Heilungkiang Prov., 1932. Address: Tsitsihar.
Naval Officer; b. Mar., 1886; s. of Heizaemon Hanajima, farmer. Career: attached to Aviation Dept., Imp. Navy since 1914. Address: 127 Higashi-Chofu, Omoriku, Tokyo.

Ex-Diplomat; b. Feb., 1881 in Tokyo; s. of late Shinsetsu Hanaoka, educator. Career: grad., Law Coll., Tokyo Imp. Univ.; was Consul General in Hamburg and Charge d Affaires in Constantinople. Address: 1296 Chitosemura, Tokyo-fu.

Address: 35 Fujimicho-Nichome, Kojimachiku, Tokyo.

Pres., Harada Trading Co.; Auditor, Nippon Lace Co.; b. Mar., 1886 in Osaka; s. of Genjiro Harada. Career: inherited family estate, 1910; engaged in export and import business since then. Address: 37 Yurakucho, Nishinariku, Osaka.

Career: grad., Military Coll., 1894; Military Staff Coll., 1902; Comdr., 3rd and 26th Infantry Regiment; Staff-Officer, Taiwan Govt.; Comdr., 4th Infantry Regiment; Chief-Staff, 2nd Division; Dir., Toyama School; Commandant, Yura Fortress; Comdr., Taiwan Army, 1928; General, 1929; Comdr., Kwantung Army, 1930; Supreme War Councillor; present post since Aug., 1933. Address: Japanese Embassy, Hsinking.

Pres., Jochi Daigaku (Sophia Univ.); b. June, 1863 in Wuppertal-Elberfeld, Germany; n. German. Career: entered Society of Jesus and studied philosophy and theology for 9 years; came to Japan as Prof. of Philosophy. Address: 7 Kioicho, Kojimachiku, Tokyo.

n: Holmes, Ernest Hamilton C. M. G
t: British Consul-General at Yokohama; b. July, 1876 in England; n. British; s. of Lieut.-Col. W. P. Holmes (retired). Career: studied at Wellington Coll., England; entered H. B. M. Consular Service in Japan, 1897; Vice-Consul, 1910; Consul, 1914; present post since 1920. Address: 169 Yamatecho, Yokohama.

Writer; b. Dec., 1874 in Wakayama-ken; s. of Uhei Honda. Career: grad., Tokyo Semmon Gakko and Chuo Hogakuin; passed Diplomatic and Consular Service Exam., 1898; Sec. to Foreign Minister; Sec. at Legation and Embassy; Chief, Corr. Dept., Foreign Office; Consul-Gen.; Councillor at Legation; Minister to Switzerland and Austria; Ambassador to Germany, 1923-26. Address: 1080 Kamimeguro-Shichichome, Meguroku, Tokyo.

Rigakuhakushi (D. Sc.); b. Jan., 1897 in Kumamoto; s. of Heijiro Honda. Career: grad., 5th Higher School; Science Coll., Tokyo Imp. Univ.; apptd. Asst. Prof. of same; Lecturer, Tokyo Girls' Higher Normal School. Address: 1718 Koganei, Koganeimura, Tokyo-fu.

Igakuhakushi (M. D.); b. June, 1877 in Nagasaki-ken; s. of Kunitoshi Honda. Career: passed Examination for Medical Practitioners; sent to Germany for study, 1909; inspection tour to U. S., 1931; Mem., Nippon Ishikai (Doctors' Society); Mgr., Tokyo-fu Ishikai; Vice-Pres., Kyobashi-ku Ishikai; Mgr., Doctors' Credit Assn. Address: 5 Nishigochome, Ginza, Kyobashiku, Tokyo.

General; Chief Aide-de-camp to the Emperor; b. May, 1876 in Hyogo-ken; s. of Tsuneemon Honjo. Career: grad., Military Academy, 1897; Military Staff Coll., 1906; former Comdr., Kwantang Army; Adviser, Chang Tso-lin; directed military campaign during Manchurian Conflict; Supreme War Councillor; present post since Apr., 1933. Address: 8 Uyenoharamachi, Nakanoku, Tokyo.

Rank; Jr. 5th; 4th O. M.; Colonel; Comdr. Infantry 1st. Resiment; b. Nov., 1888 in Niigata-ken; s. of Kenkichi Honma; m. Fujiko, d. of Naokitsu Takata. Career: grad., Military Academy, 1907 and Military Coll., 1915; stationed in London, 1918 and to India, 1922; Chief, Mil. Press Bureau; Present Post since Aug., 1933. Recreation: tennis. Address: 54 Aoyama-Minamicho Gochome, Akasakaku, Tokyo. Tel.: Aoyama (36) 736.

Pres., Meisei Spinning & Weaving Co.; b. Feb., 1882 in Okayama-ken; s. of Toshiro Hori. Career: grad., Tokyo Higher Com. Sch., 1904; joined Osaka Shosen Kaisha, same year; entered Fukushima Spinning & Weaving Co., 1907; Mng.-Dir., Meisei Spinning & Weaving Co., (former Osaka Hosiery Spinning & Weaving Co.), 1912; Pres., 1931. Address: Hibarigaoka, Konishimachi, Kawabe-gun, Hyogo-ken.

Mem., House of Peers; Pres., Osaka Shosen Kaisha and Hanshin Elec. Ry. Co.; Dir., Sumitomo Bank; Auditor, Japan Nitrate Fertilizer Co., Nobeoka Ammonia Silk Industry Co.; Councillor, Asahi Silk Co.; b. Jan., 1867 in Ishikawa-ken; s. of Gohei Hori, and later adopted by late Kasumi Hori. Career: grad., Law Coll., Tokyo Imp. Univ., 1893. Address: 660 Hirao, Minomomura, Osaka-fu.

Minister to Mexico; b. Feb., 1889 in Kagoshima-ken; s. of Yukio Hori, samurai. Career: grad., Tokyo Univ. of Com., 1908; entered diplomatic service since 1908; Private Sec. to Foreign Minister, 1919-22; Chief, Diplomatic Mission attached to Expeditionary Force to Siberia, 1922; Consul-General in London, 1923-25; Councillor, Embassies in Peiping and London, 1925-31; present post since 1931. Address: 1 Mita-Tsunamachi, Shibaku, Tokyo.

M. P.; Parliamentary Vice-Minister, Finance Office; b. May, 1882 in Fukushima-ken; s. of Ryohei Horikiri. Career: grad., Keio Univ., 1903; went to U. S., England and Germany to study finance and economics; apptd. Prof. of Alma Mater; joined Jiji Shimpo; Sec. to Finance Minister; Councillor Finance Office; Sec. to Prime Minister; Parl. Councillor, Dept. of Agrl. & Com.; attended World Parl. Conf.; visited Europe after World War; apptd. present post, June, [illegible]. Address: 5 Ichigaya-Tamachi-Nichome, Ushigomeku, Tokyo.

Chief Sec., Cabinet; b. Sept., 1884 in Fukushima-ken; s. of Ryohei Horikiri. Career: grad., Law Coll., Tokyo Imp. Univ., 1909; entered Home Office and served as Inspector, Councillor, Sec.; Dir. of City Planning Bureau; Dir. of Engrg. Bureau; Gov., Kanagawa-ken; Chief, Reconstruction Bureau; Mayor of Tokyo, 1929; Vice-Minister of Overseas Affairs; Dir., Legislation Bureau, May 1932; present post since Dec., 1932. Address: 27 Takada-Oimatsucho, Koishikawaku, Tokyo.

Pres., Japan Fire-Netting Co., Asahi Iron Works; Dir., Oji Paper Mfg. Co.; Mgr., Miyakojima Works of same; Auditor, Toyo Paper Mfg. Co.; b. Jan., 1869 in Nagano-ken; s. of Yojiuemon Horikoshi. Career: grad., Chemical Dept., Tokyo Higher Tech. School, 1890; Chemistry Course, Tokyo Imp. Univ., 1893; served at Patent Bureau, Dept. of Agr. & Com. as Examiner; resigning from same, entered Oji Paper Mfg. Co. Address: 17 Sadoharacho-Sanchome, Ushigomeku, Tokyo.

Dir., Bank of Japan. Career: grad., Law Coll., Tokyo Imp. Univ., 1905; joined present bank; Inspecter, London Branch of same; Chief, Inquiry Bureau of Head Office; then present post. Address: 830 Shimo-Oehiai, Yodobashiku, Tokyo.

Prop., Horikoshi Shokai; b. May, 1863 in Tochigi-ken; brother of Hanjuro Horikoshi. Career: grad., Tokyo Higher Com. School; went to America and joined Mason and Co.; as Mgr., Japan Branch. Address: 23 Nishimachi, Azabuku, Tokyo.

Brewer of Kinshi-Masamune Brand Sake; Prop., Horino Kyuzo Honten; b. Sept., 1879 in Kyoto; s. of late Kyuzo Horino, brewer. Career: grad., Kyoto First Com. School; since then engaged in present business. Address: Nijo-Kitairu Sakaemachi-dori, Nakakyoku, Kyoto.

Consul-Gen. at New York; b Mar., 1886 in Hyogo-ken; s. of Reijun Horiuchi, 1923. Career: grad., Tokyo Imp. Univ., 1910; apptd. Attaché, Japanese Embassy in China, 1911, Sec., Embassy in London, 1915; Sec., Delegation to Paris Peace Conf.; Chief, 2nd Division of Europe & America Bureau; Consul-Gen. at Tsingtao, 1923; 1st Sec., Embassy in London; Delegate to Peace-Pact Concluding Conference at Paris; Councillor, Embassy; Chargé d'Affaires in China; Councillor, Embassy in Washington, 1933. Address: 983 Park Avenue, New York City, U. S.

Pres., Japan Motor Bus Assn.; b. Nov., 1870 in Yamanashi-ken; s. of Touemon Horiuchi, farmer. Career: grad., Tokyo Hogakuin (Law Coll.); M. P.; Mem., Yamanashi-ken Pref. Assembly; Pres., Federation of Motorcar Unions; Councillor, Tokyo Motor Bus Co. and Fuji-Minobu Ry. Co.; Pres., Fuji Sanroku Elec. Ry. Co. and Fuji Sanroku Land Co.; Auditor, Yahagi Elec. Power Co. Address: 308 Yoyogi, Shibuyaku, Tokyo.

Dir., Gen Affairs Bureau, Finance Dept., Manchoukuo; b. 1892 in Kanagawa-ken. Career: grad., Law Coll., Tokyo Imp. Univ., 1917; entered Finance Dept., same year; Chief, Mng. Section, Revenue Supt. Bureau, Kumamoto; same, Osaka; Dir., Indirect Tax Bureau, Tokyo; entered Revenue Bureau, Finance Dept.; present post since 1932. Address: Tokiwa-cho, Hsinking.

Banker; b. Feb., 1876 in Hiroshima-ken; s. of late Teijiro Hoshino. Career: grad., Law Coll., Tokyo Imp. Univ., 1905; Mgr., Osaka Branch, Bank of Japan; Pres., Kawasaki One Hundredth Bank; Auditor, Tokyo Enquiry Office; Dir., Tokyo Bankers' Club; Mem., Japan Economic Federation. Address: 481 Shirokane Sankocho, Shibaku, Tokyo.

Marquis; Mem., House of Peers; b. Oct., 1883 in Kumamoto; s. of late Marquis Morishige Hosokawa. Career: grad., Higher Course, Peers' School; went to Europe and America for inspection; apptd. Mem., Tenancy System Investigation Committee, 1923; attended World Parliamentary Com. Congress at London; at present, Pres., National Treasure Preservation Society; Mem., Peers' Committee on Hereditary Property; Special Mem., Imp. Agrl. Assn., Int'l Sightseeing Committee, National Park Committee. Address: 76 Takata Oimatsucho, Koishikawaku, Tokyo.

Minister to Czechoslovakia; b. July, 1883 in Tokyo; s. of Masatada Hotta. Career: grad., Law Coll., Tokyo Imp. Univ., 1909; Chief, Personal Bureau; Europe and America Bureau, Foreign Office, 1926. Address: 4 Tangomachi, Akasakaku, Tokyo.

Count; Mem., House of Peers; Parliamentary Vice-Minister of Navy; b. Oct., 1887 in Tokyo; s. of Viscount Chokuju Nabeshima, and later adopted by Seirin Hotta. Career: grad., Law Coll., Tokyo Imp. Univ., 1915; visited Europe and America for inspection, 1919; Parl. Councillor of Navy, 1921; Dir., Yubari Ry. Co. and Kawasaki Trust Co. Address: 5 Agechimachi, Shibuyaku, Tokyo.

Mng.-Dir., Shirahama Hot Spring Estate Co., Ltd.; b. Mar., 1874; s. of late Genya; m. Michi, d. of Toyomi 1904. Career: grad., Keio Univ., 1894; served Editorial Staff, Jiji Shimpo-Sha, 1897; Chief, Econ. Dept., Osaka Jiji Shimpo, 1905; Head, Editorial Dept., same, 1915; Asst. Mgr., Osaka Branch, Chiyoda Mutual Life Ins. Co., Ltd., 1916; Head, Fukuoka Branch, of same, 1917; Mng. Dir., Osaka House Construction Co., Ltd., 1920; Aud., Naniwa Gas Co., Ltd., 1921; elected, Investigation Committee, Leased Land and House, Osaka District Court, 1930; Dir., Meiji Motocar Road Co., Ltd. Recreations: Go-gome, Haiku-poem, Utai (song). Address: 178 Senri-yama, Mishimagun, Osaka-fu. Tel.: Suita 273. Clubs: Osaka Club, Seikosha, Kojunsha.

Baron; Prof., Tokyo Imp. Univ.; Dir., League of Nations Assn.; b. Apr., 1883 in Tokyo; s. of Baron Nobushige Hozumi. Career: grad., Law Coll., Tokyo Imp. Univ., 1908; studied civil law and jurisprudence at Bonn, Berlin, Paris, London and Cambridge Univs., 1912-16; received degree, 1917; Mem., Administration Dept., Higher Civil Service Exam. Committee. Address: 9 Haraikatamachi, Ushigomeku, Tokyo.

Finance Minister and Governor of Kirin Province, Manchukuo; Dir., Manchuria Cultural Society; Lieut.-General; b. Aug., 1884 in Mukden Province. Career; grad., Military Academy. Tokyo; apptd. Instructor, Military Coll., Tungsan Province; Dir. of same; Chief Staff, Kirin Army Office; Sec.-General of Kirin Province. Address: Tungtien Town, Kirin Province.

Minister of Foreign Affairs, Manchoukuo; Chief Sec., Manchoukuo Hsiehhohui; b. 1878 in Shinchiku, Formosa, Japan. Career: grad., Shinchiku Public Sch.; Interpreter & Lecturer of Formosan Language, Oriental Society Sch.; grad., Meiji Univ., Tokyo, Japan; Chief Prof., Fukien Law Sch.; Political Adviser, Kirin Prov. Office; Chief Sec. to Chang Hsun, 1917; Dir., International Relation Bureau, Kirin, 1931; came to Japan as Envoy, returning courtesies for recognition of Manchoukuo and was received as National Guest, 1932; present post since 1932. Address: Hsinking.

Metropolitan Police General, Manchoukuo; b. 1888 in Yingkou-Hsien, Mukden Prov. Career: Chief, Kirin Police Dept.; Chief, Kirin Local Protection Corps Office; present post since 1932. Address: Hsinking.
Vice-Minister, Education Dept., Manchoukuo. Career: present post since establishment of Manchoukuo. Address: Hsinking.
Sec., Chief Executive Office, Manchoukuo; b. 1876 in Chekiang Prov. Career: Chief Sec., Liaoning Prov. Office; Adviser, Heilungkiang Prov. Office; present post since 1932. Address: Hsinking.
Chief, Industrial Dept., Mukden Prov.; Mgr., Organization Dept., Manchoukuo, Hsiehhohui. Career: present post since 1932. Address: Mukden.
Dir., Mukden High Procurator's Office. Career: present post since 1932. Address: Mukden.
Chief Sec., Chief Executive Office, Manchoukuo; b. 1869 in Kweichow Prov. Career: Pres., Peiyang Law Coll., Tientsin; present post since 1932. Address: Hsinking.
Swedish Minister to Tokyo; Dr., Philology (Upsala); LL. D. (Upsala); b. 1876 in Sweden. Career: Administration, Consular & Diplomatic Service. Address: 63, Zaimokucho, Azabuku, Tokyo.

Count; Mem. of House of Peers; b. Oct., 1886; s. of Marquis Munée Daté. Career: grad., Law Coll., Tokyo Imp. Univ., 1913; passed Higher Civil Service Exam., 1913; sent to Europe and America; apptd. Sec. and Councillor, Househod Dept., 1924; Mem., House of Peers since 1925; Chief Director of Boy Scouts of Japan since 1922; International Committee of Boy Scouts International Bureau since 1931. Address: 12 Kasumigaoka, Yotsuyaku, Tokyo.

Chargé d'Affaires of Legation at Vienna; b. July, 1894 in Ibaragi-ken; s. of late Saichi Ichige, landowner. Career: grad., Law Coll., Tokyo Imp. Univ., 1918; Elève-Consul at Hongkong, same year; served at Paris, Tokyo, Brazil, Switzerland, Vienna. Address: Japanese Legation, Vienna, Austria.

b. July, 1892 in Tokyo; s. of late Motome Ichihara. Career: grad., Engrg. Coll., Tokyo Imp. Univ.; entered his father's Co. (mfg. & sale fire pump) and after his father's death succeeded him; Auditor, Den-entoshi (Garden City) K. K. Address: 53 Takanawa-Minamicho, Shibaku, Tokyo.

Author; b. May, 1893 in Aichi-ken; d. of Tokuro Ichikawa, farmer. Career: grad., Aichi-ken Pref. Girls' Normal School; became primary school teacher, journalist, then Clerk of Labor Union; with Raicho Hiratsuka, participating in organization of New Women's Assn., started Women's Suffrage movement in Japan 1919; went to America for study of women's and labor movements, 1921–23; entered Tokyo Office, Int'l Labor Office, serving for research of labor problems 4 years; organized Women's Suffrage League of Japan, 1924; attended First Pan-Pacific Women's Conference as Japan's Delegate, visiting America on way home, 1928. Address: 20 Nakacho-Sanchome, Yotsuyaku, Tokyo.

Bungakuhakushi (D. Litt.); Prof., Tokyo Imp. Univ.; b. Feb., 1886 in Tokyo; s. of Sanken Ichikawa, Calligrapher. Career: grad., Tokyo Imp. Univ., 1909; sent to England to study English Philology, 1912–16; apptd., Asst. Prof., Tokyo Imp. Univ.; 1916; present post since 1920; received degree, 1922; elected Albert Kahn Travelling Fellowship, 1931–32, then travelled round world; Mem., High School Teachers Exam. Committee. Address: 25 Kitayamabushicho Ushigomeku, Tokyo.

Dir., Yokohama Specie Bank, Ltd.; b. Jan., 1870 in Fukuoka-ken; s. of Tadao Ichinomiya, samurai. Career: grad., Doitsu Kyokai Gakko; fought in Russo-Japanese War; joined Yokohama Specie Bank, 1896; Mgr., New York Branch; promoted Vice-Pres.; Mem., Yokohama Chamber of Com. & Industry. Address: 152 Sankocho, Yotsuyaku, Tokyo.

Toilet Goods Mfr., b. Mar., 1889; s. of Sadakichi Ida, official. Career: Mem., Honjo Urban District Assembly: Auditor, Tokyo Toilet Goods Traders' Assn. Address: 22 Hayashicho-Sanchome, Honjoku, Tokyo.

Architect, Formosan Govt.-Gen.; b. Feb., 1879 in Gifu-ken; s. of Imashige Ide. Career: grad., Archt. Coll., Tokyo Imp. Univ., 1906; joined Ninth Battation of Engineers as one year volunteer; promoted to Sub.-Lieutenant Engineer, 1908; served, Architecture Office, 1907–1910; apptd. Non-Official Staff to Formosan Govt.-Gen., 1910; made world tour for one year, 1919; present post since 1919. Address: 53 of 2, Taishomachi, Taihoku, Formosa.
Dir., Central Bank, Manchoukuo. Career: present post since 1932. Address: Hsinking.

A. B.; B. D.; S. T. D.; Missionary; b. Nov., 1878 in Greencastle, Indiana, U. S.; n. American; s. of Ferd. C. Iglehart, clergyman and editor. Career: grad., Columbia Coll., Drew Theol. Sem., New York Univ.; was Paster in New York Conference, 1899–1904; came to Japan, 1904; appointed Teacher, Aoyama Gakuin; Acting Dean of the Coll.; Acting Paster, Union Church; Chairamn of Board, Japanese School of Language and Culture; Vice-Chairman, Christian Literature Society; same, American School in Japan; Executive Committee, American Assn. of Japan. Address: 6 Aoyama Gakuin, Shibuyaku, Tokyo.
Sec., Bank of Japan; b. Feb., 1886 in Miye-ken; s. of Zenjuro Igura. Career: grad., Economic Dept., Keio Univ., 1911; joined Bank of Japan; served Osaka Branch. Address: 8 Kogaicho, Azabuku, Tokyo.

Kogakushi (B. E.); Pres., Bofu Elec. Co. and Hagi Elec. Co.; Mng.-Dir., Hiroshima Elec. Co.; b. Feb., 1873 in Yamaguchi-ken. Career: grad., Engrg. Coll., Tokyo Imp. Univ. Address: Hanayashiki, Kawanishimachi, Kawabegun, Hyogo-ken.
Acting Partner, "Japan & Japanese" Pub. Co.; b. Dec., 1870 in Matsuyama, Ehime-ken; s. of late Sakuhei Ihogi, business man. Career: studied by himself. Address: 11 Yakuojimachi, Ushigomeku, Tokyo.

Consul Honoraire, Délégué Commercial of Brazil in Japan; b. May, 1866 in Tokyo; s. of Tatsumi Iida, Dir., Bank of Japan. Career: grad., Tokyo Univ. of Com.; apptd. Chief Clerk, Bank of Japan; Prof., Tokyo Univ. of Com.; Chief Clerk, Yokohama Specie Bank; Gen. Mgr., New York Life Ins. Co.; Sec., Yokohama Chamber of Commerce; Dir. of several com. cos.; went U. S., Europe, China, South America, Tahiti, etc.; wrote several literary and commercial books. Address: 19 Nishi-Edogawacho, Koishikawaku, Tokyo.

Pres., Yurin Life Ins. Co., Ltd.; South Manchuria Taiko G. K.; b. May, 1873 in Fukuoka-ken; s. of Kyusuke Iida, farmer. Career: grad., Chuo Univ.; admitted to bar; served at Kado Hara's Law-Office; opened his own law-office. Address: 49 Kamirokubancho, Kojimachiku, Tokyo.

Rank: Sr. 6th; 6th O. M.; Pres., Iida G. K.; Takashimaya & Co., Ltd.; b. Oct., 1859 in Kyoto; s. of Shinshichi Iida, draper; m. late Fumiko, 1881. Career: inherited family estate, 1888; established Takashimaya-Iida Co., Ltd. (present Takashimaya Department Store); Mng. Dir., Kyoto Textile Mfg. Co., Ltd.; Vice-Pres., Kyoto Educational Assn.; Counsellor, Chamber of Com. & Industry, Kyoto and many other assns. and societies. Recreations: Utai, pictures and writing. Address: 1 Yakushimaecho, Karasumarudori-Matsuharaagaru, Shimo-Kyoku, Kyoto. Tel.: Shimo 679. Club: Com. & Industrial Club, Kyoto.

Acting Partner, Kaiyosha; Dir., Nippon Steamship Co.; Mng.-Dir., Osaka Iron Works; Dir., Mukojima Dockyard; Auditor, Nippon Kyodo Steamship Co.; b. May, 1888 in Osaka; adopted-s. of Mitsugu Iijima. Career: grad., Tokyo Higher Com. School, 1913; Prof., Kobe Higher Com. Sch.; Mgr., Kuhara Trading Co. Address: 1326 Enomoto, Mikagemachi, Mukogun, Hyogo-ken.

Kogakuhakushi (D. E.); Research Staff, Mitsubishi Shipbuilding & Engineering Co.; b. May, 1893 in Yamanashi-ken; s. of Jutaro Iitaka, landlord. Career: grad., Science Coll., Tokyo Imp. Univ. Address: 329 Kamikomagome, Toshimaku, Tokyo.

Igakuhakushi (M. D.); Prof., Kyoto Medical Coll.; Chief, Medical Dept., Attached Hospital; b. May, 1887 in Akita-ken; s. of Hikoshiro Iizuka, landlord. Career: grad., Agrl. Coll., Tohoku Imp. Univ., 1912; Medical Coll., Kyoto Imp. Univ., 1916; apptd. Asst. Prof., Kyoto Imp. Univ., 1922; sent abroad to study at Collège de France and L'Institut Pasteur; present post since 1926. Address: Karasumaru-Higashiiru, Kami-Goryomaedori, Kami-Kyoku, Kyoto.

Igakuhakushi (M. D.); Dir., Kitahama and Shimanouchi-Kayodo Hospital; b. Jan., 1885 in Kyoto-fu; s. of Sokichi Ijiri, druggist. Career: grad., Medical Coll., Kyushu Imp. Univ., 1910; upon graduation served as Asst. and Lecturer of same; apptd. Head Dermato-Urologist, Kaisei Hospital, Osaka, 1917; received degree, 1918; founded Kayodo Hospital, 1921; established present Hospital, 1924. Address: 466 Shimizudani-Higashinomachi, Higashiku, Osaka.

Lawyer; b. Oct., 1892 in Hokkaido; s. of Sokichi Ijuin, educator. Career: grad., Law Coll., Tokyo Imp. Univ.; entered Finance Office; served as Sec. and Head, Business Dept., Hokkaido Monopoly Bureau; transfered to Foreign Dept., 1921; Sec. in Treaty Bureau and Cultural Work Dept.; Sec., Imp. Embassy, Germany; Consul-Gen., Chengtu (China); resigned and opened law office, 1928. Address: 1 Nagasumicho, Yotsuyaku, Tokyo.

Hogakushi (B. L.); Head Translator, Nippon Roche K. K. (Sole Agents, F. Hoffman-La Roche & Co., Basle, Switzerland); b. Oct., 1902 in Shizuoka-ken; s. of Yonosuke Ikeda, civil engr. Career: grad., English Dept., Tokyo School of Foreign Languages, 1923; Law & Litt. Coll., Tohoku Imp. Univ., 1927; served as English Editor Japan Tourist Bureau until Feb., 1931 and participated in making plans for overseas propaganda; present post since Mar., 1931. Address: 1088 Daita, Setagayaku, Tokyo.

Hogakushi (B. L.); M. P.; b. Feb., 1880; s. of Tetsu Ikeda, Teacher. Career: grad., Law Coll., Tokyo Imp. Univ., 1902: passed Higher Civil Service Exam.; Staff, Asahi Shimbun, 1909; apptd. Official, Overseas Affairs Dept., 1910; Sec., same Dept., 1911; Councillor, Nagano-ken, Hiroshima-ken and Miyagi-ken; Chief, Police Dept., Gifu-ken, 1917; Sec. for Foreign and Home Affairs, 1918; Chief, Home Affairs Dept., Miyagi-ken, 1922; same, Hiroshima-ken, 1922; Gov., Akita-ken, 1924; Dir., Industry Bureau of Chosen, 1924–28; Gov., Hokkaido, 1929–31; Pres., Keijo Nippo, 1931–32; elected to Diet from Saga-ken, 1932. Address: 2122 Kamimeguro, Meguroku, Tokyo.

Mgr., Mikimoto Pearl Store; b. Dec., 1876 in Hyogo-ken; s. of Kotaro Ikeda. Career: grad., Law Coll., Tokyo Imp. Univ., 1903; joined 1st Bank; shifted to Bank of Chosen, 1909; joined Mikimoto Pearl Store, 1911; present post since 1915; made inspection tour abroad 4 times. Address: 21 Oyamacho, Shibuyaku, Tokyo.

Mem., House of Peers; b. July, 1883 in Tokyo; s. of late Takamasa Chizaka, and later adopted by late Chojun Ikeda. Career: grad., Law Coll., Kyoto Imp. Univ., 1911. Address: 6 Aoyama Minamicho, Akasakaku, Tokyo.

Mng.-Dir., Mitsui Gomei Kaisha; Mng.-Dir., Mitsui Bank.; Rep. Dir., Mitsui Trust Co.; b. Oct., 1867; s. of Nariakira Ikeda, banker. Career: grad., Keio Univ.; Harvard Univ.; Staff Mem., Jiji Shimpo; joined Mitsui Bank, 1895. Address: 1 Nagasakacho, Azabuku, Tokyo.

Igakuhakushi (M. D.); Medical Practitioner; b. June, 1883 in Osaka; s. of Taizo Ikeda, physician. Career: grad., Medical Coll., Kyoto Imp. Univ.; served as house-doctor to Fusanosuke Kuhara, 1912–19; medical practice in Osaka since 1923. Address: 26 Azuchimachi-Nichome, Higashiku, Osaka.

Surgeon; Igakuhakushi (M. D.); b. Dec., 1884 in Chiba-ken; e. s. of Yoshiro Ikeda. Career: grad., Medical Coll., Tokyo Imp. Univ., 1911; Asst. of same, 1912–15; Prof., Surgery, Nippon Univ. Medical School, 1915–29.; Chief Surgeon, Reiganjima Hospital since 1929. Address: 17 Fujimicho Gochome, Kojimachiku, Tokyo.

Igakuhakushi (M. D.); Prof., Kumamoto Medical Coll.; b. Dec., 1883 in Mie-ken; s. of Enjiro Ikegami, doctor. Career: grad., Medical Coll., Tokyo Imp. Univ., 1907; served at Fusan Hospital, Chosen, 1913; Dir. of same, 1916; received degree, 1922; present post since 1919. Address: 76 Higashi-kogaicho, Kumamoto.

Hogakuhakushi (D. L.); Ex-Imperial Household Minister; b. Apr., 1867 in Shizuoka-ken; s. of Ryoichiro Okada and later adopted by Kisashi Ikki. Career: grad., Law Coll., Tokyo Imp. Univ., 1887; studied in Germany, 1890–93; Prof., Tokyo Imp. Univ. and Sec., Home Office, 1893; Councillor, Home Office, 1899; nominated Mem., House of Peers, 1900; Vice-Minister, Home Office, 1908; changed to Home Minister from Education Minister in 2nd Okuma Cabinet; Privy Councillor, 1917; Vice-Privy Council, 1917. Address: Ichibancho, Kojimachiku, Tokyo.

Dir., Okura & Co. (Trading) Ltd.; b. June, 1885 in Nagano-ken; e. s. of Kensuke Imai, Mem., House of Peers. Career: grad., Engrg. Coll., Tokyo Imp. Univ., 1910; then studied at P.-G. Course of same; entered Okura & Co., 1911; built Honkeiko Iron Works; appointed Lecturer, Waseda Univ.; Mgr., New York Branch, Okura & Co., 1916; returned home via Europe, 1920; Dir., Okura Mining Co., Ltd., 1922. Address: 6 Shinryudocho, Azabuku, Tokyo.

Mem., House of Peers; Pres., Matsumoto Chamber of Com. & Industry; Dir., Sericultural Society; Mem., Central Committee, Federation of Nagano-ken Raw-Silk Trade Unions; Pres., Katakura Life Ins. Co., Sino-Japanese Sericultural Co., Chuo Elec. Co. and Shinano Ry. Co.; Vice-Pres., Katakura Spinning & Weaving Co.; Dir., Tokyo-Omiya Elec. Ry. Co., Nippon Kyoritsu Fire Ins. Co., Nippon Sericultural Warehouse Co. and S. America Land Co.; Adviser, Yokohama Exchange, Ltd. and Fukoku Fire Ins. Co.; b. Nov., 1859 in Nagano-ken; brother of Kentaro Katakura, company pres.; adopted s. of Taro Imai. Career: went to America, 1886; established Katakura-Gumi cooperating with his brother, 1890; apptd. its Vice-Pres., 1920. Address: 627 Yoyogi-Hatsudaicho, Shibuyaku, Tokyo.

Civil Administrative Chief of Chosen; b. Feb., 1884 in Okayama-ken; s. of Yosaburo Kunishiro; adopted by Zenjuro Imaida. Career: grad., Law Coll., Tokyo Imp. Univ., 1909; passed Higher Civil Service Exam., 1910; Chief, Kumamoto Communications Bureau; Chief, Post-Office Ins. Bureau; Chief, Elec. Bureau, Osaka City; Vice-Minister of Communications, 1929; went to Europe and America, 1914. Address: Official Residence, (Chosen Govt.) Keijo.

Kogakuhakushi (D. E.); Dir., Nippon Steel Tube Co., Ltd.; b. June, 1867 in Gunma-ken; s. of Tsuneko Imaizumi, doctor. Career: grad., Engrg. Coll., Tokyo Imp. Univ., 1892; served as Engr., Yawata Iron Works, 1896–1910; Mem., House of Peers, 1920–24; Hon. Consul-Gen., Luxenburg since 1923; sent to Europe and America 7 times, elected Life Mem., Iron & Steel Inst., England, 1903; Mem., Verein Deutscher Eisenhuttenleute; Pres., Nikkan Kogyo Shimbun (Industrial Daily); present post since 1929. Address: 4 Onden-Nichome, Shibuyaku, Tokyo.

Igakuhakushi (M. D.); Prof. and Chief, Internal Treatment, Tokyo Women's Medical Coll.; b. Feb., 1883 in Kagoshima; s. of late Akikiyo Imamura, samurai. Career: grad., Medical Coll., Tokyo Imp. Univ.; Councillor, Internal Treatment Inst. Address: 56 Yaraicho, Ushigomeku, Tokyo.

Aud., Nippon Rayon Co.; Mng. Dir., Dai Nippon Spinning Co.; b. Dec. 1879 in Nara-ken; s. of Kinzo Imamura, Ex-M. P. Career: grad., Engrg. Coll., Kyoto Imp. Univ. and Haverford Univ.; entered Settsu Spinning Co., Ltd. (present Dai Nippon Spinning oC.); Divisional Mgr., Nara-ken, of Seiyukai Party. Address: 746 Genge, Shikugawa, Nishinomiya City, Hyogo-ken.

Pres., Imamura Bank; Dir., Kisha Seizo (Cars & Locomotives Mfg.) Co.; Dir., 1st Mutual Life Ins. Co., Tropical Industry Co., and Taiwan Development & Tea Mfg. Co., Ltd.; b. Nov., 1877 in Tokyo; 2nd s. of Seinosuke Imamura. Career: studied at Trinity Coll. and Cambridge Univ. (M. A.). Address: 2808 Kokubunji, Tokyo.

Gov., Karafuto Govt.; b. Nov., 1880; s. of Tsunesada Imamura, Miyagi-ken. Career: grad., Law Coll., Tokyo Imp. Univ., 1908; passed Higher Civil Service Exam., 1909; Gov., Kokaido (Chosen); Dir., Industry Bureau of Chosen; present post since July, 1932. Address: Official Residence, Toyohara, Karafuto.

Kogakuhakushi (D. E.); Pres., Uraga Dockyard, Ltd.; Dir., Amagasaki Harbor Office and Hanshin Harbor Co., Ltd.; b. Feb., 1874 in Osaka; s. of Hitoshi Imaoka, samurai. Career: grad., Engrg. Coll., Tokyo Imp. Univ., 1898; apptd. Engr., Communications Office; served in Shipping Section, Shipping Bureau; Engr., Ry. Office, Marine Bureau and Ry. Supt. Bureau; Chief, Shipping Section, Mercantile Marine Bureau; Judge, Higher Court of Marine Inquiry; made inspection tour to Europe and America. Address: 45 Gochome, Aoyama-Minamicho, Akasakaku, Tokyo.

Igakuhakushi (M. D.); Pres. and Prof., Manchuria Medical Coll.; b. Apr., 1879 in Miye-ken; s. of Sotaro Onakamichi; adopted-s. of Samon Inaba. Career: grad., Medical Coll., Kyoto Imp. Univ., 1904; apptd. Asst. Prof. of same, 1909; Head Physician, Dairen Hospital; Pres. and Prof., S. Manchuria Medical School; Head Physician, Mukden Hospital; present post since 1922. Address: 8 Yawatacho, Mukden, Manchoukuo.

Mem., House of Peers; Pres., Inabata & Co., Japan Dyestuff Mfg. Co.; Dir., Japan Air Transport Co., South Korean Ry. Co., Nippon Beer and Mineral Water Co., Japan Radio Corporation, Fukoku Conscription Ins. Co., Ltd.; Auditor, Japan Wireless Telegraph Co., Kyoraku Land Co., Shimazu Seisaku-sho, Ltd.; b. Oct., 1862 in Kyoto; s. of Risuke Inabata. Career: while in Kyoto Normal School in 1877, was sent to France for study of Applied Chemistry, and studied art of dyeing at dyeing factory; represented Kyoto Pref. Exhibitions at International Exhibition held at Amsterdam, 1883, investigating at same time chemical industry in Holland; returned home, 1884 after investigating dyeing industry in England, Germany, Italy, Belgium and Switzerland, etc.; established Inabata & Co., 1890 and Inabata Dyeing Works, 1896; Khaki uniform so extensively used during Russo-Japanese War, manufactured by him; attended as Japanese Employers' Delegate at International Labor Conference, Geneva, 1927; Mem., Board of Tourist Industry Committee, and several committees; Pres., Osaka Chamber of Com. and Industry; Vice-Pres., Chamber of Com. and Industry of Japan; Chairman, Osaka Russo-Japanese Trade Assn., etc. Address: 51 Junkeimachi Nichome, Minamiku, Osaka.

Mng. Dir., Inabata & Co.; Dir., Inabata Dyeing Works; Vice-Consul for Portugal and Poland, Osaka; Councillor of “Institute de Rapprochement Intellectuel Franco-Japonais du Kwansai”; b. May, 1898 in Kyoto; s. of Katsutaro Inabata, business man. Career: grad., Tokyo Higher Com. School. Address: 51 Junkeimachidori Nichome, Minamiku, Osaka.

Lieut.-General; Steward, H. I. H. Prince Kan-in's Household; b. May, 1870 in Shimane-ken; s. of Ryosai Inagaki. Career: grad., Military Academy, 1891; apptd. Cavalry Sub.-Lieut., 1892; Staff, Gen. Staff Office; Aide-de-Camp; Comdr., Cavalry 1st Regiment; Attaché, Embassy in England; present post since 1930. Address: 4 Sakaedori-Nichome, Shibuyaku, Tokyo.

Mgr., Nara Branch, Hypothec Bank of Japan; b. July, 1889 in Nagoya; s. of Soshichi Inahata, business man. Career: grad., Law Coll., Tokyo Imp. Univ.; joined present bank; visited Europe and America for inspeciton, 1921; having successively served as Asst. Mgr., Kyoto and Osaka Branches, Mgr., Tottori Branch, apptd. present post. Address: 829 Kamishimizu-yokocho, Nara City.

Hogakuhakushi (D. L.); Lawyer; Attorney; Prof., Meiji Univ.; b. Feb., 1884 in Yamanashi-ken; s. of Seigoro Inomata, business man. Career: grad., Law Dept., Meiji Univ.; fought in Russo-Japanese War; admitted into bar, 1906; apptd. Prof., Meiji Univ., 1920; Liquidator, 1920; bestowed degree, 1924; assumed Pres., Tokyo Bar Assn., 1928. Address: 3 Ginza-Nishi Nichome, Kyobashiku, Tokyo.

Branch Mgr. and Chief, Silk Dept., Mitsui Bussan Kaisha; b. June, 1873 in Kyoto-fu; s. of Jihei Inoue. Career: grad., Kyoto Com. School, 1891; entered Mitsui Bussan Kaisha; Auditor, Chosen Silk Co.; Toyo Babcock Co.; Mgr., Imp. Silk-Thread Ware-House Co.; Special Mem. and Adviser, Yokohama Chamber of Com. & Industry. Address: 27 Asahigaoka, Kanagawaku, Yokohama.

Ex-Pres., Iyo Elec. Ry. Co.; b. May, 1865 in Ehime-ken; s. of Tomohei Inoue. Career: grad., Law Dept., Tokyo Imp. Univ.; elected M. P., 3 times; Pres., Matsuyama Chamber of Com. & Industry; Dir., Matsuyama Higher Com. School and Hokuyo Middle Sch. Address: 4 Toyosakamachi Nichome, Matsuyama.

Marquis; Chief, Mobilization Section, Preparatory Bureau of War Dept.; b. Feb., 1887 in Tokyo; s. of late Prince Taro Katsura, later adopted by late Marquis Katsunosuke Inoue. Career: grad., Military Coll.; stayed 3 years in Europe and America for study of military affairs; apptd. Artillery Sub.-Lieut., 1906; promoted Col., 1929. Address: 42 Miyamuracho, Azabuku, Tokyo.

Consul at Milan; b. Aug., 1890 in Tokyo; s. of Otokichi Inoue. Career: grad., Tokyo School of Foreign Languages; attached Embassies at Paris and Italy as Diplomatic Probationer and Sec.; present post since 1926. Address: Consolato Delvia Giappone, Melloni 46, Milan, Italia.

Pres., Keio Elec. Ry. Co., Sagami Gas Co., Toyo Wire-Gauze Co., Ltd; b. June, 1859 in Kanagawa-ken; s. of Matsura Inoue. Career: grad., Meiji Law Coll.; apptd. Dir., Yokohama Iron Works Co., 1889; Mgr., Nippon Silk Spinning Co., 1891; held patent right on Refining of Silk Spinning Stuff; apptd. Factory Mgr. and Com. Dept. Mgr., Fuji Spinning Co.; Adviser, Jomo Twisted Silk Co.; went to India and China to inspect com. and industry; elected to Diet from Kanagawa-ken, 1911; Mgr., Tamagawa and Oji Elec. Ry. Cos., Ltd.; same, Nambu Ry. Co., Daido Elec. Co., Tamagawa Ice-Mfg. Co., Ltd.; Auditor, Elec. Co., Tamagawa Ice-Mfg. Co., Ltd.; Auditor, Elec. Assn. Address: 594 Yoyogi-Hatsudai, Shibuyaku, Tokyo.

General; Pres., Kai-ko Sha; b. Jan., 1872 in Yamaguchi-ken; brother of Bunzo Inouye. Career: grad., Military Academy, 1893; Instructor, Military Coll. and Naval Staff Coll.; Comdr., 3rd Division; General, 1927; fought in Russo-Japanese War; Supreme War Councillor; resigned post 1932. Address: 44 Kotaki, Nakanoku, Tokyo.

Kogakuhakushi (D. E.); Emeritus Prof., Tohoku Imp. Univ.; b. Nov., 1868 in Kyoto; s. of Kinsho Inouye. Career: grad., Applied Chem. Course, Engrg. Coll., Tokyo Imp. Univ., 1896; apptd. Prof., Tokyo Imp. Univ., then Tohoku Imp. Univ.; became Dean, Engrg. Coll., then Pres. of same. Address: 1219 Ôharacho, Setagayaku, Tokyo.

Rigakuhakushi (D. Sc.); Emeritus Prof., Ryojun Coll. of Engrg.; b. Dec., 1873 in Yamaguchi-ken; s. of Nobuatsu Inouye. Career: grad., Sc. Coll., Tokyo Imp. Univ., 1896; apptd. Engr., Taiwan Govt., Agrl. & Com. Dept., Imps. Steel Works, successively; as Dir., Imp. Geological Survey and as Pres., Ryojun Coll. of Engrg., sent to Int'l Geological Congress held in Austria, Sweden and Canada; received degree, 1917. Address: 96 Shirokane Imazatocho, Shibaku, Tokyo.

Pres., Kaigai Kogyo Co., Ltd.; Peru Cotton Co.; Dir., Nana Co.; Auditor, Sumatra Kogyo Co.; Kainan Sangyo Co.; b. June, 1876; s. of Tahei Adachi and later adopted by Tobei Inouye. Career: studied at Kogyokusha, Naval Coll. and Waseda Univ.; studied Colonization Policy and Economics at Wien and Berlin Univs.; Commissioner, Communications Office; Financial Officer, Chosen Govt.; Man. Dir., Nanyo Kyokai; Dir., Toa Dobun Shoin. Address: 3547 Motosugamo, Takatamachi, Toshimaku, Tokyo.

Igakuhakushi (M. D.); Ophthalmologist; Commr., Court Physicians Bureau; Head, Ophthalmological Dept., Juntendo Hospital; b. Mar., 1875 in Nagano-ken; s. of Tatsuya Inouye, eye-especialist. Career: grad., Medical Coll., Tokyo Imp. Univ.; upon graduation, studied Opthalmology at Post-Graduate Course of same; went to Germany to study at Univs. of Leipzig and Wien, 1902; began medical practice at Inouye Ophthalmological Hospital; studied, Univ. of Berlin and Leipzig, 1909; apptd. Prof., Okayama Medical Coll.; Dir., Okayama Ophthalmological Hospital, 1912; received degree, 1914; present post since 1918; opened private hospital, 1918; apptd. Commr., Court Physicians Bureau, 1930. Address: 66 Nagatacho Nichome, Kojimachiku, Tokyo.

Mem., House of Peers; Viscount; Kogakuhakushi (D. E.); Mem., House of Peers; b. Apr., 1876 in Kumamoto-ken; s. of Okoku Okamatsu, and later adopted by Takeshi Inouye. Career: grad., Engrg. Coll., Tokyo. Imp. Univ., 1899; went to Germany and America for study, 1901; Asst. Prof., Tokyo Imp. Univ.; Prof., Osaka Higher Tech. Sch.; same, Kyoto Imp. Univ.; Parl. Vice-Minister of Navy; Ry. Minister, 1926–27. Address: 28 Takanawa Minamicho, Shibaku, Tokyo.

Igakuhakushi (M. D.); Ophthalmologist; b. Feb., 1881 in Tokyo; s. of Tatsuya Inouye, ophthalmologist. Career: grad., Medical Coll., Tokyo Imp. Univ., 1904; studied at Univ. of Leipzig and Royal London Ophthalmic Hospital; went abroad and visited many hospitals in France and America; Dir., Inouye Ophthalmic Hospital, Surugadai. Address: 14 Higashikobaicho, Surugadai, Kanda, Tokyo.

Pres., Rengo Shiki Kabushiki Kaisha; b. Oct., 1882 in Hyogo-ken; s. of Zenkuro Hasegawa. Career: established present firm, 1919; toured Europe and America for Inspection, 1929. Address: 34 Matsubaramachi, Nishinomiya-shi, Hyogo-ken.

Hogakuhakushi (L. D.); Attorney; b. Nov., 1876 in Nara-ken; s. of Seigo Inui. Career: grad., Law Coll., Tokyo Imp. Univ., 1900; sent to Germany for study at Univs. of Berlin and Bonn, 1901–1905; apptd., Prof., Tokyo Univ. of Com.; Lecturer, Law Faculty, Tokyo Imp. Univ.; Lecturer and Overseer, Hosei Univ.; Lecturer, Keio, Meiji and Senshu Univs.; apptd. twice Pres., Tokyo Bar Assn. Address: 12 Komagome-Akebonocho, Hongoku, Tokyo.

Nogakuhakushi (Dr. Agr.); Prof., Zoology, Hokkaido Imp. Univ.; b. Oct., 1897 in Nagano-ken; s. of Takeji Inukai, farmer. Career: grad., Agrl. Coll., Hokkaido Imp. Univ.; studied in U. S. as Fellow, Rockefeller Foundation, 1926–28; sent to Germany for study, 1928–29. Address: Zoological Institute, Hokkaido Imp. Univ., Sapporo City.

Ex-Pres., China Leaf-Tobacco Co.; b. Apr., 1874 in Okayama City; s. of Ishio Inumaru. Career: grad., Haverford Coll., Pa., U. S.; sent to England and America as student of Agrl. & Com. Dept.; apptd. to expert of industry, same Dept.; Mng. Dir., Tokyo Super Phosphate Works; Mng. Dir., Tokyo Rice & Produce Exchange, Ltd.; Mng. Dir., Tokyo Confectionary Co., Ltd. Address: 60 Gotanda 5-chome, Tokyo.

Mgr., Imp. Hotel, Tokyo.; b. 1888 in Ishikawa-ken; brother of Jintaro Inumaru. Career: grad., Tokyo Higher Com. Sch., 1910; joined South Manchuria Ry. Co.; having practised and inspected hotel business in China, Europe and America 7 yrds., joined present hotel as Sub-Mgr., 1919; present post since 1923. Address: 15 Hirakawacho Gochome, Kojimachiku, Tokyo.

Rank: Sr. 5th; Bungakuhakushi (D. Litt.); O. M.; Prof., Tokyo Imp. Univ.; b. Dec., 1885 in Tottori-ken; s. of Motosaburo Irisawa, famer; m. Chigusa, d. of Ryotaro Miyahara. Career: grad., Litt. Coll., Tokyo Imp. Univ. (studied especially pedagogy); was Asst. and scholarship student of same; then apptd. non-official staff for research of educational system; Prof., Jingu-Kogakkan; Asst. Prof., Tokyo Imp. Univ., 1919; present post since 1932; sent abroad to inspect educational conditions. Recreations: reading. gardening, Go-game. Address: 630 Nishidai, Tabata, Takinogawa-ku, Tokyo.

Dir., Bank of Chosen; b. Aug., 1883 in Nagano-ken; brother of Gunshichi Irobe. Career: grad., Law Coll., Tokyo Imp. Univ., 1913; Non-Commissioned officer, Finance Bureau, 1914; Comptroller, Bank of Taiwan and Bank of Chosen; Sec., Dept. of Com. & Industry and Office; Bank Inspector; retired, 1929; apptd. present post, Aug., 1932. Address: 27 Uchikoshi, Nakanoku, Tokyo.

M. P.; Dir., Ise Elec. Ry. Co.; b. Dec., Career: studied at Keio Univ.; elected to Diet 4 times since 1920; apptd. Mem., Ry. Conference; Pres., Ise Ry. Co., Ltd.; then present post. Address: Wakamatsumura, Kageigun, Miye-ken.

Pres., Yokohama Chamber of Com. & Industry; Vice-Pres., Nippon Chamber of Com. & Industry; Pres., Yokohama Exchange; Mng. Dir., Hotel New Grand, Ltd.; Pres., Kwanto Credit Bank, Yokohama Marine & Fire Ins. Co.; Dir., Nippon Yusen Kaisha, Tokyo Gas Co., Yokohama Life Ins. Co., Tokiwa Life Ins. Co., 74th Bank, Ltd., etc.; b. Dec., 1869 in Ibaragi-ken; s. of Miki Isaka, samurai. Career: grad., Law Coll., Tokyo Imp. Univ., 1896; joined Toyo Steamship Co.; became Dir.; went abroad for inspection, 1928. Address: 48 Honcho-Gochome, Naka-ku, Yokohama.

Igakuhakushi (M. D.); Head Physician and Chief, Surgical Dept., Kagoshima-ken Pref. Hospital., b. Sept., 1890 in Niigata-ken; s. of Sokichi Watanabe, farmer. Career: grad., Medical Dept., Kyushu Imp. Univ., 1920; appointed Prof., Okayama Medical Coll. Address: 80 Koraimachi, Kagoshima City.

Mgr., Tokyo Branch, Yokohama Fire & Marine Ins. Co.; b. Nov., 1885 in Miyagi-ken; s. of Makoto Ishida, doctor. Career: grad., Tokyo Univ. of Com.; entered Tokyo Branch, Yokohama Fire & Mairne Ins. Co., 1914; served at Head-Office and Kobe Branch, 1916–20; lectured Insurance at Kansei Gakuin in Kobe for 2 years; Asst. Mgr., Tokyo Branch, 1920; present post since 1927. Address: 981 Magomemachi Higashi Nichome, Omoriku, Tokyo.

Pres., Ishihara Industry and Marine Transportation Co.; b. Jan., 1888; s. of Chotaro Ishihara, Kyoto. Career: grad., Ritsumeikan Univ., 1913; Acting Partner, Nanyo Mining Co. (present Ishihara Industry and Marine Transportation Co.). Address: 13 Fujimicho Gochome, Kojimachiku, Tokyo.

former Mng. Dir., Toa Tobacco Co., Ltd.; b. July, 1872 in Hiroshima-ken; s. of late Kennosuke Takenaga. Career: grad., Law Dept., Nihon Univ., 1901; served as Chief, Pref. Monopoly Bureaus at Utsunomiya, Takasaki and Kumamoto; resigned from Toa Tobacco Co. recently. Address: Minamisawa-Gakuen, Kurumemura, Tokyo-fu.

Igakuhakushi (M. D.); Prof., Ophthalmology, Medical Coll., Tokyo Imp. Univ.; b. Sept., 1879 in Tokyo; s. of Ujimoto Ishihara, Artillery Colonel. Career: grad., Medical Coll., Tokyo Imp. Univ., 1905; sent to Germany to study medical science, 1912–14; grad., Post-Graduate Course, same Univ. and received degree, 1916; apptd. Surgeon Lieut.-Col., 1906; attached to 2nd Infantry Regiment, 1st Garrison Hospital, Tokyo; Instructor, 2nd Army Surgeon School; Dir., 2nd Garrison Hospital; present post since 1922; apptd. Surgeon-General, 1926; Commr., Dept. of Overseas Affairs, 1930. Address: 35 Miyasato, Nakanoku, Tokyo.

Stage Dancer; Prop., Ishii Bac Dance Studio; b. Dec., 1892 in Akita; s. of Ryukichi Ishii. Career: completed Akita Middle School; entered Opera Dept., Imperial Theater; studied dance under Enrico Rossi and song under Madam Tamaki Miura; often made public performances at Berlin, Muenchen, Leipzig, Paris, Olmuts, Prague, Lords, Posen, Warsaw, Ostende in Europe, and at New York, Chicago, Los Angeles, San Francisco in America. Address: Jiyugaoka, Himonya, Meguroku, Tokyo.

Consul-General at Shanghai; b. Feb., 1887 in Fukushima-ken; s. of Bungoro Ishii, company Dir., Career: grad., Com. Dept., Toa Dobun Shoin, 1908; joined S. Manchuria Ry. Co.; passed Higher Civil Service, Exam. 1913, and Diplomatic and Consular Exam. 1915; Sec., Foreign Office; Chief, 3rd Section, Com. Affairs Bureau; 1st Sec. of Embassy; Consul-Gen. at Kirin, 1920; present post since Aug., 1932. Address: Consulate-General of Japan, Shanghai, China.

Viscount; Privy Councillor; b. Mar., 1856 in Chiba-ken; brother of Kametaro Owaku; adopted-s. of Hoyu Ishii. Career: grad., Law Coll., Tokyo Imp. Univ., 1890; apptd. Attaché at Paris, 1891; 1st Sec. of legation; Dir., Bureau of Com.; Vice-Minister, Foreign Office; Minister to America and France; Foreign Minister; ennobled, 1911; Mem., House of Peers, 1926; Plenipot., Naval Disarm., Conference, 1927; Privy Councillor, same year. Address: 15 Aoba, Shibuya, Tokyo.

Business Mgr. and Printing Dir., Asahi Shimbun; b. Aug., 1889 in Fukuoka-ken. Career: grad., Kobe Higher Com. School, 1912; passed Higher Civil Service Exam., 1913; after completed P.-G. Course, Tokyo Higher Com. Sch., 1914; served as Dir., Public Peace Section, Metropolitan Police Board; Sec. and Councillor, Taiwan Govt.; visited Europe and America, 1920–22; entered Asahi Shimbun and promoted to present post. Address: 2879 Araijuku, Iriaraimachi, Omoriku, Tokyo.

M. P.; Parl. Councillor, War Office; b. Feb., 1880 in Ibaragi-ken; brother of Sozaburo Ishii. Career: grad., Chuo Univ.; first engaged in banking business, and then entered Finance Office; Mem., Hunting Inquiry Committee; toured Siberia and Manchuria; founded Foreign Policy Investigation Society; Pres., Kodo Gikai. Address: 658 Sendagayamachi, Shibuyaku, Tokyo.

Pres., Taihei Life Ins. Co., Ltd. and Tokyo Kentetsu K. K.; b. Feb., 1870 in Shizuoka-ken; s. of Hiromasa Ishii, samurai. Career: grad., Law Coll., Tokyo Imp. Univ., 1896; Dir., Nippon Yusen Kaisha, Kinkai Yusen Kaisha and Naikoku Tsuun Kaisha. Address: 157 Kogaicho, Azabuku, Tokyo.

Rigakuhakushi (D. Sc.); D. Ph. (Germany); Emeritus Prof., Tokyo Imp. Univ.; Mem., Imp. Academy; b. Jan., 1860 in Tokyo; s. of late Chôso Ishikawa. Career: grad., Tokyo School of Foreign Languages; Zoological Dept., Tokyo Imp. Univ., 1882; apptd. Asst. Prof. of same, next year; sent to Germany for study of Zoology; returning home, became Prof., Coll. of Agrl.; toured Europe, America and Australia for studies; received honorable medal from Swedish Academy; elected Correspondent, Philadelphia Academy for his scientific services; author of several books on biology. Recreations: reading, travelling. Address: 19 Obancho, Yotsuyaku, Tokyo.

Rigakuhakushi (D. Sc.); Prof., Tohoku Imp. Univ.; Staff, Institute of Physical and Chemical Research; b. Dec., 1889. Career: grad., Chemical Course, Science Coll., Kyoto Imp. Univ., 1914; Prof., 5th Higher School; then present post. Address: 10 Uwakuchi, Komegafukuro, Seidai.

Journalist; b. Mar., 1895 in Tokyo; s. of Chiyomatsu. Career: grad., 2nd Higher School; studied at English Litt. Course, Tokyo Imp. Univ., then Princeton Univ., U. S.; returning home, joined Osaka Mainichi Shimbun, then Tokyo Nichi Nichi. Address: 19 Obancho, Yotsuyaku, Tokyo.

Igakuhakushi (M. D.); b. June, 1888 in Tokyo; s. of Hakaru Ishikawa, Surg. Captain I. J. N. Career: grad., Medical Coll., Tokyo Imp. Univ., 1913; served as Asst., Aoyama and Inada Medical Hospitals, same Univ.; received degree, 1922; entered Dojin-kai and sent to Europe and America, 1921; sent to China to inspect construction of Dojinkai Hankow Hospital, 1922; apptd. 1st Dir., same Hospital, 1922–26; 1st Dir., Matsumoto Hospital, 1927–31; established Shonan Sea-side Hospital at Sajima, Kanagawa-ken by his own expense. Address: 51 Aoyama-Minamicho Itchome, Akasakaku, Tokyo.

Kogakushi (B. Engrg.); Mng. Dir., Kyoto Elec. Light Co.; b. Nov., 1882 in Tokyo; s. of Kunisaburo Ishikawa. Career: grad., Kyoto Imp. Univ.; apptd. Auditor, Daishojigawa Hydro-Elec. Co.; Mt. Atago Elec. Ry. Co.; Mt. Kurama Elec. Ry. Co.; Committee, Investigation of Domestic Application of Electricity; same, Examination for Registration, Chief Engr. of Elec. Enterprise in Japan, Communications Dept.; elected Pres., Western Branches of Elec. Assn. of Japan, Illuminating Engrg. Society and Inst. of Elec. Assn. of Japan; Pres., Alumunus Assn. of Doshisha; Dir., Elec. Development Assn. of Japan; went to Europe and America for inspection of elec. industry twice. Address: Shokokuji-Higashimonzencho, Kyoto.

Author; b. Dec., 1883 in Saga-ken; s. of Kichijiro Ishimaru. Career: grad., Naval Staff Coll.; Lieut.-Commander, (Reserve); Served as Staff, Tokyo Nichi Nichi Shimbun and Osaka Mainichi Shimbun. Address: 2931 Kichijoji, Musashinomachi, Tokyo-fu.

Architect; b. Feb., 1894 in Kobe; s. of Kisaburo Ishimoto, industrialist. Career: grad., Archit. Course, Engrg. Coll., Tokyo Imp. Univ., 1920; served at Takenaka Bldg., Engrg. and Construction Office; went abroad for inspection, 1922–23; apptd. Lecturer, Engrg. Coll., Kyoto Imp. Univ., 1926; cooperating with Dr. Yasushi Kataoka, established Kataoka-Ishimoto Architectural Office, 1927; founded Ishimoto Architectual Office, 1931; Architl. Adviser, Shirokiya Dept. Store and Jinju Life Ins. Co. Address: 96 Shirogane-Imazatocho, Shibaku, Tokyo.

Rigakuhakushi (D. Sc.); Prof., Physics, Kyoto Imp. Univ.; b. Aug., 1875 in Ishikawa-ken; s. of Kichirouemon Ishino, farmer. Career: grad., Science Course, Tokyo Higher Normal School, and Science Coll., Kyoto Imp. Univ.; went to Europe and America for study, 1913–17; was Teacher and Asst. Prof., Tokyo Higher Normal School; Teacher, Osaka Tennoji Middle School; Prof., Girls' Higher Normal School, Nara; Prof., Physic Dept., Kyoto Imp. Univ., 1918; served as Councillor of same, 1925–27; Director, Science Dept. of same, since 1928; sent to China, 1926, Europe and U. S. 1927–28; Director of Science Dept., Prof., Physics, Osaka Technical Univ. Address: 428 Yabushitamachi, Tonodan, Kamikyoku, Kyoto.

M. P.; Parl. Councillor, Education Dept.; b. May, 1874 in Toyama-ken; s. of Kaemon Ishisaka. Career: studied at Doshisha Univ.; Procurator, Toyama-ken; Sec., Karafuto Govt.; Asst. Councillor, Monopoly Bureau; Non-Commissioned-Staff, Ry. Dept.; Mem., State Property Inquiry Committee; toured Manchuria, Mongolia and Chosen; attended World Parl. Congress. Address: 46 Hasedocho, Shibuyaku, Tokyo.

Igakuhakushi (M. D.); Director of Municiple Hygienic Institute of Tokyo; b. Mar., 1884 in Okayama; s. of Shizuyoshi Ishiwara. Career: grad., Med. Coll., Tokyo Imp. Univ., 1910. Address: 47 Kamitakata, Nakanoku, Tokyo.
Igakuhakushi (M. D.); Prof., Kyushu Imp. Univ.; b. Jan., 1873 in Kanazawashi; s. of Sennosuke Ishizaka, M. P. Career: grad., Medical Coll., Tokyo Imp. Univ. Address: 115 Shin-Daikumachi, Fukuoka.

Architect; Head, Kuramae Construction Co.; b. Jan., 1885 in Fukushima-ken; s. of Kohichi Ishizu, farmer. Career: grad., Tokyo Higher Tech. School; Dir., Koseikai; Mem., Tokyo Reconstruction Committee. Address: 20 Kuramae-Katamachi, Asakusaku, Tokyo.

Mem., House of Peers; b. July, 1866 in Fukuoka-ken; s. of Wasaburo Ishizuka. Career: grad., Law Coll., Tokyo Imp. Univ., 1890; Councillor, Legislation Bureau; Adviser, Korean Govt.; Councillor, Taiwan Govt.; Civil Administrative Chief, Kwantung Govt.; Pres., Oriental Development Co., 1916; Governor, Taiwan, 1929. Address: 71 Haramachi Nichome, Ushigomeku, Tokyo.

Mem., House of Peers; Councillor, Social Bureau, Home Dept.; Pres., Hokkaido Colliery & Steamship Co.; Japan Steel Works; Yubari Ry. Co.; Kyoritsu Steamship Co.; Auditor, Santo Steel Works; Dir., Wanishi Steel Works; b. Nov., 1868; s. of Yenji Isomura. Career: grad., Keio Univ., 1889; entered Communications Office, 1890; Bank of Japan, 1894; Mitsui Bussan Kaisha, 1896; served as Business Mgr., 1903; Mgr., London Branch, 1909; Dir., Hokkaido Colliery and Steamship Co., 1913; Concillor, Social Welfare Bureau. Address: 30 Takanawa-Minamicho, Shibaku, Tokyo.

Kogakuhakusi (D. E.); Research Engr., Sibaura Engrg. Works, Ltd.; b. Feb., 1885 in Wakayama-ken; s. of Hannosuke Issiki. Career: grad., Elect. Engrg. Dept., Tokyo Imp. Univ., 1909; made research on Elec. Engrg., especially on Problem of Lightening Protection. Address: 4-tyome, Koenzi, Suginamiku, Tokyo.

Igakuhakushi (M. D.); Prof., Kyushu Imp. Univ.; b. in Iwate-ken; s. of late Masanori Itagaki. Career: completed Morioka Middle School; grad., 2nd Higher School; Medical Dept., Kyoto Imp. Univ. Address: Hirao, Fukuoka City.

Major-Gen.; Attached to Gen. Staff Office; b. in Tokyo-fu. Career: grad., Mil. Academy, 1904; Mil. Staff Coll., 1916; Comdr., 14th Infantry Regiment, 1921; Attache, Gen. Staff Office, 1922; Instructor, Mil. Staff Coll., same year; Asst. Mil. Attache to Legation, China, 1924; Attached, Staff, 33rd Brig. 1927; Comdr., 33rd infantry Reg. 1928; Staff, Kwantung Army, 1929; Dir., Army Press Bureau; present post since 1933. Address: c/o Gen. Staff Office.
Hogakuhakushi (D. L.); Prof.. Keio Univ.; b. Dec., 1879 in Hiroshima-ken; s. of Riro Itakura. Career: grad., Polit. Dept., Keio Univ., 1903. Address: 403, Togoshimachi, Ebara-ku, Tokyo.

Restaurant Owner; b. Oct., 1874 in Kyoto; s. of Zembei Tamura, draper. Career: grad., Kyoto-fu Pref. 1st Middle School; Teacher, Kyoto Pref. Girls' Coll.; same, Kyoto Girls' Coll.; same, Kyoto Pref. 2nd Higher Girls' School. Address: Fuyamachi-Higashi, Shijodori, Shimokyoku, Kyoto.

Prof., Economics, Tokyo Univ. of Com.; b. Feb., 1899 in Toyama-ken; s. of Matsujiro Itani, journalist. Career: grad., Tokyo Univ. of Com.; went to Paris, Geneva, Wien, Berlin for studies; Expert to 10th Assembly, League of Nations, 1929; Expert, Int'l Conference of Tariff Holidays, 1930; Delegate to Pacific Conference at Shanghai, Nov., 1931; published many books on world economics and economic history of Japan. Address: 42 Takata, Toyokawacho, Koishikawaku, Tokyo.

Mem., House of Peers; Shogakushi; Pres., Kabafuto Bank; b. May, 1885 in Otaru, Hokkaido; s. of late Miyakichi Itaya. Career: grad., Com. Dept., Waseda Univ.; Pres., Itaya Mercantile Steamship Co., Karafuto Bank; Dir., South Sea Mail Steamship Co.; Auditor, Owari Watch & Clock Co.; Executive Partner, Kurohime Steamship Co.; Pres., Hokumon Savings Bank; Mng.-Dir., Hokkai Hydro-Elec. Co.; Councillor, Yokohama Life Ins. Co.; High Taxpayer in Hokkaido. Address: 29 Ironaimachi Rokuchome, Otaru, Hokkaido.

M. P.; Parl. Councillor, Ry. Dept.; b. Mar., 1877 in Niigata-ken; Son-in-law of late Miyakichi Itaya. Career: grad., Keio Univ.; Man. Dir., Itaya Shosen Kaisha, Ltd.; engaged in marine transportation, brewery, agrl., live-stock, warehousing, banking and timber business; Mem., Otaru Chamber of Com. & Industry; Pres., Hokkaido Agrl. Assn.; Dir., Itaya Shosen Kaisha, Karafuto Bank, Yokohama Life Ins. Co., Otaru Exchange, Oshima Seaside Ry. Co., Doyako Elec. Ry. Co., Sharyu Ry. Co., Sharyu Elec. Co., Yufutsu Elec. Light Co., Nanyo Yusen Kaisha and Central Cultivation Co. Address: 23 Nishimachi, Azabuku, Tokyo.

Coloratura Soprano; b. Jan., 1905 in Iwate-ken; d. of Rinzo Ito. Career: grad., Vocal Dept., Tokyo Academy of Music, Ueno, 1923; studied singing under Madam Petzold and Italian opera under Attilio Belletti; once taught at Japan Music School and Tokyo Pref. 1st Com. School; established “Opera Verdiana” in Tokyo, 1929; often broadcasted over J.O.A.K.; now gives lessons at home. Address: c.o. Mr. Sugita, 913 Setagaya, Setagayaku, Tokyo.

Miso (beanmash) Brewer; b. Nov., 1880 in Aomori-ken. Career: Mem. and Councillor, Aomori-ken Pref. Assembly; Pres., Nobechi Live-Stock Assn.; same, Nobechi Riding Society; Auditor, Aomori Savings Bank. Address: 1 of 116 Nobechi, Nobechimachi, Aomori-ken.

Dir., Fukushima Higher Com. School; b. Mar., 1885 in Fukushima-ken; s. of Takehisa Ito, public notary. Career: grad., Law Coll., Tokyo Imp. Univ., 1911; apptd. Subordinate Official, 1911; Probationer, Yamagata-ken; Sec., Toyama-ken, Saitama-ken, Yamanashi-ken; Inspector and Sec., Education Dept., 1918; Councillor of same; Sec., Cultural Affairs Bureau toward China; Sec., Foreign Office; Sec., Tokyo Imp. Univ.; present post since 1927; sent to China, 1919, Europe and America, 1921–23, to inspect educational condition. Address: 34 Nishiyozan, Moriai, Shimizumura, Fukushima-shigai.

Igakuhakushi (M. D.); Physician; b. July, 1891; s. of Kenjiro Ito, physician. Career: completed 3rd Higher School; grad., Medical Coll., Kyoto Imp. Univ., 1915; studied at P.-G. Course of same; received degree, 1926. Address: 125 Horinouemachi, Takakura-Higashiiru, Rokkakudori, Kyoto.

Kogakuhakushi (D. E.); Consulting Mechanical Engr.; Prop., Ito Industrial Office; Acting Partner, Tokyo Weighing Machine Mfg. Co.; b. Mar., 1873 in Fukuoka-ken; s. of late Kanae Ito, samurai. Career: grad., Engrg. Coll., Tokyo Imp. Univ., 1898; entered Mitsubishi Shipbuilding & Engrg. Co.; inspected shipbuilding and mechanical works in England, 1911–12; studied internal combustion engines in Europe, 1912–14; investigated start-turbines in Sweden and England, 1916; investigated submarine-boats and airplane engines in England and France, 1917–18; apptd. Vice-Pres., Kobe Works, of the firm, 1917; founded and became Pres., Mitsubishi Internal Combustion Engine Works, Kobe (now Mitsubishi Aircraft Co.), 1918; retired from same, 1922; invented and patented Ito's Bridge Manoeuvering Apparatus and Ito's Propeller-blade Milling Machine, etc. Address: 6 Marunouchi Nichome, Kojimachiku, Tokyo.

Hogakuhakushi (D. L.); Min. to Poland; b. Aug., 1885 in Ehime-ken; s. of Michioki Ito. Career: grad., Advanced Course, Tokyo Higher Com. School, 1909; apptd. Elève-Consul; served as Diplomatic Probationer, 1st Sec. of Legation and Embassy, Councillor of Embassy, and resided at Italy, France, China and Switzerland; received degree, 1932; attended 11th Gen. Meeting of League of Nations, 1930, and Gen. Disarmament Conf. at Geneva, 1931. Address: Japanese Embassy, Warsaw, Poland.

Rigakuhakushi (D. Sc.); F. L. S. London); Botanist; b. Jan., 1866 in Nagoya; s. of Nobukichi Ito, physician, & grand-s. of Baron Dr. Keisuke Ito, botanist. Career: studied at Univ. of Cambridge, England. Address: 1899 Takinogawa, Takinogawaku, Tokyo.

Baron; Mem., House of Peers; b. May, 1873 in Kyoto-fu; s. of the late Shunkichi Ito, Vice-Admiral, Mem., House of Peers. Career: grad., Engrg. Coll., Tokyo Imp. Univ., 1899; entered naval service as Constructing Engineer; appointed Engineer Rear-Admiral, 1919; entered reserve service, 1923. Address: 242 Kitashinagawa, Shinagawaku, Tokyo.

Dir., Kaibogikai; b. Dec., 1861 in Ehime-ken; s. of Kijiro Ito. Career: joined Nippon Yusen Kaisha and served as Branch Mgr. at Yokohama, Shanghai and London; Mng. Dir., then Pres. of same; Dir., Nisshin Steamship Co.; Special Mem., Tokyo Chamber of Com. & Industry; Pres., Japan Times & Mail; resigned, 1931. Address: 543 Kuzugayatsu, Komachi, Kamakura, Kanagawa-ken.

Igakuhakushi (M. D.); Physician; b. Aug., 1898 in Yamaguchi-ken; s. of Shinichi Sekawa, business man. Career: grad., Medical Dept., Kyushu Imp. Univ., 1924; served Dr. Onodera's Office, Attached Hospital to the Univ.; entered South Manchuria Ry. Co., serving at its Hospital in Fushun; transferred to Ssupingkai, Hospital, May, 1930. Address: 1-chome, Chojugai, Ssupingkai, Manchukuo.

Mem., House of Peers; Pres., Matsue Bank and Hikami Ry. Co., Ltd.; Councillor, Japan Forest Assn. and Imp. Central Live-Stock Assn.; Dir., Imp. Agrl. Assn.; b. Nov., 1879. in Shimane-ken. Career: completed middle school; inherited family estate, 1911; connected with several of private and public business; decorated with Blue Ribbon Medal for his service. Address: Hachikawamura, Nitagun, Shimane-ken.

Dir., Shibaura Engrg. Works, Tokyo Elec. Co., Japan Wireless Co., Taiwan Sugar Co.; Pres., Nankoku Sangyo Co., Ashikaga Cotton Spinning Co., Radio Corporation of Japan, etc.; b. Oct., 1863 in Ishikawa-ken; s. of Takaoki Iwahara, lawyer. Career: studied at Osaka Eigo Gakko (English Language School); grad., Tokyo Higher Mercantile Marine Coll.; joined Mitsui Bussan Kaisha, serving for 5 years at its London Branch; returning home, apptd.
