Mgr., Kobe Branch; Mgr., New York Branch serving for 10 years; promoted Dir. of same firm, 1906; became Dir., Oji Paper Co. Address: 23 Fukidecho, Shibaku, Tokyo.

Pres., Iwai Shoten & Co., Ltd. b. Apr., 1863 in Kyoto-fu; 2nd s. of Genuemon Kageyama, farmer. Career: made inspection tour to Europe and America, 1911; established many relating firms such as Osaka Steel Sheet Mfg. Co., Shirogane Hosiery Works, Nippon Soda Industry Co., Kansai Paint Mfg. Co., Nihon Bridge Co., Chuo Wool Spinning Co. and Tokuyama Steel Sheet Co.; Dir., Yamaguchi Bank; Dai Nippon Fire & Marine Re-insurance Co.; Mem., Domestic Committee in Japan, Int'l Chamber of Com.; same, Domestic Products Promotion Assn.; Councillor, Osaka Chamber of Com. & Industry. Address: 165 Donoura, Gunke, Mikagemachi, Mukogun, Hyogo-ken.

M. P.; Parl. Vice-Minister of Com. & Industry; b. Jan., 1888 in Kagoshima-ken; s. of Nakaji Iwakiri. Career: grad., Law Coll., Tokyo Imp. Univ.; Police Supt., Tottori-ken; Deputy Mayor of Kagoshima; Sec., Finance Minister; Parl. Councillor, Dept. of Com. & Industry; present post since June, 1932. Address: 19 Kasumicho, Azabuku, Tokyo.

M. P.; Parl. Councillor, Justice Office; b. Dec., 1882 in Nara-ken; s. of Zentaro Iwamoto. Career: grad., Law Dept., Ritsumeikan Univ.; took P.-G. Course in Economics at same; Mem., Nara District Forestry Assembly; Dir., Yamato Forestry Society, Daido Bank and Dohokusan Cable Car Co.; Auditor, Nara-ken Agrl. & Industrial Bank; visited Europe and America for inspection; apptd. present post, June, 1932. Address: Koseikan, 13 Kobikicho Sanchome, Kyobashiku, Tokyo.

Igakuhakushi (M. D.); Surgeon; b. Feb., 1891 in Saga-ken; s. of Ryokichi Iwamoto, agriculturist. Career: grad., Medical Course, Tohoku Imp. Univ., 1919; apptd. Asst. Prof., Tohoku Imp. Univ.; served Kato Hospital in Sendai; bought and became Pres. of same, Apr., 1930. Address: 146 Mototera Koji, Sendai.

Journalist; Mng.-Dir., Shimbun Rengo-sha (Rengo); b. Sept., 1883 in Tokyo; adopted-s. of late Seiichi Iwanaga. Career: grad., Eng. Law Dept., Kyoto Imp. Univ., 1909; served South Manchuria Ry. Co. and Govt. Ry. of Japan; became Mng. Dir., Kokusai News Agency, then present post. Address: 232 Kami-Osaki, Shinagawaku, Tokyo.

Rigakuhakushi (D. S.); Lecturer, Tohoku Imp. Univ.; b. Apr., 1896 in Kumamoto-ken; s. of Choku Iwasaki, physician. Career: grad., Geological Course, Science Coll., Tokyo Imp. Univ., 1896; apptd. Prof., Kumamoto Higher Tech. School; Lecturer, Agrl. Coll., Tokyo Imp. Univ., same, Tohoku Imp. Univ. Address: 148 Tsuchitoi, Sendai, Miyagi-ken.

Vice-Pres., Mitsubishi Goshi Kaisha; s. of Baron Hisaya Iwasaki, business man. Career: grad., Litt. Coll., Tokyo Imp. Univ., 1920; then studied at P.-G. Course of same; went to England for study, 1922; returning home, joined present firm, 1926; visited South America for inspection, 1930. Address: 7 Tatsuokacho, Hongoku, Tokyo.

Baron; Pres., Mitsubishi Goshi Kaisha; Dir., Mitsubishi Bank, Yokohama Specie Bank, Mitsubishi Trading Co., Mitsubishi Shipbuilding & Engrg. Co., Mitsubishi Iron & Steel Co., Mitsubishi Marine & Fire Ins. Co., Mitsubishi Trust Co., Mitsubishi Warehouse Co. and Tokyo Marine & Fire Ins. Co.; Auditor, Asahi Glass Co.; b. Aug., 1879 in Tokyo; s. of Yanosuke Iwasaki. Career: grad., 1st Higher School; studied at Cambridge Univ.; toured Europe and America; inherited peerage, 1908; succeeded father's business. Address: 2 Toriizakamachi, Azabuku, Tokyo.

Mem., House of Peers; Hogakuhakushi (D. L.); Lawyer; b. June, 1875 in Yamaguchi-ken; s. of Hikoshichi Hiyama, farmer. Career: grad., Law Coll., Tokyo Imp. Univ., 1898; engaged in journalistic work, 1899-1909; in 1909 became lawyer; served as Mem., Legislation Consideration Committee, Imp. Economic Conference, Tenancy System Inquiry Board, and several other legal questions; conferred degree, 1916; nominated. Mem., House of Peers, 1917. Address: 12 Aoyama Takagicho, Akasakaku, Tokyo.

Councillor, Embassy, Italy; b. Mar., 1888 in Tokyo; s. of Atsuo Iwate. Career: grad., Consular Course, Tokyo Higher Com. School, 1913; served as Elève-Consul, Diplomatic Probationer, Consul, Sec. of Foreign Office, Chief of Corr. and Translation Sections and 1st Sec. of Legation in Canada; Consul-General at Honolulu 1931; present post since 1933. Address: c/o Japanese Embassy, Rome.

Igakuhakushi (M. D.); Vice-Pres., Red Cross Hospital, Osaka; b. Sept., 1879; s. of Tsunehisa Iwoka, physician. Career: grad., Medical Coll., Kyoto Imp. Univ. Address: 46 Ishigatsujimachi, Tennojiku, Osaka.

Dir., Shikoku Bank: Dir., Nankai Hydro-Elec. Co.; Auditor, Tosa Elec. Co.; b. May, 1865 in Okayama-ken; s. of Tsunezo Izawa, banker. Career: studied at Nishiyama Private School; Special Mem., Kochi Chamber of Com. & Industry. Address: 1722 Araijuku, Omoriku, Tokyo.

Mem., House of Peers; b. Nov., 1869 in Nagano-ken; brother of late Shuji Izawa. Career: grad., Law Coll., Tokyo Imp. Univ., 1895; entered official service; Governor, Wakayama-ken, Ehime-ken, Niigata-ken; Metropolitan Police Chief; nominated Mem., House of Peers; Governor-General of Taiwan, 1924; Mayor of Tokyo, 1926. Address: 2517 Sugamo Nichome, Toshimaku, Tokyo.

Hogakuhakushi (D. L.); Prof., Internal Law, Keijo Imp. Univ.; b. Oct., 1873 in Hokkaido; s. of Rintaro Izumi, farmer. Career: studied at Sapporo Agrl. Coll.; Lake Forest Coll. (B. A.), 1906; Univ., Wisconsin (M. A.), 1907; Columbia (Graduate School), 1909-13. Address: 58 Seidaimonmachi Itchome, Keijo.
Hogakushi (B. L.); Pres., Osaka Oxygen & Hydrogen Co., Ltd.; b. Apr., 1883 in Osaka; s. of Seisuke Izumi, business man. Career: grad., Tokyo Imp. Univ. Address: Hachikencho, Higashiku, Osaka.

Igakuhakushi (M. D.); Dir., Kurihara Hospital; b. Jan., 1895 in Aomori-ken; s. of Matsusaburo Izumiyama, banker. Career: grad., Medical Coll., Tohoku Imp. Univ.; apptd. Asst. of same, 1921; Lecturer of same, 1927; received degree, 1927; Sub-Dir., Miyagi Branch Hospital, Japan Red Cross Society, 1927; Head Surgeon, Hosei Hospital, 1929; present post since 1932. Address: 12 Minami Itchome, Nishi-shijo, Toyoharamachi, Karafuto.

Mem., Chamber of Com. & Ind., Yokohama; Trader; Broker, Yokohama Exchange; b. Jan., 1870 in Ehime-ken; s. of Kenshichi Joko, samurai. Career: Permanent Mem., Yokohama Chamber of Com. & Industry; Pres., Federation, Industrial Assns., Yokohama; Yokohama Silk Exporters' Assn.; Yokohama Silk & Rayon Exporters' Assn.; Yokohama Liberal Trading Assn.; Vice-Pres., Federation, Japan Silk Exporters' Assn.; Japan Silk Industry Assn.; Mng. Dir., Yokohama Traders' Assn.; besides, has been connected several other assns. in Yokohama and Kanagawa-ken. Address: 171 & 173 Bluff, Yokohama.

Merchant; b. Apr., 1878 in Osaka; n. British. Career: Chairman, Nickel & Lyons, Ltd.; same, Kobe Int'l Committee; Mem. of Committee, Kobe & Osaka Foreign Chamber of Commerce; Pres., Kobe Regatta & Athletic Club. Address: Shioya, near Kobe.

General Representative for the Far East, Philips Glowlam Works and N. V. Philips Radio, Holland; Mng. Dir., Philips Nippon Radio K. K., Tokyo; b. in Holland; n. Netherlander. Address: Kenchiku Kaikan, Ginza-Nishi-Sanchome, Kyobashiku, Tokyo.
Chevalier de la Légion d'Honneur; Croix de Guerre Française; Consul de France, Yokohama. n. French. Address: French Consulate, 65 Yamatecho, Yokohama.

Chief, Educ. Dept. and Councillor, Kirin prov.; Pres., Kirin Coll.; b. 1878 in Acheng-hsien, Kirin Prov. Career: grad., Hosei Univ., Tokyo; Sec., Vice-Commander-in-Chief, Office; North-eastern Frontier Defence Army; took part in movement for Kirin Independence 1931; present post since 1932. Address: Kirin.

Count; Vice-Pres., America-Japan Society; Emeritus Dr. of Law (Weslyan Univ., Ohio); b. May, 1865 in Kagoshima; s. of late Count Sukenori Kabayama. Career: grad., Amherst Univ., Wisc., U. S.; founded Kokusai News Agency, 1914, presiding over same until it was merged into Nippon Shimbun Rengo Agency, 1926; Vice-Pres., America-Japan Society since 1924; went to England to attend World's Parl. Com. Conf. as Japan's Delegate, May, 1926; attended London Naval Conference as Subordinate to Japanese Delegates, Nov., 1929. Address: 6 of 215 Sodegasaki, Kita-Shinagawa Gochome, Shinagawaku, Tokyo.

Mem., House of Peers; Dir., Daito Bunka Kyokai (Great Eastern Cultural Assn.); Pres., Manchuria Cotton Wool Co.; b. July, 1868 in Kagoshima-ken; s. of Sukeo Kabayama, samurai. Career: grad., 1st Higher School; studied at Columbia Univ.; grad., Law Coll., Yale Univ., and its P.-G. Course (LL. D.); entered War Office, 1895; Sec. to Premier and Education Minister; Pres., Toyo Fire Ins. Co.; Dir., S. Manchuria Ry. Co.; Chief Sec. of Yamamoto Cabinet. Address: 20 Obancho, Yotsuyaku, Tokyo.

Vice-Pres., Okura & Co.; Pres. Okura Engrg. and Contracting Co.; b. Sept., 1867 in Miye-ken; s. of W. Kadono, samurai. Career: grad., Keio Univ., and Tokyo Imp. Univ., 1891; served Sanyo Railway as Engr., 1896-1897, entered Okura & Co., 1897. Address: 51 Shinsakamachi, Akasakaku, Tokyo.

Dir., Sumitomo Bank; Mng.-Dir., New Osaka Hotel Co.; b. Jan., 1875; s. of Tadashichi Kaga. Career: grad., Tokyo Univ. of Com. and P.-G. Course of same, 1898; apptd. Asst. Mgr., Business Dept., Sumitomo Bank; Yokohama and Kobe Branches; Auditor and Mng.-Dir., Head Office of same; present post since Mar., 1932. Address: 685 Motoyamamura-Noyori, Mukogun, Hyogo-ken.

Mem., House of Peers; Pres., Nippon Yusen Kaisha; Chairman, Board of Dirs., Meiji Fire Ins. Co., Mitsubishi Trust Co., Mitsubishi Marine & Fire Ins Co.; Dir., Standard Oil Co. of New York, Tokyo Salvage Co.; Auditor, Mitsubishi Bank; Adviser, Okura Marine & Fire Ins. Co. and Toyo Marine & Fire Ins. Co.; Pres., Ship-Owners' Assn.; Dir., Japan Industrial Club; b. Dec., 1868 in Tokyo; brother of Koichiro Kagami. Career: grad., Tokyo Higher Com. School, 1888; attended Gen. Meeting, Int'l Chamber of Com., 1931. Address: 2 Otsuka-Kubomachi, Koishikawa, Tokyo.

M. P.; Landlord; Pres., Hinomaru Mutual Financing Co. (Mujin Kaisha); b. Dec., 1886 in Hyogo-ken; s. of Juuemon Tachibana. Career: grad., Military Academy; then studied Polit. Economy at Kyoto Imp. Univ. for 2 years; served as Pres. & Councillor, Land Division Readjustment Assns. and Real Estate Assns. in Osaka; Reserve Infantry Major; became Pres., Komin Newspaper Co.; often toured Manchuria and China for inspection; sent to Diet from Hyogo-ken twice. Address: Himeji-machi, Nishiyodogawa-ku, Osaka.

Pres., Kaijima & Co. and Kaijima Coal Mining Co.; b. Nov., 1881 in Fukuoka-ken; s. of Tasuke Kaijima, mine operator. Career: grad., Tokyo Higher Com. School; went abroad to inspect coal-mining and commercial affairs, 1906-09; Pres., Kaijima & Co., 1919, Kaijima Mining Co., 1931; Auditor, Wakamatsu Harbor Co., 1919; Dir., Central Fire & Accident Ins. Co., 1922; Auditor, Kaijima Dry Distillation Co., 1925; Kaijima Chemical Industry Co., 1931; Adviser, Shimonoseki Chamber of Com. & Industry, 1921; Counsellor, Japan Industrial Club and Chikuho Mining Assn., 1931. Address: 2793 Samuraimachi, Chofu, Yamaguchi-ken.

Pres., Kajima-gumi (Civil Engineers, Contracters and Builders); b. July, 1875 in Iwate-ken; s. of Seinei Kasai, and later adopted by Iwazo Kajima. Career: grad., Civil Engrg. Dept., Tokyo Imp. Univ., 1899; apptd. Mem., Tokyo Chamber of Com. & Industry; Mng. Dir., Toho Concrete Co.; Nippon Pipe Mfg. Co.; Inspector, Taiwan Real Estate and Building Co., Ltd. Address: 3 Makicho Nichome, Kyobashiku, Tokyo.

Surgeon Lieut.-Col.; Igakuhakushi (M. D.); b. Sept., 1888 in Miyagi-ken; s. of Ryuan Kajitsuka, physician. Career: grad., Medical Coll., Tokyo Imp. Univ.; apptd. Surgeon-Lieutenant, 1915; served as Instructor, Military Surgeon School; Head, Research Bureau, Japan Red Cross Hospital since 1924; visited Europe and America, 1928-29. Address: 12 Nishitakaido Nichome, Suginamiku, Tokyo.

Hogakushi (B. L.); Auditor, Gakushi-kai (Bachelor's Association), Nogikai (Gen. Nogi Society), Dedication Association of Meiji Shrine, Taiwan Elec. Co.; b. July, 1871 in Yamagata-ken; s. of Hyosaburo Kajiwara, merchant. Career: grad., Law Coll., Tokyo Imp. Univ.; Dir., Investigation Bureau, Bank of Japan; Vice-Pres., then Pres., Yokohama Specie Bank; Pres., Hypothec Bank of Japan. Address: 57, 5-chome, Gotanda, Shinagawaku, Tokyo.
Vice-Min., National Roads Dept., Manchoukuo; b. in Tokyo-fu. Career: grad., Civil Engrg. Coll., Tokyo Imp. Univ.; Civil Engr., Civil Affairs Dept.; present post since 1933. Address: Hsinking.

M., Comm. Sc.; Sec.-Archivist, Finnish Legation in Tokyo; b. Mar., 1909; s. of J. H. Kala, (M. A.) Dir., Statistical Dept., Finnish Govt. Ry. Career: Official in the Nat. Bank, Helsinki, 1928-1932; entered Finnish Diplomatical Service, May, 1933; present post since July, 1933. Address: c/o Finnish Legation, 62 Tansumachi, Azabu-ku, Tokyo.

Privy Councillor; Pres., Kojunsha; Pres., Education Assn.; Mem., Special Roman Letter Investigation Committee; b. Jan., 1875 in Wakayama City; s. of Shuzo Kamada. Career: grad., Keio Univ.; apptd. Prof., Keio Univ.; Head-Instructor, Zoshikan Inst.; Commr., Home Office; Principal, Oita Middle School and Oita Normal School; sent to Diet from Wakayama-ken, 1894; Pres., Keio Univ., nominated Mem., House of Peers, 1906-1927; Education Minister in Kato Cabinet; toured China, Europe and America; Japan's Delegate to 1st Int'l Labor Conf., 1919. Address: 555 Shimo-Meguro, 3-chome, Meguroku, Tokyo.

Pres., Kaitaku-Sha; Dir., Dai Nippon Kokubo Gikai; Chief Dir., National Resources Inquiry Council; Prop. of Farm; b. Aug., 1876 in Niigata-ken; s. of late Dengo Kambayashi, business man. Career: studied at Tokyo Higher Com. School, Chuo Univ. and Law Coll., Tokyo Imp. Univ.; founded Imp. Colonization School, 1902; Dir., and Prof. of same up to 1919. Address: 108 Fukazawacho, 4-chome, Setagayaku, Tokyo.

Persian Minister to Tokyo; Grand Officier de Instruction Publique et de Lion et de Soleil de Perse; Commandeur de la Legion d'Honneur; Grand Cordon de l'Ordre du Nil Egypte; b. 1878 in Teheran; s. of H. K. Hedayat, Minister. Career: Began studies in Persia, and terminated in France by graduating l'Ecole de Science et Politique; on return home, entered Civil Service, later apptd. Min. of Justice, afterwards Min. of Finance, entered Diplomatic Service. Recreation: bridge and billiards. Address: Persian Legation, Azabuku, Tokyo. Tel.: Aoyama (36) 3010. Clubs: Tokyo Club, Kojunsha.

Hogakuhakushi (D. L.) Prof., Kyoto Imp. Univ.; b. Apr., 1877 in Aichi-ken; s. of Nushimasa Kambe. Career: grad., Law Coll., Tokyo Imp. Univ., 1900; Asst. Prof., Kyoto Imp. Univ., 1902; Prof. of same, 1907; went to Europe twice, 1904-7, 1913-14.; Mem., Imp. Academy, 1930; at present, Mem., Tariff Investigation Committee: Special Mem., Imp. Agrl. Assn.; Adviser, Kyoto Chamber of Com. & Industry; Dir., Labor and Capital Harmonization Assn. Address: 70 Jodoji-nishidamachi, Kyoto.

Hogakuhakushi (D. L.); Doctor Juris; Prof., Keio Univ.; b. Dec., 1868 in Shizuoka-ken; s. of Jujiro Kambe. Career: grad., Law Coll., Keio Univ., 1892; went abroad for study, 1899-03; present post since 1903; received degree, 1914; Pres., Jurists Assn. Address: 21 Kageoka, Shibuyaku, Tokyo.

Hogakuhakushi (D. L.); Prof., Tokyo Imp. Univ.; b. Dec., 1889 in Miye-ken; s. of Tsujimatsu Okuyama; adopted by Ryokichi Kamikawa. Career: grad., Law Coll., Tokyo Imp. Univ., 1915; studied P.-G. Course, same; Asst. Prof., Tokyo Imp. Univ., 1917; went abroad, 1918; present post since 1917; received degree, 1929. Address: 359 Komachi, Kamakuramachi, Kanagawa-ken.
Chief Sec., State Council, Manchoukuo. Career: Sec., State Council, Manchoukuo 1932; present post since Oct., 1933. Address: Hsinking.
Dir., Education Bureau, Education Dept., Manchoukuo. Career: present post since 1932. Address: Hsinking.

M. P.; Parl. Councillor, Finance Office; b. May 1890 in Kumamoto-ken; brother of Hidekatsu Kamitsuka. Career: grad., Kobe Higher Com. School, 1912; joined South Manchuria Ry. Co.; engaged in economic research in China, Manchuria, Mongolia, French Indo-China, South Seas as Non-Commissioned-Official of Foreign Office and Dept. of Agrl. & Com.; Dir., Kokushikan and Aikoku Savings Bank; Auditor, Teitoza Theater; Sec. to Agrl. & Com. Minister; same to Com. & Industry Minister; attended Int'l Parl. Congress; Sec. to Finance Minister; present post since June, 1932. Address: 41 Otsuka Nakamachi, Koishikawaku, Tokyo.

Pres., Tropical Development Co.; Argentine Agrl. & Pastoral Co.; Davao Trading Co.; Piso Cocoanut & Cattle Ranch Inc. of Philippine Islands; Dir., Toshin Fire Ins. Co., Toho Securities Holding Co., Takasago Trading Co., Japan Motor Road Co., Kamakurayama Real Estate Co., Kawazugawa Hydro-Elec. Co., Dorosha Printing Co.; Japan Asphalt Emerian Co., Ltd.; Auditor, Tokyo Movables Fire Ins. Co., Oriental Elec. Works, etc.; b. Dec., 1880 in Aichi-ken; s. of late Ichiji Kamiya, samurai. Career: studied at Meiji Law Coll. (present Meiji Univ.); went to Europe and America for study; traveled abroad several times; engaged in emigration and colonization enterprises in South Seas, South America, etc. Address: Daibutsu-mae, Hase, Kamakuramachi, Kanagawa-ken.

Mem., House of Peers; former Gov. of Taiwan; b. Sept., 1869 in Yamaguchi-ken; s. of Yozaemon Kamiyama. Career: grad., Law Coll., Tokyo Imp. Univ., 1895; apptd. Councillor, Aomori-ken, Yamaguchi-ken and Legislation Bureau; Judge, Court of Administrative Litigation; Dir., Forestry Bureau, Agrl. & Com. Dept.; Gov., Kumamoto-ken; Vice-Minister, Agrl. & Com. Dept.; nominated Mem., House of Parliament, 1918; Lord-in-Waiting, Kinkei Hall; Gov. of Taiwan, 1926-28. Address: 28 Takanawa-Minamicho, Shibaku, Tokyo.
Dir., Political Affairs Bureau, Foreign Dept., Manchoukuo. Career: present post since 1932. Address: Hsinking.

Kogakuhakushi (D. E.); Prof., Tokyo Imp. Univ.; b. Aug., 1876 in Ehime-ken; s. of Hiromasa Kamo, samurai. Career: grad., Engrg. Coll., Tokyo Imp. Univ., 1898; Asst. Prof. of same; sent to France, Germany and U. S. for study, 1906; apptd. Engr., Ry. Office, 1908; received degree, 1913; present post since 1912. Address: 312 of Ni, Mukogaoka-Yayoicho, Hongoku, Tokyo.
Inspector, Central Bank, Manchoukuo. Career: present post since 1932. Address: Hsinking.
Chief, Gen. Affairs Office, Mukden Prov. Office. Career: present post since 1932. Address: Mukden.

D. L.; Supt., Custom House in Moji; b. May, 1883 in Oita-ken. Career: grad., Tokyo Imp. Univ., 1908; served Financial Dept.; apptd. Chief, Local Monopoly Bureau; Supt., Custom House, Nagasaki; since then present post. Address: Official Residence of Custom House, Kuzaha, Moji City.

Vice-Pres., Chamber of Com. & Ind., Osaka; Pres., Osaka Elec. Tramway Co.; b. Feb., 1873 in Osaka-fu; s. of Matabe Kanamori. Career: Mng. Dir., Osaka Elec. Tramway Co.; Pres., Sangu Express Tramway Co.; Auditor, Imazato Estate Co.; Dir., Sakigawa Canal Co.; Mem., Osaka Chamber of Com. & Industry. Address: 76 Matsuzakicho Nichome, Sumiyoshiku, Osaka.

Viscount; Privy Councillor; Pres., Meiji Restoration History Editing Office and Imperial Editorial Dept.; b. Feb., 1853 in Fukuoka-ken; s. of Seizo Kaneko, samurai. Career: studied Law at Harvard Univ., 8 years; Sec. to Premier; Sec. to Pres., Privy Council; Chief Sec., House of Peers; Agrl. & Com. Minister, 1898; Justice Minister, 1900; nominated Mem., House of Peers, 1823; received Honorary LL. D., Harvard Univ., 1899. Address: 30 Ichibancho, Kojimachiku, Tokyo.

Dir., Matsuyama Higher School; b. Apr., 1876 in Yamaguchi-ken; s. of Taisuke Kaneko, samurai, Yamaguchi clan. Career: grad., Litt. Coll., Tokyo Imp. Univ., 1902; Principal, Otaki Middle School, Chiba-ken and Iwakuni Middle School, Yamaguchi-ken; Prof., Matsuyama Higher School; present post since 1927. Address: Masakicho, Itchome, Matsuyama City.

Priv. Sec. to Minister of Commerce & Industry; b. Dec., 1896 in Tokyo; s. of Viscount Kentaro Kaneko, Privy Councillor. Career: grad., Tokyo Imp. Univ.; successively apptd. Private Sec. to Prime Ministers, Count Yamamoto, Viscount Kiyoura and Viscount Kato, 1923-26; again same to Prime Minister and Foreign Minister, Baron Giichi Tanaka, 1927-29; joined Mitsui Bussan Kaisha. Address: 30 Ichibancho, Kojimachiku, Tokyo.

M. P.; Mem., Tokyo Chamber of Com. & Industry; Pres., Nippon Eiga Gekijo and Oji Elec. Ry. Co.; Chairman, Board of Dirs., Chiyoda Trust Co.; Mgr., Shin Nippon Fire & Marine Ins. Co., Taisho Life Ins. Co. and Nippon Kyoiku Life Ins. Co.; Dir., Nambu Ry. Co., Ikegami Ry. Co., Keio Elec. Ry. Co., Meguro-Tamagawa Elec. Co., and Toa Tobacco Co.; Auditor, Sugawa Elec.-Power Co.; b. Mar., 1877 in Oita-ken; s. of Yoshizo Kanemitsu. Career: Head, Taxation Office, Nagasaki Custom-House and Kumamoto Revenue Office; joined Suzuki Shoten, Kobe, 1908; Mng.-Dir., Taiyo Life Ins. Co.; established Taisho Life Ins. Co.; sent to Diet 4 times. Address: 31 Sarugakucho, Shibuyaku, Tokyo.

Mem., House of Peers; Pres., Kodokan; b. Oct., 1860 in Hyogo-ken; s. of late Jirosaku Kano, Naval Officer. Career: grad., Polit. Econ. Course, Tokyo Imp. Univ., 1881; Philosophy Special Course of same, 1892; apptd. Lecturer, Peers' School, 1882, successively promoted Prof., Mgr. Head Prof. of same; often visited America, Europe and China; Councillor, and Dir. of Common Education Bureau, Education Dept.; Dir., 5th and 1st Higher Schools; same, Tokyo Higher Normal School; nominated Mem., House of Peers; 1922; founded Kobunkan School, 1882, and Kodokan (Judo training school); organized Kobun Gakuin (aiming at education for Chinese), 1901, and Kodokan Cultural Society, 1922. Address: 114 Sakashitacho, Otsuka, Koishikawaku, Tokyo.

Mng.-Dir., Onoda Cement Co.; Dir., Oita Cement Co.; b. July 1883 in Tokyo; s. of Kotetsu Oki, and later adopted by Toyokatsu Kanoh. Career: grad., Engrg. Coll., Tokyo Imp. Univ., 1907; made further study at Technische Hochschule in Berlin, and Göttingen Univ., Germany, 1910-13; Engineer, Onoda Cement Co., 1907; Chief, Technical Dept. of same, 1909; Mgr., 1915; Technical Dir., 1918; Mng. Dir. 1927. Address: Onoda, Yamaguchi-ken.

Shinto Bishop; b. July, 1867 in Kanagawa-ken; s. of Tomie Kanzaki, Shinto Priest. Career: grad., Toyo and Kokugakuin Univs.; after having taught at secondary school, apptd. Supt. and Bishop of Shinto; Councillor, Kyochokai (Cooperation Assn.) and League of Nations Assn.; Mgr., Dai-Nippon Religion Assn. and Civic Society. Address: 655 Sendagaya, Shibuyaku, Tokyo.

Mgr., Sapporo Branch, Dai-Nippon Brewery Co., Ltd.; b. Oct., 1874; s. of Sakuji Kasahara, farmer. Career: grad., Sapporo Agr. Sch., 1899; joined Sapporo Beer Brewery Co. which later merged into present firm, 1900; went to America to investigate Brewery Industry, 1916; apptd. Factory Chief, Sapporo, 1917; same at Azumabashi, 1921; Chief, Testing Section, 1923; present post since 1928. Address: 10 Higashi 5-chome, Kitaichijo, Sapporo.
Former Mgr., Sumitomo Bank; b. Jan., 1872 in Niigata-ken; s. of Bunpei Kasahara, business man. Career: grad., Keio Univ.; Harvard Univ., U. S. Address: 11 Natsugimachi, Nishinomiya, Hyogo-ken.

Pres., Fuji Minobu Ry. Co. & Toden Shoken Kabushiki Kaisha; b. Jan., 1874 in Yamanashi-ken; s. of Hyoichiro Kasai, landlord. Career: grad., Seiki School; upon grad. entered business; Pres. and Dir. of several Elec. and Ry. Concerns; elected to Diet from Yamanashi-ken 3 times. Address: 278 Nishi-Okubo, Yodobashiku, Tokyo.

Hogakuhakushi (D. L.); Envoy Extraordinary & Min. to Portugal; b. May, 1885 in Ishikawa-ken; s. of Takeo Nonaka, scholar. Career: grad., Law Coll., Tokyo Imp. Univ., 1909; went to America and France for study; apptd. Councillor, Foreign Office, 1907; Technical Delegate to Peace Conference, 1918-22; Chief, Intelligence Bureau, Foreign Office, 1923-24; Diplomatic Representative at Constantinople, 1925; Chargé d'Affaires, Bukarest, 1926; Councillor of Embassy, Paris, 1929; Dir., Japanese Bureau to Int'l Lab. Org., 1927-30; E. E. & M. P. to Teheran, 1929-32; present post since Aug., 1932. Address: Japanese Legation, Lisbon, Portugal.

Physician; (Specialist in internal troubles, nervous disorders, physical treatment); b. Mar., 1881 in Tokyo; s. of Masanori Kashida. Career: grad., Medical Coll., Tokyo Imp. Univ. Address: 1 Tori-Sanchome, Nihonbashiku, Tokyo.

Lieut.-General; Chief, Headquarters of Military Instruction Board; b. Jan., 1881 in Fukuoka-ken; s. of Sako Kashii, samurai, and later adopted by Shuntaro Kashii. Career: grad., Military Academy; apptd. Sub.-Lieut., 1901 and promoted Lieut.-General, 1917; grad., Military Coll.; studied in Germany; Adjutant, Field-Marshal; Pres., Toyama Military School; Garrison Comdr. to China; Dir., Munition Dept.; present post since 1932. Address: 16 Utagawacho, Shibuyaku, Tokyo.
Consul at Changsha, China; b. Feb., 1883 in Aichi-ken; s. of late Sauemon Kasuya. Career: grad., Toa Dobun Shoin, Shanghai. Address: c/o Japanese Consulate, Changsha, Huan Province, China.

M. P.; b. Jan., 1891 in Akita-ken; s. of late Shigeru Katano, high taxpayer in Akita-ken. Career: grad., Tokyo Imp. Univ.; often elected Mem., Akita-ken Pref. Assembly; elected to Diet from Akita-ken twice; Head, Yokotemachi, Akita-ken; Infantry Lieut.; Pres., Akita Shimpo; Dir., Akita Brewery Co.; Yokote Textile Co.; Auditor, Ugo Bank, Yokosho Ry. Co., etc. Address: Yokotemachi, Akita-ken.

Mem., House of Peers; Adviser, Minseito; b. Sept., 1859 in Kochi-ken; s. of Magogoro Kataoka, samurai. Career: studied at Kochi Toya Gakko; entered Home Office; Chief, Police Affairs Dept., Shiga-ken up to 1892; sent to Diet 8 times since then; Parl. Vice-Minister of Home Affairs, 1924; Minister of Com. & Industry, 1925; Finance Minister, 1926-27; Pres., Nippon Life Ins. Co. and Nippon Kairiku Ins. Co.; Adviser, Nippon Yusen Kaisha and Kyoto Hotel; Pres., Kyodo Bank; nominated Mem., House of Peers, 1930. Address: Horiuchi-mura, Kiigun, Kyoto-fu.

Pres., Nomura Securities Co., Ltd.; b. Feb., 1881 in Okayama-ken; s. of Tokutaro Kataoka. Career: grad., Tokyo Univ. of Com., 1904; joined Industrial Bank of Japan; resigned same and apptd. present post. Address: Kotobukidori Itchome, Okamachi, Toyono-gun, Osaka-fu.

Kogakuhakushi (D. E.); Pres., Federation of Osaka Credit Unions; Pres., Nippon Architectural Assn.; Pres., Nippon Elevator Mfg. Co.; Dir., Miyako Hotel and Nippon Life Ins. Co.; Prop., Kataoka Archtl. Office; b. June, 1876 in Kanazawa City; s. of Tadashige Hosono, samurai; adopted by Naoharu Kataoka. Career: grad., Engrg. Coll., Tokyo Imp. Univ., 1897; Mem., City Planning Committee, Tokyo and Osaka. Address: 36 Dojima Nichome, Kitaku, Osaka.

Resident Com. Commr. of Foreign Office at Shanghai; b. Jan. 1892 in Saga-ken; s. of Jushiro Kato, M. P. Career: grad., Toa Dobun Shoin, 1913; entered Mitsubishi G. K.; transferred Mitsubishi Trading Co., serving at its Shanghai, Hongkong, Kanton, Wuchu, Dairen, Hsinking, Kirin and Tokyo Offices; present post since 1922. Address: 34 Sekoro, Senairi, Shanghai.

Admiral; Supreme War Councillor; b. Nov., 1870 in Tokyo; s. of Naokata Kato, samurai. Career: grad., Naval Academy, 1891; apptd. Sub.-Lieut., 1894; fought in Russo-Japanese War as Gunnery Officer on board H. M. S. Asahi and Mikasa, 1904; Vice-Comdr., H. M. S. Asama and Tsukuba; Attaché, Embassy in England; Comdr., H. M. S. Ibuki, Tsukuba and Hiei; Dir., Naval Gunnery School; Staff-Gen., Yokosuka Naval Station; Pres., Naval Staff Coll.; attended Washington Conf.; Comdr., 1st and 2nd Squadron; Chief, Naval General Staff. Address: 17 Sankocho, Yotsuyaku, Tokyo.

7th O. M.; Pres., Kato Shokai, Ltd.; Permanent Mem. and Trade Dept. Mgr., Nagoya Chamber of Com. & Industry; b. Aug., 1885 in Nagoya; s. of Shuzaburo Kato, business man. Career: after grad. Nagoya Com. Coll., stayed at Hongkong for years for study of commerce and languages; long served as Mem., Rice Problem Inquiry Committee; besides connected with several public organizations and commercial firms; high taxpayer in Aichi-ken. Address: Minami-Kuwanamachi, Nakaku, Nagoya.

Pres., Bank of Chosen; b. Apr., 1873 in Aichi-ken; s. of Hiroshi Kawamura, and later adopted by late Atsuhiro Kato, ex-Mayor of Toyama. Career: grad., Nippon Univ., 1897; passed Higher Civil Service Exam.; entered Communications Dept.; Dir., Communications Bureau and Communications Supt. Bureau; Dir., Hypothec Bank of Japan, 1913 and Hokkaido Colonization Bank, 1924; present post since Feb., 1927. Address: 110 Nandaimon-dori, Keijo, Chosen.

Lawyer; b. Oct., 1882 in Wakayama City; s. of Yasunosuke, official. Career: grad., Law Dept., Kansai Univ.; served as Judge, 1906-13; practised law, 1913; elected Chairman, Wakayama Municipal Assembly, 2 terms from 1920; same, Wakayama-ken Pref. Assembly, 1928-31; Mgr., Nankai Yu-en K. K., 1926; Wakayama Sangyo K. K., 1930; Adviser, Wakayama Chamber of Com. & Industry. Address: 3 Sanbancho, Wakayama City.

M. P.; b. Oct., 1884 in Miye-ken; brother of Isaburo Kato. Career: grad., Nippon Univ.; apptd. Dir., same Univ.; Sec. to Home Minister; Councillor, Meiji Shrine Construction Bureau; sent to Diet from Miye-ken 5 times; Parl. Councillor, Home Office in Tanaka Cabinet; Pres., Invented Articles Mfg. Co.; Dir., Nippon Patent Ink Co.; Parl. Vice-Minister of Overseas Affairs, 1931-32. Address: 33 Shirokane-Sarumachi, Shibaku, Tokyo.

Mng. Dir., Mitsubishi Trading Co.; Dir., Mitsubishi Elec. Engrg. Co., Nippon Raw Silk Co., Toyo Weaving Co.; Auditor, Chiyoda Oil Co.; b. Jan., 1883 in Tokyo; s. of Soichi Kato, samurai. Career: grad., Law Coll., Tokyo Imp. Univ., 1905; joined Mitsubishi Goshi Kaisha and apptd. its Branch Mgr. at Hongkong Office; Mgr., Kobe and Osaka Branches, Mitsubishi Trading Co.; Chief, Metal Dept. and Machinery Dept., Tokyo Head Office; Councillor of same; went abroad several times. Address: 350 Kitashinagawa, Shinagawaku, Tokyo.

Hogakuhakushi (D. L.); Prof., Tokyo Imp. Univ.; Mem., Legislative Deliberation Committee; b. Mar., 1871 in Nagano-ken; brother of Yukio Hirabayashi; later adopted by Masayoshi Kato, Ex-Vice-Pres., Nippon Yusen Kaisha. Career: grad., Law Coll., Tokyo Imp. Univ., 1897; studied in Germany and France; received degree, 1904. Address: 2 Motozonocho Itchome, Kojimachiku, Tokyo.

Mem., House of Peers; Adviser, Hokkaido Kyokai and Daito Bunka Kyokai; b. July, 1854 in Saitama-ken; s. of Tadaemon Kato. Career: grad., Keio Univ.; Editor, Hokkaido Shimbun; Corr., Jiji Shimpo; Pres., Dewa Oil Co.; Pres., Hakodate Tramway Co. and Tojo Ry. Co.; Chairman, Saitama-ken Pref. Assembly, 1880-89; sent to Diet 12 times; visited Europe and U. S. twice; nominated Mem., House of Peers, 1927. Address: Nerima-Toshidamachi Itchome, Itabashiku, Tokyo.

Mng. Dir., Oriental Linoleum Co.; b. Mar., 1884; s. of late Masaroku Nakano, and later adopted by Chojiro Kato. Career: grad., Econ. Dept., Keio Univ., 1908; entered Yamaguchi Bank; having served successively as Section Chief, Branch and Business Dept. Mgr.; promoted Dir. of same; present post since Oct., 1929. Address: 19 Takarazuka, Hyogo-ken.

Igakuhakushi (M. D.); Prof., Keio Univ.; b. Feb., 1890 in Okayama-ken; s. of Torao Kato. Career: grad., Med. Coll., Kyoto Imp. Univ., 1916; apptd. Asst. of same Univ.; Lecturer, Keio Univ.; Prof. of same, 1919; received degree, 1920; spent a year in Europe and America; attended World Biological Congress, America. Address: 14 Sakyomachi, Yotsuyaku, Tokyo.

Prof., Rissho Univ.; b. Sept., 1886 in Tottori-ken; s. of Umekichi Kato. Career: grad., English Litt. Course, Waseda Univ., 1909; published "Cho" (literary critical magazine published every 10 days); translated and introduced Polish and English Literature to Japan; edited Hawaii Daily News in Batavia, 1922-23; bestowed Order of Golden Cross by Polish Gov't, 1931. Address: 1018 Seta, Tamagawamachi, Setagayaku, Tokyo.

Trader; b. Dec., 1870 in Shizuoka-ken; s. of Kanju Kato, farmer. Career: grad., Keio Univ.; for years engaged in Chinese and Manchurian trade; Pres., Tokai Enterprise Promotion Co.; Mng.-Dir., Mukden Hempdressing Co. and Manchurian Industrial Co., Ltd.; Auditor, Tokyo Bldg. Co., Ltd.; sent to Diet from Shizuoka-ken 3 times. Address: 733 Gotenyama, Kitashinagawa, Shinagawaku, Tokyo.

Councillor, Emb., London; b. 1890 in Toyama-ken. Career: grad., Kobe Higher Com. Sch.; Eleve-Con., Mukden & New York, 1914; Attache, Emb., Brazil, 1915; Italy, 1916; France, 1918; Mem., Peace Delegation, 1919; Mem., Committee, Paris Peace Treaty, 1920; 2nd Legation Sec., Roumania, 1921; Mem., 3rd Gen. Meeting of League of Nations, 1922; Chief, 2nd Section, Europe & America Bureau, 1923; 1st Leg. Sec., China 1926; Con.-Gen., Tientsin, 1927; 1st Emb. Sec., Washington, 1929; Mem., Naval Conf. at London, 1929; Emb. Councillor, Wash., 1930. Address: c/o Japanese Embassy, London.

Viscount; Vice-Admiral; Chief, Naval Aviation Headquarters; b. 1883 in Tokyo; s. of Tomosaburo Kato. Career: grad., Naval Staff Coll.; Delegate, Permanent Advisory Commission on Naval, Military, and Air Questions, League of Nations: Delegate to Int'l Aviation Committee, League of Nations; Aid-de-camp to H.I.M. the Emperor; Staff, Naval Gen. Staff; Pres., Naval Staff Coll. Address: 6 Aoyama-minamimachi, Akasakaku, Tokyo.

Mng.-Dir., Mitsubishi Bank; Dir., Nippon Elec. Battery Co.; Auditor; Meiji Fire Ins. Co., Tokyo Marine & Fire Ins. Co., Mitsubishi Warehouse Co. and Mitsubishi Trust Co.; Councillor, Keio Univ.; b. June, 1883 in Tochigi-ken; s. of Shochiro Kato. Career: grad., Keio Univ., 1901; joined Mitsubishi Goshi Kaisha and apptd. Asst. Mgr., Kobe and Kyoto Branches, then Mgr., Osaka Office; was abroad 2 years; Mng. Dir., Mitsubishi Bank, 1919. Address: 9 Kawadacho, Ushigome, Tokyo.
Sub.-Mgr., Mikimoto Pearls Store; b. Oct., 1884 in Miye-ken; s. of Kuranosuke Kato. Career: grad., Kobe Higher Com. Sch.; entered present firm. Address: 30 Koyodo, Nakanoku, Tokyo.

Lawyer; M. P.; Parl. Councillor, Home Office; b. Nov., 1888 in Osaka-fu; s. of Teizaburo Katsuda. Career: grad., Law Coll., Tokyo Imp. Univ., 1913; opened law office; Dir., Japan Physical Education Society, Japan Lawn Tennis Assn., Osaka Physical Educ. Soc.; Auditor, Kashima Trust Co.; Dir., Toyama Spinning Co., Naigai Provision Co., Taiwan Pine-apple Co.; Vice-Pres., Osaka Bar Assn.; Mem., Int'l Sight Seeing Committee. Address: 53 Shimo-Nibancho, Kojimachiku, Tokyo.

Ex-Mem., both Houses of Diet; Marine Transportation Business; b. Oct., 1873 in Matsuyama, Ehime-ken; s. of Rinjiro Katsuda. Career: grad., Aoyama Gakuin Inst.; started marine transportation business on his own account in Kobe, 1900; converted it into Katsuda Steamship Co., Ltd., and assumed its presidency; Pres., Kobe Shipowners' Assn.; Kobe Branch, League of Nations Assn.; Mem., Kobe Municipal Assembly; Ex-Chairman, Kobe Municipal Assembly; Ex-Mem., Kobe Chamber of Com. & Industry, etc. Address: 27 Nakamachi, Kobe.

Pres., Hospital; Prof., Univ.; b. Aug., 1886 in Kobe; s. of Goro Katsunuma, captain. Career: grad., Medical Dept., Tokyo Imp. Univ.; studied under Kinnosuke Miura, Katsusaburo Yamagiwa and Dr. Mataro Nagayo; went to France as Mem., Prince Saionji's Suites, 1919; apptd. Prof., Nagoya Medical Coll. and promoted Pres., Hospital attached to same; bestowed Imperial Academy Prize, 1926; Pres., Japan Society of Internal Medicine. Address: 4 Nakanomachi, Higashiku, Nagoya.

Dir., Kawachi & Co., Ltd.; Marine & Fire Insurance Agents for domestic & foreign importers & exporters; Prop., Kawachi Shipping Agents and Osaka Marine Transportation Co., Ltd.; b. Mar., 1884 in Hyogo-ken; s. of Isuke Kawachi, business man. Career: completed Kobe Commercial School; joined Mitsui Bussan Kaisha, and then Oji Paper Mfg. Co.; succeeded father's business. Address: 125 Tomihisacho, Ushigomeku, Tokyo.

Councillor, Embassy to Manchoukuo; b. Jan., 1881 in Miyazaki-ken; s. of Susumu Kawagoe, Ex-M. P. Career: grad., Law Coll., Tokyo Imp. Univ., 1908; Consul at Hankow; Sec., Foreign Office; 1st Sec., Embassy; Consul-General at Honolulu and Kirin; same at Tsingtao, 1929-32; Chief Suite, Special Envoy to Manchoukuo, 1933; present post since 1933. Address: c/o Japanese Special Envoy's Office, Hsinking, Manchukuo.

Collaborator, League of Nations, Tokyo; b. Oct., 1902 in Tokyo; s. of Kesataro Kawahara, reserve Vice-Admiral. Career: grad., Polit. Econ. Dept., Waseda Univ., 1928; took P.-G. Course in Int'l Politics and History of Diplomacy at same; at time of Shanghai Incident, appt. Non-official Staff, 3rd Squadron, serving as Assistant Adviser of Int'l Law; present post since 1929. Address: 30 Ogikubo, Sanchome, Suginamiku, Tokyo.

Major; Attache, Army Press Bureau; b. 1896 in Kagawa-ken. Career: grad., Mil. Academy, 1918; grad., Mil. Staff Coll., 1927; Instructor, Mil. Academy, 1930; Attache, Staff, 5th Div., 1932; present post since June, 1933. Address: c/o Army Press Bureau.

General; Privy Councillor; b. Sept., 1864 in Oita-ken; s. of Morimasu Kawai. Career: grad., Military Academy and Military Coll.; Sub.-Lieut., 1886; Staff, Taiwan Govt.; Prof. and Pres., Military Coll.; Staff, Manchurian Army; Comdr., 7th Brigade; Comdr., Kwantung Army; Supreme War Councillor; Chief of General Staff; General, 1921; Privy Councillor, 1927. Address: 47 Horinouchi, Suginamiku, Tokyo.

Pres., Japan Musical Instruments Mfg. Co.; b. Mar., 1885 in Shizuoka-ken; s. of Jisaburo Kawakami, landlord. Career: grad., Engrg. Coll., Tokyo Imp. Univ.; entered Tokyo Gas Co.; Sumitomo Steel-Tube & Copper-Works, 1919; sent to Europe and America by Sumitomo for 2 years; apptd., Dir Sumitomo Elec. Wire Mfg. Co.; present post since 1927; Mem., Hamamatsu Chamber of Co. & Industry. Address: 344 Hirosawamachi, Hamamatsu-shi.

M. P.; b. Oct., 1881 in Ehime-ken; s. of late Setsutaro. Career: grad., Tokyo Univ. of Com., 1905; Head, Financial Dept., Kokumin Shimbun; Councillor, Dept. of Education; Mem., Religious System & Social Work Research Committee; went to Europe and America for study; visited China and Manchuria for inspection; elected to Diet 6 times. Address: 26 Kasumicho, Azabuku, Tokyo.

Pres., Kita-Karafuto Mining Co.; b. Dec., 1861 in Niigata-ken; s. of Sentaro Kawakami, samurai. Career: grad., Russian Course, Tokyo School of Foreign Languages, 1884; diplomatic service as Sec. and Interpreter at Consulates and Embassies; then Consul-Gen. at Harbin and Moscow; Dir. and Chief Negotiator of S. Manchuria Ry. Co.; Minister to Poland. Address: 17 Kawadacho, Ushigomeku, Tokyo.

b. July, 1872 in Ehime-ken; s. of Yokichi Kawakami, business man. Career: grad., Waseda Univ.; Pref. Gov., Chosen; Dir., Oriental Development Co.; Pres., Japan Trust Bank. Address: Ashiya, Mukogun, Hyogo-ken.

Dir., Resources Bureau, Cabinet; b. August 1882 in Nagasaki-ken; s. of Heinosuke Kawakubo. Career: grad., Law Coll., Tokyo Imp. Univ. 1908; Patent Examiner; Councillor, Agrl. & Com. Dept.; Dir., Com. Affaires Bureau, Com. & Ind. Dept.; present post since Nov., 1933. Address: 18 Wakagi, Shibuya-ku. Tokyo.

Ex-M. P.; Dealer in Honey; Pres., Japan Turpentine-Oil Co., Central Gum Industry Co., Feigtien Sanrin Co., Marusan Cocoon Co., Chugai Chemical Industry Co.; Dir., Korea Tobacco Industrial Enterprise Co., Nakai Shoten, Daido Paper-Store; Pres., Shinkoron-Sha, Gifu Maiyu Shimbun, Nobi Nippo; Adviser, Japan Sole Association of Feeding Bees (Zen Nippon Yo Ho Kumiai); Chairman, Central Cocoon Association of Gifu Prefecture; Pres., Japan Royalistic Association (Dai Nippon Teikoku Seikwakai); b. 1876 in Gifu-ken. Career: sent to Diet from Gifu-ken. Address: 6 Hongokucho Sanchome, Nihonbashiku, Tokyo.

Mng.-Dir., Daian Life Ins. Co.; b. Apr., 1869 in Nagano-ken; s. of Kiyoto Kawamura, samurai, Tanokuchi Clan. Career: Grad., Law Coll., Tokyo Imp. Univ., 1894; entered Finance Dept., same year; Asst. Mgr., Nippon Churitsu Bank, 1895; Deputy-Mayor of Kyoto, 1917; Mem., Investigation Committee, Manchuria Ry. Co., 1908; Dir., same Co., 1917-20. Address: 11 Komagome 4 chome, Toshimaku, Tokyo.

Mem., House of Peers; Adviser, Seiyukai; Trustee, Kawamura Jogakuin; b. July, 1871 in Akita-ken; s. of Toshiharu Kawamura, samurai, Akita Clan. Career: grand., Law Coll., Tokyo Imp. Univ., 1897; Gov., Wakayama-ken, Aomori-ken and Kagawa-ken; Chief, Police Bureau and Colonization Bureau; attended 6th Int'l Post Congress in Rome; Vice-Minister of Home Office in Hara Cabinet; Pres., South Manchuria Ry. Co.; nominated Mem., House of Peers; Gov.-Gen. of Taiwan, 1928–29; Justice Minister, Mar., 1932. Address: 1642 Takatamachi, Tokyo.

Kogakuhakushi (D. E.); Councillor, Mitsubishi Mining Co.; Dir., Tokyo Steel Works., Nippon Accumulator Co., Lead Powder Paint Co.; b. Nov., 1878 in Okayama; s. of late Joichi Kawamura, soldier. Career: grad., Engrg. Coll., Tokyo Imp. Univ.; entered Mitsubishi Co. as Engineer of Osaruzawa Mine and later promoted to Asst. Mgr., same mine; shifted to Headquarters of Mitsubishi Co. to investigate erection of Iron and Steel Works at Kenjiho, Korea, 1913; promoted to Chief Engr., Designing & Erecting Section of Iron Works Preparatory Dept., 1915; Mgr., Iron & Steel Mfg. Dept., same works; transfered to Head Office of Mitsubishi Iron & Steel Co., 1919; Dir., same Co., 1923–32; Lecturer on Iron & Steel Metallurgy, Engrg. Coll., Tokyo Imp. Univ., 1921–22; Twice elected as President of Iron & Steel Institute of Japan, 1924 & 1932 each for two years; 5 times despatched abroad by Mitsubishi Co. to investigate mining, metallurgical engrg., iron & steel technology, chemical industry. Address: 1526 Yoyogi, Tokyo.

Dir., Mitsui Bussan Kaisha, Ltd.; Dir., Toyo Rayon Co. Ltd.; b. Jan., 1871 in Miye-ken; s. of Shichizaemon Kawamura. Career: grad., Tokyo Higher Com. School, 1891; after having served as Mgr., Shipping and Shipbuilding Depts., promoted present post; besides Dir., Toyo Rayon Co., Ltd.; Pres., Kobe Shipping Exchange, Ltd.; Trustee, Tokyo Higher Merchantile Marine School. Address: 29 Mikawadaimachi, Azabuku, Tokyo.

Pres., Taiwan Nichinichi Shimposha; b. Nov., 1884; s. of Masato Kawamura, Tokyo. Career: grad., Law Coll., Tokyo Imp. Univ., 1911; Police Supt. of Taiwan Govt.; Dir., Taiwan Camphor Mfg. Co.; joined present firm 1927; went to Europe and America for inspection, 1921. Address: 25 Motozonocho, Taihoku City.

Mng. Dir., Kawanishi Warehouse Co., Kawanishi Aeronuatics Co., Kawanishi Machinery Works, Asahi Transportation Co.; Dir., Meiko Warehouse Co.; b. May, 1892 in Kobe; s. of Seibei Kawanishi, business man. Career: grad., Econ. Dept., Keio Univ., 1916. Address: 22 Takakuramachi Itchome, Kobeku, Kobe.

Mng. Dir., Nippon Woolen Fabric Co., Sanyo Leather Co., Showa Worsted Co., Kobe Raw Silk Co.; Adviser, Kobe Chamber of Com. & Industry; Auditor, Yasuda Bank, Nippon Air Transport Co.; Dir., Yasuda Trust Co., Kobe Gas Co., Tokyo Fire Ins. Co.; b. July, 1865 in Osaka; s. of Saburosuke Tsukushi, trader. Career: elected Mem. and Councillor, Kobe Municipal Assembly; Pres., Kobe Chamber of Com. & Industry. Address: 15 Higashi-Hosozawacho, Sumaku, Kobe.

M. P.; b. 1898 in Kanagawa-ken; s. of Jihei Kawano, business man. Career: grad., Polit. Econ. Dept., Waseda Univ., 1923; apptd., Sec. to Agrl. and Forestry Minister, 1932; elected to Diet from Kanagawa-ken. Address: 14 Tori-Shinmachi, Shibaku, Tokyo.

Rear-Admiral; Comdr., Ominato Naval Station; b. Dec., 1881 in Iwakuni, Yamaguchi-ken; s. of Sosuke Kawano, samurai. Career: grad., Naval Coll., 1903; Sub.-Lieut., 1908; Comdr., 1918; Captain, 1922; fought in battle of Japan Sea in Russo-Japanese War; Staffs, Combined Fleet, Naval General Staff; Naval Attaché to Embassy in Brazil; Comdr., H. M. S. Kitakami and Ise; Chief Staff, Sasebo Naval Station; Chief, Naval Intelligence Bureau, Naval General Staff. Address: Official residence, Ominato Naval Station, Ominato, Aomori-ken.

b. Jan., 1886 in Okayama-ken; adotped-s. of Moroyoshi Kawarada. Career: grad., Law Coll., Tokyo Imp. Univ., 1909; entered Home Dept. and apptd. Sec. and Councillor; Head, Labor Dept., Social Welfare Bureau, 1922; attended Int'l Labor Conf. as Govt. Delegate, 1924 & 1928; Director-General, Taiwan Gov't., 1928–29; Vice-Minister, Home Office of Inukai Cabinet. Address: 33 Matsunami, Shibuyaku, Tokoy.

M. P.; Parl. Vice-Minister of Justice; b. Dec., 1880 in Miye-ken; s. of Kijuro Kawasaki. Career: grad., Law Dept., Nippon Univ., 1901; studied French at Tokyo School of Foreign Languages; entered Tokyo Municipal Office; Pres., Chosen Genzan Mindan; Corr., Nippon Shimbun; Publisher and Editor, Genzan Shimpo; elected to Diet 6 times from Miye-ken; Councillor, War Dept.; same, Communications Dept.; Sec.-Gen., Minseito. Address: 94 Shirogane-Sarumachi, Shibaku, Tokyo.

Journalist; Pres., Kokkosha; b. Oct., 1884 in Tottori-ken; s. of Imazo Kawasaki, farmer. Career: grad., Tottori-ken Normal School; taught at same; apptd. Principal, Senkyo Primary School, Tottori City; School-Inspector and Head, Educ.-Affairs Section of Tottori City. Address: Satoni, Tottori-shigai.
Acting Dir., Information & Publicity Bureau, Foreign Dept., Manchoukuo. Career: present post since 1932. Address: Hsinking.

Minister to Greece and Albania; b. Mar., 1880 in Kyoto-fu; s. of Tahei Kawashima, brewer. Career: grad., Tokyo Higher Com. School; passed Diplomatic & Consular Service Exam.; served as Elève-Consul; Diplomatic Probationer; 3rd and 2nd Sec. of Embassy; Sec. and Councillor, Foreign Office; Consul-General at Hamburg; then present post; sent as Japan's Delegate to Conference for codifying international law on cheques at Geneva, and Gen. Meeting of League of Nation; Director of Bureau of Peace Treaties, etc. Address: Legation de Japon, Athenes, Greece.

Parl. Councillor, Navy Dept.; b. July, 1890 in Tokyo. Career: grad., Econ. Dept., Senshu Univ.; Chief, Com. & Industrial Section, Tokyo Municipal Office; Corr., Polit. Dept., Tokyo Nichi Nichi Shimbun; went to Europe and America for inspection. Address: 2158 Omori-Araijuku, Omoriku ,Tokyo.

Vice-General; Comdr., Chosen Army; b. May, 1878 in Ehime-ken. Career: grad., Military Academy, 1898; Military Staff Coll., 1908; sent to Germany for study of military affairs, 1911–13; Sub.-Lieut., 1899; then successively served as Staff, Battalion Adjutant, Infantry 22nd Regiment; Adjustant, 10th Division; same, 11th Div.; Company Comdr., 22nd Reg.; Staff, Military Instruction Board; Instructor, Toyama School; Asst. Military Attaché to Embassy in Berlin; Staff, 65th Reg.; Instructor, Military Academy.; Comdr., 7th Reg.; Section Chief, Military Instruction Board; Comdr., Imp. Guards 1st Brigade; Dir., Personnel Affairs Bureau, Office; Comdr., 19th Div., 1929; same, 3rd Div., 1930; Chief, Military Instruction Board, 1932; fought in Sino-Japanese and Russo-Japanese Wars. Address. Official Residence, Comdr. of Chosen Army, 10 Kanko-dori, Keijo.

Overseas Vice-Minister; b. Sept., 1883 in Tokyo; s. of Kyu Kawata. Career: grad., Law Coll., Tokyo Imp. Univ., 1908; entered Finance Office; Inspector, Revenue Supt. Bureau; Sec. to Finance Minister; Trade Commissioner staying in France and England, 1914–16; Chief, Budget Settlement Section; Dir., Accountant Bureau; Vice-Minister, Finance Office, 1929; present post since May, 1932. Address: 28 Higashi-Shinanomachi, Yotsuyaku, Tokyo.
Lawyer; Hogakuhakushi (D. L.); b. May, 1882 in Yamanashi-ken. Career: grad., Chuo Univ.; Mem. and Alderman, Tokyo Municipal Assembly. Address: 14 Shimbashi Rokuchome, Shibaku, Tokyo.

Captain (Retired Army Officer); Reuters Corr.; b. Jan., 1895 in Edinburgh; n. Scottish; s. of James Young Kennedy. Career: grad., Trinity Coll., Glenalmond; Royal Military Coll., Sandhurst; commissioned 2nd Lieutenant, Cameronians (Scottish Rifles), 1913; served during World War in France and Flanders; severely wounded at battle of Neuve Chapelle, 1915; promoted Lieut., 1915; Captain, 1916; seconded to Japan as Language Officer, 1917–19; Far Eastern Section, War Office, 1920–22; invalided out of Army on account of wounds, 1922; returned to Japan in civilian capacity; apptd. Reuters Corr. in Tokyo; Writer on Japanese Army in Encyclopædia Britanica, 1929 Edition. Address: 47 Akasaka-Daimachi, Tokyo.

O. M., Imp. Red Cross Soc. Japan; Pres., A. Kern & Co.; Chairman, Yokohama & Tokyo Foreign Board of Trade; b. 1884. Career: came to Japan, 1905; connected with several Raw Silk Expert Firms; founded present firm, 1928. Address: 77 Yamashitacho, Bldg. 25, Yokohama.

Dipl. Engr.; Mgr., Bamag-Meguin A. G. and Int'l Cement Gun Co., Tokyo; n. German; b. Dec., 1875 in Breslau. Career: grad., Tech. Univ., Berlin; after having served as mech. engr. in Prussian Gov't Ry., and as erecting engineer in gas works in Germany, Switzerland, Belgium, arrived in Japan, July, 1908; served in Osaka Gas Works as erecting engr.; has kept present posts for nearly 25 yrs. Address: 17 Hikawacho, Akasakaku, Tokyo.
1st Secretary of Afghan Legation to Tokyo. Career: present post since Sept., 1933. Address: Afghan Legation, Iigura 4-chome, Azabuku, Tokyo.

Pres., Nichi-Man Warehouse Co.; b. Jan., 1877 in Fukuoka-ken; e. s. of Shigeru Kibe, clansman. Career: grad., University Course, Peers' School, 1902; apptd. Elève-Consul, 1904, and promoted to Secretary of Foreign Dept.; Sec. of Embassy; Consul; Consul-General; resigned same and entered Furukawa G. K., 1916; became Mgr., Tokyo Branch and Chief, General Affairs Dept., Head Office, South Manchuria Ry. Co.; present post since 1929. Address: 1 Mita-Tsunamachi, Shibaku, Tokyo.
Dir., Elec. Administrative Bureau, Harbin. Career: present post since 1932. Address: Harbin.

Adviser, South Manchurian Ry. Co.; b. April, 1871 in Tokyo; s. of Shirateru Kihara. Career: grad., Military Academy, 1896; Military Coll., 1903; Lieut.-General, 1927; Prof., Military Coll.; Military Traffic Manager; apptd., Chief, 12th Division (famous “Three Human Bullet Heroes” in Shanghai Incident were once under his command); served British Army during World War; Comdr., Capital Guard; Present post since Oct. 1933. Address: 21 Koracho Ichigaya, Ushigomeku, Tokyo.

Mng. Dir., Mitsui Bank; Dir., Showa Bank; Institute for Banking and Financial Research, Inc.; b. Sept., 1870 in Miye-ken; s. of Yasuari Kikumoto, banker. Career: grad., Economy Dept., Keio Univ.; formerly Mgr., Fukagawa and Osaka Branches, and Metropolitan Office, Mitsui Bank; Mem., Control Committee, Extraordinary Industrial Rationalization Commission. Address: 113 Minamicho-Rokuchome, Aoyama, Akasakaku, Tokyo.

Chief-Secretary to Minister of Education; b. Sept., 1885 in Hyogo-ken; s. of Yasutaka Kikusawa, military man. Career: grad., Law Coll., Tokyo Imp. Univ., 1913; entered Education Dept., 1914; apptd. Secretariat, Tottori-ken, 1918; Asst. Prof., Tohoku Imp. Univ., 1920; served at Higher Education Dept., Social Education Dept, 1923–27; Secretariat, Tokyo Imp. Univ., 1927–31. Address: 21 Sankocho, Yotsuyaku, Tokyo.
Vice-Gov., Hsing-an Gen. Administrative Office. Career: grad., Tokyo Foreign Language Sch.; present post since 1932. Address: Hsinking.

Yakugakuhakushi (Phar. D.); Pharmacist; b. Feb., 1879 in Osaka; s. of Hikojiro Kimura, physician. Career: grad., Medical Dept., 5th Higher School; studied pharmacology at Berlin Univ.; Dir., Osaka Pharmacist's Assn.; Sec. and Prof., Osaka Higher School of Pharmacy; Mem., Pharmacist Exam. Committee: Special Mem., Osaka City Planning Committee; Pres., Kimura Chemical Laboratory. Address: 14 Komiyacho, Tennojiku, Osaka.

Consul-General at Manila; b. Oct., 1891 in Miyagi-ken; s. of Seizo Kimura. Career: grad., Law Coll., Kyoto Imp. Univ., 1915; Sec., Tokyo-fu; Sec., Foreign Office and Education Dept.; Consul at Chicago, 1928. Address: Japanese Consulate-General, Manila.

Author; b. Feb., 1894; s. of Shigeshi Kimura, farmer. Career: grad., Eng. Litt. Dept., Waseda Univ., 1917; Labor Coll., London; stayed 4 years to study literature and social conditions in Europe and America; Mem., Central Executive Committee, Zenkoku Rono Taishuto. Address: 47 Nishi-Okubo, Yodobashiku, Tokyo.

M. P.; Parl. Councillor, Overseas Dept.; b. Feb., 1888 in Shimane-ken; s. of late Gisaburo Kimura. Career: grad., Waseda Univ.; Auditor, Shimane-ken Agrl. & Industrial Bank; Dir., Shimane Savings Bank and San-indo Industrial Co.; Mng. Dir., Hikami Ry. Co.; Pres., Mitsuba Motorcar Co.; Sec. to Home Minister, and Finance Minister; apptd. present post, May, 1932. Address: 73 Komagome Kamifujimaecho, Hongoku, Tokyo.

Dir.-Gen., Mitsubishi Goshi Kaisha; Dir., Mitsubishi Bank, Mitsubishi Mining Co., Mitsubishi Trust Co., Mitsubishi Aircraft Co., Mitsubishi Elec. & Engrg. Co., Wakamatsu Harbor Co., Mitsubishi Trading Co., Mitsubishi Warehouse Co.; Councillor, Tokyo Chamber of Com. and Industry; Chief Dir., Japan Industrial Club; b. Dec., 1865 in Kochi-ken; s. of Ichiji Okada, samurai; adopted by Zen Kimura. Career: grad., Law Col., Tokyo Imp. Univ., 1890; joined Bank Dept., Mitsubishi Goshi Kaisha, serving at its Nagasaki and Kobe Branches; Dir., & Mgr. of Gen. Affairs Dept. and Head., Mining Dept. Address: 76 Bentencho, Ushigomeku, Tokyo.

Mem., House of Peers; Councillor, Bank of Japan; Dir., Chiyoda Life Ins. Co.; b. Nov., 1861 in Okayama-ken; s. of Kansuke Kimura. Career: grad., Keio Univ., Business Dept., Bank of Japan, 1901; Dir., same, 1906–19; Vice-Governor, same, 1919–26; Mem., Economic Relief Committee for Siberia, Finance and Econ. Committee, Cereal Committee, Committee on Deposit Section, War-time Exchange Committee, etc. Address: 35 Zaimokucho, Azabuku, Tokyo.

B. A.; A. M.; B. D.; LL. D.; Dir., Rikkyo Univ.; b. May, 1874 in Nara-ken; s. of Yoshisaburo Kimura, teacher. Career: grad., Rikkyo Univ., Harvard Univ., Hobart Coll.; Prof., Keio Univ., 1905–1909; teacher, Rikkyo Middle School, 1904–1909; Prof., Yamaguchi Com. Coll., 1909–1917; same, Tokyo Univ. of Com., 1917–1923; Dir., Nagasaki Com. Coll., 1923–1930; present post since 1930. Address: 1 Asagaya, Suginamiku, Tokyo.

Hogakushi (LL. B.); Pres., Tokyo Life Ins. Co. and Fuji Industrial Co.; Dir., Kongosan Elec. Ry. Co., Joto Elec. Co., Tokyo Canal & Real Estate Co.; Auditor, Chosen Savings Bank and Life Ins. Bond Co.; b. June, 1874 in Miye-ken; s. of late Ippo Kimura. Career: grad., Law Coll., Tokyo Imp. Univ., 1899; entered Daiichi Ginko (First Bank); apptd. Dir. and Business Mgr., Kankoku Bank, 1909; Dir., Bank of Chosen. Address: 600 Sendagaya, Shibuyaku, Tokyo.

Ex-Gov., Kwantung Govt.; Adviser, Seiyukai; b. Feb., 1869 in Oita-ken; s. of Yuji Kinoshita. Career: grad., Tokyo Law Inst., 1892; sent to Diet from Oita-ken 9 times since 1902; Councillor, Communications Dept.; same, Ry. Dept.; Dir., Tokyo Dental Coll.; Pres., Matsudaira Educational Inst.; Dir., Toyo Life Ins. Co. and Kyosai Life Ins. Co.; resigned, 1929. Address: 29 Tansumachi, Azabuku, Tokyo.

Ex-Sec.-Gen., Taiwan Govt.; b. Feb., 1884 in Nagano-ken; s. of Hikoshiro Kinoshita. Career: grad., Law Coll., Tokyo Imp. Univ., 1909; District Headman and Sec., Nagano-ken; Chief, Police Dept., Akita-ken; Chief, Development Dept., Hokkaido Govt.; Chief, Police Affairs Dept., Metropolitan Police Board; Gov., Tottori-ken; Chief, Home Affairs Dept. and Educ. Affairs Dept., Taiwan Govt.; Ehimeken and Nagasaki-ken; Sec.-Gen., Taiwan Govt., 1931. Address: 110 Denenchofu, Omoriku, Tokyo.

Executive Dir., Japan Trade Promotion Assn.; b. June, 1889 in Tottori-ken; s. of Manjiro Kinoshita, farmer. Career: studied Econ. and Social Science at Univs. of California and Southern Calif., U. S.; Acting Principal, Rikkyo Training School; Corr., at Washington Disarm. Conference; Editor, Tsingtao Leader (English Daily); Sec.-Gen., Tokyo Press Assn.; Dir., Liberal News Agency. Address: 2 Nishi-Gochome, Ginza, Tokyo.

Igakuhakushi (M. D.); Gynecologist and Obstetrician; b. Aug., 1889 in Fukui-ken; s. of Hiromu Kinoshita, physician. Career: grad., Medical Coll., Tokyo Imp. Univ., 1894; apptd. Asst. Surgeon, Tokyo Imp. Univ.; Chief Surgeon, Fukushima Hospital, 1895; sent to Germany to study Obsterics, 1897., Osaka Medical School, 1899; Asst. Prof., Tokyo Imp. Univ.; Chief Gynecologist and Obsterician, same Univ., 1900; Prof., 1904; resigned 1915 and established Hamacho Maternity Hospital; opened Kinoshita Maternity Hospital. Address: 96 Morikawacho, Hongoku, Tokyo.

Dir., Osaka Mainichi Shimbun, Meiji Life Ins. Co., Kirin Beer Brewery Co., Tokyo Marine & Fire Ins. Co. and Nippon Nitrogen-Fertilizer Co.; Auditor, Tomei Fire Ins. Co.; b. Oct., 1868 in Kochi-ken; e. s. of Masachika Kirishima, samurai. Career: studied at Law Coll., Tokyo Imp. Univ.; joined Mitsubishi Goshi Kaisha; made inspection tour to Europe and America, 1923; Mem. and Chairman, Tokyo Municipal Assembly. Address: 122 Komagome-Fujimaecho, Hongoku, Tokyo.

Sec. to Foreign Minister; b. 1878 in Akita-ken. Career: Foreign Office Clerk, Hankow, 1900; Hungchow, 1901; Singapore, 1906; England, 1910; Vice-Con., Shanghai, 1916; Con., Liverpool, 1919; Con., Los Angeles, 1923; Con.-Gen. at London, 1929; 1st Emb. Sec., Eng., same year; transferred to France, same year. Address: Foreign Office, Tokyo.

Pres., Fukuhaku Motor-Bus Co.; Mng. Dir., Osaka Kogata Taxi Co.; b. Feb., 1890 in Fukuoka-ken; s. of Einosuke Okazaki, official. Career: served Nippon Life Ins. Co.; Mng. Dir., Kokuryukai; present post since 1923. Address: 20 Daido Nichome, Tennojiku, Osaka.

Igakuhakushi (M. D.); Ophthalmologist; b. Apr., 1876 in Fukuoka-ken; s. of Keiji Kitamura, farmer. Career: grad., Medical Coll., Tokyo Imp. Univ., 1902; studied Ophthalmology at Medical Coll., Kyoto Imp. Univ. for 2 years; studied Ophthalmology at Breslau Medical Coll. for 3 years; received degree, 1909; apptd. Chief Ophthalmologist, Fukuoka-ken Pref. Hospital, 1903–05; served in South Manchuria Ry. Hospital and was Prof., Nan-Man Igakudo, 1908–16; established Ophthalmic hospital in Osaka on his account. Address: 66 Koyama-Kazusamachi, Kamikyoku, Kyoto.

Author; Journalist; b. Feb., 1890 in Nagano-ken; s. of Ichiya Kiyosawa, farmer. Career: studied in Japan and America; apptd. Editor, New World, San Francisco, Calif.; Foreign Editor, Chugai Shogyo Shimpo, Tokyo, and Tokyo Asahi Shimbun; Special Corr. at Naval Conference, London, 1930, for Chuo-Koron (Central Review) and Chugai Shogyo Shimpo; represented Hochi Shimbun in America, 1931–32. Address: 921 Chofuminemachi, Omoriku, Tokyo.

Count; Ex-Premier; Pres., Nippon Press Assn., Industrial Education Assn. and Kitoku Club; b. Feb., 1850 in Kumamoto-ken; s. of Ryoin Okubo, Buddhist Priest; adoptd. s. of Hidesato Kiyoura, samurai. Career: apptd. Public Procurator; Chief Sec., Home Office; Dir., Police Bureau; Vice-Minister of Justice; Minister of Justice, 3 times; Mem., House of Peers; Privy Councillor; Pres., Privy Council; Premier, 1924; made Viscount, 1902; Count, 1928; accorded honors of Ex-Premier. Address: 2211 Araijuku, Omoriku, Tokyo.

Hogakuhakushi (D. L.); Dr. Phil. (German); Mem., House of Peers; b. Sept., 1860 in Kagoshima-ken; s. of Kiyonari Koba. Career: grad., Polit. Econ. Dept., Tokyo Imp. Univ.; studied 3 years at Univs. in Germany; after having served as Sec. Councillor, Bureau Dir. in Education Dept. successively, apptd. Sec., Hyogo-ken; Councillor, Legislative Bureau; Prof., Hosei Univ.; Lecturer, Tokyo Imp. Univ. and Tokyo Higher Normal School, etc.; Mem., Meiji Restoration History Editing Office; same, Educ. Administration Inquiry Committee; nominated Mem., House of Peers, 1906. Address: 4 Sakuragaoka, Shibuyaku, Tokyo.

Barrister-at-Law, Middle Temple, London; Lawyer; b. 1890 in Yamagata-ken; s. of Genzo Kobayashi. Career; Grad., Law Coll., Tokyo Imp. Univ. 1915; Apptd. Judge of Court 1917–20; studied in England 1920; called to British Bar, 1923 (Middle Temple, London); returned Home and Practised Civil, Com. and Maritime Law. Office: Tokyo Kaijo Bld., Marunouchi, Tokyo.

Pres., Hanshin Kyuko Elec. Ry. Co.; Vice-Pres. and Businses Mgr., Tokyo Elec. Light Co.; Dir., San-yo Chuo Hydro-Elec. Co., Meguro-Kamata Elec. Ry. Co., Tokyo-Yokohama Elec. Ry. Co. and Iiyama Ry. Co.; Auditor, Showa Fertilizer Co. and 1st Life Ins. Co.; Adviser, Shochiku Kogyo K. K. and Toyo Can Mfg. Co.; Prop. Takarazuka Opera House; b. Jan., 1893 in Yamanashi-ken; s. of Jimpachi Kobayashi. Career: grad., Keio Univ., 1892; joined Mitsui Bank; established Hanshin Kyuko Elec. Co., and became its Mng. Dir., 1907; Pres. of same, 1927. Address: 1967 Ikedamachi, Toyonogun, Osaka-fu.

b. Dec., 1873 in Hiroshima; s. of Yoshinao Kobayashi, samurai. Career: grad., Tokyo Higher Com. School, 1895; joined Yokohama Specie Bank; served its Branches at Tientsin and Dairen; Mng. Dir., Industrial Bank of China. Address: 6 of Ha 10 Nishikatamachi, Hongoku, Tokyo.

Vice-Pres., Kobayashi Shoten, Ltd.; b. Dec., 1899 in Tokyo; s. of Tomijiro Kobayashi, business man. Career: grad., Econ. Dept., Keio Univ., 1923; went to England for study. Address: 8 Sugamo-Sanchome, Toshimaku, Tokyo.

A. B.; J. D.; M. P.; b. 1888 in Hyogo-ken; s. of Hyotaro Kobayashi. Career: grad., Polit. Dept., Univ. of Calif. and School of Jurisprudence, U. C.; Chief Editor, Chuo Shimbun; entered South Manchuria Ry. Co.; Sec. Councillor, New York Branch Mgr., Head Secretariat of same. Address: 35 Yamamotocho, Azabuku, Tokyo.

Dir., Naigai Amimono K. K.; b. Nov., 1888 in Yamanashi-ken; brother of Masaharu Kobayashi. Career: grad., Com. Coll., Northern Univ., U. S., 1912; joined Overland Car Co.; joined Morimoto-Gumi, 1914; resigning same returned home, 1920, and established present firm. Address: 48 Aoyama-Kitamachi-Rokuchome, Akasakaku, Tokyo.

Dir., Mitsui Bussan Kaisha; Pres., Electro Chemical Industry Co., Yodogawa Hydraulic Power Co.; Dir., Matsushima Mining Co., Japan Flour Mill Co., Kyushu Electric Power Co., Kurobegawa Hydraulic Power Co., Toyo Rayon Co.; Auditor, Tsurumi Rinko Ry. Co., Keeling Mining Co., Chosen Anthracite Coal Co.; b. Apr., 1873 in Kyoto-fu; s. of Yoshinao Kobayashi. Career: grad., Doshisha Univ., Kyoto, 1893; entered Mitsui & Co.; after having served as Mgr., Nagasaki, Hongkong, Moji, New York Branches, promoted Dir. and then present post of the firm. Address: 75 Owada, Shibuyaku, Tokyo.

Admiral; Supreme War Councillor; b. 1877 in Hiroshima-ken; adopted s. of Tokinosuke Kobayashi. Career: grad., Naval Staff Coll., 1909; Naval Attache, Japanese Emb., London & Washington; Instructor, Naval Staff Coll.; attended Geneva Naval Conf., 1927; Chief, Construction Dept., Navy, 1929; Vice-Minister of Navy, 1930; Commander-in chief, Combined Squadron and Comdr., 1st Squadron 1931–33; present post since Sept. 1933. Address: 1741 Fukazawa, Setagaya-ku, Tokyo.

Prof., Keio Univ.; b. June, 1886 in Nagano-ken; s. of late Yoriharu Kobayashi. Career: grad., Keio Univ.; studied in Europe and U. S., 1914–17; visited Europe, 1927. Address: 1462 Yoyogi Tomigayacho, Shibuyaku, Tokyo.

Mng. Dir., Koike Bank, Koike Bonds & Securities Co., Karafuto Agrl. Enterprises Co.; b. Dec., 1878 in Nagano-ken; s. of Shichirobei Kodaira. Career: grad., Law Dept., Meiji Univ., 1902; apptd. Chief, Inquiry and Trust Section, Koike G. K.; Auditor, Enoshima Elec. Ry. Co.; present post since 1917. Address: 6 Shin-Ryudomachi, Azabuku, Tokyo.

Count; Mem., House of Peers; Dir., Teikoku Gunjinkai Koenkai; b. July, 1876; s. of Viscount Gentaro Kodama. Career: grad., Law Coll., Tokyo Imp. Univ., 1900; Sec., Finance Office and Residency-Gen.; Sec.-Gen. of Chosen; Chief Sec. of Cabinet; Pres. Gen., Board of Decorations; Gov.-Gen. of Kwantung; Chief, Civil Administration Dept., Chosen Govt. Address: 30 Ichigaya-Yakuojimachi, Ushigomeku, Tokyo.

Pres., Yokohama Specie Bank; Mem., Com. and Industry Deliberation Committee; same, International Loan Deliberation Committee; Mem., League of Nations Assn.; b. Nov., 1871; s. of Koretoki Kodama, samurai, Tokyo. Career: grad., Tokyo Higher Com. School, 1893; joined Yokohama Specie Bank; gradually promoted to Pres. Address: 2 Fujimicho Nichome, Kojimachiku, Tokyo.

M. P.; b. Sept., 1873 in Yamaguchi-ken; s. of Hikaru Kodama. Career: grad., Law Coll., Tokyo Imp. Univ.; joined Samuel & Samuel Co., serving at its Taiwan and Tokyo Branches; joined Asahi Shimbun, Okayama Chugoku Mimpo, Oita Chusei Nippo, Peking Toho and Tokyo Nichi-Nichi Tsushin as Corr.; Pres., Niroku Shimpo, Tairiku Tsushinsha (Continental News Agency); elected to Diet 6 times. Address: 22 Shiba Park, Shibaku, Tokyo.

M. P.; Pres., Tsingtao Shimpo; b. Jan., 1885 in Okayama-ken; s. of Kiichiro Kondo, farmer. Career: grad., Dobun Shoin, Shanghai; then stayed in Manchuria as Staff, Furukawa Mining Co., 1909–15; founded Ten-yu Co. in Tsingtao on his account, 1916; apptd. Political Adviser, Wu-Pei-Fu, 1923; elected to Diet from Okayama-ken twice. Address: 12 Jeho Road, Tsingtao, China.

Dir., Taiwan Development & Tea Mfg. Co., Ltd.; Auditor, Keelung Mining Co., Taiwan Warehouse Co.; Mgr., Taihoku and Takao Branches, Mitsui Bussan Kaisha; b. May, 1883; s. of Tsutomu Kodera, samurai, Gifu clan. Career: grad., Law Coll., Tokyo Imp. Univ., 1906; joined Mitsui Bussan Kaisha; Mgr., Nagasaki Branch. Address: 2 Kodamacho Sanchome, Taihoku City.

Composer; Shogakushi (B. Com.); b. in Fukuoka-ken. Career: grad., Com. Dept., Meiji Univ.; joined Columbia Gramophone Co. as Composer; composed several popular songs such as “Is Wine Tear or Sigh?”, “Pursueing Shadows”, “Beyond the Hills”, “Moonlit Beach”, etc. Address: 1153 Yoyogi Uehara, Shibuyaku, Tokyo.

M. P.; Mem., Domestic Products Promotion Committee and Tariff Inquiry Committee; b. Feb., 1893 in Gumma-ken; s. of Budayu Kogure. Career: grad., Econ. Dept., Keio Univ., 1917; joined Mitsui Bank, same year; Pres., Ikao Hot-Spring Union; elected to Diet 4 times. Address: 9 of 553 Ikaomachi, Gumma-ken.

Mng. Dir., Sumitomo Life Ins. Co.; b. Sept., 1880 in Okayama-ken; s. of Daikichi Koh. Career: grad., Polit. Course, Law Coll., Tokyo Imp. Univ., 1906; entered Sumitomo Bank; Mgr., San Francisco Branch of same, 1916–22; Mgr., Tokyo Branch, 1922–23; for years served as Dir. of the Bank. Address: Sumiyoshimura, Mukogun, Hyogo-ken.
Author; M. P.; b. Mar., 1892 in Tokyo; s. of Tan Koike. Career: grad., Mining Dept., Tokyo Imp. Univ.; served Coal Mine Dept., Suzuki Shoten, Kobe. Address: 1117, 7-chome Zoshigaya, Toshimaku, Tokyo.

Lieut.-Gen.; Chief Staff, Kwantung Army; Mem., National Resources Deliberation Committee and Central Statistics Committee; b. Mar., 1880 in Utsunomiya City; s. of Susumu Koiso, samurai. Career: apptd. Sub.-Lieut., 1901; Staff, Gen. Staff Office; Comdr., Infantry 51st Regiment; Instructor, Military Coll.; Chief, Gen. Affairs Section, Aviation, Army; Dir., Military Preparatory Bureau; Dir., Military Affairs Bureau; Chief Sec., Supreme War Council; Judge, Gen. Court-Martial; Councillor, National Resources Bureau; Vice-Minister of War, 1932; present post since July, 1932. Address: Hsinking, Manchoukuo.

Pres. Keio Univ.; b. May, 1888 in Tokyo; s. of late Shinkichi Koizumi, Dir., Yokohama Specie Bank; Pres., Keio Univ. Career: grad., Keio Univ., studied Economics in London, Cambridge, Berlin and Paris; student of social sciences. Address: 323 Kitashinagawa, Shinagawaku, Tokyo.

Kogakuhakushi (D. E.); Dir., Osaka Seiren K. K.; b. Dec., 1895 in Kanazawa City; s. of Jinshichiro Kojima, samurai. Career: grad., Engrg. Coll., Tokyo Imp. Univ., 1898; Furukawa Mining Co.; apptd. Mgr. of same, 1920; Dir., Furukawa G. K. and Pres., Osaka Seiren K. K., 1923; resigned Presidency of Osaka Seiren K. K., 1931. Address; 735 Morigu-Renge, Nishinomiya, Hyogo-ken.

Mem., House of Peers; Dir., Odawara Express Ry. Co.; b. Mar., 1865 in Miyagi-ken; s. of Tokichi Kokubo, farmer. Career: studied Chinese Classics under Buzen Nakajima; joined Jiyuto; Vice-Pres., Ibaragi-ken Pref. Assembly, 1892; elected to Diet from Ibaragi-ken 6 times during 1908–28; Councillor, Communications Dept.; Pres., Jiyu News Agency; nominated Mem., House of Peers, 1928. Address: Tanido, Omoriku, Tokyo.

D. L.; Councillor, German Embassy, Tokyo; b. Dec., 1891 in Darmstadt; n. German; s. of Heinrich Kolb, Official. Career: grad., Muenchen and Berlin Univs.; Oriental Seminary, Berlin; diplomatic and consular posts, Tokyo (1913); New York, Washington, Prague, Stockholm, Kobe, Tokyo, Berlin, Teheran; present post since 1929. Address: German Embassy Kojimachiku, Nagatacho, Tokyo.

Ex-privy Councillor of Manchoukuo; b. June, 1885 in Shiga-ken. Career: completed Osaka 2nd Middle School; grad., Agrl. Coll., Hokkaido Imp. Univ.; sent to Manchuria for study by Hokkai Times; joined South Manchuria Ry. Co.; assisted Oriental Development Co. in expanding its business in Manchuria and Mongolia, 1917; returned to Tokyo and served as Non-Official Staff, Asia Bureau, Foreign Office 5 years; after Manchurian Incident, Sept., 1931; again went to Manchuria and took part in founding Manchoukuo; apptd. privy Councillor, Manchoukuo, Oct., 1932; Resigned post 1933. Address: Tokiwamura, Awatagun, Gunma-ken.

Composer; b. Apr., 1897; s. of Heizo Komatsu. Career: studied Keio Univ.; founded National Symphony Orchestra, 1929; Prof., Imp. Music School; Conductor, National Symphony Orchestra and Tokyo Civil Orchestra. Address: 645 Asagaya, Suginamiku, Tokyo.

Composer; Pianist; Lecturer, French Language, Tokyo Higher School; b. April, 1900 in Akita-ken; s. of Heizo Komatsu. Career: grad., 1st Higher School; French Literature Course, Tokyo Imp. Univ.; Piano Course, Tokyo Academy of Music; Head “Dora-no-kai” (Gong Society); Conductor, Dora Glee Club; Mgr., National Music Assn.; Sec., New Composers' Assn.; endeavoured in introducing Modern French music, and in establishing Japan's National Music. Address: 69 Asagaya, Suginamiku, Tokyo.

6th Order of Sacred Treasure; Prof., Peers' School; Lecturer, Nippon Univ.; Chief, Japan Composers' Assn.; Pres., National Music Assn.; Non-commissioned-Staff, J.O.A.K.; prominent composer in Japan; b. Dec., 1884 in Akita-ken; s. of Heizo Komatsu, farmer. Career: grad., Tokyo Academy of Music, 1907; P.-G. Course of same; studied Composition under C. M. Widor and Harmony under P. Fochet, of Conservatoire de Paris for 3 years. Address: 485 Asagaya, Suginamiku, Tokyo.

LL. D.; Writer; b. 1865 in Fukushima-ken; adopted s. of Mitsuaki Komatsu. Career: grad., Keio Univ., 1887; studied Polit. Sc. in Yale Univ. and Princeton Univ.; Sec., Legation, U.S.; Acting Minister to Siam; attached Residency-Gen., Korea, 1906; Chief Sec., Privy Council; resigned post, 1916; attended Intl. Labour Conf., Geneva as Representative of Employees, 1929. Address: 38 Sakuradacho, Azabuku, Tokyo.

A. B.; A. M.; Asst. to Pres., Asano Dozoku Kaisha; Mng. Dir., Asano Shipbuilding Co.; Dir., Oriental Paper Bag Co.; b. Mar., 1886 in Shizuoka-ken; s. of Mikisaburo Komatsu. Career: grad., Monmouth and Harvard Univs., U. S.; Sec. to Pres., Toyo Kisen Kaisha, 1914–22; Mgr., Toyo Kisen Kaisha, San Francisco, 1922–1926; Sec. to Admiral Hiroharu Kato at Washington Conference, 1921; Mem., Japanese Delegation, 3 Power Naval Conference at Geneva, 1927. Address: 2370 Araijuku Itchome, Omoriku, Tokyo.

Marquis; Captain (Navy); Mem., House of Peers; b. Aug., 1888 in Tokyo; 4th s. of late Prince Yoshihisa Kitashirakawa. Career: grad., Naval Staff Coll.; went to England to study naval affairs; apptd. Captain, Torpedo-Destroyer “Hokaze”; Staff, Naval General Staff; Comdr., “Isuzu” and “Nagato”; Captain, “Itsukushima” & “Jungei”, etc. Address: 102 Tokiwamatsu, Shibuyaku, Tokyo.

Igakuhakushi (M. D.); Dir., Kondo Hospital; Non-Official Physician, Tokyo Teishin Shinryojo; b. May, 1879 in Aichi-ken; s. of Tanpei Kondo. Career: grad., Osaka Higher Med. School, 1904; studied at Med. Coll., Kyoto Imp. Univ.; studied Clinic under Prof. Norde of Wien Univ. and Prof. Lehmann of Breslau Univ., 1908–12; practised medicine at his native place; apptd. Head Physician, Surugadai Hospital, 1917; opened present Hospital, 1918. Address: 2516 Nishimachi, Nakanoku, Tokyo.

Mng. Dir., Nichibei Koyu (Mineral Oil) K. K.; Dir., Nippon Juyu (Crude Petroleum) K. K., Fuji Trading Co. and Kimura Trading Co.; Chief Sec., Tokyo Oil Assn.; Councillor, Tokyo Mineral Oil Traders' Assn.; b. Dec., 1897 in Okayama-ken; s. of Shigejiro Kondo. Career: grad., Tokyo Com. School; joined Nichibei Koyu, K. K., 1911; Mgr., Tokyo Branch Office of same, 1925; Dir., 1928. Address: 109, Mamakosunahara, Ichikawamachi, Chiba-ken.

Agent for Toilet Articles Mfr.; Ins. Agent; b. May, 1885 in Saitama-ken; s. of Nobujiro Kondo, brewer. Career: established Agency for Toilet Articles Mfr., 1907; expanded its market in East Japan; Vice-Pres., Toilet Articles Trade Union. Address: 362 Sendagaya, Shibuyaku, Tokyo.

Pres., Nippon Parker-Rising Co.; Dir., Sanken Kogyo Co.; b. Sept., 1891 in Tokyo; s. of late Baron Renji Kondo, Pres., N. Y. K. Career: grad., Tokyo Higher Tech. School; Pres., Nippon Kenki K. K.; Dir., Sanken Industrial Co.; same, Komatsu Seisaku-jo; Auditor, Tokyo Adding-Machine Mfg. Co. Address: 1 Nagatacho Nichome, Kojimachiku, Tokyo.

Igakuhakushi (M. D.); Prof., Tohoku Imp. Univ.; b. Feb., 1893 in Niigata; s. of Ichizo Kondo, Merchant. Career: grad., 1st Higher School; Medical Coll., Tokyo Imp. Univ.; made special study of hygiene. Address: 59 Gobancho, Sendai-shi.

Igakuhakushi (M. D.); Prof. Emeritus, Tokyo Imp. Univ.; b. Dec., 1856 in Matsumoto, Nagano-ken; s. of Tsugitaka Tsurumi, samurai. Career: grad., Medical Coll., Tokyo Imp. Univ., 1891; sent to Germany to study at Univs. of Strassburg, Heidelberg, Berlin and Wien; apptd. Prof., Medical Coll., Tokyo Imp. Univ., 1898; resigned same and established Surugadai Hospital, 1924; bestowed degree, 1899. Address: 23 Minamikogacho, Surugadai, Kandaku, Tokyo.

Dir., Tech. Section, Capital Construction Bureau, Manchoukuo; b. 1887 in Kochi-ken; adopted s. of Katsunosuke Kondo. Career: grad. Civil Engrg. Course, Tech. Coll., Kyoto Imp. Univ., 1916; entered South Manchuria Ry. Co., same year; Engr., Reconstruction Buerau, 1923; present post since 1933. Address: Hsinking.

Prince; Pres., House of Peers; Lord-in-Waiting, Jako Hall; Mem., Civil Administrative Committee; b. Oct., 1891 in Kyoto; s. of Prince Atsumaro Konoe. Career: grad., Law Coll., Tokyo Imp. Univ., 1917; present post since 1931; attended Peace Conf. as Mem., Prince Saionji's suite, 1918; Dir., Nippon Seinen Kan. Address: 26 Nagatacho-Nichome, Kojimachiku, Tokyo.

Viscount; Mem., House of Peers; Composer; Founder and Conductor, New Symphony Orchestra; b. Nov., 1898 in Tokyo; s. of Prince Atsumaro Konoe. Career: grad., Coll. Course, Peers' School; studied at Litt. Coll., Tokyo Imp. Univ.; studied in Germany, 1922–25; made musical tour through Europe, 1930; presented many musical performances and composed several songs and orchestral works; Mem., House of Peers, 1932. Address: 437 Shimo-Ochiai, Yodobashiku, Tokyo.

Rigakuhakushi (D. Sc.); Prof., Kyoto Imp. Univ.; b. Sept., 1882 in Aomori-ken; s. of Naoyo Koriba, clansman of Tsugaru. Career: grad., Science Coll., Tokyo Imp. Univ., 1907; completed P.-G. Course of same and bestowed degree, 1912; apptd. Prof., Agrl. Coll., Tohoku Imp. Univ., 1915; sent to U. S., England, Italy, France to study Botany, 1918–20; present post since 1920; went to Java, 1929; visited Europe and South America, 1931. Address: 11 Koyama-Horiikecho, Kami-Kyoku, Kyoto.

Gov. of Tokyo-fu; b. Feb., 1881 in Tokyo; s. of Masakuni Kosaka, official. Career: grad., Law Coll., Tokyo Imp. Univ.; passed Higher Civil Service Exam.; Sec., and Councillor, Ehime-ken; Chief, Home Affairs Dept., Akita-ken and Saitama-ken; Chief, Police Dept., Okayama-ken and Kumamoto-ken; Gov., Fukushima-ken, 1929; present post since May, 1932. Address: 7 of 18 Shiba-koen, Shibaku, Tokyo.

Mng.-Dir., Shinano Mainichi Shimbun-sha; Dir., Azusagawa Electric Power Co.; b. Jan., 1895; s. of late Zennosuke Kosaka, M. P. Career: grad., Law Coll., Tokyo Imp. Univ., 1919; joined Furukawa Mining Co.; attended World Motive Power Conference in Berlin. Address: 5 Tademachi, Nagano City.

Con.-Gen., Batavia; b. 1883 in Tokyo. Career: grad., Post & Telegraph Sch., Tokyo, 1902; Foreign Office Clerk, Tientsin, 1906; Bombay, same year; Italy, 1909; Attache, Emb. in China, 1913; Italy, 1916; Paris, 1919; 2nd. Emb. Sec., same year; Con. at Milne, 1921; 2nd. Legation Sec., Mexico, 1924; 1st Legation Sec., 1926; Con. Gen., Manila, 1928. Address: c/o Japanese Embassy, Batavia.

Mgr. & Dir., Tokyo Marine & Fire Ins. Co., Ltd.; b. Nov., 1880 in Tokyo; s. of late Eigoro Kosuge. Career: grad., Tokyo Univ. of Com., 1903; upon graduation entered present firm and served up to date. Address: 629 Harada, Nadaku, Kobe.

Justice Minister; b. Sept., 1869 in Mito City; s. of Giheiji Takahashi; adopted-s. of Takamitsu Koyama. Career: grad., Doitsu Kyokai Gakko, 1892; Judicial Probationer, Miyagi-ken Pref. Office, 1893; Public Procurator, Local Courts at Nagasaki, Kumamoto and Tokyo, 1896; Judge, Nagasaki Local Court and Appeal Court, 1901; Public procurator, Tokyo Court of Appeal and Tokyo Local Court, 1906; same, Supreme Court; Public Procurator-Gen., 1924; present post since 1932. Address: 20 Aoyama-Takagicho, Akasakaku, Tokyo.

M. P.; Pres. Nagoya Shimbun; b. Jan., 1876 in Nagano-ken; s. of Yozaemon Koyama. Career: studied under Chomin Nakae; grad., Tokyo Semmon Gakko (present Waseda Univ.); joined Osaka Asahi Shimbun; went to China for inspection; apptd. Mgr., Nagoya Branch of same, 1802; founded Nagoya Shimbun on his account, 1906; sent to Diet 6 times since 1907; Parl. Vice-Minister of Agr. & Forestry Dept., 1925; Vice-Speaker of Lower House., 1903; Adviser, Minseito. Address: 12 Aoyama-Takagicho, Akasakaku, Tokyo.

Lieut. J. G. U. S. Navy; Asst. Naval Attaché and Language Student; b. Sept., 1903 in Worcester, Mass., U. S.; n. American; s. of Albin Maximilian Kramer, civil engr. Career: grad., Central High School, Springfield, Mass., 1921; U. S. Naval Academy, 1925; served (France); Officier de Leopold (Belgium); Sub. Mgr., Metal as Ensign, U. S., Navy on Board U. S. S. Tennessee, 1925–26; Submarines, 1927; Lieut. J. G. U. S. Navy on Board U. S. S. Rochester on duty in Central America and ashore in Nicaragua, 1928–29; U. S. Navy Rifle and Pistol Teams, 1929, ’30, ’31; in charge of U. S. Navy Small Arms School, 1931; Engrg. and Gunnery Duties in U.S.S. Detroit, 1930–31; designated “Distinguished Marksman U. S. Navy” 1931; present post since 1932. Address: American Embassy, Tokyo.

A. B. (DePauw); S. T. B. (Boston Univ.); Missionary, Methodist Episcopal Church, New York; b. Aug., 1894, Portland, Indiana, U. S.; n. American; s. of Leroy M. Krider, Minister. Career: studied at Univ. of Chicago; Teacher, Aoyama Gakuin and Chinzei Gakuin, Keiho Middle School, Akunoura English School at Nagasaki; District Missionary, Nagasaki-ken and Chosen for Japan Methodist Church. Address: 12 Higashi Yamate, Nagasaki.

1st Sec., Czechoslovak Legation, Tokyo; b. 1896 in Brno, Czechoslovakia; s. of Dr. L. Krupka, Mem., Czechoslovak Senate. Career: grad., Consular Academy, Vienna, Diplomatic High School of Former Austro-Hungarian Monarchy; Attaché, Czechoslovak Legation in Budapest, 1919; Foreign Office in Prague, 1921–25; Sec. and Chargé d'Affaires in Copenhagen, 1925–28; Political Section of Foreign Office in Prague, 1928–30; 1st Sec., Czechoslovak Legation in Tokyo, 1930–31 and Chargé d'Affaires since April, 1931 until May 1932. Address: Czechoslovak Legation, Tokyo.

Pres., Russo-Japanese Fishery Co.; Dir., Chuo Blanket Co. and Miyako Shimbun; Auditor, Tokyo Stock Exchange and Sino-Japanese Life Ins. Co.; Adviser, Uchida Steamship Co., Uchida Trading Co., Chuo Elec. Co. and Bank of Taiwan; b. May, 1873 in Ibaragi-ken; s. of Hiroshi Uchida, samurai. Career: grad., Tokyo Higher Com. School, 1896; joined Mitsui Bussan Kaisha serving at its Kobe, Hongkong and Hankow Branches; Mng. Dir., Sakai Celluloid Co., 1907; Dir., Hokkaido Colliery & Steamship Co., 1910; Mng. Dir., Hazami Mining Co., 1913; established Kubota Trading Office; Pres., Fuji Paper Mfg. Co., 1918; Pres., Hayakawa Elec. Power Co.; Pres., Russo-Japanese Fishery Co., 1932. Address: 4 Tangocho, Akasakaku, Tokyo.
