Patent Druggist; Dir., Japan New Medicines Mfg. Co.; Mem., Kyoto Chamber of Com. & Industry; Councillor, Yasuda Bank; b. June, 1868 in Kyoto; s. of late Shozaemon Kubota. Career: succeeded estate and business of his father who originated a patent medicine “Sokkosan”, 1883; besides, connected with Hinode Shimbun as Auditor; high taxpayer in Kyoto-fu. Address: Nishitoin, Gojo, Shimokyoku, Kyoto.

Supt., Kobe Custom House; Chief, Treasury Section, Kobe Branch Office of Finance Dept.; b. Aug., 1885 in Yamanashi-ken. Career: grad., Law Coll., Tokyo Imp. Univ., 1911; entered Finance Dept., same year; apptd. Taxation Officer, 1914; Chief, Taxation Office of Urawa, Nagasaki & Kobe; Administrative Official; Chief, Gen. Affairs Section, Kobe Custom House, 1918; sent to Canada & U. S., 1921; Chief, Observation Bureau on return, same year; Sec., Finance Dept. & Chief, Savings Bank Section, Bank Bureau, 1923; Supt., Nagasaki Custom House, 1929; Chief, Kumamoto Tax Observation Bureau, 1931; present post since 1932. Address: 75, 2-chome Nakayamatedori, Kobe-ku, Kobe.

Lawyer; b. Jan., 1887 in Kumamoto-ken; s. of Satoru Kuboyama, farmer. Career: grad., Law Coll., Tokyo Imp. Univ.; served Aikoku Life Ins. Co., Toko Life Ins. Co.; started present business, 1914. Address: 1 Omotemachi Itchome, Akasakaku, Tokyo.
Privy Councillor, Manchoukuo; b. 1859 in Inner Mongolia. Career: Sub.-Gov. General, Hulunbuir, Mongolian Govt.; exerted in Foundation of Manchoukuo; present post since 1932. Address: Hailar.

Ph. D.; S. J.; Count; Prof., Sophia Univ. (Jochi Daigaku); b. Mar., 1886 in Hollabrunn, Austria; n. Austrian; s. of Leo Kuenburg, Councillor of Gov't. Career: studied Law at Vienna Univ., Theology at Innsbruck Univ., Philosophy at Munich and Freiburg Univs., 1904–21; apptd. Prof. of Philosophy, Innsbruck, 1922; came to Tokyo 1925. Address: c. o. Sophia Univ., 7 Kioicho, Kojimachiku, Tokyo.

Officier de la Legion d'Honneur (France); Officier de Leopold (Belgium); Sub. Mgr., Metal Dept., Mitsubishi Shoji Kaisha; b. Dec., 1886 in Chiba-ken; s. of Naosaburo. Career: grad., Tokyo Univ. of Com., 1912; joined Mitsubishi Shoji Kaisha; occupied posts at Nagasaki, Karatsu, Shanghai, Osaka, London Branches; Sub. Mgr., General Merchandise & Machinery Depts., Tokyo Head Office; Administrateur delagué, S. A. F. Mitsubishi, Paris; Jury Int'l Exhibition, Paris, 1925; Japanese Delegate to Int'l Chamber of Com. during 7 years' stay in Paris (1921–27); Hon. Vice-Pres., Franco-Asiatic Chamber of Com., Paris; Councillor, Franco-Japanese Society, Paris (1925–1927); Councillor, Franco-Japanese Society, Tokyo, since 1931. Address: 1288 Kichijoji, Tokyo-fu.

Seiyukai Leader; b. June, 1869 in Yamaguchi-ken; s. of Shozaburo Kuhara. Career: grad., Keio Univ., 1889; joined Morimura-Gumi, then Fujita-Gumi; established Kuhara Mining Co., 1905; founded Kuhara Trading Co. and Godo Fertilizer Co. and became their Pres.; sent to Russia, 1927; Communications Minister, 1927–29; elected to Diet 3 times. Address: 18 Shirogane-Imazatocho, Shibaku, Tokyo.

Igakuhakushi (M. D.); Dir., Maternity Hospital, Japan Red Cross Society; b. Dec., 1881 in Morioka; s. of Gen-ichiro Kuji, Principal, Konan Com. School. Career: grad., Medical Dept., Tokyo Imp. Univ., 1906; conferred degree, 1877; went to America for study, 1907; Head, Obstetrics and Gyncocology Dept., Iwate Hospital, 1903–1913; Medical Officer, Chosen Govt. Hospital, 1913; Prof., Keijo Medical Coll., 1916; sent to Europe for inspection, 1919–1921; Prof., Kanazawa Medical Coll., 1923; present post since Nov., 1927. Address: 11 Ebisudori Itchome, Shibuyaku, Tokyo.

M. P.; b. Sept., 1883 in Iwate-ken; s. of Heisuke Kumagae. Career: grad., Law Coll., Tokyo Imp. Univ., 1909; passed Higher Civil Service Exam.; Chief, Police Dept., Saga-ken; Chief, Public Peace Section, Metropolitan Police Board; sent to Diet 4 times from Iwate-ken; Director, Seiyukai. Address: Miyafurumachi, Iwate-ken. (Tokyo home) 35 Kurumamachi, Shibaku, Tokyo.

Spritual Conductor in Personal Fate; Founder of Chushindo (Shintoism); Author; Publisher, “Kosei” (magazine on new fatalism); b. May, 1881 in Gifu-ken; s. of late Kenjiro Kumazaki. Career: studied by himself; joined Editorial Staff, Nagoya Shimbun, Ise Shimbun, Osaka Shimpo; came to Tokyo, 1905; connected with Jiji Shimpo for 20 years, during which period published several books including “Japanese Stenography”, “Chinese Stenography”, etc.; writer for “Encyclopædia Japanese” on Imperialism and Nationalism; after resigning from same, 1927, founded Goseikaku and started publishing “Kosei” monthly; diligent student of new fatalism; author of “Mystery of Names”, “Mystery of Divination”, etc. Address: 671 Araijuku, Omori, Tokyo: 22 Sudacho, Kandaku, Tokyo.

Dir., General Staff Bureau, Defence Dept., Manchoukuo; b. in Liaoyang-hsien, Manchoukuo. Career: Chief, Defence Army, Kirin Prov. after Manchurian Incident; present post since 1932. Address: Hsinking.

Dir., Mitsukoshi Dept. Store, Ltd.; b. Mar., 1867 in Kanazawa, Ishikawa-ken; s. of Shingo Kurachi, merchant. Career: grad., Keio Univ., 1890; Mgr., Kyoto Branch, Meiji Fire Ins. Co.; same, Trade Dept., Murai Bros.; Mng. Dir., Kyodo Fire Ins. Co.; Mng. Dir., Present firm; then present post. Address: 1 Mita Tsunamachi, Shibaku, Tokyo.

Mem., House of Peers; Lord-in-Waiting, Kinkei Hall; Dir., Nippon Ironstone China Co., Kinka Spinning Co., Kongosan Elec. Ry. Co., Western Chosen Elec. Power Co., Pacific Marine & Fire Ins. Co. and Hokkaido Marine & Fire Ins. Co.; Auditor, Dai Nippon Ammonia Sulphate Co. and Hokkaido Colliery & Steamship Co.; b. Dec., 1870 in Kanazawa City; s. of Tsuranori Kurachi. Career: grad., Law Coll., Tokyo Imp. Univ., 1894; entered Home Office; and later, Foreign Office; apptd. Sec. of Legation and Residency-General; Councillor, Foreign Office; Dir., Political Affairs Bureau; Vice-Minister; Vice-Pres., Sino-Japanese Industrial Co. Address: 19 of 170 Harajuku, Shibuyaku, Tokyo.
Rear-Admiral; b. Aug., 1885; s. of Chojiro Kuragano, officer. Address: Official Residence, Kure Naval Station, Kure City.

Dir. Gen., Assn. for Promotion of Industrial Problems; b. Nov., 1887 in Shiga-ken; s. of Toshiro Kurahashi. Career: grad., Osaka Higher Technical School, 1909; studied in U. S., 1916–19; attended Int’l Econ. Conference, 1927, 11th Gen. Assembly of League of Nations, 1930 and 16th Int’l Labor Conf. 1932; Lecturer, Osaka Univ. of Tech. and Meiji Univ.; Dir. Gen., Koseikan; same, Nippon Power Assn.; Auditor, Yamatame Glass Works, Ltd., Osaka; same, Paosan Glass Works, Ltd., Shanghai. Address: 70 Shimo-Nibancho, Kojimachiku, Tokyo.

M. P.; b. Dec., 1879 in Fukuoka; s. of Seijiro Kuramoto, farmer. Career: grad., Special Course, Meiji Univ.; Sec., Fukui-ken and Shizuoka-ken; Sec. to Education Minister; elected to Diet from Shizuoka-ken 4 times; Mem., Hamamatsu City Assembly and Shizuoka City Planning Committee. Address: 33 Hiroocho, Azabuku, Tokyo.

Baron; Hogakuhakushi (D. L.); Councillor and Pres., Privy Council; Mem., House of Peers; b. July, 1853 in Fukuoka-ken; s. of late Taneatsu Kuratomi, Confucian scholar of Kurume clan. Career: grad., Law School in Justice Dept., 1879; Chief Public Procurator, Courts of Appeal at Osaka and Tokyo; Councillor and Vice-Minister of Residency-General in Chosen; Chief-Sec. to Imperial Household Minister. Address: 1 Tangomachi, Akasakaku, Tokyo.

M. P.; Pres., Chugai Shinron-sha; b. Mar., 1879 in Tochigi-ken; s. of Kizo Kurihara, landlord. Career: studied at Aoyama Gakuin, Waseda and Nippon Univs.; apptd. Mem., Akasaka Ward Assembly, Tokyo; Mem., Tokyo Municipal Assembly; elected to Diet 3 times. Address: 28 Hikawacho, Akasakaku, Tokyo.

Consul-Gen. at Hsinking, Manchukuo; b. Mar., 1890 in Ibaragi-ken; s. of Shuntaro Kurihara, samurai. Career: grad., Law Coll., Tokyo Imp. Univ., 1915; Elève-Consul at Mukden and Lyons; Diplomatic Probationer in Spain; attended Peace Conf., Paris; Consul at Foochow and Hsinking; Sec., Foreign Office; Chief, Corr. and Translation Sections, 1929; Con.-Gen. Hsinking, 1932; present post since Aug., 1933. Address: Japanese Consulate-General, Hsinking, Manchoukuo.

Pres., Kurimoto Iron Works; Rep. Dir., Japan Cast Iron Pipe Co.; Consulting Dir., Osaka Iron Industry Assn.; Mem., Osaka Chamber of Com. & Industry; b. 1875 in Wakayama; s. of Hanjiro Kurimoto, official. Career: grad., Law Coll., Tokyo Imp. Univ., 1898; attended Int’l Labor Conference as Japan’s Capital Delegate 1930. Address: Uyenomiyacho, Tennojiku, Osaka.
Dir., Judicial Affairs Bureau, Justice Dept., Manchoukuo. Career: grad. German Law Coll., Tokyo Imp. Univ.; present post since 1932. Address: Hsinking.

Dir., Treaty Bureau, Foreign Dept.; b. 1886 in Fukui-ken; s. of Shunichi Kuriyama. Career: grad., French Law Coll., Tokyo Imp. Univ., 1913; Diplomatic Probationer, Japanese Emb., France; 3rd Class Sec., same; 2nd. class Sec., same; Sec., Foreign Dept.; Chief, 1st Section, Treaty Bureau, Foreign Dept.; Chief, 3rd Section, Treaty Bureau, Foreign Dept.; 1st class Sec., Emb., France, 1927; Councillor, Emb., France; present post since 1933. Address: c/o Treaty Bureau, Foreign Dept.

b. May, 1885 in Matsumoto. Career: studied at Law Coll., Tokyo Imp. Univ.; toured China, 1913; Sec. to Justice Minister, 1914; apptd. Officer of Ceremonies for the Grand Coronation of H. M. the Emperor, 1915; went Europe and America to inspect political and economical conditions, 1922; elected to Diet, 1925. Address: 3 Daimachi, Akasakaku, Tokyo.

Vice-Minister, Finance Office; Mem., House of Peers; b. Sept., 1879 in Okayama-ken; s. of Kazumichi Kuroda. Career: grad., Law Coll., Tokyo Imp. Univ., 1905; entered Finance Office; Councillor of same; Sec. to Finance Minister; Dir., Bank Bureau; same, Revenue Bureau; Vice-Minister, Finance Office, 1927–1929; visited Europe and America for inspection; again apptd. present post, Dec., 1931. Address: 26 Komagome Oiwakecho, Hongoku, Tokyo.

Marquis; Privy Councillor; Mem., House of Peers; former feudal lord of Fukuoka Clan; b. May, 1867 in Fukuoka City; s. of Nagatomo Kuroda, lord of Fukuoka Clan. Career: grad., Cambridge Univ. (M. A.), 1884; ennobled same year; Master of Ceremonies, 1889; Mem., House of Peers; 1892; Vice-Pres. of same, 1895; Privy Councillor, 1924. Address: 1 Fukuyoshicho, Akasaka, Tokyo.
Admiral (retired); b. May, 1856 in Yonezawa City; s. of Shigekuni Kuroi, samurai of Yonezawa Clan. Career: grad., Naval Staff Coll. Address: 61 Shirokane Sarumachi, Shibaku, Tokyo.

Pres., Kurokawa Shoten, Ltd.; Dir., Ishizaki & Co. and Elec. Chemical Industry Co.; Auditor, Kimura Tokubei Shoten; Broker, Osaka Stock Exchange; b. Jan., 1893 in Tokyo adopted by Koshichi Kurokawa. Address: 8 Uyehonmachi-Hatchome, Tennojiku, Osaka.

Pres., Kokusai Kisen Kaisha; b. July, 1875 in Yamagata-ken; s. of Masachika Kanai, samurai; adopted by Yotaro Kurokawa. Career: grad., Aoyama Gakuin Coll., 1894; joined Nippon Yusen Kaisha, 1894; Asst. Mgr., Shanghai Branch, 1911; Mgr., Foreign Service Dept., Head Office, 1916; Mgr., Kobe Branch, 1920; promoted Dir. and Vice-Pres., 1923; resigned, 1924; Delegate on Shipping Affairs, Peace Conference, Paris, 1919; Pres., Kokusai Kisen Kaisha, 1927; elected Pres., Japan Shipowners' Assn., 1932; besides, holds many important offices in various Gov't. Commissions. Address: 14 Shoto, Shibuyaku, Tokyo.

Prop., Kurosawa Shoten; b. Jan., 1875 in Tokyo; s. of Keisuke Kurosawa. Career: inherited family estate, 1902; engaged in import business of typewriters; went to America to study typewriter business. Address: 2 Ginza-Rokuchome, Kyobashiku, Tokyo.

Mayor of Kobe; Auditor, Kobe Chamber of Com. & Industry; b. Jan., 1883 in Kumamoto-ken; s. of Matao Kurose. Career: grad., Law Coll., Tokyo Imp. Univ., 1909; apptd. Chief, Police Stations of Takanawa and Nihonbashi; Chief, Police Dept., Okayama-ken; Chief, Home Affairs Dept., Yamaguchi-ken and Hyogo-ken; Gov., Yamanashi-ken. Address: 1 of 149 Yamamotodori-Sanchome, Kobe.

Rank: Jr. 4th; 3rd Imperial Order of Sacred Treasure; Dir., Com. Bureau; b. Mar., 1886 in Kanagawa-ken; s. of Sobei Kurusu; m. Alice, American. Career: grad., Consular Course, Tokyo Higher Com. School; Consul at Chicago; Consul-General at Manila; 1st Sec., Legations in Chile and Greece; 1st Sec., Embassy in Italy; Consul-General at Hamburg; Envoy Extraordinary and Minister Plenipotentiary in Peru; present post since 1932. Address: 25, 2-chome Nagata-cho, Kojimachi-ku, Tokyo.

Composer; b. Feb., 1893 in Nagano-ken; s. of Kazunari Kusakawa, banker. Career: grad., Tokyo Academy of Music, 1917; apptd. Teacher of same; same, Tokyo-fu 3rd Girls' High School; Lecturer, Seikei Higher School. Address: 558 Amanuma, Suginamiku, Tokyo.

Mem., Special Industry Deliberation Committee and Tokyo Chamber of Com. & Industry; Pres., Tokyo Bankers' Club; Pres., Mitsubishi Bank; Dir., Tokyo Marine & Fire Ins. Co.; Meiji Life Ins. Co.; Mitsubishi Fire & Marine Ins. Co.; Mitsubishi Trust Co.; Auditor, Mitsubishi Shipbuilding & Engrg. Co., Mitsubishi Mining Co., Mitsubishi Iron Works, Mitsubishi Trading Co.; b. Feb., 1867 in Tokyo; s. of Magosaburo Kushida. Career: studied at Daigaku Yobimon & grad., Pennsylvania Univ., 1890; joined Mitsubishi Bank, 1894. Address: 17 Nagatacho Itchome, Kojimachiku, Tokyo.

Igakuhakushi (M. D.); Prof. and Chief, Medical Dept., Osaka Imp. Univ.; b. Jan., 1871 in Nagasaki-ken; s. of Kunitaro Kusumoto, physician. Career: grad., Medical Coll., Tokyo Imp. Univ.; apptd. Teacher, Osaka Higher Medical School, 1905; sent to Germany for study, 1906; Prof., Osaka Medical Coll., 1919; Dean of same, 1924; present post since 1931. Address: 20 Dojima-Kami-Sanchome, Kitaku, Osaka.

Rigakuhakushi (D. Sc.); Prof., Kyushu Imp. Univ.; b. Sept., 1878 in Tokyo; s. of Aishin Kuwaki, Official. Career: grad., 1st Higher School; Physical Course, Science Coll., Tokyo Imp. Univ., 1899; apptd. Asst. and later Lecturer of same; studied Physics at Berlin Univ., 1906–09; returning home, apptd. Prof., Meiji Technolog. Coll.; present post since 1911; Member of National Research Council, Education Dept. Address: 10 Jigyo-Nishimachi, Fukuoka.

Bungakuhakushi (D. Litt.); Prof., Tokyo Imp. Univ.; b. June, 1874 in Tokyo; s. of Aishin Kuwaki, official. Career: grad., Philosophy Course, Litt. Coll., Tokyo Imp. Univ., 1896; P.-G. Course of same; apptd. Prof., 1st Higher School, 1899; Lecturer, then Asst. Prof., Tokyo Imp. Univ.; Prof., Literary Dept., Kyoto Imp. Univ., 1906; sent to Europe and America for study, 1908–10; Prof., Tokyo Imp. Univ., 1914; Mem., Imp. Academy, 1923; toured abroad, 1926 and 1930; Lecturer, Waseda Univ., Nippon Women's Univ. Address: 34 Kitamachi, Ushigomeku, Tokyo.

Pres., Matsuo Screw Mfg. Works, Nippon Kokusan Shokai G. K.; Dir., Healing Co., Ltd.; b. May, 1888 in Niigata-ken; s. of Tadasu Kuwamoto, official. Career: completing middle school course, entered Healing Co. and promoted present post; Auditor, Anritsu Elec. Co.; Nichi-Bei Star Automobile Co.; Pres., Kanto Students' Soft Ball Tennis Assn.; Vice-Pres., Marunouchi Athletic Assn. Address: 12 Fujimicho-Rokuchome, Kojimachiku, Tokyo.

Rank: Sr. 5th; 4th O. M.; Dir., Asia Bureau, Foreign Office; b. Mar., 1884 in Kagawa-ken; s. of Yasuzo Kuwashima; m. Yaeko, d. of Tasaburo Aiura, of Tokyo. Career: grad., Polit. Dept., Waseda Univ., 1906; Sec., Foreign Office and Tokyo Reconstruction Bureau; 1st Sec., Embassy; attached to Consulates at Mukden, Hankow, Bombay, Chicago and Embassy at Washington; Councillor, Embassy; Consul-General at Honolulu; Consul-Gen., Tientsin, 1930; present post since July 1933. Recreations: reading, golf. Address: 11 Miyajimagai, Japanese Settlement, Tientsin. (Tokyo home) 11 Jochi, Shibuyaku, Tokyo.

Hogakuhakushi (D. L.); Councillor, Social Bureau; Prof., Chuo Univ.; Dir., Japan Red Cross Society and Saiseikai; b. Nov., 1868 in Tottori-ken; s. of Tojuro Kuwata. Career: grad., Law Coll., Tokyo Imp. Univ., 1893; founded Inst. of Social Policy, 1896; studied in Europe 2 years; received degree, 1904; elected Mem., House of Peers, same year; attended World Red Cross Society Conf., 1921. Address: 19 Komagome-Hayashicho, Hongoku, Tokyo.
Manchoukuo Consul, Blagovestchensk. Career: Vice-Consul, Vladivostok, 1917; present post since 1932. Address: Blagovestchensk.

B. A.; Chinese Consul-General at Yokohama; b. Mar., 1893 in Tientsin; n. Chinese; s. of Y. F. Kuo. Career: Sec., Ministry of Foreign Affairs, 1929–31; then present post. Address: 152 Yamashitacho, Yokohama.

Diplomatist; Chargé d'Affaires of Peru in Japan and China; b. Oct., 1892 in Lima, Peru; n. Peruvian. Career: studied in England and Peru; was in diplomatic service of Peru in United States, Ecuador, Columbia, Bolivia and Japan, and also in Foreign Office in Lima. Address: Peruvian Legation, 13 Shinsakamachi, Akasakaku, Tokyo.
Manchoukuo Consul, Chita. Career: present post since 1932. Address: Chita.

Chief Sec., Kirin Prov. Office; b. 1878 in Heishan-hsien, Mukden Prov. Career: Sec., Mil. Gov.'s Office, Heilungkiang Prov.; Dir., Forestry Bureau and Chief, Gold Mining Bureau, Kirin; Dir., Administrative Bureau, Kirin-Hailung Ry. 1926; resigned post, 1931; present post since 1932. Address: Kirin.
Pres., Supreme Procurator's Office. Career: present post since establishment of Manchoukuo. Address: Hsinking.

Dir., Heilungkiang High Court; b. 1882 in Lishu-hsien, Mukden Prov. Career: grad., Mukden Law Coll.; Chief, Heilungkiang High Court, 1926; resigned, 1928; exerted in establishment of Manchoukuo, 1931; present post since 1932. Address: Tsitsihar.
Chief, Kirin High Procurator's Office; b. 1887 in Mukden Prov. Career: Chief, Kirin District Court; present post since 1932. Address: Kirin.

Pres., Supreme Court, Manchoukuo; b. 1884 in Minhou-hsin, Fukien. Career: grad., Waseda Univ., Japan; Dir., Bureau of Special Sch. Affairs, Education Dept., China, 1912; Pres., High Court, Peiping; present post since 1932. Address: Hsinking.

B. A.; G. C. M. G.; C. B.; C. B. E.; Privy Councillor; British Ambassador to Tokyo; b. June, 1872 in London; n. English; s. of Nathaniel Lindley, Life Peer. Career: grad., Winchester and Magdalen Coll., Oxford; Counsellor, Embassy at Petrograd, 1915; High Commr., Vienna, 1919–20; Minister to Austria, 1920; at Athens, 1922–23; Oslo, 1923–29; Ambassador to Portugal, 1929. Address: British Embassy, Tokyo.

Gov., Northern Sub-Province, Hsingan; b. in Solon. Career: Adviser, Public Peace Headquarters, Three Eastern Provinces; Adviser, Military Commander to Mongolia; present post since 1932. Address: Hulunbuir.

Dir., Kirin Central Bank, Manchoukuo; b. 1890 in Shulan-hsien, Kirin Prov. Career: grad., Hosei Univ., Tokyo; Sec., Kirin Prov. Office; Pres., Kirin Prov. Bank, 1932; present post since. Address: Kirin.

Chief Sec., Legislative Council, Manchoukuo; b. in Liaoyang-hsien, Mukden Prov. Career: grad., Mukden Law Coll.; studied law in Japan; Chief, Hsingho-tao, Tsitsihar Special District, 1921; took part in Foundation Movement of Manchoukuo, 1931; present post since 1932. Address: Hsinking.
Dir., Heilungkiang Central Bank, Manchoukuo; b. 1889 in Hopei Prov. Career: Chief, Industrial Dept., Heilungkiang Prov. Bank, 1930; Pres. Heilungkiang Prov. Bank, 1932. Address: Tsitsihar.
Privy Councillor, and Pres. Supervisory Council, Manchoukuo; b. 1865 in Chekiang Prov. Career: exerted in Foundation Movement of Manchoukuo, 1931; present post since 1932. Address: Hsinking.

Chief, Heilungkiang High Court; b. 1891 in Pin-hsien, Kirin. Career: studied law in Chaoyang Univ., Peiping; grad. Peiping Law Educational Institute; Chief Procurator, Heilungkiang High Court; present post since 1932. Address: Tsitsihar.

Mayor of Harbin; Dir., Municipal System Administrative Bureau, Tungsheng Special District; b. 1890 in Fushun, Mukden Prov. Career: grad., Kiangsu Law Coll.; Vice-Pres., Mukden Assembly; sent to Washington Conf. as Rep., Three Eastern Provinces, 1922; went to Russia, 1923; Chairman, Soviet-Chinese Conf. & Mukden-Soviet Conf.; Pres., Chinese Eastern Ry., 1924; Gov., Chinese Eastern Ry., 1927; resigned post during Soviet-Chinese Conflict, 1929; present post since 1932. Address: Harbin.
Dir., Com. Affairs, Foreign Dept., Manchoukuo. Career: Editor, Taitung Daily, Dairen; present post since 1932. Address: Hsinking.

M. P.; Adviser, Minseito; b. Mar., 1863; s. of Nagahide Machida, samurai of Akita Clan. Career: grad., Daigaku Yobimon (present Tokyo Imp. Univ.;) published magazine “Toyo Keizai Zasshi”; went to Europe; joined Bank of Japan; then Yamaguchi Bank; became Dir. of same; sent to Diet 7 times from Akita-ken; Councillor, Agrl. & Com. Dept.; Agr. & Forestry Minister.; then Councillor, Minseito; Pres., Hochi Shimbun. Address: 73 Minami-Enokicho, Ushigomeku, Tokyo.

Hon. Consul for Greece at Kobe; Merchant; b. Nov., 1885 in Glasgow, Scotland; n. British; s. of late James John MacNaughton, civil engr. Career: grad., Kelvinside Academy, Glasgow, Scotland; arrived in Japan, 1909; Asst., Findlay Richardson & Co., Yokohama and Kobe; served in World War, 1917–19; returned to Japan, 1919; Mgr., above Co., Kobe; apptd. Hon. Vice-Consul for Greece. 1921; promoted Consul, 1921; commenced business on his own account, 1924. Address: 26 B, Naniwa-machi, Kobe.
Rear-admiral; Chief, Naval Ordinance, Yokosuka Naval Arsenal; b. June, 1882 in Yamaguchi-ken; s. of Masanori Maebara. Address: Chofu-Unokimachi, Omoriku, Tokyo.

(M. D.) Dir., Branch Hospital, Japan Red Cross Society in Osaka; b. 1877 in Fukui-ken; s. of Shokaku Maeda, samurai. Career: grad., Medical Coll., Kyoto Imp. Univ. 1904; served, Red Cross Society Hospital same year; took degree of Igaku Hakushi (M. D.) 1910; present post since 1930. Recreation: reading, gardening. Address: 29 Nishinomachi, 1-chome, Higashiku, Osaka.

Business Mgr., Manchuria Telephone & Telegraph Co.; b. 1883 in Mie-ken. Career: grad., Law Coll., Tokyo Imp. Univ., 1909; Chief, Telephone Section, Communication Bureau; Dir., Sendai Communication Bureau, 1927; Dir., Tokyo Communication Bureau; present post since Aug., 1933. Address: Hsinking.

Editorial Writer, Tokyo Asahi Shimbun; Dir., Pacific Problems Research Committee; Dir., Tokyo City Administration Research Committee; b. in Tokyo. Career: grad., Law Coll. (German), Tokyo Imp. Univ., 1909; Private Sec. to Home Ministers; Deputy Mayor of Tokyo, 1921–23; Govt. Delegate to Int'l Labor Conference, Geneva, 1923–26. Address: 18 Hikawamachi, Nakanoku, Tokyo.

Marquis; Comdr., Infantry 2nd Brigade; Mem., House of Peers; Dir., Tokyo Jikeikai; b. June, 1885; s. of Toshiaki Maeda and later adopted by Toshitsugu Maeda. Career: grad., Military Academy; Staff Coll.; Instructor, Military Coll.; studied in Germany; served British Army in World War; later went to England again as Mil. Attaché to Embassy; Comdr., Infantry, 2nd Regiment, Imperial Guard Div., 1930. Present post since Aug., 1933. Address: 861 Komaba, Kamimeguro, Meguroku, Tokyo.

Proprietor of Watch, Jewelry, & Spectacles Store; b. Apr., 1890 in Nagasaki, s. of Tsurumatsu Maeda. Career: served Army Administrative office at Eiko as employee during Russo-Japanese War, 1904; grad., Chinese Language Sch. 1908, and Russian Language Sch. 1910; entered barrack for a year 1910; engaged in com. business at Vladivostok 1912–1918; opened watch shop at Harbin, Jun., 1917, same business since then; mem., Harbin Chamber of Com. & Ind. since 1932. Address: 47, Mostowaya St., Harbin.

M. P.; Adviser, Seiyukai; Lawyer; b. Feb., 1882 in Wakayama-ken; brother of Shoichi Maeda. Career: grad., Tokyo Hogakuin; French Dept., Tokyo School of Foreign Languages; German Dept., Doitsu Kyokai Gakko; upon graduation, practiced law; sent to Diet 5 times since 1917; Dir.-Gen., Seiyukai; Dir., Chuo Shimbun, East-India Industrial Co., Hayakawa Elec. Power Co., Keijo Elec. Ry. Co. and Minato Ry. Co.; Auditor, Tokyo Elec. Power Co., Azumagawa Elec. Power Co.; apptd. Pres., Legislation Bureau in Tanaka Cabinet, 1927; Com. & Industry Minister in Inukai Cabinet, 1931–32. Address: 28 Mikawa-Daimachi, Azabuku, Tokyo.

M. P.; Lawyer; Parl. Vice-Minister of Communications; b. May, 1885 in Gifu-ken; s. of Ihei Makino. Career: grad., Law Coll., Tokyo Imp. Univ., 1911; Sec., Communications Supt. Bureau; Sec. to Education Minister; later opened law office; sent to Diet 5 times; Councillor, Com. & Industry Dept.; present post since 1932. Address: 12 Fukuromachi, Surugadai, Kandaku, Tokyo.

Count; Lord Keeper of Privy Seal; Pres., Toadobunkai, Nippon Giin; b. Oct., 1861; s. of Toshimitsu Okubo, and later adopted by Kichinojo Makino. Career: Sec. to Premier; Gov., Fukui-ken and Miyagi-ken; Vice-Minister of Education; Minister to Austria, then Italy; Education Minister; Privy Councillor; Agrl. & Com. Minister of Foreign Affairs; Peace Delegate at Paris; Minister of Imperial Household; Mem., House of Peers. Address: 5 Mitadaimachi Itchome, Shibaku, Tokyo.

Viscount; Mem., House of Peers; Pres., Dai Nippon Sanshi-Kai (Sericultural Society); Auditor, Nippon Oil Co.; b. Oct., 1870; s. of Tadayasu Makino, Lord of Nagaoka Clan. Career: grad., Keio Univ., 1893; elected to Diet 5 times since 1897; Pres., Kenkyukai; first Mayor of Nagaoka. Address: Nishi-Okubo-Itchome, Yodobashiku, Tokyo.

Keizaigakuhakushi (Dr. of Econ.); Adviser, Tokyo Asahi Shimbun-Sha; b. Jan., 1879 in Kumamoto-ken; s. of Teizo Makino, village headman. Career: grad., Waseda Univ.; apptd. Teacher, Kumamoto Com. School; Official, Dept. of Agrl. & Com.; entered Asahi Shimbun-Sha, 1911, and served as Corr.; Chief, Polit. Econ. and Editorial Depts.; received degree (Tokyo Imp. Univ.), 1928; present post since 1930; done many publications on econ. topics. Address: 562 Sendagayamachi, Shibuyaku, Tokyo.

Dir., La Fédération Equestre Impérial du Japon, Int'l Equestrian Assn., Tokyo Riding Club; b. Mar., 1887 in Tokyo; s. of Kiyonari Makita, draper. Career: studied English Litt. at Waseda Univ.; became Pres., Makita Orimono (Textile) Goshi Kaisha; Com. Councillor, Toyokuni Bank; in cooperation with Count Matsudaira, founded La Fédération Equestre Imperial du Japon and Int'l Equestirian Assn., etc. Address: 10, Horiecho-Sanchome, Nihonbashiku, Tokyo.

M. P.; Pres., Chosen Shimbun; Mng. Dir., Kongosan Elec. Ry. Co.; Pres., To-a Telegraphic News Agency; Councillor, Chosen Ry. & Bus Co.; b. May, 1882 in Nagasaki-ken; 3rd s. of late Ishichi Makiyama. Career: grad., Polit. Econ. Dept., Waseda Univ., 1906; sent to Diet 6 times from Nagasaki-ken; leader of Minseito Party; apptd. Parl. Vice-Minister of Navy in Wakatsuki Cabinet; mine operator in Chosen. Address: 9 Onden, Shibuyaku, Tokyo.

P. C. (Can.); LL. D.; B. C. L.; Canadian Minister to Japan; b. Mar., 1876 in Montreal, Que.; n. Canadian; s. of W. de M. Marler, prof. and rotary. Career: grad., McGill Univ.; apptd. Mem., Educational Council, Quebec Province; Fuel Administrator of same, 1917–18; sent to Diet from St. Lawrence, St. George, 1921; Chairman, Parliamentary Committee on Soldiers' Pensions and Civil Re-establishment, 1922; Chairman, Transportation Committee negotiating trade agreement between Canada and British West Indies, 1925; took active part in last revision of Bank Act, also in Dominion and Ry. finance and tariff questions; entered Rt. Hon. W. L. Makenzie Kin's Cabinet, 1925; National Treasurer and Chairman, National Finance Committee for Celebration of Diamond Jubilee of Confederation, 1927; present post since 1929. Address: Canadian Legation, Marunouchi, Tokyo.

M. P.; Mem., Sapporo Municipal Assembly; b. Mar., 1871 in Nagano-ken; s. of Jitsuta Maruyama, farmer. Career: grad., Meiji Coll.; apptd. Mem., Vice-Pres. then Pres., Hokkaido Assembly; Pres., Iwauchi Shimpo; sent to Diet 3 times. Address: Sapporo, Hokkaido.

Mem., House of Peers; b. Sept., 1883 in Hiroshima-ken; brother of Mokichi Maruyama. Career: grad., Law Coll., Tokyo Imp. Univ., 1909; entered Metropolitan Police Board and apptd. successively Police Supt., Inspector and Dir. of Public Peace Dept.; sent to Europe and America to study police affairs, 1917; entered Home Office and apptd. Dir., Police Affairs Bureau, Chosen Govt.; Deputy-Mayor of Tokyo, 1926; Metropolitan Police Chief, 1929–31; nominated Mem., House of Peers, 1931. Address: 96 Owadacho, Shibuyaku, Tokyo.
Lieut.-Col.; French Mil. Attache; b. Jan., 1889 in Paris. Address: c/o French Embassy; (Office) 12 Shin-Ryudo-machi, Azabu; (Home) 503, 8-chome, Kami-Meguro, Meguroku.

Pres., Daido Elec. Power Co., Showa Electric Power Co., Tateyama Hydro-Elec. Power Co.; Councillor, Osaka Elec. Power Co.; Dir., Tenryugawa Elec. Power Co., Sanshin Ry. Co., Daido Fertilizer Co., Kamioka Hydro-Elec. Power Co.; Auditor, Hokoku Cement Co., Shikoku Hydro-Elec. Power Co.; b. Feb., 1869; s. of late Giemon Masuda, Shizuoka-ken. Career: Sec. to Count Shimpei Goto; once elected to Diet. Address: 48 Kamichi, Shibuyaku, Tokyo.
Dir., Masuda Copper Works; b. Sept., 1885 in Osaka; s. of Nobuyuki Masuda. Career: grad., Osaka Com. School; engaged in banking and mining. Address: 1 Tamaecho Itchome, Kitaku, Osaka.

Pres., Masuda Agrl. Co.; Adviser, Mitsui Gomei Kaisha; b. Nov., 1847; s. of Takayoshi Masuda, samurai. Career: apptd. Kiheinokami (Cavalry Inspector) and Zohei-Gonnokami (Ordnance Inspector) of Shogunate; Vice-Pres., Senshu Kaisha; participated in establishment of Mitsui Bussan Kaisha and apptd. its Pres.; Mng.-Dir., Mitsui Gomei Kaisha; elevated to peerage because of his contribution to commerce. Address: Kitashinagawa-Itchome, Shinagawaku, Tokyo.

Baron; Mng. Dir., Taiwan Sugar Mfg. Co.; b. Sept., 1875 in Tokyo-fu; s. of Baron Takashi Masuda. Career: grad., Com. Inst. of Antwerp, Belgium; Dir., Imp. Theater, Morinaga Confectionery Co., Chiyoda Fire Ins. Co., Nippon Brick Co., Masuda Noji Co. Address: 2 Hirakawacho-Gochome, Kojimachiku, Tokyo.

Dir., Chosen Grain Warehouse Co.; Auditor, Kanjo Bank; Vice-Pres., Bank of Chosen; b. Mar., 1884; s. of Tokunori Matsubara, Okayama-ken. Career: grad., Kobe Higher Com. School; joined Bank of Chosen; Business Mgr., Head Office; Mgr., Dairen Branch. Address: Minamidaimon Sanchome, Keijo.

Hogakuhakushi (D. L.); Lecturer, Tohoku Imp. Univ.; Tokyo Imp. Univ.; Chuo Univ.; Senshu Univ.; b. Oct., 1877 in Fukui-ken; s. of Kazushiro Matsubara. Career: grad., Law Coll., Tokyo Imp. Univ., 1902; Consul at Chicago and Hsinking; Sec., Foreign Office, 1912; 2nd Sec., Legation; 1st Sec., same; Head, Translation Section, Foreign Office; Councillor of Embassy and attached to Embassy in Germany. Address: 46 Kagomachi, Koishikawaku, Tokyo.

Rigakuhakushi (D. Sc.); Honorary Prof., Tokyo Imp. Univ.; Mem. and Chairman, Chemistry Division, National Research Council; b. May, 1872 in Nagoya; s. of Yasoichi Matsubara, samurai of Owari Clan. Career: grad., Tokyo Imp. Univ., 1896; studied at Univs. of Manchester and Berlin, 1903–1906; apptd. Asst. Prof., 1899; Prof., 1909; Dean, 1929; Honor. Prof., 1933; Faculty of Sc., Tokyo Imp. Univ.; representing Imperial Gov't., attended 2nd Int'l Convention of Int'l Catalogue Sc. Litt., London, 1905, and 6th Int'l Congress of Applied Chemistry, Rome, 1906; as delegate, National Research Council of Japan, sent to Extraordinary General Assembly of Itn'l Research Council, Brussels, 1926, and to 7th General Assembly of Int'l Union of Pure and Applied Chemistry, Washington, 1926; is serving on several committees of Ministry of Education, etc. Address: 10 Akebonocho, Komagome, Hongoku, Tokyo.
Customs Supt., Yingkow. Career: present post since 1932. Address: Yingkow.

M. P.; Adviser, Minseito Party; b. Oct., 1875 in Oita-ken; s. of Ginbei Matsuda. Career: grad., Nihon Univ.; apptd. Judicial Probationer; opened law office, 1898; sent to Diet 9 times since 1907; Vice-Speaker, House of Rep.; Dir.-Gen., Seiyu-Honto Party; made inspection tour through America; nominated Councillor, Home Office.; Overseas Minister in Hamaguchi Cabinet up to Apr., 1931. Address: 4 Onden, Shibuyaku, Tokyo.

Baron; Dir., Monopoly Bureau, Chosen; b. Nov., 1892 in Saga-ken; s. of Baron Masahisa Matsuda, Ex-Minister of Finance, Education and Justice. Career: grad., Law Coll., Kyoto Imp. Univ., 1918; passed Higher Civil Service Exam. and apptd. Judge, Marine Court of Inquiry; Sec., Colonization Bureau of Cabinet, 1924; Sec., Taiwan Gov't, 1931; sent to Europe, America and Africa, 1930; Gov., South Sea Govt., 1932; present post since 1933. Address: c/o Monopoly Bureau, Keijo, Chosen.

Hogakuhakushi (D. L.); Ambassador to Italy; b. Mar., 1876 in Tokyo; s. of Michio Matsuda, samurai, Tokyo. Career: grad., Law Coll., Tokyo Imp. Univ., 1900; 3rd Sec., Embassy in Italy, 1917; Embassy in France, 1921; Sec., Foreign Office; Chief, Treaty Bureau; attended Gen. Assembly, League of Nations, Geneva, 1921., present post since 1933. Address: Japanese Embassy, Rome, Italy.

LL. D., Lafayette Coll., Rutgers Coll. and Univ. of Missouri (U. S.); Ambassador to England; b. Apr., 1877 in Tokyo; s. of late Katamori Matsudaira, Lord of Aizu Clan. Career: grad., Law Coll., Tokyo Imp. Univ., 1902; attaché, Embassy, London, 1902; 3rd Sec., then 2nd Sec.; Staff, Treaty Revision, 1911; 2nd Sec., Legation, Peking, 1912–14; Consul-Gen., Tientsin, 1914; Chief, Diplomatic Mission in Siberia, 1918; Mem., Inter-Allied Ry. Comm., Siberia, 1919; Chief, Europe & America Dept., Foreign Office, 1920; Sec.-Gen., Japanese Delegation, Disarmament Conference, Washington, D. C., 1921; Vice-Minister for Foreign Affairs, 1923; Ambassador to U. S., 1925–28; present post since 1929; Delegate to Gen. Assembly, League of Nations, 1929 and 1930; same to London Naval Conf., 1930; same to Gen. Disarm. Conf., Geneva, 1932. Address: 10 Grosvenor Square, London.

Count; Vice-Pres., House of Peers; Pres., Teikoku Horse Improvement Assn.; Vice-Pres., Teikoku Horse-Race Society; Auditor, Bank of Japan; Dir., Daito Bunka Kyokai; b. Dec., 1875 in Tokyo; 8th s. of Count Yorifusa Matsudaira. Career: grad., Peers' School, and Law Dept., Waseda Univ., 1897. Address: 15 Komagome-Shichome, Toshimaku, Tokyo.

Lieut.-Gen.; Comdr.-in-Chief, Taiwan Army; b. 1878 in Aichi-ken; s. of Takekuni Matsui. Career: grad., Mil. Academy, 1892; Staff, Kwantung Army Hdqrs.; Chief, 2nd Section; Staff, Gen. Office; Comdr., 11th Div., 1929; present post since Aug. 1933. Address: Taihoku, Taiwan.

Baron; Mem., House of Peers; Dir., Maison Franco-Japonaise; b. Mar., 1868; s. of Yasuzo Matsui, Osaka. Career: grad., Law Coll., Tokyo Imp. Univ., 1890; 3rd Sec., Legation; 2nd Sec., same; 1st Sec., same; Councillor, Foreign Office; Vice-Minister of Foreign Office; Foreign Minister, 1924; Ambassador to Britain; Delegate, Paris Peace Conference, 1916. Address: 52 Shimorokubancho, Kojimachiku, Tokyo.

Pres., Kyoto Imp. Univ.; b. 1873 in Fukuoka-ken; s. of Tsukuda Matsui. Career: grad., Sc. Coll., Tokyo Imp. Univ., 1898; studied chemistry at Giessen Univ., Germany & Liverpool Univ., England; Prof., Kyoto Imp. Univ.; present post since Sept., 1933. Address: 450 Bishamoncho, Kyoto.

Hogakuhakushi (D. L.); Lord-in-Waiting, Kinkei Hall; Vice-Pres., Police Assn. and Fire-Prevention Assn.; Dir., Japan Red Cros Society, Meiji Univ., Civil Education Society, Polit. Educ. Soc. and Central Social Welfare Assn.; b. Sept., 1866 in Hiroshima-shi; s. of Yurin Matsui, samurai. Career: grad., Law Coll., Tokyo Imp. Univ., 1893; apptd. Police Supt.; Chief, Yotsuya Police-Station; Chief, 1st, 2nd Dept. and Fire Dept., Metropolitan Police Board; Procurator, Chosen Gov't; Gov., Shizuoka-ken and Aichi-ken; sent to Europe and America for inspection of police and fire protection; received degree, 1910. Address: 3141 Oi-Kashimacho, Shinagawaku, Tokyo.

Rep. Mgr., Matsu Shokai; b. Dec., 1865; s. of late Prince Masayoshi Matsukata. Career: grad., Tokyo Imp. Univ.; studied at Oxford, Yale and Paris Univ.; Sec. to Prime Minister; elected to Diet; Pres., Kawasaki Dockyard Co.; Special Mem., Kobe Chamber of Com. & Industry; visited USSR on business, 1932. Address: 20 Yamamoto-dori Shichome, Kobe.

Rank: Sr. 4th 2nd O. M.; Lieut.-Gen.; Attached to General Staff Office; b. Nov., 1876 in Yamaguchi-ken; s. of Ichiro Matsuki; m. Tsuta. Career: grad., Military Academy, 1898; grad., Military Staff Coll.; Battalion Comdr., Infantry 13 Regiment; Instructor, Infantry School; Staff, Military Affairs Bureau; Instructor, Military Staff Coll.; Adjutant, War Office; Comdr., Taiwan 1st Guards; Head, Mobilization Preparations Bureau; Lieut.-Gen., 1927; Comdr., 14th Division; present post since Aug., 1933. Address: Nishiharamachi, Utsunomiya. Tel.: Utsunomiya 845.

Councillor, Legislation Bureau, Manchukuo; b. Mar., 1898 in Yamaguchi-ken; s. of Kiyonao Matsuki, official. Career: grad., Law Coll., Tokyo Imp. Univ., 1922; entered South Manchuria Ry. Co., same year; apptd. Legal Adviser to Kwantung Army, 1931; Dir., Legislation Bureau, Manchoukuo, 1932; Present post since 1933. Address: Hagoromocho-Nichome, Hsinking, Manchoukuo.

Hogakuhakushi (D. L.); Mem., House of Peers; Mem., Legislative Investigation Committee and Imp. Academy; Prof., Chuo Univ.; Auditor, Kawasaki Trust Co. and Yamakanae Shokai; Lawyer; b. Oct., 1877 in Tokyo; s. of Soichiro Matsumoto, samurai. Career: grad., Law Coll., Tokyo Imp. Univ., 1900; Councillor, Agrl. & Com. Dept.; Asst. Prof., Tokyo Imp. Univ.; went to Europe to study com. code; received degree, 1910; apptd. Councillor, Agrl. & Com. Dept. and Legislation Bureau; Vice-Pres., South Manchuria Ry. Co.; Pres., Legislation Bureau; Pres., Kansai Univ.; opened law office. Address: 1 of 2 Marunouchi-Itchome, Kojimachiku, Tokyo.

Pres., Tomemoe Ry. Co., Kurosaki Pottery Industry Co., Wakamatsu Harbor Co., Japan Coal Mining Ass'n.; Mng.-Dir., Kyushu Steel Works; Dir., Mitsui Trust Co.; Auditor, Yasukawa Elec. Works; Showa Coal Co.; Acting Partner, Meiji Spinning Co.; b. Oct., 1870 in Fukuoka; s. of late Baron Keiichiro Yasukawa, and later adopted by Sen Matsumoto, of Fukuoka Clan; m. Hideko, d. of late Viscount Yoshika Inoue. Career: succeeded family estate, 1923; is one of most influencial business men in north Kyushu. Recreations: golf, Utai. Address: Tobata City, Fukuoka-ken. Clubs: Japan Industrial Club, Kojunsha.

Mng.-Dir., Oji Seishi Co. Ltd.; Dir., Kabafuto Ry. Co.; b. Aug. 1882 in Osaka-fu; s. of Toyojiro Matsumoto. Career: grad., Law Coll., Tokyo Imp. Univ., 1908; entered Finance Office; joined Industrial Bank of Japan, 1915; apptd. Dir. of same bank, 1920–30; was in America and China for 4 years; present post since 1930. Address: 27 Kitatani, Shibuyaku, Tokyo.

Dir., Police Affairs Bureau, Home Dept.; b. 1886 in Okayama-ken; s. of Yoshio Kawakita. Career: grad., Law Coll., Tokyo Imp. Univ., 1911; Councillor, Kagoshima-ken; Sec., Home Dept., Kagoshima-ken; Gov., Fukuoka-ken; present post since 1932. Address: 8 Marunouchi 1-chome, Kojimachiku, Tokyo.

Mem., House of Peers; Pres., Nitto Flour Mill Co.; b. May, 1878 in Saitama-ken; s. of Heizo Matsumoto, business man. Career: grad., Tokyo Higher Com. School, 1900; Dir. of several banks and cos.; Permanent Mem., Tokyo Chamber of Com. & Indutsry; elected Mem., House of Peers, Sept., 1932. Address: 87 Kohinata-Suidocho, Koishikawaku, Tokyo.

Pres., Fujikura Elec. Wire Mfg. Co. and Fujikura Kogyo K. K.; Dir., Relief Printing Co.; b. Nov., 1868 in Tochigi-ken; 5th s. of Kumakichi Fujikura, landlord. Career: went to America to inspect elec. wire mfg. industry; established Fujikura Elec. Wire Mfg. Co. with his brother; Vice-Pres., Nippon Elec. Assn.; Head, Kanto Branch of same. Address: 47 Temmacho-Itchome, Yotsuyaku, Tokyo.

Mem., House of Peers; b. Sept., 1883 in Yamaguchi-ken; s. of Reizo Matsumura, farmer. Career: grad., Law Coll., Tokyo Imp. Univ., 1909; passed Higher Civil Service Exam.; Commr., Kanagawa-ken, Saga-ken, Tottori-ken; Governor, Oita-ken, 1923; Dir., Police Bureau, Home Office, 1924; nominated Mem., House of Peers, 1926; Vice-Minister, Dept. of Com. & Industry, 1931; resigned at end of same year; being Minseito and Koseikai member. Address: 448 Nishi-Okubo, Yodobashiku, Tokyo.

M. P.; Parl. Councillor, Agr. & Forestry Dept.; b. Jan., 1883 in Toyama-ken; s. of Kazuichiro Matsumura. Career: grad., Polit. Econ. Dept., Waseda Univ., 1906; Corr., Hochi Shimbun; sent to Diet from Toyama-ken 3 times since 1928; Sec. to Agr. & Forestry Ministry; apptd. present post, 1932. Address: 1587 Shimo-Ochiai, Yodobashiku, Tokyo.

M. P.; Parl. Councillor, Com. & Industry Dept.; b. Dec., 1882 in Tochigi-ken; s. of late Kozo Matsumura. Career: grad., Tokyo Higher Com. School, 1909; joined Furukawa Gomei Kaisha; apptd. Chief, Purchasing Section, Furukawa Mining Co., and Dir., Dai Nippon Artificial Fertilizer Co. and Asahi Elec. Industry Co.; sent to Diet 3 times since 1928; apptd. present post, 1932. Address: Hachiyamamachi, Shibuyaku, Tokyo.

Prof., Kogyokusha; b. Aug., 1901 in Yamanashi-ken; s. of Yoshimatsu Matsumura. Career: grad., Nagoya Higher Com. School; completed P.-G. Course of same; Econ. Coll., Tokyo Imp. Univ.; Non-Regular Staff, Tokyo Office, League of Nations; Dir., Japan-Manchuria Trading Assn.; Mgr., Neo-Liberalism Assn.; Sec. to Yusuke Tsurumi; Dir., Young Men's League of Nations Club. Address: 473 Koyama-machi, Ebara-ku, Tokyo.

Envoy Extroadinary & Minister Plenipotentiary to Austria & Hungary; b. Apr., 1883 in Saga-ken; s. of Kanichi Matsunaga. Career: grad., Law Coll., Tokyo Imp. Univ., 1908; Diplomatic Probationer at Peking; Eléve-Consul at Seattle and Ottawa; Dir., Treaty Bureau; Minister to Netherlands since 1930; presetn post since 1933. Address: Japanese Legation, Vienna, Austria.

Pres., Toho Elec. Power Co.; b. Dec., 1875 in Nagano-ken; s. of Yasuzaemon Matsunaga, brewer. Career: grad., Law Dept., Keio Univ., 1896; apptd. Mgr., Hirotaki Hydro-Elec. Co., 1906; amalgamating it with others, founded Kyushu Elec. Co., 1910; established many firms and cos. of elec., gas, brick, oil, vehicles, etc. in Kyushu; Pres., Hakata Chamber of Com. & Industry, 1917; elected to Diet from Fukuoka, 1917; went to Europe and America to inspect industrial, political and econ. condition after the War, 1919; Pres., Elec. Assn., 1924; present post since 1927. Address: 367 Shimo-Ochiai, Yodobashiku, Tokyo.
Customs Supt., Lungchingtsun. Career: present post since 1932. Address: Lungchingtsun, Manchoukuo.

Hogakuhakushi (D. L.); Mem., Imp. Academy; Prof. and Chief, Com. Dept., Nippon Univ.; Vice-Pres., Harbor Assn. and Naval Assn.; Pres., Japan Univ. Profs.' League; b. Jan., 1868 in Osaka-fu; s. of Niemon Matsunami. Career: studied at Doshisah, Kyoto; grad., Law Coll., Tokyo Imp. Univ., 1893; apptd. Code Investigation Committee; Adviser for Navy Office on War-time Int'l Law; Instructor, Naval Staff Coll.; Prof., Tokyo Imp. Univ.; received degree, 1901; sent to Europe and America, 1931. Address: 17 Nakamachi, Ushigomeku, Tokyo.

M. P.; b. Dec., 1883 in Kumamoto-ken; s. of Chohachi Matsuno. Career: sent to Diet 4 times since 1920; Dir., Kikuchi Elec. Ry. Co., Nippon Dempo News Agency and Ryubunkan Publishing Co.; Parl. Vice-Minister, Home Office in Inukai Cabinet, 1931. Address: 2 Mita-Tsunamachi, Shibaku, Tokyo.

Mem., House of Peers; Pres., Matsuoka Steamship Co., Owada Spinning Co.; Prop., Matsuoka Farm, Hokkaido; Dir., Kurecha Spinning Co., Kashima Trust Co., Tokyo Takarazuka Theatre Co.; Auditor, Dai Nippon Artificial Fertilizer Co., Hanshin Kyuko Elec. Ry. Co.; b. Sept., 1888 in Hyogo--ken; s. of Shuzo Matsuoka. Career: grad., Econ. Dept., Keio Univ.; elected Mem., House of Peers, Sept., 1932. Address: 1611 Daiso, Ashiya, Mukogun, Hyogo-ken.

Baron; Hogakuhakushi (D. L.); Mem., House of Peers; Auditor, Special Industry Rationalization Bureau; Mem., Temporary Elec. Industry Inquiry Committee; Dir., Toyo Kyokai Univ. and Kyocho-Kai; Councillor, Mitsubishi Goshi Kaisha; Auditor, Mitsubishi Ship-building & Engrg. Co. and Mitsubishi Mining Co.; b. Nov., 1876 in Tokyo; s. of Baron Yasuki Matsuoka. Career: grad., Law Coll., Tokyo Imp. Univ., 1899; Prof., same; Gov't Delegate, Int'l Labor Conf.; Mem., City Planning Committee and Econ. & Finance Inquiry Committee; Dir., Indo-China Assn.; Dean, Toyo Kyokai Univ.; attended World Peace Conf., Switzerland, 1914; went abroad several times; Councillor, Mitsubishi Goshi Kaisha since 1924. Address: 24 Zaimokucho, Azabuku, Tokyo.

M. A. (Wisc. Univ., U. S.); Editorial Adviser, Osaka Mainichi and Tokyo Nichi Nichi; b. 1880 in Aomori-ken; s. of Totaro Matsuoka, Lawyer. Career: grad., Polit. Dept., Keio Univ.; Post-Graduate Course, Wisc. Univ.; Lecturer, Tokyo and Kobe Univs. of Com.; Keio Univ.; Kagoshima Higher Agrl. & Forestry School; Commr., Taiwan Gov't.; Head, Financial Dept., Osaka Mainichi; Pres., Keijo Nippo. Address: 147 Kagomachi, Koishikawaku, Tokyo.

M. P.; b. Mar., 1880 in Yamaguchi-ken; s. of Sanjuro Matsuoka. Career: grad., Oregon Law Coll., Oregon, U. S.; diplomatic services for many years; promoted to Consul-Gen.; Vice-Pres., South Manchuria Ry. Co.; sent to Diet from Yamaguchi-ken, twice; attended Gen. Assembly of League of Nations, 1932. Address: 10 Miyamuracho, Azabuku, Tokyo.

Ambassador to Italy; b. Feb., 1883 in Nagano-ken; 3rd s. of Shotaro Matsushima. Career: grad., Law Coll., Tokyo Imp. Univ., 1907; Diplomatic Probationer in Siam; Sec. to Foreign Minister; Councillor, Foreign Office; Consul-Gen.; Chief, Polit. Dept., Expeditionary Army at Vladivostok; Councillor, Embassy at Paris, 1923; Minister to Poland, 1927; Dir., Europe & America Bureau; present post since 1932. Address: Japanese Embassy, Rome, Italy.
Dir., Gen. Affairs Bureau, and Agr. & Mining Bureau, Industrial Dept., Manchoukuo. Career: present post since 1932. Address: Hsinking.

Auditor, Morotani Shokai; Dir., Broadcasting Corporation of Japan; b. Sept., 1867 in Kyoto City; s. of Nagahide Matsushiro, samurai. Career: grad., Tokyo Telegraph School, 1888; entered Communications Office, 1888; served to construct Submarine Cable between Mainland and Taiwan for War Office, 1896; apptd. Mem., Wireless Telegraph Investigation Committee, Navy Dept., 1900; Mgr., Osaka Branch, Nippon Elec. Co., 1905; General Sales Mgr., Head Office, 1917; present posts since 1932. Address: 38 Hasedo, Shibuyaku, Tokyo.

Mem., House of Peers; Kogakuhakushi (D. E.); Pres., Kyushu Imp. Univ.; b. Jan., 1872; s. of Moto Matsuura, samurai of Ehime Clan. Career: grad., Law Coll., Tokyo Imp. Univ.; Sec. to Education Minister; Councillor, Education Dept.; Chief, Technical Education Bureau; Chief, Examination Committee of Civil Service; Pres., Keijo Imp. Univ.; nominated Mem., House of Peers. Address: Kitaminatocho, Fukuoka-shi.

Vice-Admiral; Vice-Chief, Naval Gen. Staff, Navy Office; b. in Nagasaki-ken. Career: grad., Naval Academy; Chief, Aviation Headquarters; present post since 1933. Address: 1518 Kami-Igusa-machi, Suginamiku, Tokyo.

Consul-Gen. at London; Com. Councillor, Embassy at London; b. June, 1882 in Nagano-ken; s. of Rokuro Nakamura. Career: grad., Tokyo Higher Com. School, 1903; joined Nozawa-Gumi, then Chugai Trading Co.; apptd. Com. Commr., Embassy at London; attended 4th and 5th Gen. Assemblies of Int'l Trade Conf., Stockholm, 1927; present post since 1927. Address: Embassy of Japan, 37 Portman Sq., London, W. I., England.

General; Vice-Chief, General Staff Office; b. Nov., 1876; s. of Yoshichi Mazaki, Saga-ken. Career: grad., Military Academy, 1897; Comdr., Infanrty 1st Regiment, Imperial Guard Div.; Comdr., Infantry 1st Brigade; Pres., Military Academy; Comdr., 1st Division Lieut.-Gen.; apptd. General, May, 1933. Address: 102 Higashi-sanya, Yoyogi, Shibuyaku, Tokyo.

Asst. Canadian Govt. Trade Commr. at Kobe; b. June, 1901 in Union Bay, British Columbia, Canada; n. British; s. of C. A. McLane, retired. Career: grad., Univ. of British Columbia, Vancouver, B. C. (B. A.); Univ. of California, Berkeley, U. S. (M. A.); Com. Intelligence Service, Dept. of Trade & Com., Ottawa, Canada, 1928; present post since 1929. Address: P. O. Box 230, Kobe.

M. D.; Doctor of Medicine and Surgery; b. Apr., 1884, North Carolina, U. S.; n. American; s. of James Erasmus McSparran, Clergyman. Career: grad., Virginia Public Sch.; Randolph-Macon Academy; Randolph-Macon Coll.; Medical Univ., Richmond, Va.; Medical School, Vienna Univ.; hospital and private practice in Virginia for 5 years; 16 years practice in Japan. Address: 7 Nippon-Odori, Nakaku, Yokohama.

[illegible]ng. Dir., Toppan Insatsu (relief printing) Co.; s. of Shinjiro Miwa, musician. Career: grad., Keio Univ., 1918; joined Tokyo Paperware Co., 1917; present post since 1918. Address: 1 Urasarugakucho, Kandaku, Tokyo.

Pres., German East Asiatic Society, Tokyo; Pres., K. K. L. Leybold Shokwan, Tokyo and Osaka; b. Mar., 1885 in Hamburg; n. German. Career: arrived in Japan, 1906, since then has been actively concerned in trade business between Germany and Japan; Partner in the following firms; G. K. Kenzaisha, Tokyo and Osaka; P. Schmitz & Co., Eng. Co., Tokyo; Chien Hsin Eng. Co., Ltd., Shanghai, Hongkong; Simon, Evers & Co., G. m. b. H., Hamburg; also author of several books regarding Japanese grammar and things Japanese, “Der Krieg der alten Dachse”, etc. Address: 5081 Oi-Izurushimachi, Shinagawaku, Tokyo.

Journalist and Foreign Trade Delegate; b. Sept., 1894 in Budapest; n. Hungarian; s. of late Ferdinand Joseph Metzger. Career: after finishing Gymnasium, studied Catholic Theology and Oriental languages at Pázmány Univ. in Budapest; Examiner of “Dolmetsch School” (Military Interpreter Service) of Imp. & Roy. Austro-Hungarian Army Headquarters, 1918; Sworn English Interpreter, Royal Courts of Justice in Budapest, 1921; Sec. and Interpreter of Imp. Japanese Consulate in Budapest, 1922; Sec., “Commission de la Delimitation de la Frontière” Japanese Delegation, 1923; came to Japan as Corr. for Hungarian newspapers, 1929; apptd. Corr. for Hungarian Official Press Agency, Agence Telegraphique Hongroise S. A., 1931; gave several lectures on Hungary and promoted Hungarian Arts Exhibition held in Tokyo, Jan., 1932. Address: 393 Motomachi, Hommoku, Nakaku, Yokohama.

Chief, Civil Adm. Office, Port Aurther, Kwantung Gov't.; b. Feb., 1892 in Ishikawa-ken; s. of Tomokuni Mikagechi, samurai. Career: grad., Law Coll., Tokyo Imp. Univ., 1917; Inspector, Shiga-ken; Sec. of same; Chief, Education Section, Home Affairs Dept.; School Inspector of Shiga-ken; Sec. and Chief, Education Dept., Hiroshima-ken; present post since 1929. Address: Civil Adm. Office, Ryojun.

Prop., Mikimoto Pearl Store; b. Jan., 1858 in Miye-ken; s. of Otokichi Mikimoto. Career: invented artificial pearl cultivation and engaged in its export throughout world; awarded Supreme Hon. Grand Medal at St. Louis Exhibition, Paris; elected Mem., House of Peers, 1924; made inspection tour through Europe and America. Address: 3 Ginza-Shichome, Kyobashiku, Tokyo.

Gov., Aichi-ken; b. 1886 in Toyama-ken; s. of Chozaburo Minabe. Career: grad., German Law Coll., Tokyo Imp. Univ., 1911; Councillor, Home Dept.; Sec., Home Dept.; Chief, Executive Section, Prefectural Bureau, Home Dept.; Gov., Yamanashi-ken; same, Okayama-ken; Dir., Civil Engrg. Bureau; Gov., Miyagi-ken; present post since 1932. Address: Minami Takehiracho, Nagoya.
Chief Sec., State Council, Manchoukuo; b. in Yamagata-ken. Career: grad., German Law Coll., Tokyo Imp. Univ.; present post since 1932. Address: Hsinking.

Communications Minister; Mem., House of Peers; b. Oct., 1869; s. of Kakuhei Iwama, Toyama-ken and later adopted by Heikichi Minami. Career: grad., Law Coll., Tokyo Imp. Univ.; Sec. of Cabinet; Gov., Fukuoka-ken; Vice-Minister of Education; nominated Mem., House of Peers; Gov.-Gen. of Taiwan, Mar., 1932. Address: 5 Yobancho, Kojimachiku, Tokyo.

General; Supreme War Councillor; b. Aug., 1874 in Oita-ken; s. of Kihei Minami. Career: grad., Military Academy, 1895; Military Coll., 1903; Instructor, Military Coll.; same, Naval Staff Coll.; same, Cavalry School; Comdr., Cavalry 13th Regiment; Pres., Military Cavalry School; same, Military Academy; Comdr., 16th Division; Vice-Chief of General Staff; War Minister in Wakatsuki Cabinet, 1931. Address: 173 Kawara, Zaimokuza, Kamakuramachi, Kanagawa-ken.

Mng.-Dir., Dainihon Jochugiku (Japan Pyrethrums) Co.; Dir., Nihon Kyoritsu Ins. Co. & Wakayama Land Co.; b. 1861 in Wakayama-ken; s. of Kiyomatsu Minami. Career: Mgr., Wakayama Spinning Co.; Mem., Chamber of Com. & Ind., Wakayama. Address: 3 Rokubancho, Wakayama City.

Pres., Dai Nippon Automobile Ins. Co., Hokkai Hydro-Elec. Co., Hakodate Hydro-Elec. Co.; Dir., Tenryu Elec. Power Co.; b. Dec., 1869; s. of Hideyoshi Minobe. Career: grad., Law Coll., Tokyo Imp. Univ., 1893; served Agrl. & Com. Office; Councillor of same; Sec. to Finance Minister; Pres., Bank of Chosen. Address: 9 of 5 Shiba-Koen, Shibaku, Tokyo.

Mem., House of Peers; Hogakuhakushi (D. L.); Mem., Imp. Academy; Prof., Tokyo Imp. Univ. and Tokyo Univ. of Com., Councillor, Legislation Bureau; b. May, 1873 in Hyogo-ken; brother of Shunkichi Minobe, Ex-Pres., Bank of Chosen. Career: grad., Law Coll., Tokyo Imp. Univ., 1897; sent to Europe for study of history of comparative legislation, 1899; apptd. Prof., Tokyo Imp. Univ., 1902; received degree, 1903; Mem., Imp. Academy, 1911; apptd. Prof., Tokyo Univ. of Com., 1920; Prof., Kyushu Imp. Univ., 1924. Address: 124 Takehayacho, Koishikawaku, Tokyo.

Cavaliere, Ufficiale (Italy); Officier d'Academie (France); Dir., Shochiku Theatre Co.; b. June, 1886 in Tottori-ken; s. of late Jinzaburo Mishima. Career: grad., Com. Dept., Waseda Univ., 1908; served Daimaru and Shirokiya Dept. Stores; toured Europe and America for inspection; returning home, 1916, founded Koriyama Spinning Co. which was later merged into Nagoya Spinning Co.; entered present firm, 1924. Address: 707 Amanuma, Suginamiku, Tokyo.

Igakuhakushi (M. D.); Prof., Tokyo Imp. Univ.; b. Jan., 1876 in Morioka-City; s. of Shunjiro Mita, physician. Career: grad., Medical Coll., Tokyo Imp. Univ., 1909; apptd. Asst. Prof. of same; sent to Germany and France for study of Medical Jurisprudence; received degree, 1914. Address: 40 Mita, Meguroku, Tokyo.

Chairman, Board of Dirs., Mitsubishi Mining Co.; Pres., Yubetsu Colliery and Ry. Co., Iizuka Mining Co., Naihoro Colliery & Ry. Co., Bibai Ry. Co.; Dir., Furukawa Elec. Co., Chosen Anthracite Co.; b. Oct., 1871 in Hiroshima-ken; s. of Keiichiro Mitani. Career: grad., Tokyo Univ. of Com.; entered Mitsubishi Co., 1896; after having served as Mgr., Shanghai, Nagasaki and Karatsu Branches, promoted Mgr., Coal Dept., Tokyo Head Office; when Mitsubishi Mining Co. was established in 1918, was elected its Mng. Dir., and promoted present post, 1924; besides, holding Dir., Japan Economic Federation, Japan Industrial Club, Japan Mining Society, Coal Mine Assn., Josuikai; Councillor, Japan Mining Institute; Auditor, Japan Power Assn., etc. Address: 255 Kagomachi, Koishikawaku, Tokyo.

Ry. Minister; M. P.; b. June, 1871 in Kagawa-ken; s. of Seikichi Miyawaki, and later adopted by Tsunetaro Mitsuchi. Career: grad., Tokyo Higher Normal School, 1897; went to Europe to study pedagogy and history; Prof., Tokyo Higher Normal School; Editor, Tokyo Nichi-Nichi Shimbun; Councillor of Educational System, Chosen Govt.; Councillor, Finance Office; Chief Sec., Cabinet; Vice-Minister, Agrl. & Com. Dept.; same, Agr. & Forestry Dept.; Education Minister in Tanaka Cabinet; Communications Minister in Inukai Cabinet. Address: 16 Hiroocho, Azabuku, Tokyo.

Kogakuhakushi (D. E.); Engr., Elec. Experimental Station; same, Communications Dept.; same, Imperial Household Dept.; Prof., Waseda Univ.; b. Mar., 1885 in Toyama-shi; s. of Seizo Mitsuda. Career: grad., Engrg. Coll., Tokyo Imp. Univ., 1911; apptd. Engr., Communications Dept., 1913; went to America and Germany to study electricity. Address: 14 Ichigaya-Nakanocho, Ushigomeku, Tokyo.

Mem., Investigation Committee of Rice; Mng. Dir., Mitsubishi Warehouse Co.; Pres., Ryoka Warehouse Co.; Kyodo Transportation Co.; b. Apr., 1876; s. of Takejiro Mitsuhashi, Tokyo. Career: Pres., Hiroshima Mercantile Marine School; Engineer, Hiroshima-ken; served in Russo-Japanese War; Special Mem., Tokyo Chamber of Com. & Industry. Address: 60, 5-chome Gotanda Shinagawa-ku, Tokyo.
M. P.; Business man; b. Oct., 1875 in Yamanashi-ken. Career: apptd. Mem. and Vice-Pres., Hokkaido Assembly; sent to Diet 3 times. Address: 28 Shirokane-cho, Ushigomeku, Tokyo.

Rigakuhakushi (D. Sc.); Prof. of Chemistry, Tohoku Imp. Univ.; b. Sept., 1893 in Tokyo; s. of Kakichi Mitsukuri, Prof. of Tokyo Imp. Univ. Career: grad., Chemical Institute, Faculty of Science, Tokyo Imp. Univ. Address: 46 Nakasugiyama-dori, Sendai.

Chemist; Composer; b. Oct., 1895 in Tokyo; s. of Genpachi Mitsukuri, Prof., Tokyo Imp. Univ. Career: grad., 1st Higher School, 1918; Applied Science Course, Engrg. Coll., Tokyo Imp. Univ., 1921; studied in Europe, 1921-25; studied Physical Chemistry at Kaiser Wilhelm Research Institute, Berlin; educated Musical Composition by George Schumann; served Scientific Research Dept., Naval Technical Research Institute; founded New Musical Composers' Assn., 1930. Address: Naval Club, Hiratsuka City, Kanagawa-ken.

Mng. Dir., Taiwan Warehouse Co.; Dir., Taiwan Stone Co., Tokai Motor-car Transportation Co.; b. Sept., 1879 in Yamaguchi-ken; s. of late Major-General Hiroyoshi Mitsumaki. Career: grad., Law Coll., Kyoto Imp. Univ., 1904; joined Bank of Taiwan; Mng. Dir., Taiwan Warehouse Co., 1926. Recreations: golf, Utai. Address: 8 Tsukijicho-Itchome, Taihoku, Taiwan.

Kogakuhakushi (D. E.); Engineer and Chief, Chemical Elec. Dept., Patent Bureau; b. June, 1873; s. of Atsutoshi Mitsuyama, Chiba-ken. Career: grad., Engrg. Coll., Tokyo Imp. Univ. and went to England, Germany and America for study of Applied Chemistry; Asst.-Prof., Tokyo Imp. Univ.; Dir., Chuo Shikenjo; Pres., Keijo Higher Tech. School. Address: 37 Kitamachi, Ushigomeku, Tokyo.
Dir., Nagoya Chamber of Com. & Industry; b. May, 1882 in Sendai, Miyagi-ken; s. of Kako Miura. Career: grad., Polit. Econ. Dept., Waseda Univ., 1906. Address: 25 Minamiyamacho, Nakaku, Nagoya.

Ringakuhakushi (D. Sc.); Prof., Forest Chemistry, Tokyo Imp. Univ.; b. Apr., 1885 in Wakayama; s. of Yasujiro Miura, farmer. Career: grad., Forestry Course, Faculty of Agr., Tokyo Imp. Univ., 1912; studied for 2 years in Europe and Ameirca; apptd. Lecturer, Tokyo Imp. Univ., 1915; Asst. Prof. of same, 1918; present post since 1926. Recreation: travelling. Address: 17 Sakuragaokamachi, Shibuyaku, Tokyo.

Chief, Gen. Affairs Dept., Kirin Prov. Office; b. Sept., 1882 in Kyoto-fu; s. of Satoru Miura. Career: grad., Law Coll., Tokyo Imp. Univ., 1907; apptd. Chief, Eitaibashi Taxation Office; Inspector, Metropolitan Police Board; Chief, Fukagawa and Yotsuya Police Stations; Inspector, Taiwan Gov't.; Sec. of same; Gov., Takao, Taihoku and Taichu Provinces; Dir., Home Affairs Bureau, Kwantung Gov't. since 1930; present post since 1932. Address: Official Residence, Kirin Gov't., Manchoukuo.

Sec., Foreign Office; Chief, 2nd Section, Asia Bureau; b. Aug., 1893 in Aomori-ken; s. of Takesaburo Miura. Career: grad., Law Coll., Tokyo Imp. Univ., 1917; apptd. Elève-Consul; 3rd Sec., Embassy at London, 1922; Administrative Official, Foreign Office, 1926; present post since 1928. Address: 1512 Higashi-Teraomachi, Tsurumiku, Yokohama.

Kogakuhakushi (D. E.); Prof., Tohoku Imp. Univ.; b. Aug., 1883 in Saitama-ken; s. of Tojiro Miyagi, farmer. Career: grad., Engrg. Coll., Tokyo Imp. Univ., 1908; appt. Prof., Sendai Higher Tech. School, 1909; after 2 years' study of Mechanical Engineering in England and America, apptd. present post, 1919; conferred degree, same year; became Mem., Scientific Research Council, 1927; again went to Europe and America for Study, 1930. Address: 28 Kita-yoban-cho, Sendai.

Pres., Nisshin Spinning Co.; Dir., Kawasaki Trust Co.; Auditor, Nippon Beer and Mineral Co., Nanyo Trading Co.; Councillor, Nanao Cement Co.; Dir., Japan Industrial Club, Japan Trades Assn.; b. Jan., 1879; s. of Shotaro Kobayashi. Career: grad., Law Coll., Tokyo Imp. Univ., 1906; Mem., Tokyo Municipal Assembly. Address: 10 Isaragomachi, Shibaku, Tokyo.
Dir., Legislation Office, State Council, Manchoukuo; b. Kochi-ken. Career: grad., Post & Telegraph Sch., Tokyo; present post since 1932. Address: Hsinking.

Igakuhakushi (M. D.) Mem., House of Peers; Emeritus Prof., Tokyo Imp. Univ.; Mem., Imp. Academy; Central Hygienic Assn.; Lord-in-Waiting, Kinkei Hall. Career: served in Univ. as Asst. Prof.; apptd. Acting Principal, Tokyo Medical School; served Home Office; Chief, Medical Dept., Tokyo Imp. Univ.; Chairman, School Hygiene Advisory Assn.; Councillor, Japan Exhibition; sent to Philadelphia, as Vice-Pres. of World Medical Congress: nominated Mem., House of Peers, 1891. Address: 81 Takehayacho, Koishikawaku, Tokyo.

Mng. Dir., Dai San Shoken K. K. (3rd Bond Co., Ltd.); b. Mar., 1888 in Ehime-ken; s. of Sokichi Miyauchi, later adopted by Sutekichi Miyake. Career: grad., Polit. Econ. Dept., Keio Univ., 1914; after having served as Chief Editor, Osaka Bankers' Club, Mgr., Inquiry Section, Nomura Co.; same, Tokyo Branch, Nomura Bank, Ltd.; Auditor, Nomura Bond Co., Ltd., and apptd. present post. Address: 80 Komagome Hayashicho, Hongoku, Tokyo.

Consul-Gen. at Calcutta, India; b. Sept., 1888 in Wakayama-ken; s. of Shin-ichiro Miyake. Career: grad., Tokyo Higher Com. School, 1912; passed Diplomatic & Consular Service Exam., 1914; apptd. Elève-Consul, Councillor of Foreign Office, Chief, 3rd Section, Treaty Bureau; 1st Sec. of Legation; Consul-Gen., Batavia, 1927; present post since 1933. Address: Consulate-General of Japan, Calcutta, India.

Pres., Nippon Raw Silk Co., Mitsubishi Trading Co.; Dir., Mitsubishi Iron & Steel Works, Mitsubishi Aircraft Co.; Auditor, Mitsubishi Shipbuilding & Engrg. Co.; b. June, 1869 in Aichi-ken; s. of Seizaburo Miyakegawa. Career: grad., Tokyo Higher Com. School, 1892; joined Mitsubishi Goshi Kaisha; Mgr., its Branches of Shanghai, Peking, Wakamatsu and Moji; Head, Steamship Dept. and Oriental Dept.; Special Mem., Yokohama Chamber of Com. & Industry. Address: 812 Nakano, Tokyo.

Hogakushi (LL. B.); Lawyer; M. P.; Dir., Kanto Spinning Co. Ltd.; b. Apr., 1816 in Ibaragi-ken; s. of Gembei Imaizumi, farmer, and later adopted by Yonosuke Miyako. Career: grad., Law Coll., Tokyo Imp. Univ., 1892; sent to Diet from Ibaragi-ken 8 times since 1902; attended World Parl. Congress, Paris as Councillor; on way home toured Europe and America; Member of Seiyukai Party; also author of several books. Address: 16 Komagome Akebonocho, Hongoku, Tokyo.

Prof., Anglo-American Law, Kyoto Imp. Univ.; b. July, 1888 in Shizuoka-ken; s. of Takeo Miyamoto, teacher. Career: completed Shizuoka-ken Pref. Kakegawa Middle School; grad., 6th Higher School; Law Coll., Kyoto Imp. Univ., 1915; apptd. Probationary Judge, 1915; Lecturer, Law Coll., Kyoto Imp. Univ., 1916; Asst. Prof. of same, 1918; Prof. of same, 1921; Dean, Law Coll. of same, 1931. Address: 8 Junibomachi, Takao, Kamikyoku, Kyoto.

M. P.; Tea Producer; b. Dec., 1876 in Shizuoka; s. of Shohei Miyamoto, farmer. Career: Pres., Shizuoka-ken Pref. Assembly, 1923 and 1927; Dir., Shizuoka-ken Tea Assn. since 1924; same, Japan Tea Promotion Committee since 1925; sent to Diet from Shizuoka-ken, 1932. Address: 122 Inagawamachi, Shizuoka.

Lord-in-Waiting, Kinkei Hall; b. Jan., 1868 in Niigata-ken; s. of Gonkuro Miyao. Career: grad., Law Coll., Tokyo Imp. Univ., 1896; Chief, Colonization Bureau. Govt. of Formosa; Gov., Aichi-ken; same, Hokkaido-Cho; Vice-pres., Tokyo Reconstruction Office; Pres., Oriental Development Co. Address: 541 Shimomeguro-Sanchome, Meguroku, Tokyo.

Lawyer; b. Jan., 1866 in Osaka. Career: toured United States, 1883; grad., Law Coll., Tokyo Imp. Univ., 1887; served in Foreign Office as Assistant in Law Bureau, 1887-92; Sec., Legation at Washington, 1892-94; Sec. and Charge d'Affaires at Berlin and Brussels, 1894-99; Minister Resident in Diplomatic Service, 1900-06; Counsellor, Embassy at Washington, 1906-08; retired from diplomatic service to practice law, 1909; in addition to law practice, Special Corr., Carnegie Endowment for Int'l Peace since 1910; Hon. Mem., American Bar Assns., 1918; visited London and Paris as guest of Bars of England and France; Associate Mem., Bar Assn., City of New York, 1918; apptd. by President Coolidge, American Non-national Mem., Permanent Int'l Commission provided for by Treaty of 1914 between U.S. and Uruguay for advancement of peace, 1928. Address: 22 Aoyama-Minamicho Shichome, Akasakaku, Tokyo.

1st Class Sec., Embassy in France; b. Apr., 1892 in Ehime-ken; s. of Shinjiro Miyazaki. Career: grad., Law Coll., Tokyo Imp. Univ., 1917; entered Com. & Industry Bureau, Agrl. & Com. Dept.; Sec. of Foreign Office; Sec. of Embassy; Chief, 1st Section, Europe & America Bureau, 1926; present post since 1932. Address: Japanese Embassy, Paris, France.

Dean, Kyoritsu Jogakko, Yokohama; b. June, 1872 in Kumamoto-ken. Career: grad., Waseda Univ., 1898; San Francisco Theological Seminary, 1910; ordained Presbyterian Minister, by San Francisco Prebytary; then paster of Japanese presbytarian Church, 'Frisco; Paster, Union Church in Moji, 1915-23; Executive Sec., Christian Council of Japan, 1923-27; present post since 1928. Address: 115 Honmoku, 1-chome, Yokohama.

Chief Sec., Dojunkai; b. Nov., 1882 in Miyagi-ken; e. s. of Hangoro Miyazawa, official. Career: Sec., Akita-ken; Chief, Gen. Affairs Section, Tokyo City Traffic Bureau; Chief Accountant of same. Address: 2831 Kichijoji, Musashinomachi, Tokyo-fu.

Mng.-Dir., Mitsubishi Goshi Kaisha; b. Feb., 1871; s. of late Taizo Miyoshi, Mem., House of Peers. Career: grad., Keio Univ., 1895; served Kyushu Ry. Co.; toured Europe and America to study transportation business; entered present firm, 1908. Address: 57 Ichigaya-Nakanocho, Ushigomeku, Tokyo.

Prof., Sociological Dept., Meiji Gakuin; b. Aug., 1894 in Ibaraki-ken; s. of Katsutaro Miyoshi, business man. Career: grad., Sociological Course, Litt. Coll., Tokyo Imp. Univ.; served at Social Bureau, Tokyo City by making research in social work and sociological affairs; apptd. Chief, Social Work Dept., Kumamoto-ken; present post since 1929. Address: 2225 Fusumamachi, Meguroku, Tokyo.

Dir., 3rd Higher School; b. Dec., 1870 in Kochi-ken; s. of Wataru Mizobuchi. Career: grad., Litt. Coll., Tokyo Imp. Univ., 1895; apptd. Teacher, Kochi Middle School, 1895; Prof., 2nd Higher School, 1897; Principal, Chiba Middle School, 1898; Prof., Tokyo Higher Normal School, 1899; sent to Europe and America for study, 1899-1903; Prof., Sapporo Agrl. Coll., 1908; Dir., 4th Higher School, 1911; same, 5th Higher School, 1921; present post since 1931. Address: Official Residence, 3rd Higher School, Kyoto City.

Count; Major-Gen., Reserve; Mem., House of Peers; Auditor, Nippon Elec. Power Co.; b. Apr., 1878; s. of Count Naomasa Mizoguchi. Career: grad., Mil. Academy, 1898; apptd. Artillery Sub-Lieut.; grad., Mil. Coll.; Chief, Artillery Section, War Office; Mem., Mil. Technical Committee; attached to Divisions at Hiroshima, Zentsuji, Utsunomiya, and Nagoya; fought in Russo-Japanese War; elected Mem., House of Peers, 1924; Supreme War Councillor, 1925; Parl. Vice-Minister of War, 1929-30. Address: 164 Onden, Shibuyaku, Tokyo.

Hogakuhakushi (D. L.); Privy Councillor; Supreme Adviser, Manchukuo; b. Mar., 1864 in Saga-ken; s. of late Kunizane Mizumachi, samurai of Saga Clan. Career: grad., Law Coll., Tokyo Imp. Univ., 1889; Councillor, Finance Office; Revenue Officer; Sec. to Finance Minister; Prof., Peers' School; Chief, Financial Bureau, Finance Office; Vice-Minister of Finance; Vice-Pres., Bank of Japan; Pres., Board of Audit. Address: 55 Kamiyamacho, Shibuyaku, Tokyo.

Retired Captain (Navy); Author; b. Oct., 1877 in Matsuyama; s. of late Mitsuyuki Mizuno. Career: grad., Naval Coll.; went to Europe and America for inspection during World War; to Germany after the War. Address: 143 Kamiuma, Komazawa, Setagayaku, Tokyo.

Hogakuhakushi (D. L.); Mem., House of Peers; Dir., Nippon Marine Ekiseikai; b. Jan., 1868 in Tokyo; s. of Ryuzaburo Mizuno, samurai. Career: grad., Law Coll., Tokyo Imp. Univ., 1892; apptd. Councillor, Home Office, 1894; Sec. to Home Minister; Dir., Shrines Bureau and Engrg. Bureau; Vice-Minister of Home Affairs; Home Minister 3 times; Education Minister, 1927-28; accorded privileges of Minister. Address: 61 Shirokane-Sarumachi, Shibaku, Tokyo.

M. P.; Vice-Pres., Polit. Affairs Committee, Seiyukai; b. Nov., 1882 in Kyoto-fu; s. of Sakuzo Mizushima, farmer. Career: grad., Polit. Econ. Dept., Waseda Univ.; became editorial staff., Tokyo Nichi-Nichi and Tokyo Mainichi Shimbun; served Fuji Paper Mfg. Co.; Headman, Maizuru Town; Vice-Pres., Town and Village Headman's Assn. of Japan; Chairman, Kyoto-fu Pref. Assembly; Chief, Kyoto Branch., Seiyukai Party; sent to Diet from Kyoto-fu 3 times. Address: 406 Isatsu, Nakasuji-mura, Kasagun, Kyoto-fu.

Acting Partner, Mizushima Shokai; Dealer in Automobile; b. Oct., 1877; s. of Rinta Mizushima, Hokkaido. Career: grad., Keio Univ. and went to Europe; established Mizushima Shokai, 1913; Dir., Tohoku Gum Co., Ltd. Address: 40 Kaminibancho, Kojimachiku, Tokyo.

M. P.; Adviser, Seiyukai Party; b. Feb., 1867 in Hiroshima-ken; s. of Tonosuke Mochizuki; adoptd. by Shunkichi Mochizuki, uncle. Career: studied Law, Economics and Politics at Kogyokusha, Kyoritsu Gakko and Meiji Eigo Gakko; engaged in mining industry; sent to Diet 11 times since 1898; Councillor, Agrl. & Com. Dept. in Hara Cabinet; Communications Minister in Tanaka Cabinet, 1927; Home Minister, 1829-30. Address: 307 Harajuku, Shibuyaku, Tokyo.

Yakugakuhakushi (Dr. of Pharmacology); Mng.-Dir., Momotani Juntendo; Dir., Momoi Shoji Co.; b. Sept., 1890 in Wakayama-ken; s. of Masajiro Momotani. Career: grad., Pharmaceutical Dept., Tokyo Imp. Univ.; established Momotani Toilet Article Laboratory, 1913; went to France to inspect toilet article factories, 1920; Mem., Pharmacist Exam. Committee, Home Office, 1927; Auditor, Osaka Pharmacy School, 1932. Address: 12 Minamimachi-naka-Itchome, Sumiyoshiku, Osaka.

Mng.-Dir., Isorite Kogyo K. K.; b. Sept., 1876 in Kyoto; s. of Gembei Mori. Career: grad., Law Coll., Tokyo Imp. Univ., 1902; apptd. Kobe Branch Mgr., Sumitomo Warehouse Co.; Business Mgr., Sumitomo Steel Works; Mgr., Sumitomo Wakamatsu Colliery Office; Mng. Dir., Japan Sheet Glass Co., 1923-27; Auditor, Sumitomo Fertilizer Works, 1927-31; present post since 1927. Address: Gakuin-mae, Teizukayama, Sumiyoshiku, Osaka.
Mng.-Dir., Morigo Co., Ltd.; Dir., Daimaru, Ltd.; b. June, 1881 in Shiga-ken; s. of Senzaburo Mori. Career: grad., Econ. Dept., Keio Univ. Address: 12 Aoyama Takagicho, Akasakaku, Tokyo.

Mem., House of Peers; Manufacturer and Dealer in medicine and toilet articles; b. Apr., 1874 in Osaka, and later adopted by late Heibei Mori. Career: grad., Kyoritsu Medical School, Osaka; connected with several business firms and societies; became Vice-Pres., Osaka Chamber of Com. & Industry; Pres., Federation, Osaka Industrial Assns.; Pres., Osaka Trading School; Honorary Consul, Republic of Turkey; High Taxpayer in Osaka-fu. Address: 30 Junkeimachi-dori Sanchome, Minamiku, Osaka.

Kogakuhakushi (D. E.); Dir., Nagoya Coll. of Technology; Adviser, Nagoya Chamber of Com. & Industry; b. Mar., 1867 in Okayamashi; s. of Shozo Mori. Career: grad., Engrg. Coll., Tokyo Imp. Univ., 1891; served as Asst. of R. F. Trevishick at Kobe Factory, Ry. Office; Chief, same factory, 1896; sent to Europe and U. S. for inspection, 1903-04; Chief Engr., Shimbashi Factory; Lecturer, Tokyo and Kyoto Imp. Univs.; Dir., South Manchuria Ry. Co., 1912; received degree, 1915; present post since 1920. Address: 25 Yamawakicho-Itchome, Nakaku, Nagoya.

Vice-Pres., Yasuda Bank; Dir., Mitsui Trust Co. and Yasuda Trust Co.; Auditor, Nippon Wireless Telegraph Co. and Tokyo Credit Bureau; Dir., Yasuda Hozensha; b. Feb., 1873 in Tottori-ken; s. of Jinjuro Mori. Career: grad., Tokyo Higher Com. School, 1897; joined Yokohama Specie Bank and served at Head Office, branceh at Shanghai, London and Neuchwang; Mgr., Kobe Branch; Special Mem., Kobe Chamber of Com. & Industry; Asst. Mgr., London Branch; Dir., Bank of Taiwan; then Pres. of same. Address: 47 Takanawa-Minamicho, Shibaku, Tokyo.

Mng.-Dir., Nagoya Shimbun-Sha; b. June, 1877 in Okayama-ken; s. of Eitaro Mori, scholar of Chinese Classics. Career: grad., Tokyo Semmon Gakko (present Waseda Univ.). Address: 17 Gokenyacho, Nakaku, Nagoya.

Lieut.-Gen.; Comdr., 1st Division; b. Jan., 1876 in Tokyo-fu; s. of late Miyabito Oe, Shinto priest. Career: grad., Shuyukan, Fukuoka; Waseda Semmon Gakko; Military Acad.; Military Staff Coll., apptd. Major; attached Imp. Guard Infantry 2nd Regiment; promoted to Staff; Instructor; commanded garrison force in Tientsin; Regimental Comdr.; Chief-Staff Officer, 10th Reg.; present post since 1930. Address: 24 Mikawadaimachi, Azabuku, Tokyo.

Hogakuhakushi (D. L.); Prof., Tokyo Imp. Univ.; b. Mar., 1887 in Shiga-ken; s. of Shuku Mori, landowner. Career: grad., Peers' School, 1909; Law Coll., Tokyo Imp. Univ., 1913; commercial study at Research Course; sent by order of Education Minister to Europe to study Theory of Insurance, 1914-17; apptd. Asst. Prof., Chair on Insurance & Commerce, Tokyo Imp. Univ., 1917; Prof., same Univ., 1919; Councillor, same univ., 1929; Dean, Faculty of Economics, same, 1931. Address: 30 Ichigaya Nakanocho, Ushigomeku, Tokyo.

Mng.-Dir., 15th Bank; Pres., Imp. Warehouse Co.; b. Mar., 1878 in Fukushima-ken; s. of Sozaemon Mori, samurai of Aizu Clan. Career: grad., Law Coll., Tokyo Imp. Univ., 1902; passed Higher Civil Service Exam., same year; apptd. Sec., Finance Office, 1903; went to Europe and America on official mission, 1908-10; Dir., Banking Dept., Finance Office, 1916; Vice-Pres., Bank of Taiwan, 1920; Dir., South Manchuria Ry. Co., 1922. Address: 45 Shoto, Shibuyaku, Tokyo.

Ex-Minister to Chile and Bolivia; b. July, 1880 in Fukuoka-ken; s. of Hisashi Mori. Career: grad., Law Coll., Tokyo Imp. Univ., 1906; apptd. successively Consul Sec. at Chosen Govt. Office and Kwantung Govt., Consul-Gen. and Councillor Embassy, serving at Honolulu, China and Italy; Minister to Chile and Bolivia, 1927-1933. Address: c/o Foreign Office, Tokyo.

Hogakuhakushi (D. L.); Chief Dir., Women's Econ. Coll. Girls' High School and Bunka Fukuyukai Foundation; b. Mar., 1877 in Kyoto; s. of Jun-ichiro Masuyama, and later adopted by Katsuzo Morimoto. Career: grad., Hokkaido Univ.; Johns Hopkins Univ.; sent to America to study Economics and Finance, 1914; made seven trips to America and Europe as lecturer; Prof., Tohoku Imp. Univ., 1918; same, Hokkaido Imp. Univ. Address: Nishi-Sanchome, Kita-Jyunijo, Sapporo; c/o Bunka Apts., 5 Motomachi-Itchome, Hongoku, Tokyo.

Baron; Pres., Japan Trades Assn.; Pres., Morimura-Gumi; Chairman, Board of Dirs., Fuji Elec. Power Co.; Dir., Fuji Gas Spinning Co., Toyo Chinaware Co., Kyushu Hydro-Elec. Dec., 1873 in Tokyo; s. of late Baron Ichizaemon Morimura. Career: grad., Keio Univ., 1892; went to America where he stayed 9 years for study; joined Morimura-Gumi; inherited peerage, 1920. Address: 33 Takanawa-Minamicho, Shibaku, Tokyo.

Chief, 1st Section, Asia Bureau, Foreign Office; b. May, 1891 in Fukuoka. Career: grad., Law Coll., Tokyo Imp. Univ., 1916; apptd. Sec. of Embassy in Germany and America; 1st Sec., Legation in China, 1930; present post since May, 1930. Address: 58 Zaimokucho, Azabuku, Tokyo.

Consul-General at Harbin; b. Feb., 1896 in Kanazawa City; s. of Hiko-o Morishima. Career: grad. from Law Coll. of Tokyo Imp. Univ.; entered Foreign Office; Consul at Mukden; then present post. Address: Japanese Consulate-General, Harbin, Manchoukuo.
Dir., Gen. Affairs Bureau, Ry. Bureau, and Water Transportation Bureau of Communication Dept., Manchoukuo. Career: present post since 1932. Address: Hsinking.

Mng. Dir., Moritani & Co.; b. May, 1889 in Okayama-ken; s. of Gohei Moritani, business man. Career: grad., Keio Univ., 1913; then Economic Dept., Columbia Univ., New York; later succeeded business of his father who founded present firm. Address: Gofukubashi-Nichome, Nihonbashiku, Tokyo.

Lawyer; M. P.; b. Nov., 1884 in Miyagi-ken; s. of Tokuro Moriya. Career: grad., Law Coll., Tokyo Imp. Univ.; passed Higher Civil Service Exam., 1910; apptd. Official, Home Office; Sec., Chiba-ken and Aichi-ken, '13; Inspector and Councillor, Home Office '17; Chief Sec. and Chief, Gen.-Affairs Section, Korean Govt.; Chief, 2nd Section, Social Bureau, Home Office; Govt. Delegate, Int'l Labour Council, '25; Chief, Social Section, Social Bureau, '26; sent to Diet 3 times since 1928. Address: (office) 406 Toyo Bldg., Uchiyamashitacho, Kojimachiku, Tokyo. (home) 74 Nishigaharamachi, Takinogawaku, Tokyo.

Rank: Jr. 5th; 6th Order of Sacred Treasure; Consul-Gen. at Foochow, China; b. Nov., 1893 in Miyagi-ken; s. of Tokuro Moriya; m. Katsu, d. of T. Shibuya, Mayor of Sendai. Career: grad., Law Coll. (German), Tokyo Imp. Univ., 1917; Legal Sec., Kwantung Leased Territory (Port Arthur), 1920; Sec., Treaty Bureau, Foreign Office, 1923; Mem., Delegation to Chinese Tariff Conference, Peking, 1925-26; attached to Delegation to Extraterritorial Commn., Peking, 1925-26; 2nd Sec., Embassy at London, 1926; 1st Sec. of same, 1929; 1st Sec., Legation in China, 1930; present post since 1932. Recreations: golf, reading, Go-game. Address: Consulate-General, Foochow, China.

Pres., Moroto Shokusan Co.; b. July, 1888 in Miye-ken; s. of late Seiroku Moroto. Career: Auditor, Mitsubishi Mining Co.; Acting Partner, Moroto Gomei Kaisha; Pres., Ikueikai. Address: Kuwana, Nishi-Kuwanamachi, Miye-ken. 41 Motozonocho-Itchome, Kojimachiku, Tokyo.

Polish Minister to Tokyo; b. Sept., 1894 in London; s. of Ignace Moscinecki, Pres., Republic of Poland. Address: 3 Hiroocho, Azabuku, Tokyo.

Privy Councillor; Councillor, Seiyukai; Lawyer; b. May, 1858; s. of Eizo Inomata, and later adopted by Nao Motoda. Address: 8 Kioicho, Kojimachiku, Tokyo.

Kogakuhakushi (D. E.); Prof., Kyoto Imp. Univ.; b. June, 1879 in Yokohama; s. of late Morimichi Motono, Pres., Yomiuri Shimbun. Career: grad., Electrical Dep't., Engrg. Coll., Kyoto Imp.
