Address: 21 Shogoin-Entomicho, Sakyoku, Kyoto.

Prof., Econ. Dept., Keio Univ.; b. Mar., 1888 in Ehime-ken; s. of Gen-ichi Mukai, landowner. Career: grad., Econ. Dept., Keio Univ., 1914; apptd. Asst., Alma Mater, 1914; sent to Europe and America to study economics, 1919-22; present post since 1922; besides, Chief, Keio Com. & Tech. School since 1929; went abroad to inspect economic condition. Address: 412 Den-en-Toshi, Higashi-Chofu, Omoriku, Tokyo.

Dir., Mitsui Bussan Kaisha; b. Jan., 1885; s. of Tadashiro Mukai. Career: grad., Tokyo Higher Com. School; served as Mgr., Dairen and London Branches of present firm. Address: 433 Shirokane Sankocho, Shibaku, Tokyo.
Dir., Statistics Bureau, State Council, Manchoukuo. Career: present post since 1932. Address: Hsinking.

Baron; Diploma of Imp. Coll., London; Engr. Captain (Naval); Chief, Elec. Sec., Kure Naval Arsenal; b. Oct., 1891 in Tokyo; s. of Shinkichi Mukoyama, Vice-Admiral. Career: grad., Elec. Engrg. Course, Engrg. Coll., Tokyo Imp. Univ.; P.-G. Course, City and Guilds (Engrg.) Coll., South Kensington, London; L'Ecole Superieure d'Electricité (Section de Radio Telegraphie), Paris; succeeded to peerage, 1911; apptd. Chief Naval Ordnance Officer, Lieut.; 1914; sent to England and France, 1918-21; Inspector of Naval Ordnance, 1930; Chief, Elec. Dept., Kure Naval Arsenal, 1930. Address: 7 Yawatadori-Itchome, Kure, Hiroshima-ken.

Bachelor of Sc.; Consulting Engineer; Mng. Dir., Munakata Trading Co.; Dir., Yamamoto Trading Co., Koun Steamship Co., Osaka Hoshi Pharmaceutical Co.; The Sumoca Kabushiki Kaisha; b. Aug., 1901 in Osaka; s. of Masazo Munakata, business man. Career: grad., Lafayette Coll., Eaton; Bethlehem Preparatory School, Bethlehem, Pa., U. S.; returning home, entered business. Address: 740 Sumiyoshimachi, Sumiyoshiku, Osaka.

Hogakushi (LL. B.); b. Sept., 1856 in Yamaguchi-ken; s. of Yoshihiko Munesue. Career: grad., Law Coll., Tokyo Imp. Univ.; former Dir., Elec. Chairman, Dairen Chamber of Com. & Industry; Pres., Bank of Manchuria; Dir., South Manchuria Mining Co. and Dairen Exchange Trust Co.; b. Mar., 1878 in Fukuoka-ken; s. of Rinji Murai, samurai. Career: grad., Law Coll., Tokyo Imp. Univ., 1898; joined South Manchuria Ry. Co.; Mayor of Dairen. Address: 17 Hoshigaura Park, Dairen.

Consul-General at Sydney; b. Jan., 1888 in Aomori-ken. Career: grad., Special Consular Course, Tokyo Higher Com. Judge, Court of Administrative Litigation; b. Aug., 1883 in Tottori-ken; s. of Ken Murakami, official. Career: grad., Law Coll., Tokyo Imp. Address: 12 Aoyama-Minamicho Rokuchome, Akasakaku, Tokyo.

Envoy Extroadinary and Minister Plenipotentiary to Peru; b. Apr., 1889 in Ishikawa-ken; s. of Yoshinori Murakami. Career: grad., Kobe Higher Com. School, 1910; apptd. Address: Ambassade du Japon, Avendia Arequipa 610, Lima, Peru.

Lecturer, Keio Univ.; Author and Translater; b. Apr., 1895 in Tokyo; s. of Koishiro Muramatsu, statesman. Career: grad., Litt. Coll., Tokyo Imp. Address: 2 Kamiyacho, Shibaku, Tokyo.

Mem., National Park Commission; Councillor, Osaka Chamber of Com. & Industry; Pres., Settsu Marine & Fire Ins. Igakuhakushi (M. D.); Head Physician, Tokyo Municipal Komagome and Honjo Hospitals; Lecturer, Medical Coll., Tokyo Imp. Univ.; b. Com. Councillor, Investigation Committee of Noted and Historical Places in Osaka; Councillor, Eastern Culture Assn.; b. June, 1873 in Hyogo-ken; s. of Jirosuke Tsuji, and later adopted by Murotani. Viscount; Ambassador to Turkey; b. Aug., 1882 in Tokyo; s. of Viscount Saneyo Mushakoji. Career: grad., Law Coll., Tokyo Imp. Univ., 1907; apptd. Assembly, League of Nations, Geneva, 1930; attended Disarm. Conf., 1931; Minister to Sweden, Norway, Finland, Denmark; present post since May, 1933. Address: Japanese Embassy, Constantinople, Turkey.

Pres., Jiji Shimpo; Adviser, Kanegafuchi Spinning Co.; b. Mar., 1867 in Gifu-ken; s. of late Kunisaburo Sakuma, M. P.; and later adopted by Matsuemon Muto. Rank: Sr. 3rd; 2nd O. M.; Bungakushi; b. July, 1867 in Kumamoto-ken; s. of late Kazutada Muto, M. P. Career: grad., Litt. Coll., Tokyo Imp. Univ.; apptd. Address: 94 Uchitsuboicho, Kumamoto 3275.

Dir., Dunlop Rubber Co. F. E., Ltd., Kobe; b. Oct., 1868 in Oita-ken; s. of Nobusato Mutoh, samurai. Career: grad., Meiji Gakuin, 1888; Asst. Chief, Kobe Branch, International Assn. of Japan; Hon. Count; b. Mar., 1869 in Osaka; s. of Count Munemitsu Mutsu, statesman. Career: grad., Inner Temple, London (Barrister-at-Law); Minister to Belgium; In diplomatic service, 1894-1916. Address: Yuigahama, Kamakura, Kanagawa-ken.

Igakuhakushi (M. D.); Prof., Tokyo Imp. Univ.; b. Nov., 1876 in Hiroshima-ken; s. of Keisuke Nagai, scholar of Chinese classics. Career: grad., Medical Coll., Tokyo Imp. Address: 70 Minami Nichome, Numabukuro, Nakanoku, Tokyo.
Consul-Gen. at Chientao; b. July, 1883 in Niigata-ken; s. of Yoshitomi Nagai, official. Career: grad., Law Coll., Tokyo Imp. Univ. Address: Consulate-General, Chientao, Manchoukuo.

Address: Official Residence, 1 Urakasumigaseki, Kojimachiku, Tokyo.

Doctor of Economics; b. Dec., 1878 in Tokyo; s. of Iwanojo Nagai, judge. Career: grad., Law Coll., Tokyo Imp. Univ.; Sec., Agrl. and Com. Dept.; Dir., Financial Bureau, Ry. Dept.; Mng.-Dir., Kyochokai; sent to China, 1905; to Europe and America, 1921. Address: 126 Haramachi, Koishikawaku, Tokyo.

Vice-Admiral; Comdr.-in-Chief, Yokosuka Naval Station; b. June, 1880 in Kochi-ken; s. of Harukichi Nagano. Career: grad., Naval Staff Coll.; Pres., Naval Academy, Etajima; Vice-Chief, Naval Gen. Staff; present post since Nov. 1933. Address: 229 Ishikawamachi, Omoriku, Tokyo.

Publisher; Pres., Dai Nippon Yubenkai Kodansha; Pres., Hochi Shimbun-sha; b. Dec., 1878 in Gumma-ken; s. of Yoshio Noma. Career: grad., Gumma-ken Normal School; Special Training School of Teachers, Tokyo Imp. Univ.; served as Teacher of Primary School and Middle School; apptd. School-Inspector, Okinawa-ken; Sec., Tokyo Imp. Univ.; Publisher of magazines "Yuben", "Kodan Club", "Fuji", "Shonen Club", "Fujin Club", "King", "Gendai", "Shojo Club" and "Yonen Club"; publisher of over 400 books; Dir., Nippon Paper Mfg. Co.; Auditor, Chugai Printing Co. Address: 19 Otowacho 3-chome, Koishikawaku, Tokyo.

Hogakuhakushi (D. L.); Prof., Tokyo Imp. Univ.; b. June, 1876 in Kanazawa; s. of Munesada Nomura, samurai. Career: grad., Law Coll., Tokyo Imp. Univ., 1900; entered Home Office; apptd. Asst. Prof., Tokyo Imp. Univ.; promoted Prof., 1908. Address: 15 Ueno Sakuragicho, Shitayaku, Tokyo.

Admiral; Supreme War Councillor; b. Dec., 1877 in Wakayama-ken; s. of Kisaburo Masuda, samurai; adopted by Masatane Nomura. Career: grad., Naval Academy, 1898; dispatched to Austria and Germany; Adjutant, H. M. S. Otowa; Staff, Naval Affairs Bureau, Navy Dept.; Sec. to Navy Minister; Attache, Embassy in U. S.; attended Peace Conf. and Washington Conf.; Staff, Naval Board of Command; Dir., Naval Instruction Bureau; Vice-Chief, Naval Board of Command; Comdr.-in-Chief, Kure and Yokosuka Naval Stations: Comdr., 3rd Squadron, 1932; Comdr.-in-chief, Yokosuka Naval Station 1932-33; present post since Oct. 1933. Address: 854 Sendagaya 5-chome, Shibuyaku, Tokyo.

Musical Critic; b. Sept., 1895 in Osaka. Career: grad., Litt. Course, Keio Univ., 1920; studied music and literature in England, 1921-23; has served Tokyo Nichi-Nichi Shimbun in charge of its musical critic since 1927; Committee, Foreign Music Dept., J. O. A. K., and Prof., History of Music Dept., Teikoku Music School, Tokyo. Address: 45 Gochome, Aoyama-Minamicho, Akasakaku, Tokyo.

Kogakuhakushi (D. E.); Lord-in-Waiting, Kinkei Hall; Pres., Nambu Ry. Co., Tokyo Metro Co. and Ominato Hydro-Elec. Power Co.; Chairman, Board of Dirs., Shonan Elec. Ry. Co.; b. Jan., 1859 in Gifu-ken; s. of Akira Nomura, samurai. Career: grad., Sc. Coll., Tokyo Imp. Univ., 1881; received degree, 1899; Chief Engr., Ry. Dept.; Vice-Pres., Ry. Dept.; Pres., Civil Engrg. Society; Pres., Imp. Ry. Assn.; Pres., South Manchuria Ry. Co.; made inspection tour throughout Europe and America. Address: 35 Shinsakamachi, Akasakaku, Tokyo.

Member, House of Peers; High Tax-Payer in Osaka; Acting Partner, Nomura Gomei Kaisha; Pres., Borneo Rubber Industry Co., Nomura Bank; Mng.-Dir., Osaka Gas Co., Osaka Canal Co., Overseas Industrial Co., Izuo Real Estate & Bldg. Co., Fukushima Spinning Co.; Auditor, Nomura Securities Co., Oji Paper Mfg. Co., Sugimura Warehouse Co., Kyoto Com. Co., Nikka Spinning & Weaving Co.; Adviser, Osakaya Co.; b. Aug. 1878 in Osaka; s. of Joko Nomura; m. Kiku, sister of Jihei Yamada. Career: grad., Osaka High Com. Sch., 1897, entered business; became Pres. to various Companies above mentioned; receivde decoration from French Govt., 1928. Address: 1802 Kobayashi, Sumiyoshimura, Mukogun, Hyogo-ken.

Pres., Toko Jitsugyo K. K.; b. Aug., 1873 in Fukuoka-ken; s. of Katsuyoshi Nonaka, judge. Career: grad., Law Coll., Tokyo Imp. Univ., 1898; Commr., Yokohama Customs, 1899; sent to Australia and India to inspect customs affairs; Sec., Finance Office; Supt., Kobe Customs; Dir., Monopoly Bureau, 1918-25; present post since 1928. Address: 16 Kamiyamacho Shibuyaku, Tokyo.
Lawyer; b. Oct., 1863 in Okayama; s. of Dosen Nose, physician. Career: grad., Law School, Justice Office; former Dir., Nagoya Appeal Court. Address: 25 Minami-Kojiyacho, Nakaku, Nagoya.

Prop., Nozawa Shoten; Asbestos-Slate Mfr.; Dealer in Building Materials; b. June, 1871 in Shiga-ken; s. of Tazaemon Tonoike, brewer. Career: served at Raw Silk Dept., and Mogi Shoten, Yokohama; left there, 1896, and went to Brazil; returning home began Indigo Import, 1897, and Asbestos-Slate Import, 1906, at Kobe; established Nippon Asbestos-Slate Mfg. Co., 1913; elected Mem., Kobe Chamber of Com. & Industry, 1921; Acting Partner, Asbestos-Slate Co.; Dir., Kobe Raw-Silk Co. and Higo Filature Co. Address: 2 of 11 Kitanagasa-dori Sanchome, Kobeku, Kobe.

Pres., Oana Elec. & Mfg. Co.; Mng.-Dir., Nippon Wireless Telegraph & Telephone Co.; Dir., Nippon Carbonic Acid Gas Co.; Auditor, Nippon Bean-Mash Co.; b. Apr., 1881 in Nagano-ken; s. of late Yasaburo Oana. Career: grad., Engrg. Coll., Tokyo Imp. Univ., 1905; studied at Technische Hoch Schule, Karlsruhe, Baden, Germany, 1910-13; Engr., Tokyo Elec. Power Co., 1905-07; Chief Elec. Engr., Asano Cement Co., 1907-09; Chief Engr., and Mgr., Fukuhaku Elec. Ry. Co. (present Toho Elec. Power Co.), 1909-10; established Oana Seisakusho, 1914; Lecturer, Waseda Univ. Address: 5 Hashiba-Nichome, Asakusaku, Tokyo.

Asst. Mng. Editor and Financial Editor of Chugai Shogyo Shimpo; b. Dec., 1889 in Shimane-ken; s. of Ichiro Obama. Career: grad., Polit. Dept., Waseda Univ.; became Sec. to Speaker of House of Representatives, 1915; joined Masuda Trading Co., 1917; Editorial Staff of Chugai Shogyo Shimpo, 1921. Address: 388 Unokimachi, Omoriku, Tokyo.

Dir., Kuhara Gomei Kaisha; b. Dec., 1884 in Hiroshima-ken; s. of Shingoro Obata, business man. Career: grad., Econ. Dept., Keio Univ.; Non-Commissioned Officer, Agrl., Com. & Industry Dept., Korean Govt., 1909-10; joined Oriental Development Co., 1910 and resigned, 1917; joined Kuhara Gomei Kaisha, 1917; in service of Mgr., Kuhara Shoji Kaisha; Rep. Dir., Dairen Central Land Co.; went to U. S. to adjust Kuhara Iron Foundry, U. S. and on trading business. Address: 49 Kitayacho, Shibuyaku, Tokyo.

Dir., S. M. R. Co.; Head, Tokyo Branch Office; b. Aug., 1885 in Fukuoka-ken. Career: grad., Law Coll., Tokyo Imp. Univ., 1911; passed Higher Civil Service Exam.; joined present firm, same year; sent to Germany and America for study 2 years; Chief, General Affairs Section, Tokyo Branch of the firm, 1919; Head, Accountants Section of same, 1925; Auditor, 1927; made official tour to Europe and America 8 months; Head, Shanghai Office, 1929; as Representative. S. M. R., became Mng.-Dir., Hanshin Harbor Co., Dir., Nichiman Warehouse Co., Shantung Mining Co., Shoko Glass Co., Toyo Nitrogen Industry Co. Address: 2 Hirakawacho Gochome, Kojimachiku, Tokyo.

Viscount; Mem., House of Peers; Parl. Vice-Minister of Agr. & Forestry Dept.; b. 1889 in Tokyo-fu; adopted s. of Nobutoshi Oda. Career: grad., Law Coll., Kyoto Imp. Univ., 1915; entered Bank of Japan, same year; toured China & Europe; served in Tokyo Asahi Press; Sec. to Ry. Minister, 1926; became Mem., House of Peers, same year; Foreign Councillor, 1929; present post since 1933. Address: Yakuoji-machi, Ichigaya, Ushigomeku, Tokyo.

M. P.; Pres., Jiyu News Agency; b. Nov., 1890 in Chiba-ken; s. of Kikujiro Odaka. Career: grad., Polit. Dept., Nippon Univ.; compiled "History of Seiyukai Party"; engaged in newspaper and publication business; entered present firm and gradually promoted present post; sent to Diet from Chiba-ken. Address: 771 Iriyamazu, Iriaraimachi, Omoriku, Tokyo.

M. P.; Dir., Yamato Rubber Cultivation Co.; Auditro, Sumatra Gum Co.; b. Apr., 1885 in Aichi-ken; s. of Chosaemon Ogasahara, landlord. Career: grad., Law Coll., Tokyo Imp. Univ.; entered Taiwan Bank; served as Mgr., Branch offices; Asst. to Pres. of same bank; Mng. Dir., China & Southern Bank. Address: 1557 Ikebukuro, Sanchome, Toshimaku, Tokyo.

Count; Mem., House of Peers; b. Mar., 1885 in Tokyo; s. of Tadanobu Ogasawara, Mem., House of Peers. Career: grad., Peers' Academy; then studied at Cambridge; apptd. Master of Ceremonies, to H. M. the Emperor; Councillor, War Dept.; Pres., Nat. Census Board; Mem., Administrative System Deliberation Committee; Pres., Japan-Czechoslovakia and Japan-Roumania Assns.; Mem., Ry. Council and Cultural Work Committee toward China. Address: 17 Kawadacho, Ichigaya, Ushigomeku, Tokyo.

Igakuhakushi (M. D.); Prof., Tokyo Imp. Univ.; b. Jan., 1883; s. of Koreyoshi Ogata, physician. Career: grad., 3rd Higher School, 1903; Medical Coll., Tokyo Imp. Univ., 1908; went to Germany for study, 1910-13; apptd., Asst. Prof., Tokyo Imp. Univ., 1913; Prof., Pathological Anatomy, of same. Address: 50 Sendagicho, Hongoku, Tokyo.

Hogakuhakushi (D. L.); M. P.; Adviser, Minseito; b. June, 1876 in Okayama-ken; s. of Tomoaki Ogawa, physician. Career: grad., Law Coll., Tokyo Imp. Univ., 1903; apptd. Asst. Prof., Kyoto Imp. Univ., 1904 and promoted Prof., same Univ.; Head of Econ. Dept., same Univ., 1922-24; elected to Diet from Okayama-ken 5 times; Dir., Minseito; Vice-Minister of Finance in Hamaguchi Cabinet. Address: 32 Sakurayamacho, Nakanoku, Tokyo.

Mayor of Dairen; b. Nov., 1883 in Tokyo; s. of Yajiro Ogawa. Career: grad., Law Coll., Tokyo Imp. Univ., 1911; entered Home Office, serving in Home Dept., Nagano-ken, 1912; Headman, Shimo-Iwai-gun District; Procurator, Osaka-fu; Councillor, Kwantung Gov't; Chief, Industry Section, Home Dept., same gov't.; present post since 1931. Address: Dairen Municipal Office, Satsumacho, Dairen.

Asst. Prof., Tokyo Univ. of Litt. & Science; b. Dec., 1880 in Nagano-ken; s. of Souemon Ogihara, Landlord. Career: grad., Tokyo Higher Normal School; sent to Germany by Education Authorities for ethical study 2 years; Teacher, Shiga-ken Normal School; Lecturer, Tokyo Girls' Higher Normal School; Prof., Tokyo Higher Normal School. Address: 151 Horinouchimachi, Toshimaku, Tokyo.

M. A. (U. S.); Adviser, Okura-Gumi; Dir., Haramachi Spinning Co. and Mikado Real Estate Co.; b. Mar., 1879 in Kanagawa-ken; s. of Kyubei Ogino, business man. Career: grad., Law Dept., Keio Univ., 1903, Washington Univ., U. S., 1904 and Berlin Univ., 1905; Sec. to Sec.-Gen. of Taiwan; Editorial Writer, Nippon Shimbun and Osaka Mainichi; joined Okura-Gumi and served as Head of its Taiwan Branch, 1915-19; then present post. Address: 291 Toyooka Itchome, Tsurumiku, Yokohama.

Igakuhakushi (M. D.); Prof., Nagoya Medical Coll.; b. Jan., 1875 in Nagano-ken; s. of Sadahei Oguchi, merchant. Career: grad., Saisei Gakusha; served Sino-Japanese War as Surgeon-Sub.-Lieut., 1895; Surgeon Captain during Russo-Japanese War, 1904-05; promoted Surgeon-Major, 1911; Instructor, Army Medical School, 1911; Prof., South Manchuria Medical School, 1912; sent to Europe for study 2 years; bestowed degree, 1916; Dean and Prof., Aichi Medical Coll., 1926; present post since 1931. Address: 22 Hazamamachi, Nakaku, Nagoya.

M. P.; Pharmacist; b. May, 1870 in Aichi-ken; s. of Kiroku Oguchi, druggist. Career: grad., Tokyo School of Pharmacy; Med. Dept., Tokyo Imp. Univ.; apptd. Mayor of Toyohashi; Mem., Aichi-ken Prefectural Assembly; elected to Diet 7 times; Dir., Toyohashi Elec. Co.; Pres., Toyohashi Shimbun; Mem., Toyohashi Chamber of Com.; Parl. Vice-Minister of Finance. Address: 89 Funamachi-Otsu, Toyohashi-shi.

Auditor, Dai Nippon Sugar Mfg. Co., Toho Colliery Co.; Dir., Shuseisha; b. Mar., 1867 in Fukuoka-ken; e. s. of Kazuhisa Ogura. Career: grad., Tokyo Law Coll. (present Chuo Univ.); entered Dai Nippon Sugar Mfg. Co.; promoted Secretary, then Auditor of same; besides has been connected with several other firms. Address: 16 Nakacho, Ushigomeku, Tokyo.

Dir. General, Sumitomo Goshi-Kaisha; Chairman, Board of Dirs., Sumitomo Besshi Mine, Sumitomo Collieries, Sumitomo Steel-Tube & Copper Works, Sumitomo Steel Works, Sumitomo Elec. Wire & Cable Works, Sumitomo Fertilizer Works, Sumitomo Trust Co., Sumitomo Life Ins. Co., Sumitomo Warehouse Co., Sumitomo Building Co., Osaka North Harbour Co., Tosa-Yoshinogawa Hydro-Elec. Power Co., Fuso Marine & Fire Ins. Co.; Dir., Sumitomo Bank, Fujikura Elec. Wire & Cable Co., Osaka Shosen Kaisha, Chin-fu Ry. Co., To-a Kogyo Co., Japan Elec. Bond & Share Co.; Auditor, Kyushu Power-Transmission Co., South Manchuria Ry. Co.; b. Mar., 1875 in Kanazawa; s. of Masamichi Ogura. Career: grad., Law Coll., Tokyo Imp. Univ.; apptd. Commr., Home Office and Supt. Commr. of Civil Engrg. of same, 1897; then apptd. Councillor. Yamaguchi-ken; resigned, 1899 to join Sumitomo Firm; went to Europe and America for commercial inspection, 1900; returned, 1902; became Mgr., Kobe Branch Office, Sumitomo Firm, Sumitomo Bank and Sumitomo Warehouse Co.; transferred to Asst.-Mgr., Sumitomo Head Office; promoted, Mgr., same office, 1913; Mng. Dir., 1921; Dir. General, Sumitomo Goshi-Kaisha, 1930. Address: 24 Aioi-dori Itchome, Sumiyoshiku, Osaka.

Rigakuhakushi (D. Sc.); Asst. Prof., Tokyo Imp. Univ.; b. June, 1895 in Sendai; s. of Chotaro Ogura. Career: grad., Faculty of Science, Tokyo Imp. Univ.; 1919; apptd. Lecturer, Tokyo Imp. Univ., 1919; Asst. Prof. of same, 1927; studied in England, Germany and U. S., 1928-30. Address: 93 Yushima-Shinhanacho, Hongoku, Tokyo.

Hogakushi (LL. B.); Judge; Pres., Tokyo Court of Appeal; b. Jan., 1877 in Niigata-ken; s. of Keijiro Tanaka; adopted by Tomotada Ohara. Career: grad., Law Coll., Tokyo Imp. Univ., 1902; apptd. Judicial Probationer, same year; Judge, Tokyo District Court, 1904; Public Procurator, Chiba Local Court, same year; same, Tokyo District Court, 1908; Councillor, Dept. of Justice, 1919; Chief Public Procurator, Yokohama Local Court, 1920; made official tour through U. S. and Europe, 1921-22; Chief Public Procurator, Tokyo District Court, 1921; same, Nagasaki Court of Appeal, 1923; Public Procurataor, Supreme Court, 1924; Vice-Minister of Justice, 1927; present post since 1931. Address: 23 Nakacho, Nakanoku, Tokyo.

Hogakushi; Public Procurator, Supreme Court; b. Apr., 1890 in Simane-ken; s. of Junnosuke Ohara, engr. Career: grad., Law Coll., Tokyo Imp. Univ., 1914; entered judicial service; apptd. Judge, 1916; then Councillor and Sec., Justice Dept.; present post since Mar., 1932. Address: 2164 Oisegahara, Omoriku, Tokyo.

Vice-Foreign Minister, Manchoukuo; b. 1893 in Gifu-ken. Career: grad., Law Coll., Tokyo Imp. Univ., 1918; apptd. Diplomatic Probationer, 1st Class Sec. of Legation; Consul-Gen. at Harbin, 1931; apptd. present post, 1932. Address: Foreign Affairs Bureau, Changchun, Manchoukuo.

Mem., House of Peers; Adviser, Tokyo Chamber of Com. & Industry; Chairman, Board of Directors, Chosen Kogyo Co. Ltd. Pres., Ohashi Honten, Hakubunkan; Dir., Mitsui Trust Co., Chosen Ry. Co., Daiichi Mutual Life Ins. Co., Hokuetsu Paper Mfg. Co., Oji Seishi Co.; Auditor, Dai Nippon Brewery Co., Mitsui Bank; Supt., Ohashi Library; b. July, 1863; s. of Sahei Ohashi, Echigo. Career: studied at Dojinsha; published Etsusa Mainichi Shimbun (present Hokuetsu Shimpo); established Hakubunkan; founded Ohashi Library; elected to Diet from Tokyo, 1902; nominated Mem., House of Peers, 1926. Address: 43 Kamirokubancho, Kojimachiku, Tokyo.

Mgr., General Affairs Dept., Asahi Glass Co.; b. Apr., 1890 in Okinawa-ken; s. of late Yoshishige Ohnaga. Career: grad., Law Coll., Tokyo Imp. Univ., 1915; joined present firm, 1916; made inspection tour to Europe and America, 1924-25; present post since 1929. Address: 276 Shirokane Sankocho, Shibaku, Tokyo.

Mayor of Yokohama; b. July, 1887 in Kagawa-ken; s. of Michiji Ohnishi. Career: grad., Law Coll., Tokyo Imp. Univ.; apptd. Chief, Police Dept., Kagawa-ken; Sec. and Councillor. Chosen Govt.; Chief, Home Affairs Dept., Keisho-Hokudo, Chosen; made inspection tour to Europe, 1923; Sec., Reconstruction Bureau, 1924; Deputy-Mayor of Tokyo, 1926; same of Yokohama, 1929; present post since June, 1931. Address: 10 Oimatsucho, Yokohama.

Mgr. and Dir., Asahi Glass Co.; b. Apr., 1884 in Tokyo; s. of Nizo Ohno. Career: grad., Ceramic Industry Course, Tokyo Higher Tech. Coll.; joined Asahi Glass Co.; apptd. Factory Dir., same firm and promoted to present post; Lecturer, Tokyo Higher Tech. School, Meiji Semmon Gakko, Engrg. Coll. of Kyushu Imp. Univ.; Mgr., Dai Nippon Cerematic Industry Assn.; Mem., Tobata Chamber of Com. & Industry; Mem., Yokohama Chamber of Com. & Industry. Address: 1336 Higashi 1-chome, Magome, Omoriku, Tokyo.

Minister on Waiting List; b. Mar., 1879 in Tokyo; s. of Naosuke Ohno. Career: grad., Law Coll., Tokyo Imp. Univ., 1904; Minister to Austria and Hungary. Address: 10 Komagome-Nishikitamachi, Hongoku, Tokyo.

LL. D.; German Consul-General at Kobe; b. Oct., 1868 in Holstein, Germany; n. German; s. of Johannes Ohrt, Commisisoner of Woods & Forests. Career: grad., High School at Rendsburg, Univs. of Munich, Berlin, Kiel; entered German Foreign Service, 1893; Student Interpreter, Tokyo, 1893-98; Vice-Consul at Yokohama, 1898-1906; Sec., German Embassy at Tokyo, 1907-11; Consul at Nagasaki, 1911-13; Consul at Kobe, 1913-14; Consul-General at Yokohama, 1921-23; present post since 1923. Address: 115 Higashimachi, Kobe.

Vice-Pres., Nippon Yusen Kaisha; b. 1874 in Fukui-ken; s. of Fumoto Ohtani, samurai. Career: grad., Tokyo Higher Com. School, 1896; immediately joined N. Y. K. and served in its offices at London, Hongkong, Singapore, Calcutta, New York; travelled in interests of N. Y. K. to Australia, Malay Peninsula, Dutch Indies, British India, French Indo-China, Siam, Philippines, etc.; attended Int'l conferences in London, Paris, Gothenburg, etc. as Delegate of Japanese interests, 1920-23; Mng. Dir., 1923; present post since 1929. Address: 275 Chojamaru, Osaki, Shinagawaku, Tokyo.

Mgr., Gen. Affairs Dept. and Executive & Administrative Dept., Sumitomo Goshi Kaisha; Dir., Aluminium-Sumitomo Co., Nippon Sheet Glass Co., Kyushu Hydro-Elec. Power Co., Victor Talking Machine Co. of Tokyo, etc.; b. Sept., 1884 in Tokyo; s. of Gennojo Nagai. Career: grad., Elec. Engrg. Course, Engrg. Coll., Tokyo Imp. Univ.; apptd. Engr., Elec. Bureau, Communications Dept., 1911; Lecturer, Engrg. & Tech. Dept., Waseda Univ., 1911; joined Sumitomo Firm, 1918; apptd. Mgr., Executive & Administrative Dept., 1925; Mgr., Gen. Affairs Dept., 1930. Address: 1447 Shironomae, Mikagemachi, Mukogun, Hyogo-ken.

Mem., House of Peers; Baron; Retired Gen.; b. Sept., 1863 in Yamaguchi-ken; s. of Matahei Oi. Career: grad., Military Academy, 1883 and Military Coll., 1888; Mem., General Staff Office; Staff Officer, 2nd Army; Instructor, Military Coll.; Sec. to War Minister; Attaché to Embassy in Berlin; Comdr., Infantry 19th Brigade; same, 12th Division; same, 8th Division; Comdr., Vladivostok Expeditionary Force; Supreme War Councillor. Address: 74 Izumi Wadaborimachi, Suginamiku, Tokyo.

Mayor of Nagoya; Lawyer; Adviser, Nagoya Chamber of Com. & Industry; b. May, 1867; s. of Tazo Oiwa, Aichi-ken. Career: grad., Tokyo Hogakuin, 1891; elected to Diet from Aichi-ken, 1915. Address: 74 Minami-Isemachi Sanchome, Nakaku, Nagoya.

Prof., Senshu Univ., etc.; b. June, 1877; s. of Shinko Ojima, vassal of Shogun. Career: grad., Meiji Gakuin and studied law at Hogakuin; apptd. Mem., Executive Commission of Peace Treaties, 1912, and sent to Geneva, Switzerland, as attendant of Japanese Delegates to 2nd Assembly of League of Nations; Non-Regular Staff of Com. & Industry Office 7 years; engaged in writing books and in teaching at several schools. Address: 56 Shotomachi, Shibuyaku, Tokyo.

Pres., Dairen Suburban Real Estate Co.; Dir., Manchuria Cultural Assn.; b. Mar., 1858 in Miye-ken; s. of Kaheiji Oka, fish wholesaler. Career: apptd. Pres., Tsu-shi 105th National Bank, 1879; Pres., Miye-ken Chamber of Com., 1881; joined Mitsui Bussan Kaisha, 1887; Mgr., Tokyo Elec. Light Co., 1894; went to China, 1901, and engaged in shipping business between Japan and China; served World War, at Tsingtao, 1914; Pres., Dairen Credit Bank, 1924; in employ of S. Manchuria Ry. Co. Address: 2 Yamashirocho, Dairen.

Mem., House of Peers; Teikoku News Agency; Councillor, Minseito; b. Apr., 1868; s. of Kisaburo Itami, Okayama-ken and later adopted by Yasutaka Oka, samurai of Tokyo. Career: grad., Law Coll., Tokyo Imp. Univ., 1891; Gov., Akita-ken and Tottori-ken; Dir., Police Bureau; Metropolitan Police Chief; nominated Mem., House of Peers, 1914. Address: 53 Aoyama-Minamicho Gochome, Akasakaku, Tokyo.

Hogakuhakushi (D. L.); Journalist; Chairman, Board of Dirs., Osaka Mainichi and Tokyo Nichi-Nichi; b. Sept., 1873 in Osaka; s. of Yoshisuye Oka. Career: grad., Polit. Dept., Law Coll., Tokyo Imp. Univ., 1898; apptd. Councillor, Legislation Bureau; same, Dept. of Agr.; Chief, Industrial and Commercial Section of same, 1913; Dir., Industrial and Com. Bureau, Dept. of Agrl. and Com.; upon resigning from govt. service, 1918, apptd. Japanese Government Representative to Paris Peace Conference, and became Mem. of Committee for Codification of Labor Charter of Versailles Treaty in Paris, 1918; also apptd. Mem. of Committee for the Revision of Treaty of Commerce; representing Tokyo Gov't., attended First International Labor Conference at Washington, 1919; Gov't. Repr. at Paris and Geneva for revision of economic boycott clauses in League of Nation's Pact; visited China, South Seas, Europe and America to investigate financial and economic conditions; contributed in making of Laws on Trade Unions, Factory and Petty Insurance; became Dir., Osaka Mainichi Pub. Co., 1927; Editor, Tokyo Nichi-Nichi. Address: 276 Shirokane Sankocho, Shibaku, Tokyo.

M. P.; Pres., Hokkaido Agr. & Forestry Co.; Corn-Chandler; b. Dec., 1877; s. of Inohei Okada, Ishikawa-ken. Career: toured Manchuria; elected to Diet 3 times; Mem., Hokkaido Assembly. Address: Ebetsumachi, Sapporogun, Hokkaido.

Consul-General at Honolulu; b. Apr., 1882 in Yamagata-ken; s. of Kanenobu Okada, official. Career: studied at Tokyo School of Foreign Languages and Waseda Univ.; Commr., Foreign Office; 3rd Class Sec., Embassy in London; 2nd Class Sec., Legation in Sweden; Consul at Antung; Consul-Gen. at Chientao; present post since Nov., 1932. Address: Consulate-General of Japan, 1742, Nu uanu Ave., Honolulu, Hawaii.

Retired Admiral; Supreme War Councillor; b. Jan., 1868; s. of late Kitota Okada, Fukui-ken. Career: grad., Naval Academy, 1889; Comdr., H. M. S. Kasuga and Kashima; Chief, Personal Bureau; Chief, Saseho Naval Arsenal; Vice-Minister of Navy; Navy Minister, 1927-29. Address: 875 Tsunohazu, Yodobashi-ku, Tokyo.

Privy Councillor; Mem., Educational Council; b. May, 1864; s. of late Ryoichi Okada, samurai of Kakekawa Clan. Career: grad., Litt. Coll., Tokyo Imp. Univ., 1889; Sec., Education Dept.; Councillor, same; Pres., Kyoto Imp. Univ.; Vice-Minister of Education; nominated Mem., House of Peers; Education Minister in Takaaki Kato Cabinet; Pres. Toyo Univ. Address: 125 Haramachi, Koishikawaku, Tokyo.

Pres., Kobe Nichi-Nichi Shimbun-Sha; b. Aug., 1884 in Shiga-ken; s. of Kumekichi Okada, landlord. Career: grad., Waseda Univ.; upon grad. joined Kobe Shimbun; founded Shinko Nippo, daily (present Kobe Nichi-Nichi Shimbun), 1917. Address: 15 Rikumaecho, Suma-ku, Kobe.

b. Mar., 1866 in Shimane-ken; s. of Hisajiro Okada, business man. Career: grad., Law Coll., Tokyo Imp. Univ.; Dir., Nippon Yusen Kaisha, Sumitomo Warehouse Co., Sumitomo Bank, Sugimura Warehouse Co. Address: Uchide, Seidomura, Mukogun, Hyogo-ken.

M. P.; Adviser, Seiyukai; Mem., Economic Resources Investigation Committee; b. Nov., 1878; s. of Kimpei Okada, samurai of Okayama Clan. Career: grad., Law Coll., Tokyo Imp. Univ., 1903; Gov., Nagasaki-ken, Saitama-ken, Nagano-ken and Kumamoto-ken; Dir., Police Bureau, Home Office; elected to Diet twice from Okayama-ken; Deputy-Mayor of Tokyo. Address: 31 Nagatacho-Nichome, Kojimachiku, Tokyo.

Mng.-Dir., Sumitomo Bank; Dir., Buzen Bank; b. Dec., 1883 in Fukuoka-ken. Career: grad., Tokyo Higher Com. School, 1906; joined Sumitomo Bank and served as Mgr. of its Shimonoseki, Nagoya, and Tokyo Branches; then promoted present post. Address: 102 Nango-cho, Nishinomiya, Hyogo-ken.

Pres., Federation of Poulty-Raising Union; Lord-in-waiting, Kinkei Hall; b. Sept., 1871 in Osaka-fu; grandson of Hanzo Okamoto, Shinto Priest. Career: grad., Law Coll., Tokyo Imp. Univ., 1898; apptd. official, Agrl. & Com. Dept.; Commr. and Sec., Forestry and Supt. Bureaus; Dir., Forestry Com. Affairs, War Ins. and Agrl. Bureaus; Vice-Minister of Agrl. & Com.; Dir., Patent Bureau; attended 3rd Labor Conf. as Gov't. Delegate. Address: 1613 Araijuku, Omoriku, Tokyo.

Dir., Yamaguchi Higher Com. School; b. Dec., -1880; s. of Jirouemon Okamoto, farmer. Career: grad., Law Coll., Kyoto Imp. Univ.; apptd. Teacher, Okayama-ken Pref. Com. School; Lecturer, 6th Higher School; Dir., Ibaragi-ken Pref. Com. Sch.; Sec., Kyoto Imp. Univ.; Prof.; Kyoto Higher Sericultural Sch.; Dir., Wakayama Higher Com. Sch. Address: 2303 Shinmichi, Yamaguchi City.

Pres., Toho Gas Co. and Nagoya Gas Co.; Vice-Pres., Tokyo Gas Co.; Dir., Toho Elec. Power Co.; Auditor, Nagoya Pier Warehouse Co. and Nippon Motorcar Road Co.; Adviser, Kyushu Gas Co., Seibu Gas Co. and Godo Gas Co.; b. Apr., 1878 in Aichi-ken; s. of Tei Okamoto, samurai. Career: grad., Engrg. Coll., Tokyo Imp. Univ., 1930; inherited family estate, 1911; Mng. Dir., Toho Elec. Power Co. Address: 1070, Chitosemura, Funabashi, Tokyo Shigai.

Chief, 2nd Section, Europe & America Bureau, Foreign Office; b. Aug., 1892 in Kyoto-fu; s. of Buzaemon Okamoto. Career: grad., Law Coll., Tokyo Imp. Univ., 1917; apptd. attaché, Japanese Embassy, London; Staff, 1st Section, Europe & America Bureau; Second Sec., Japanese Embassy, Wash.; Consul at Seattle; present post since Apr., 1831. Address: 1 Tamachi-Hatchome, Shibaku, Tokyo.

Mng.-Dir., Naigai Mining Co., Korean Raw Silk Co., Tokyo Shokai, Kyokuto Condensed Milk Co., Mochikoshi Gold Mining Co., Eido Mining Co., Hishisan Co., Kyodo Gum Co.; Auditor, Yanase Automobile Co., Nihon Explosive Mfg. Co., Chugai Percussion-cup Co., Nihon High Grade Lacquer & Paints Co.; b. Sept., 1870 in Shiga-ken; s. of Shigai Okano, business man. Career: grad., Osaka Higher Com. School; joined Mitsui Bussan Kaisha; Mgr., Nagoya Branch of same; Dir., Nagoya Weaving Mill Co., Toyodo Weaving Machinery Co., Dai Nippon Mining Co.; Pres., Yashu Mino Co., Koshiji Mine Co.; Mgr., Japan-China Spinning Co., Int'l Wireless Telephone Co.; Pres., Nichi-Ran Trading Co.; Auditor, Nagoya Pottery Co. Address: 1 Kasumicho, Azabuku, Tokyo.

Acting Partner, Okawa Gomei Kaisha; Pres., Chosen Ry. Co.; Pres., Japan Art Paper Co., etc.; b. Oct., 1860 in Saitama-ken; s. of Shuzo Okawa, Samurai. Career: engaged in paper mfg. industry and several sorts of productive industry in Japan. Address: 367 Nazato-machi, Takinogawaku, Tokyo.

Vice-Pres., Nagoya Chamber of Com. & Industry; Acting Partner, Okaya & Co.; Dir., Nippon Savings Bank, Aichi Bank, Fukuju Life Ins. Co.; b. Aug., 1887; s. of late Sosuke Okaya. Career: inherited family estate, 1926. Address: 50 Ebisumachi, Nakaku, Nagoya.

Pres., Tokyo Stock Exchange; Dir., 3rd Bank, Chiyoda Trust Co. and Taisha-Miyajima Ry. Co.; Pres., Shoyo Shimpo; b. June, 1874 in Shimane-ken; s. of Mataichiro Katsube; adopted by Umpei Okazaki. Career: grad., Law Coll., Tokyo Imp. Univ., 1900; apptd. Proculator, Forestry Bureau; Councillor and Sec., Agrl. & Com. Dept.; Chief, Corr. Section; Agrl. & Com. Minister's Secretariat; Chief Sec. of Cabinet; present post since 1918. Address: 68 Gotanda, Shinagawaku, Tokyo.

Mem., House of Peers; Adviser, Seiyukai; b. Mar., 1854; s. of Gakuya Nagasaka, samurai, and later adopted by Bunzaemon Okazaki. Career: studied in America; entered Communications Dept.; Adviser, Ichibei Furukawa; Dir., Furukawa Mining Co., Chuo Shimbun, Daido Elec. Power Co., Keihan Elec. Ry. Co.; elected to Diet 11 times; Dir., Seiyukai, 1924; Agr. & Forestry Minister, 1925. Address: 3034 Oi Kashima-machi, Shinagawa-ku, Tokyo.

M. P.; Pres., Karafuto Nichi-Nichi Shimbun; Pres., Tokyo Drugs Co.; b. Mar., 1885 in Shimane-ken; e. s. of Kinzo Okishima. Career: grad., Law Dept., Nihon Univ., 1906; Mng.-Dir., Saghalien United Transportation Co., Toyokita Saw Mill; Auditor, Saghalien Pharmaceutical Co., Saghalien Elec. Co.; Special Mem., Toyohara Chamber of Com. & Industry; sent to Diet twice from Shimane-ken. Address: 58 Daimachi, Akasaka, Tokyo.

Marquis; Mem., House of Peers; Mem., Meiji Restoration History Editing Office; Lord-in-waiting, Kinkei Hall.; Dir., Japan Red Cross Society; b. Apr., 1866; s. of late Toshimichi Okubo, statesman. Career: grad., Yale Univ., U. S.; studied Univs., Halle, Heiderberg and Berlin; Sec., Home Minister, 1896; Gov., Oita-ken, Tottori-ken and Osaka-fu. Address: 5 Minami-Igacho, Yotsuyaku, Tokyo.

Vocalist; b. June, 1903 in Sapporo, Hokkaido; s. of Ryohei Okuda, physician. Career: studied at Vocal Dept., Tokyo Academy of Music; grad., Santa Cecilia Musical Academy, Rome, Italy, 1928; then studied at Berlin Academy of Music; received Art Medal at Philharmony Concour, Rome, 1927; apptd., Prof., Vocal Dept., Tokyo Musical Academy, 1929; invited to Academie Santa Cecilia Concert, 1932; received Silver Medal and Diploma at Int'l Musical Concour, Wien, same year. Address: care Dr. Kiyoka Sakurai, 5040 Oimachi, Shinagawaku, Tokyo.

Pres. and Dir., Kohoku Middle School, Okayama-ken; b. July, 1875 in Okayama-ken; s. of Tsuneyoshi Okuda, samurai. Career: grad., Keio Univ., 1895; passed Higher Civil Service Exam., 1898; entered Foreign Office, 1899; passed Diplomatic Service Exam., 1899; served as Sub.-Consul, Jinsen and Tientsin; as Sec., Chargé d'Affaires, Austria and Switzerland; Mem., Commercial Treaty Revision Committee, 1910; Consul at Hankow, 1911; Consul-General at Humburg, 1912-1915; 1st Sec., Embassy, Paris, 1915-17. Address: 354 Minamigata, Okayama City.

Mem., Legislative Investigation Commission; Repr. Dir., Daido Match Co.; b. Nov., 1880 in Kumamoto-ken; s. of Hanbu Okumura, landlord. Career: grad., Law Coll., Tokyo Imp. Univ., 1905; entered Finance Office; joined Mitsubishi Goshi Kaisha, 1906-32; was Master, Elementary School and Post-Office, 1910-14; sent to Moscow as Mem., Delegation for negotiating on Russo-Japanese Problems. Address: 81 Sakuragaoka, Shibuya, Tokyo.

Pres., Nippon Steel Foundry; Okumura & Co.; b. Oct., 1872 in Fukuoka-ken; s. of Rihei Okumura, brewer. Career: grad., Fukuoka Middle School; Vice-Pres., Osaka Steel Industry Assn. Address: 19 Maruyamadori-Nichome, Sumiyoshiku, Osaka.

Baron; Mem., House of Peers; Adviser, South Manchuria Ry. Co.; b. July, 1882 in Tokyo; s. of Baron Heizo Okura, Lieut.-Gen. Career: grad., Engrg. Coll., Tokyo Imp. Univ., 1904; apptd., Engr., Ry. Dept.; joined South Manchuria Ry. Co. being apptd. Mgr., Traffic Dept., then Dir. and Mgr., Planning & Development Dept.; resigned same, 1931. Address: c. o. South Manchuria Ry. Co., Hoshigaura, Dairen.

Baron; Pres., Okura-Gumi, Imperial Hotel, France Trading Co., Okura Paper Mfg. Co., Tokai Paper Stock Co.; Dir., Locomotive Mfg. Co., Nippon Elec. Battery Co., Niitaka Sugar Refinery Co., Dai Nippon Brewery Co., Imperial Theatre, Akita Timber Co.; Auditor, Nippon Chemical Industry Co., Ujigawa Elec. Co., Nippon Shoes Mfg. Co.; Councillor, Nippon Automobile Co., Okura Marine & Fire Ins. Co., Nanbu Gum Mfg. Co., Japan Industrial Club; b. June, 1882; s. of Kihachiro Okura, business man. Address: 30 Shimonibancho, Kojimachiku, Tokyo.

Bill Broker; b. Mar., 1873 in Yamagata-ken; s. of Jutaro Okuyama, official. Career: grad., Keio Univ., 1901; joined Bank of Japan and Konoike Bank; opened bill-broker business at Fushimimachi, Osaka, 1909. Address: Tantakabashi, Sumiyoshi, near Kobe.

Supreme Adviser, Japanese Embassy to Manchoukuo; b. Nov., 1876 in Yamagata-ken; s. of Chozo Okuyama. Career: grad., Law Coll., Tokyo Imp. Univ., 1903; apptd. Diplomatic Probationer in Austria; Councillor, Foreign Office; Sec. of Embassy; Commr., Foreign Office; Chief, Sections of Personnel and Corr.; Foreign Minister's Secretariat; Vice-Chief, League of Nations Secretariat; Minister to Greece. Address: Komagome-Sanchome, Toshimaku, Tokyo.

b. Jan., 1896 in Ibaragi-ken; s. of Enji Omi. Career: grad., English Litt. Course, Tokyo Imp. Univ., 1920; diplomatic service as 2nd Sec. of Legations at Mukden, Washington, Santiago, Peking, Teheran; Consul at Tientsin, 1929. Address: 1443 Shimo-Kitazawa Nishi-Sanya, Setagayaku, Tokyo.

Comdr., Maizuru Fortress; Vice-Admiral; b. July, 1879; s. of Shusuke Ominato, samurai, Yamagata-ken. Career: grad., Naval Coll., 1901; Comdr., H. M. S. Yamashiro; Chief of Staff, Combined Fleet; Pres., Naval Coll. Address: Nakamaizurumachi, Kyoto-fu.

Baron; Mem., House of Peers; b. Aug., 1883 in Tokyo; s. of late Baron Shoichi Omori, Grand Master to Empress Dowager. Career: grad., Polit. Course, Law Coll., Tokyo Imp. Univ., 1909; started life as official of Chiba-ken, then Gumma-ken, Shiga-ken; apptd. Chief, Police Dept., Shiga-ken, Tochigi-ken; Chief, Home Affairs Dept., Iwate-ken, Yamagata-ken, Ibaragi-ken, Gumma-ken, successively; Governor, Gumma-ken and Shimane-ken; sent to Europe and America for study, 1923; present post since Sept., 1931. Address: 58 Kami-Ogikubo, Iogimachi, Suginami-ku, Tokyo.

Mayor of Kyoto; b. Apr., 1883 in Okayama-ken; s. of Kyugoro Omori. Career: grad., Law Coll., Kyoto Imp. Univ., 1908; apptd. Headman, Kuwatagun District; Deputy Mayor of Kyoto; Procurator, Kumamoto-ken; Chief, Police Affairs Dept., Ehime-ken and Kanagawa-ken; Chief, Harbor Affairs Dept., Kanagawa-ken; Chief, Home Affairs Dept., Kumamoto-ken and Nagasaki-ken; Chief, Home Dept. and Engrg. Dept., Hokkaido Gov't; Gov., Yamaguchi-ken and Kumamoto-ken; Dir., South Manchuria Ry. Co., 1930; present post since 1933. Address: Official Residence, Kyoto.

Dir., Civil Affairs Bureau, Justice Dept.; b. in Miye-ken; s. of late Yotaro Omori. Career: grad., Law Coll., Tokyo Imp. Univ.; Judge, Tokyo District Court; Councillor, Justice Dept.; Repr. and Judge of Mixed Arbitral Tribunal; stationed at London, 1922-26; Judge, Supreme Court; present post since Mar., 1933. Lecturer, Tokyo Imp. Univ. Address: 129 Hinode-cho I-chome, Toshimaku, Tokyo.

M. D.; Prof., Psychiatry, Manchuria Medical Coll. b. June, 1885 in Hiroshima-ken. Career: grad., Medical Coll., Kyoto Imp. Univ.; psychiatrical specialist; present post since 1917. Address: care Manchuria Medical College, Mukden, Manchoukuo.

Igakuhakushi (M. D.); b. June, 1885 in Aichi-ken; s. of Kihei Ono, physician. Career: grad., Osaka Medical Coll., 1910; studied Pediatrics at Osaka Medical Coll. and Medical Coll., Tokyo Imp. Univ.; commenced medical practice, 1913; studied at Takeo Tubercle Laboratory, 1919; received degree, 1926. Address: 47 Minami-Watayacho, Minamiku, Osaka.

Mng.-Dir., Fuji-Minobu Ry. Co.; Pres., Toyo Recreation-Ground Co.; Dir., Minobu Bus Co., Hokkaido United Elec. Co., Asahigawa Elec. Power Co., Pine Machine Co.; Auditor, Hokkaido Elec. Light Co.; b. Jan., 1879 in Yamanashi-ken; s. of Hachizaemon Ono, landlord. Career: grad., Engrg. Coll., Tokyo Imp. Univ., 1905. Address: 46 Minamihiradai, Shibuyaku, Tokyo.

Hon. Consul-Gen. for Bolivian Republic and Hon. Consul for Guatemala Republic at Yokohama; Pres., Ono Shoten, Ltd.; Dir., Teikoku Sericultural Co., Teikoku Sericulture Warehouse Co., Yokohama Marine & Fire Ins. Co. and Dai-ichi Marine & Fire Ins. Co.; b. Jan., 1890 in Yokohama; s. of Mitsukage Ono, Ex-Mem., House of Peers and Co. dir. Career: grad., Keio Univ., 1915; went to America and Canada to inspect com. and industry. Address: 4481 Oyado, Hommokumachi, Nakaku, Yokohama.

Chief Dir., Dojinkai; Lawyer; b. June, 1869 in Yamanashi-ken. Career: grad., English Law Course, Waseda Univ.; passed Examination for Judicial Probationer, 1898; served as Public Procurator at Yokohama and Odawara Local Courts; Prosecutor, Taiwan Local Court; Chief Prosecutor, Taihoku Local Court; Judge, Taiwan Higher Court; present post since 1921. Address: 28 Shiroyamamachi, Nakanoku, Tokyo.
Rear-admiral; Pres., Mech. & Engr Sch., Yokosuka; b. May, 1882 in Miye-ken. Career: grad., Naval Engrg. Coll.; then Naval Academy; ardent Christian. Address: 492 Koyamamachi, Ebaraku, Tokyo.

Mng.-Dir., Osaka Refining Co., Toyo Fertilizer Co.; Dir., Nippon Metallurgy Co., Dai Nippon Elec. Wire Co.; Auditor, Kansai Sulphuric Acid Trade Co.; b. Oct., 1880 in Oita-ken; s. of Doun Ono, physician. Career: grad., Law Dept., Waseda Univ.; joined Furukawa Gomei Kaisha, holding office up to date. Address: 525 Seidomura Ashiya, Mukogun, Hyogoken.

Dir., Paymasters Bureau, War Office; b. Mar., 1876; s. of Kampei Onodera, Miyagi-ken. Career: grad., Law Coll., Tokyo Imp. Univ., 1905; Military Intendant, 1929; Inspector, Paymasters School. Address: 942 Noyashiki, Shimokitazawa, Setagayaku, Tokyo.

Hogakuhakushi (D. L.); Mem., House of Peers; Pres., Tokyo Imp. Univ.; Mem., Imp. Academy; Mem., National Treasury Inquiry Committee and Civil Administration Inquiry Committee; b. Dec., 1870 in Niigata-ken; s. of Heikichi Onozuka. Career: grad., Law Coll., Tokyo Imp. Univ., 1895; went to Europe and America for study; apptd. Asst. Prof., Prof., Dean of Law Coll., Tokyo Imp. Univ.; received degree, 1902; present post since 1928. Address: 36 Kobinatadaimachi-Nichome, Koishikawaku, Tokyo.

Former Adviser and Partner, Taisho Trading Co., Osaka; landowner; b. Oct., 1883 in Akita; s. of Kosuke Akagawa, Governor; later adopted by Tohei Osakatani, business man. Career: studied at Keio Univ.; went to Europe and America for study; served Nitto Trading Co.; then became Sub-station Agents, Standard Oil Co. of New York, and Head of its branch office. Address: 50 Kujo-dori Itchome, Minatoku, Osaka.

Ex-War Minister; Mem., Civil Administration Deliberation Committee; Mem., House of Peers; b. May, 1858 in Gifu-ken; s. of Keinoshin Oshima, clansman. Career: grad., Military Academy; then studied in France and Germany; apptd. Instructer, Alma Mater and Gunnery School; served in Sino-Japanese War; Staff, Military Instruction Board; Bureau Dir., General Staff Office; Staff, Imp. Headquarters in Russo-Japanese War; Vice-Chief, General Staff Office; Vice-Minister of Army; War Minister; Committee on Foreign Affairs; Comdr., Garrison at Tsingtao; went to Russia as Subordinate to late Prince Yamagata, special envoy to Russian Emperor's Colonation Ceremony; toured Europe, as Subordinate to Prince Kan-in; attended Int'l Parl. Trade Conf., Berlin. Address: 365 Kashiwagi, Yodobashiku, Tokyo.

Chief Dir., Imp. Educational Society; Lecturer, Tokyo Imp. Univ. and Tokyo Univ. of Litt. & Science; b. Nov., 1880 in Kanagawa-ken; s. of Masayoshi Oshima, landlord. Career: grad., Litt. Coll., Tokyo Imp. Univ., 1904; Head, Tokyo City Educational Bureau; Prof., Tokyo Imp. Univ.; Mem., Thought Problem Investigation Committee; Councillor Federation of Central Cultural Insts. Address: 52 Komagome-Sendagicho, Hongoku, Tokyo.

M. P.; b. Feb., 1875 in Niigata-ken; s. of Kichizaemon Oshima, farmer. Career: grad., Tokyo Law Coll.; apptd. Mem., Hakodate Municipal Assembly; same, Hokkaido Govt. Assembly; Mem., Towns and Cities Planning Committee. Address: 64 Jizomachi, Hakodate, Hokkaido.

Kogakuhakushi (D. E.); Prof., Tokyo Imp. Univ.; b. Sept., 1882; s. of Shoji Kurosawa, Hyogo-ken and later adopted by Rokuro Oshima. Career: grad., Engrg. Coll., Tokyo Imp. Univ., 1907; Asst., Tokyo Imp. Univ., 1908; went to America to study Applied Chemistry, 1915; went to Europe and America, 1922; attended World Coal Conference. Address: 121 Yoyogi, Yoyohatamachi, Shibuyaku, Tokyo.

Admiral; Minister of Navy; b. May, 1876; s. of Tohei Osumi, Aichi-ken. Career: grad., Naval Academy, 1897; Sec. to Navy Minister; Comdr., H. M. S. Asahi; Embassy Attaché in France; Comdr., 3rd Squadron; Vice-Minister of Navy; Comdr., 2nd Squadron; Navy Minister. Supreme War Councillor; present post since Jan., 1933. Address: 57 Shimo-Takanawamachi, Shibaku, Tokyo.
Sec. of Legation; b. June, 1902 in Yamanashiken; s. of Hideo Ota, official of Justice Office. Address: care Japanese Legation, Shanghai, China.

Keizaigakuhakushi (D. Econ.); M. P.; Ex-Councillor, Finance Office; b. Nov., 1886 in Shizuoka-ken; s. of Mankichi Ota. Career: grad., Econ. Dept., Law Coll., Tokyo Imp. Univ., 1912; joined Hochi Shimbun, 1919; apptd. Vice-Pres. of same; resigned same, 1928; sent to Diet, 1930 & 1932. Address: 2616 Sannoshita I-chome, Omoriku, Tokyo.

Ambassador to USSR.; b. Nov., 1880 in Tottori-ken; s. of Isaburo Ota. Career: studied at Nippon Univ.; apptd. Elève-Consul; Commr., Kwantung Gov't.; Sec., Embassy in U.S.; same, Legation in Mexico; Consul-Gen. at San Francisco and Ottawa; Councillor of Embassy; Attaché, Legation in China; Minister to Spain and Portugal, 1925; present post since Oct., 1932. Address: Ambassade du Japon, Malaya Nikitskaya 13, Moscow, USSR.

Mng. Dir., Kyoto Hotel; b. Sept., 1890 in Tokyo; s. of Genbei Uchiyama, and later adopted by late Tsuru Otsuka. Career: grad., Tokyo Higher Com. School, 1910; Mgr., Yamamoto Hotels under management of South Manchuria Ry.; Passenger Agent of same Co. President's Sec.; New York Rep.; resigning from same, entered Wordorf Astoria, New York; Asst. Mgr., Imp. Hotel, Tokyo. Address: Awataguchi, Kyoto.

Rear-Admiral (reserve); Mng. Dir., Mitsubisih Elec. Engrg. Co.; b. Feb., 1874 in Hyogo-ken; s. of Mampei Ouchi. Career: grad., Naval Engrg. Coll.; Naval Staff Coll.; entered Naval Office; Chief Engr., Sasebo Naval Arsenal; Mgr., Kobe Works, present concern. Address: 14 Aoyama-Takagicho, Akasakaku, Tokyo.

Consul at Cheng-kiatun, Manchoukuo; b. Dec., 1881 in Chiba-ken; s. of Kametaro Owaku, landlord. Career: sent to Peking (Peiping) as student of Foreign Office; Chancellier, 1905; Vice-Consul at Chientao 1919; Consul at Kiukiang, 1925; present post since 1930. Address: 836 Den-en-Chofu, Omoriku, Tokyo.

Hogakuhakushi (L. D.); Author; b. Dec., 1870 in Tokushima-ken; s. of Takeji Tojo, samurai; later adopted by Iwao Oyama, samurai, Tokushima Clan. Career: grad., Tokyo Univ. of Com.; former Consul-General, San Francisco. Recreations: reading, travelling. Address: 123 Nichome, Umabashi, Suginamiku, Tokyo.

Dr., Shizuoka Bank; Aud., Shizuoka Elec. Ry. Co., Tokai Ins. Co.; Pres., Fuji Tea Mfg. Co.; Councillor, Tea Traders Central Assn.; Pres., Shizuoka City Educ. Assn.; Dir., Boy Scout Federation, Japan; b. Sept., 1870 in Shizuoka. Career: grad., Shizuoka Middle School; sent to Diet several times. Address: Anzaicho, Shizuoka.

M. P.; b. Nov., 1859 in Miye-ken; s. of Kukimasa Ozaki, samurai. Career: grad., Keio Univ.; Corr., Kyochu Shimpo and Yubin Hochi Shimbun; Editor, Niigata Shimbun; Commr., Statistics Bureau; sent to Diet from Miye-ken 18 times since 1890; Councillor, Foreign Office; Minister of Education; Minister of Justice; Mayor of Tokyo; went abroad to inspect Europe after World War, 1919; again went to Europe and America, 1931. Address: 1774 Hiroo, Zushimachi, Kanagawa-ken.

Wholesaler in Woollen Goods and Upholstery; b. Mar., 1896 in Tottori-ken; s. of Yotaro Ozawa, farmer. Career: engaged in present business since 1912. Address: 18 Awajimachi Sanchome, Higashiku, Osaka.
Chief, Home Affairs Office, Manchoukuo; Chief Executive, Manchoukuo; b. 1871 in Manchuria. Career: present post since 1932. Address: Hsinking.

Vice-Minister of Civil Affairs, Manchoukuo; Chief, Land Administrative Bureau, Tungsheng Special District; b. 1882 in Mukden Province. Career: Chief, Finance Dept., Tsitsihar, 1920; Chief, Taxation Office, Mukden, 1923; Chief, Finance Dept., Tsitsihar, 1926; Chief, Civil Affairs Dept., Tungsheng Special District; present post since 1932. Address: Hsinking.

Ex-Envoy of Manchoukuo to Japan; b. 1897 in Chinkiang-hsien, Kiangsu. Career: grad., Peiyang Univ.; served in Foreign Dept.; Adviser to Chang Tsu-lin, 1920; Dir., Telephone Bureau, Shanghai, 1923; Gov.'s Sec., Anhwei Prov., 1930; exerted in Manchoukuo Foundation Movement, 1931; Mayor of Harbin, 1932; Envoy to Japan, 1932. Address: Hsinking.

M. D.; Medical Practitioner; b. 1874 at Ennenda, Glarus, Switzerland; n. Swiss; s. of Emil Paravicini, physician. Career: studied at Swiss Schools and Univs.; after receiving degrees in Switzerland, served as Asst. and Locumtenens at Univ.-Clinics and Hospitals of Basle, Berne, Zurich, Engadine and German Hospital, London; post-graduate work in Germany, France, U. S.; in charge of Sanatorium near Zurich; practised in Switzerland and Milan; in Yokohama and Tokyo since 1905; Med. Officer for British Embassy, Tokyo, 1921-28; visited prisoners' camps on behalf of Int'l Red Cross Committee during World War. Address: 734 Honmoku, Yokohama.

Naval Attache, Italian Emb., Tokyo; Captain, Italian Royal Navy; b. 1885 in Venice, Italy. Career: grad., Livorno Naval Coll., 1904; took part in war with Turkey, 1911-1912; also in Great War; Commandant, Italian Legation Guard, Peking, 1920-1922; present post since Apr., 1932. Address: 2 Hiroocho, Azabuku, Tokyo.

Violin Virtuoso; Prof., Tokyo Academy of Music; b. in Vienna, Austria; s. of Julius Polius Pollak, business man. Career: grad., Coll. in Vienna, and Conservatories at Leipzig and Geneva, 1905; apptd. Prof. at Conservatory in Geneva, 1905-12; same at Lausanne, 1912-14; same at Moscow, 1917-19; same in Vienna, 1920-26; same in San Francisco, 1926-30; present post since 1930; one of leading violinists in the world. Address: c. o. Omori Hotel, Omoriku, Tokyo.

Prof., Tokyo Academy of Music; Conductor and Composer; b. July, 1883 in Munich; n. German; s. of Alfred Pringsheim, Prof. Dr.; m. Lala Koszler. Career: grad., Univ. of Munich; studied music under Gutsav Mahler in Vienna, and piano under Bernhard Stavenhagen in Munich; conducted State-Opera in Vienna, operas in Geneva, Prague; became musical director of The Reinhadt-Theatre in Berlin; engaged in musical critic in Berlin and contribution to several musical magazines; present post since 1931. Address: 143 Hommuracho, Azabuku, Tokyo. Clubs: German East Asiatic Society, German Club.

Chief Executive of Manchoukuo; b. 1905 in China. Career: Succeeded to The Throne as 12th Emperor of Chinchao-eror, 1908; abdicated, 1912; studied with Johnston (Englishman) and Chen Pao-chuan at Peking, since; came to Japanese Legation, Peking, 1924; resided in Hsinking, 1925; left Hsinking for Manchuria, 1931; present post since Mar., 1932. Address: c/o Chief Executive Office, Hsinking, Manchoukuo.

Counsellor, Ministry of Foreign Affairs; Gov., Manchoukuo; Publisher, the Far Eastern Review; b. Aug., 1870 in U. S.; s. of Joseph B. Rea. Career: Elec. & Mech. Engr., Cuba, 1890-1895; War Correspondent, N.Y. Herald, & N.Y. World during Spanish American War; Engr. & Contractor, Cuba, 1899-1902; Founded Far Eastern Review, Manila, 1904; Philippine Govt. Tariff Expert, 1905; Adviser to Dr. Sun Sat-sen & Deputy Dir.-Gen., Chinese Nat. Ry. Corp., 1912-1913; Tech. Sec., Ministry of Communications, Peking, 1913-1914; Capt., U.S. Army, 1917-1919; Asst. Mil. Attache, Madrid, same year; Tech. Sec. to Chinese Delegation, Peace Conf., same year; Rep., American Chamber of Com., Washington, 1927-1929; Deputy to Sun Fo, Min. of Ry., Nat. Govt. of China; present posts since 1932. Address: c/o Ministry of Foreign Affairs, Hsinking, Manchoukuo.

B. A.; M. A.; L. H. D.; D. D.; Pres., Rikkyo Univ.; Bishop and Educator; b. Nov., 1875 in Frederick Maryland, U. S.; n. American; s. of Charles David Reifsnider, railroad man. Career: grad., Kenyon Coll. and Bexley Theological Seminary; ordained Deacon, 1900; Priest, 1901; Rector, Christ Church, Hudson, Ohio, 1900-01; Missionary to Japan since 1901; at Nara, 1902-03; Fukui, 1903-12; present post since 1912; consecrated Bishop, 1924. Address: 1 Rikkyo Daigaku, Ikebukuro, Toshimaku, Tokyo.

Secretary, Norwegian Legation, Tokyo; Order of Polonia Restituta; Order of Christ; b. May, 1900 in Bergen, Norway; n. Norwegian; s. of Christian Reusch, Director. Career: grad., Oslo Univ.; apptd. Attaché of Legation, Copenhagen; same, Lisbon; Secretary of Consulate-General, London; same, Hamburg; Secretary in Foreign Office, Oslo; then present post. Address: 4, Hikawacho, Akasakaku, Tokyo.

Barrister; LL. D.; Venezuelan Consul-General, Tokyo; b. Jan., 1900 in Upata-Dto. Piar-Estado Bolivar-Venezuela; n. Venezuelan; s. of Antonio Rodriguez, merchant. Career: grad., Central Univ. of Venezuela, 1924; Sec., Venezuela's 1st Criminal Court; Gen. Mgr., General Syndicate of Mica, Boilvar State, 1925-26; Lawyer in Bolivar State; Judge, 1st Criminal Court, 1st Civil Court, Supreme Court; Dir., Polit. and Administrative Dept. of the State, 1928-30; Gen. Sec. of Govt., Bolivar State, 1930-31; present post since Mar., 1931. Address: 217, Bunka Apts., Ochanomizu, Hongoku, Tokyo.

Dr. Jur.; German Consul in Osaka; b. 1890 in Bartenstein, East-Prussia; n. German; s. of Gustav Rohde, Privy Councillor. Career: studied law at Univs. of Tübingen and Berlin, 1909-13; Administrative service, 1913-19; entered Foreign Office, 1920; Sec., German Legation, Peking, 1921-24; Vice-Consul, German Consulate-Gen., Melbourne, 1924-26; Consul German Consulate-Gen., Pretoria, 1926-27; Foreign Office, Berlin, 1928-30; Acting Consul, Yokohama, 1930; present post since July, 1930. Address: 150 Yamamotodori-Sanchome, Kobe.

M. A. (Cambridge); British Consul-General at Keijo, Chosen; b. June, 1879 in Reading, England; n. British; s. of Dr. W. A. S. Royds. Career: grad., St. John's Coll., Cambridge Univ.; entered Japan Consular Service, 1902; Acting Consul at Tainan, Chemulpo, etc.; Vice-Consul in Manila, 1912; Acting Consul-Gen., there; on Special Service at Norfolk, Virginia, U. S., 1915-17; Consul at Honolulu, 1919-25; Consul-Gen. at Kobe, 1925-31; present post since 1931. Address: British Consulate-Gen., Keijo, Chosen.

Major; Acting Military Attache, American Emb.; b. Sept., 1892 in York, S. Carolina; s. of Colonel T. S. Bratton, retired. Career: grad., U. S. Military Academy, 1914; Infantry Sch., 1922; Command and General Staff Sch., 1931; 2nd, Year Course, Rikugun Dai-Gakko, 1932; Asst. Military Attache, American Emb., 1924-1926; present post since 1933. Address: c/o American Embassy, Tokyo.

Head, 1st and 2nd Section, Cultural Work Dept., Foreign Office; b. Oct., 1888 in Yamanashi-ken; s. of Shigeaki Horiuchi and later adopted by Kunitaro Saegusa. Career: grad., Law Coll., Tokyo Imp. Univ., 1914; Vice-Excise Officer, Finance Office, Member of the 1st, 2nd, 3rd, 4th, 5th & 6th Gen. Meeting of League of Nations at Geneva, 1920-1925; Supr., Tax Office, Shimokyo; 1st Sec., Legation. Address: 1061 Nakanobu-Oharakita, Ebaraku, Tokyo.

Gov., Hokkaido Govt.; b. Dec., 1882; s. of Heijiro Sagami, Hiroshima-ken. Career: grad., Law Coll., Tokyo Imp. Univ., 1900; Sec., Home Office and Ry. Dept.; Councillor, Home Office; Sec. to Home Minister; Chief., Shrine Bureau; Gov., Nagasaki-ken and Okayama-ken; Chief, Prefectuarl Bureau; Gov., Kyoto-fu. Address: Official Residence, Nishi Nichome, Kitanijo, Sapporo.

Dir., Board of Tourist Industry; b. Nov., 1889 in Kobe; s. of Shigenori Sato, and later adopted by Sahara's family. Career: passed Higher Civil Service Exam., 1914; grad., Law Coll., Tokyo Imp. Univ., 1915; entered Ry. Dept.; Councillor, Ry. Bureau; Ry. Inspector; Chief, Gen. Affairs Section, Transportation Bureau; Chief, Law & Regulations Section; Sec. to Ry. Minister; present post since Jan., 1932. Address: 655 Sendagaya 4-chome, Shibuyaku, Tokyo.

Poet; Prof., French Litt., Waseda Univ.; b. Jan., 1894 in Tokyo; s. of Jubei Saijo, soap mfr. Career: grad., English Litt. Course, Waseda Univ.; studied at Japanese Litt. Course, Tokyo Imp. Univ.; sent to Europe as student of Waseda Univ. to study in Paris and Sorbonne Univs., 1924-26; then travelled to England and Italy; author of many books on poetry, such as “Gold Dust”, “Unacquainted Lover”, “Beautiful Forfeiture”, “Poetical Work by Yaso Saijo”, “Collection of Folk Songs by Yaso Saijo”, etc. Address: 433 Kashiwagi, Yodobashiku, Tokyo.

Prince; Genro; Mem., House of Peers; b. Oct., 1849 in Kyoto; s. of late Kimizumi Tokudaiji and later adopted by Morosue Saionji. Career: apptd. General to San-in, Hokuroku and Obu Clan during Restoration War; studied Law and Politics in France, 1870-1880; published Tokyo Jiyu Shimbun; went to Europe and America in company with late Prince Ito for investigation of Parliamentary system, 1882; Minister to Austria; same to Germany; Chief, Decoration Bureau; Vice-Pres., House of Peers; Privy Councillor; Minister of Education in 2nd and 3rd Ito Cabinet; Foerign Minister; Finance Minister and Premier; Pres., Seiyukai; formed his Cabinet 1903 and 1911; attenedd World Peace Conference as chief delegate of Japan. Address: 5 Minami-Kogacho, Surugadai, Kandaku, Tokyo.

Violoncellist; b. May, 1902 in Tokyo-fu; s. of Hidesaburo Saito, English scholar. Career: studied at National Music Academies in Leipzig and Berlin; Mem., New Symphony Orchestra in Tokyo. Address: 2 Gobancho, Kojimachiku, Tokyo.

Minister, Netherland Legation; b. 1886 in Niigata-ken. Career: grad., Law Coll., Tokyo Imp. Univ.; Eleve Con., Wash., 1910; 3rd Emb. Sec., 1915; Eng., 1918; France, same year; Mem., Peace Conf. at Paris, 1919; 2nd Emb. Sec. in England and sent to France, same year; Mem., 1st Gen. Meeting, League of Nations at Geneva, 1920; Con., Seattle, 1921; Con.-Gen. at New York, 1923; Dir., Information Bureau, Foreign Office, 1929; Emb. Councilor, England, 1930. Address: c/o Japanese Legation, Netherlands.

Lecturer, Tokyo Fine Art Academy; b. April, 1887. Career: grad., Tokyo Fine Art Academy; his works were often exhibited in Imp. Fine Arts Exhibition; appt. Non-Commissioned Officer, Tokyo Municipal Office, and Social Bureau, Home Office; Mng. Dir., Japan New Dancers' Assn. Address: 1 Honchodori Itchome, Nakanoku, Tokyo.

Viscount; Admiral; Prime Minister; b. Oct., 1858 in Sendai City; s. of Kohei Saito. Career: apptd. Sub.-Lieut.; Staff, Navy Dept., Gen. Staff Office; Adjutant, H. M. S. Fuji and Izumi; Staff, Standing Squadron; Comdr., H. M. S. Akitsushima and Itsukushima; Dir., Naval Affairs Bureau, Navy Dept.; Vice-Minister of Navy Minister, 1906; Gov., Chosen Gov't., 1919; ennobled, 1925; attended Disarm. Conf., Geneva, 1927; Privy Councillor; again Gov., Chosen Gov't., 1929-31; Prime Minister 1932. Addrses: (home) 44 Nakacho-Sanchome, Yotsuyaku, Tokyo; (office) 1 Nagatacho-Itchome, Kojimachiku, Tokyo.

Gov., Kyoto-fu; b. Apr., 1881; s. of Genzaburo Saito, Shizuoka-ken. Career: grad., Law Coll., Tokyo Imp. Univ., 1908; Chief, Police Dept., Yamagata-ken, Shizuoka-ken and Miyagi-ken; Chief, Home Affairs Dept., Kumamoto-ken; Gov., Miyazaki-ken; Kumamoto-ken; Lawyer; Gov., Osaka-fu. Address: Official Residence, Nakadachiuri, Karasumaru, Kyoto.

Prop., Saito Forestry Industry Office; Adviser, Nippon Christian Assn., Keijo; Councillor, Keijo Y.M.C.A.; b. Sept., 1866 in Niigata; s. of Zensaku Saito, agriculturist. Career: grad., Forestry Dept., Tokyo Imp. Univ., 1890; served Forestry Bureau, Agrl. & Industry Dept., 1890; apptd. Chief, Forestry Cultivation Office, Taiwan Govt.; Chief, Forestry Bureau, Ishikawa-ken and Yamanashi-ken; Chief, Forestry Administrative Bureau and Forestry Experimental Station, Hokkaido Govt.; Expert, Forest Bureau, Agrl. & Industry Dept. of Korea, 1909; Chief, Forest Bureau of same to 1918; retired and engaged in forest cultivation work in Chosen; Adviser, Forestry Dept., Kokaisha, Ltd., 1920; Mem., Keikido Pref. Assembly; Recreation: horticulture. Address: 2 Shinkyodo, Keijo, Chosen.

Adviser, Kwantung Army; Hogakuhakushi (D. L.); b. Nov., 1880; s. of Ryojun Saito, samurai of Hiroshima Clan. Career: grad., Law Coll., Tokyo Imp. Univ., 1908; Consul at Foochow; Sec., Foreign Office; 2nd Sec., Embassy; Chief, Com. Bureau; Dir., South Manchuria Ry. Co.; present post since Aug., 1932. Address: 42 Shoto, Shibuyaku, Tokyo.

Trader; b. Jan., 1874 in Chiba-ken; s. of Nihei Saito, landowner. Career: grad., Yokohama Com. School; Eastman Coll., U. S.; sent to New York as Student of Agrl. & Com. Office; commenced present business, 1913; Dir., Kojimachi Ward Assn.; Councillor, Kojimachiku Educ. Inst. Address: (office) Marunouchi Bldg., Marunouchi-Nichome, Kojimachiku, Tokyo.

Secretary, Tokyo Y.M.C.A.; Mng. Dir., Institute for Pacific Problems; b. July, 1886; s. of Isamu Saito, Fukuoka-ken. Career: grad., Litt. Coll., Tokyo Imp. Univ., 1911; Prof., 5th Higher School; went abroad several times. Address: 62 Hayashicho, Koishikawaku, Tokyo.

M. P.; Parl. Vice-Minister of Home Affairs; b. Aug., 1870 in Hyogo-ken; s. of Hachiroemon Saito. Career: grad., Waseda Univ.; Yale Univ., 1904; became lawyer, 1895; sent to Diet from Hyogo-ken 7 times since 1912; apptd. Parl. Vice-Minister of Home Affairs; attended Int'l Parl. Conf., Sept., 1913; Dir., Legislation Bureau; apptd. present post, June, 1932. Address: 315 Kitashinagawa-Sanchome, Shinagawaku, Tokyo.

Dir., Yokohama Koshin Bank, 77th Bank; b. July, 1878 in Gumma-ken; s. of Matsugoro Saito, landowner. Career: grad., Law Coll., Tokyo Imp. Univ., 1905; joined Bank of Japan, 1905; Sec., Investigator, then Acting-Mgr., Business Dept. of same; Mng. Dir., Yokohama Credit Bank, 1921-31. Address: 150 Takinoue, Nakaku, Yokohama.

Dir., Jinchu Ry. Co.; Chief Councillor, Waseda Univ.; b. May, 1864 in Shizuoka-ken; adopted-s. of Sueharu Saito, samurai. Career: grad., Polit. Econ. Dept., Waseda Univ., 1884; Mng. Editor, Miyako Shimbun; Dir., Chuo Shogyo Bank; Mng. Dir., Narita Ry Co., 1909-20; Lecturer, Waseda Univ.; Pres., Jinchu Ry. Co., 1922-27. Address: 14 Minamicho, Ushigomeku, Tokyo.

Non-Commissioned Staff, Yasuda Hozen-sha; b. May, 1874 in Yamagata-ken; s. of Jirosaku Sajima, merchant. Career: grad., Tokyo Imp. Univ., 1899; Prof., Osaka Higher Tech. School for 5 years; Gen. Sec., Osaka Y.M.C.A. for 20 yrs.; joined Yasuda Holding Co. and Yasuda Bank, 1926. Address: 1931 Nishi-Sugamo 2-chome, Toshimaku, Tokyo.

Prop., Sakabe Shoten (Manufacturers and Exporters of Toilet Brushes); Pres., Osaka Brush Makers' Assn.; b. Dec., 1873 in Kameoka, Kyoto-fu; s. of Katashi Sakabe, samurai. Career: grad., Higher Com. School; Dir., Osaka Chamber of Com. & Industry for 2 terms; Educational Commr., Osaka, for 8 years from 1922; sent to Geneva by Govt. as Capitalist Delegate at World Labor Conf., 1924; representing Osaka Chamber of Com. & Industry, attended Com. Conf. at Honolulu, Hawaii, 1925. Address: Minami-shinmachi Itchome, Higashiku, Osaka.

Mng.-Dir., Chosen Ry. Hotel Co.; b. May, 1882; s. of Korehae Sakai. Career: grad., English Course, Central Trading Academy of Ry. Dept.; engaged in Hotel Business since 1911; Supervisor, Sanyo Hotel in Shimonoseki; Sawabumi Hotel in Kyoto; Station Hotel in Shingishu; and Fuzan Station Hotel, Heijo Ry. Hotel; sent to U. S. A. to study Hotel Business for a year and practiced at Hotel Ambassador, Pennsylvania and at other big Hotels; apptd. Supervisor, Chosen Hotel in Keijo, 1927; Mng.-Dir., Chosen Ry. Hotel Co., 1932; present post since, Recreation: reading, hunting. Address: 87 Hasegawamachi, Keijo-Fu.

Count; Mem., House of Peers; Dir., Dai-To Bunka Kyokai; b. June, 1893; adopted-s. of Count Tadaoki Sakai. Career: grad., Peers' School and Law Coll., Tokyo Imp. Univ., 1918; apptd. Sec. to Justice Minister and Ry. Minister; elected Mem., House of Peers, 1923; went abroad, 1929. Address: 12 Haramachi, Koishikawaku, Tokyo.

Dir., Mitsui Gomei Kaisha; b. June, 1868; s. of late Hisashi Sakai, Aichi-ken. Career: grad., Rikkyo Univ. and Harvard Univ., U. S.; Sec. to Foreign Minister; Sec. to Premier; joined Mitsui Gomei Kaisha., 1914. Address: 20 Aoyama-Takagicho, Akasakaku, Tokyo.

Civil and Bldg. Contractor; b. Mar., 1882 in Hiroshima-ken. Career: grad., Tokyo Artisan Sch.; engaged in civil engineering work at Arai, Horiuchi and Sugawara Corporation office in Manchuria and Korea, 1904; established Sakakiya Corporation and contracted various civil works as a contractor of Manchurian Ry Co.; Chairman, Japan and Manchoukuo Civil and Bldg. Assn. Address: 15 Noto-machi, Dairen.

Retired Vice-Admiral; Dir., Kaiji Kenkyukai (Marine Resech Society); Councillor, Kochi Ry. Co.; b. Oct., 1859 in Kochi; s. of Hayashi Sakamoto, samurai. Career: grad., Naval Coll.; Vice-Admiral (Retired). Address: 2667 Sanno, Araijuku, Iriaraimachi, Omoriku, Tokyo.

Lieut.-General; Comdr, 6th Division; b. Jan., 1879; s. of Seihachi Sakamoto, Kochi-ken. Career: apptd. Infantry Sub.-Lieut., 1900; Pres., Military Academy, 1929. Address: Military Official Residence, Kumamoto City.

Mng. Dir., Tozan Agrl. Co.; b. Apr., 1877 in Kochi-ken; s. late Masaki Sakamoto. Career: grad., Tokyo Marcantile Marine School; sent to U. S. for study, 1903–06; joined Mitsubishi Goshi Kaisha, 1906; served at Moji, Karatsu, Nagasaki, Otaru, Kobe Offices, 1907–18; Mng.-Dir., Mitsubishi Trading Co., 1919; resigned and apptd. Mng.-Dir., Mitsubishi Iron & Steel Co., 1921; Councillor, Mitsubishi Goshi Kaisha, 1922; toured abroad, 1923–24; present post since 1925. Address: 36 Nakacho-Sanchome, Yotsuyaku, Tokyo.

Commr., Foreign Office and Overseas Dept.; Chief, 3rd Section, Com. Bureau; b. June, 1894 in Fukuoka-ken; s. of Momojiro Sakamoto, samurai. Career: grad., Law Coll., Tokyo Imp. Univ., 1917; apptd. Sec., Embassy in America; Consul in Argentine; Consul at Amoy, China; present post since 1929. Address: 24 of 76 Den-en-chofu, Omoriku, Tokyo.

Mem., House of Peers; b. June, 1857 in Nagoya; s. of Masatake Nagai, and adopted by the late Masahito Sakamoto, Mem., Genroin. Career: when young, studied Chinese literature and English; entered Home Office; appointed Gov., Fukui-ken, 1902; same, Kagoshima-ken; 1908; Mayor of Nagoya, 1911–17; Vice-pres., Japan Red Cross Society; nominated Mem., House of Peers; for merit of his service, 1911. Address: 24 Iigura Sanchome, Azabuku, Tokyo.

Dir. and Mgr., Sumitomo Life Assurance Co.; b. Oct., 1885 in Osaka; s. of Genryo Sakamoto, M. D. Career: grad., Law Coll., Tokyo Imp. Univ.; served Sumitomo Kaisha; present post since 1925. Address: 3261 Tennoji-machi, Sumiyoshiku, Osaka.

Baron; Retired Vice-Admiral; Mem., House of Peers; Mem., Resources Delireration Committee; b. Oct., 1858 in Nagano-ken; s. of Daizo Sakamoto, samurai. Career: grad., Naval Coll., 1882; apptd. Sec. to Navy Minister; Adjutant, H. M. S. Hiyei and Yoshino; Staff, Naval Affairs Bureau, Navy Dept.; Head Instructor, Naval Staff Coll.; fought in Russo-Japanese War; Vice-Admiral, 1898; ennobled, 1907. Address: 32 Ichigaya-Koracho, Ushigomeku, Tokyo.

Auditor, Doko Spinning Co.; Mem., Int'l Board of Tourist Industry; Dir., Hanshin-Kokudo Bus Co.; Chief Dir., Osaka Econ. Society; Dir., Osaka Club; b. Dec. 1879 in Yamaguchi-ken; s. of Masaharu Sakata, Lieut.-Comdr. Career: grad., Law Coll., Tokyo Imp. Univ., 1903; Gov., Ehime-ken and Kagawa-ken; Mayor of Takamatsu; Dir., Osaka United Spinning Co. Address: Mikagemachi, Hyogo-ken.

Baron; Hogakuhakushi (D. L.); Mem., House of Peers; Adviser, Tokyo Chamber of Com. & Industry; Pres., Central Statistics Committee, Senshu Univ., "Mikasa" Preservation Society, Imp. Aviation Society, Imp. Invention Assn.; Mem., Educational Council, Earthquake Bill Settling Committee; Dir., Saiseikai, Tokyo Bay Reclamation Co., Hakone Hot-spring Supply Co., Asano Cement Co., Amagasaki Harbor Co., Oki Elec. Co., Iwaki Colliery Co., Sengokuhara Real Estate Co.; Auditor, Shibusawa Family Co.; Councillor, Japan Air Transport Co. and Tokyo Subway Co.; Mem., Romaij Investigation Committee; b. Jan., 1863 in Okayama-ken; s. of late Roro Sakatani, Confusinian scholar. Career: grad., Litt. Coll., Tokyo Imp. Univ., 1884; entered Finance Office; Vice-Minister of Finance, 1901; Finance Minister, 1906–08; Mayor of Tokyo, 1912–15; attended Int'l Statistical Assn. Conference, World Economics Conf. in Swiss, Allies Economics Conf., etc. Address: 126 Haramachi Koishikawaku, Tokyo.

Head, Literary Dept., Tokyo Asahi Shimbun; b. Mar., 1887. Career: grad., English Litt. Dept., Waseda Univ., 1910; joined Asahi Shimbun-Sha, 1913; toured Europe, 1921–23; Lecturer, Waseda Univ. since 1924. Address: 201 Nishi-Okubo, Yodobashiku, Tokyo.

Councillor, Embassy, Soviet; b. Feb., 1887 in Kagoshima; s. of Jutaro Sako, business man. Career: grad., Tokyo Univ. of Com., 1911; Sec., Foreign Office; Head, 2nd Section, Com. Bureau, Foreign Office; 1st Sec., Embassy; Attaché to Embassy in USSR.; Consul-Gen., Calcutta; present post since 1933. Address: c/o Japanese Embassy, Moscow, Soviet.

Vice-Admiral; Attendant, Naval Gen. Staff; b. June, 1879 in Yonezawa City; s. of Mascaki Sakonji, samurai; adopted by Rokuzo Sakonji. Career: grad., Naval Coll., 1900 and Naval Staff Coll., 1912; apptd. Staff, 1st Squadron; Staff, War Affairs Bureau, Navy Dept.; Comdr. H. M. S. Yahagi and Yamato; Dir., Personnel Bureau and War Affairs Bureau, Navy Dept.; Councillor, National Treasury Bureau; Comdr., Training Squadron; Vice-Admiral, 1928; Vice-Minister of Navy; Attendant, Naval Board of Command; Comdr., 3rd Squadron; Comdr., Kure Naval Station, 1932; Comdr-in-chief, Saseho Naval Station 1932–33. Address: 44 Nakacho-Sanchome, Yotsuyaku, Tokyo.

Lawyer; M. P.; b. May, 1887 in Hiroshima-ken; s. of late Ikujiro Sakuda, farmer. Career: completed Onomichi Com. School; grad., Chuo Univ.; passed Exam. for Advocates; engaged in present post since; sent to Diet 3 times. Address: Nippon Kogyo Kaikan, 7 Ginza-Nishi-Hatchome, Kyobashiku, Tokyo.

Mng. Dir., 1st Bill Broker Co.; b. Feb., 1895 in Tokyo; s. of Kitaro Sakuma. Career: grad., Econ. Dept., Keio Univ., 1919; joined Takata Shokai; then Taguchi Bank; present post since 1927. Address: 3 Yayoicho, Mukogaoka, Hongoku, Tokyo.

Dir., Osaka Real Estate, Telephone & Housing Co., Kyoto Ry. Co.; Auditor, Kyowa Savings Bank; Shipping Business Mgr.; b. Dec., 1885; s. of Kumaichiro Sakurada, samurai. Career: grad., Meiji Gakuin; Sec. and Mgr. to late Rinzaburo Imanishi; Ex-Pres., Osaka Chamber of Com. & Industry; Sec. to late Michio Doi; Pres., Osaka Elec. Light Co.; Mng.-Dir., Doi Dozokukai; Vice-Pres., Union Glass Co.; Chief Sec., Heian Credit Assn. Address: 52 Takashio, Imazumachi, Mukogun, Hyogo-ken.

Int'l Committee, Kojunsha; Dir., Tokyo Economic Assn.; b. Aug., 1867; s. of late Chikayoshi Sakurada, samurai of Uwajima Clan. Career: studied at Doninsha of Keiu Nakamura; went to Holland and Belgium; studied Economics and Law at Senshu Gakko; studied at Freiburg in Baden and Lyons Univs.; studied Litt. and Philosophy at Brusseles Univ.; studied Economics & Law at Liège Univ., Belgium; joined Bank of Japan, 1897. Address: 53 Fujimicho, Azabuku, Tokyo.

Hon. LL. D.; Privy Councillor; Pres., Imp. Academy; Pres., National Research Council; b. Aug., 1858 in Kanazawa City; s. of Jintaro Sakurai, samurai. Career: entered Daigaku Nanko, 1871; studied Chemistry at Kaisei Gakko, 1874–76, and Univ. Coll., London, 1876–81; Prof., Chemistry, Tokyo Imp. Univ., 1882–1917; elected Mem., Imp. Academy, 1898; Mem., National Research Council, 1920; Mem., House of Peers, 1920; Privy Councillor, 1926; Pres., 3rd Pan-Pacific Science Congress, 1926; Hon. Mem., Chemical Society of France, 1923; Hon. Mem., Society of Chemical Industry, London, 1923; Hon. Mem., Royal Institution of Great Britain, 1925; Hon. Mem., American Chemical Society, 1926; Hon. Mem., Academy of Science of USSR, 1927; Hon. Mem., Chemical Society of Poland, 1929; Hon. Mem., Chemical Society of London, 1931; Delegate to Celebration of 9th Jubilee, Foundation of Glasgow Univ., 1901, and to various int'l conferences at London 1907, Rome 1910, London and Paris 1922, Melbourne and Sydney 1923, Brussels 1928, Hague 1928. Address: 3 Akebonocho, Hongoku, Tokyo.

Igakuhakushi (M. D.); b. Sept., 1870 in Wakayama-ken; s. of Kichibei Sakurane. Career: grad., Osaka-fu Pref. Medical School, 1890; apptd. Prof., Osaka Medical Coll., 1900; resigned, 1926, and conducted Sakurane Hospital (skin and sexual diseases speciality); besides promoted spread of Romaji. Address: 46 Kitahama-Shichome, Higashiku, Osaka.

M. C.; Chairman, Sale & Co., Ltd., Japan; same, Sale Tilney & Co., Ltd., London; b. Oct., 1896 in Japan; s. of Charles V. Sale. Career: Member, British Delegation to Int'l Pacific Relations Conf. at Kyoto, 1929; Major Commanding Middlesex Yeomanry (Territorial Army) Address: Sale & Co., Marunouchi, Tokyo; Sale & Co., 10 St. Swithin's Lane, London, E. C. 4.

Kogakuhakushi (D. E.); Adviser; Capital Construction Bureau; Manchoukuo; b. Apr., 1880 in Yamagata-ken; adopted-s. of Seiichiro Sano, educator. Career: grad., Engrg. Coll., Tokyo Imp. Univ., 1903; apptd. Asst. Prof., 1906 and Prof., 1918, same; went to Europe, 1910; Engr., Household Dept. and Finance Dept.; Dir., Tokyo Reconstruction Office; Pres., Tokyo City Building Bureau; Dean, Engrg. Dept., Nippon Univ.; Vice-Pres., Shimizu Gumi (Goshi Kaisha); Present post since 1933. Address: Hsinking.

Count; Rear-Admiral (reserve); Dir., Japan Red Cross Society; b. July, 1871; s. of late Count Tsunetami Sano. Career: Attaché to Embassy in Germany; Comdr., H. M. S. Haruna; Mem., Red Cross; fought in Russo-Japanese War. Address: 2995 Terazato, Magomemachi, Omoriku, Tokyo.

Hogakuhakushi (D. L.); Pres., Tokyo Univ. of Com.; b. Aug., 1873 in Shizuoka-ken; s. of Chujiro Sano, business man. Career: grad., Tokyo Univ. of Com., 1895; went to Europe and America for further study of economics, 1897 and 1910; returning home, apptd. Prof. of Alma Mater; present post since 1914. Address: near Kunitachi Station, Central Railway Line, Tokyo-fu.

C. M. G.; Com. Councillor, British Embassy; b. Nov., 1883 in London; n. British; s. of G. W. M. Sansom. Career: studied in France and Germany; entered consular service in Japan, 1904; author of Historical Grammar of Japanese, Oxford Press., 1928; "Japan. A Short Cultural History." Cresset Press, London, 1931. Address: British Embassy, Tokyo.

Consul-General at Alexandrovsk; b. June, 1877; s. of Denkuro Sasaki. Career: grad., Law Dept., Kansai Univ.; Consul; 2nd Sec., Legation. Address: Japonskoe General-noe Konsulstvo, 3 Ulitea Dejinslky, Alexandrovsk, Saghalien, USSR.

Hogakuhakushi (D. L.); Ex-Prof., Kyoto Imp. Univ.; b. Mar., 1878; s. of Sozaburo Sasaki, Tottori-ken. Career: grad., Law Coll., Kyoto Imp. Univ., 1903; Asst. Prof., same Univ., 1906; went to Germany, France and England for study of administrative law, 1909; Dean, Law Coll., Kyoto Imp. Univ.; Resigned, Kyoto Imp. Univ. Aug. 1933. Address: 1 Shimokamo Izumimachi, Kamikyoku, Kyoto.

Marquis; Mem., House of Peers; Auditor, 2nd Fuji Eec. Co.; b. July, 1893 in Tokyo; s. of Marquis Takayoshi Sasaki. Career: succeeded peerage, 1910; grad., Law Coll., Tokyo Imp. Univ., 1917; studied at Litt. Coll. of same. Address: 108 Aoyama-Minamicho-Rokuchome, Akasakaku, Tokyo.

Adviser, First Bank; b. Aug., 1854 in Tokyo-fu; s. of Naoemon Sasaki. Career: joined First Bank, 1874; promoted Mgr. and Dir. of same, Nov., 1896; retired, 1931; decorated with Order of Rising Sun for his service. Address: 19 Yumicho Nichome, Hongoku, Tokyo.

Proprietor of Chinese Restaurant; b. Aug., 1887. Career: grad., Electric Course, Tokyo Industrial Coll.; succeeded father's business; First Chinese Restaurant in Tokyo; named "Kairaku-En"; 50 Years since opened business. Address: 8 2-chome, Kaebacho, Nihonbashi-ku.

Nogakuhakushi (D. A. S.); Prof., Tokyo Imp. Univ.; Dean of Agrl. Teacher's School; Vice-Pres., Zenkoku Jitsugyo Kyoiku Kai; b. Jan., 1879 in Yonezawa-Shi; s. of Buntaro Sato, farmer. Career: grad., Agrl. Coll., Tokyo Imp. Univ., 1904; sent abroad for study, 1918–20; Dir., Nippon Nogaku Kai; same, Agrl. Econ. Inst.; Mem., Rice Committee of Tenancy System, Agr. & Forestry Inquiry Committee, Cultural Work Committee toward China, and Educ. Policy Inquiry Committee; Tech. Adviser to Employers' Delegate, 3rd Int'l Labor Conference, Geneva; Delegate, Int'l Econ. Conference Geneva. Address: 440 Akatsutsumicho-Nichome, Setagayaku, Tokyo.

Ex-Ambassador to Belgium; Delegate to League of Nations; b. Oct., 1882; s. of Kenroku Tanaka, Okinawa-ken and later adopted by Aimaro Sato. Career: grad., Tokyo Higher Com. School, 1904; Minister to Poland; Secretariat to League of Nations; Committee, Int'l Econ. Conf., Geneva; Committee, Naval Conf., London; Ambassador to Belgium; resigned post 1933. Address: 4 Toriizaka, Azabuku, Tokyo.

Commr., Foreign Office; Chief, 3rd Section, Treaty Bureau; b. Jan., 1894 in Morioka City; s. of Shobei Sato. Career: grad., Law Coll., Tokyo Imp. Univ., 1918; apptd. Sec., Embassy in France; Commr., League of Nations Secretariat; present post since 1930. Address: 190 Den-en-Chofu, Omoriku, Tokyo.

Rank: Sr. 3rd; 1st O. Rising Sun; Nogakuhakushi (D. Agr.) Ph. O.; LL.D.; Baron; Ex-Pres., Hokkaido Imp. Univ.; b. Nov., 1863; s. of Shozo Sato, samurai of Iwate Clan; m. Yau, aunt of Baron Masatane Inada. Career: grad., Sapporo Agrl. Coll.; studied Agricultural Economy in Jones Hopkins Univ.; Prof., Sapporo Agrl. Coll.; Ex-Pres., Hokkaido Imp. Univ. Recreation: reading. Address: 1 Higashi-1-chome, Kitaichijo, Sapporo. Tel.: Sapporo 156.

Poet and Author; b. Dec., 1890 in Kawasaki City; s. of Keijiro Sato, merchant. Career: studied at higher school; devoted to vers libre movement; wrote poems, essays, novels. Address: 26 Isago Itchome, Kawasaki-shi, Kanagawa-ken.

Mng.-Dir., Nippon Pencil Mfg. Co.; b. July, 1887 in Miyagi-ken; s. of Seisuke Sato. Career: grad., Econ. Dept., Keio Univ.; went to America for inspection, 1914; Mng. Dir., Japan Amateur Athletic Assn. Address: 49 Asagaya Gochome, Suginamiku, Tokyo.

Vice-Admiral (Retired); b. July, 1856 in Tsuruoka City, Yamagata-ken; s. of Yasuyuki Sato, samurai. Career: grad., Naval Coll., 1887; Staff, Naval Gen. Staff; Intsructor, Naval Staff Coll.; Pres., same; Vice-Admiral, 1916; Commdr., Maizuru Naval Station. Address: 359 Kichijoji-Hondenkita, Musashino-machi, Tokyo-fu.

Soprano Singer; Soliste de Concerto Lamoureux; b. May, 1905 in Kyoto; d. of Tomotaro Sato. Career: went to Paris for vocal study under Germanie Martinelli; returned, 1932; again went to Paris for further study under Monto Carlo. Address: Tsukimigaoka, Tsurumiku, Yokohama.
Hotel Mgr.; b. Apr., 1868 in Nagano-ken; adopted-s. of late Mampei Satow. Career: founder of Mampei Hotels at Karuizawa, Atami, Tokyo and Nagoya. Address: c. o. Mampei Hotel, Atami, Shizuoka-ken.

Councillor to Embassy in France; b. Oct., 1888 in Tottori-ken; s. of Shingo Sawada. Career: grad., Law Coll., Tokyo Imp. Univ., 1914; Head, Telegraph Section, Foreign Office; attended Paris Peace Conference, Washington Disarm. Conf., and Customs Tariff Conf. in Peking, 1st Legation Sec., Foreign office Sec. & Chief, Telegraph Section, Foreign Office; Served in Imp. Household Dept.; 1st Embassy Sec., Eng.
