Address: Japanese Embassy, Paris, France. (Tokyo home) 29 Iigurakatamachi, Azabuku, Tokyo.

Dir., Japanese Bureau, League of Nations, Paris; b. Sept., 1884; s. of Shingo Sawada, Tottori-ken. Career: grad., Law Coll., Tokyo Imp. Univ., 1909; Head, Telegraph Section; Corr. Section; Translation Section; Councillor, Embassy; Consul-General at New York; Dir., Japanese Bureau of League of Nations; gov't. Delegate to Simla Conference 1933. Address: Bureau Imperial Japonais de la Société des Nations, Rue Theophile Gautier, Paris (16e), France. (Tokyo home) 59 Hiroocho, Azabuku, Tokyo.

Deputy Mayor of Tokyo; M. P.; b. May, 1880 in Yamaguchi-ken; s. of Namihei Sawamoto. Career: grad., Polit. Dept., Waesda Univ., 1898; Corr., Yomiuri Shimbun; Editor, Niigata Shimbun; Sec. to Ry. and Justice Ministers; sent to Diet from Yamaguchi-ken 3 times since 1928; Councillor, Foreign Office, 1932; present post since Aug., 1933. Address: 45 Shirokane-Imazatocho, Shibaku, Tokyo.
Merchant. Address: (home) 1692, Araijuku-Nichome, Omoriku, Tokyo. (office) 2 Muromachi-Sanchome, Nihonbashiku, Tokyo.

Hogakuhakushi (D. L.); Mayor of Osaka; b. Sept., 1873; s. of Chikayoshi Seki, Tokyo. Career: grad., Tokyo Higher Com. School; Studied Commercial Science in Belgium; School-Inspector, Education Dept.; Deputy Mayor of Osaka, 1914. Address: 13 Kamihonmachi, Tennojiku, Osaka.

Kogakuhakushi (D. E.); Prof., Tokyo Univ. of Tech.; Engr., Patent Bureau; b. Aug., 1875 in Tokyo; s. of Toyojiro Sekiguchi. Career: grad., Tokyo Higher Polytechnic School, 1896; apptd. Asst. Prof. of same, 1898; studied in England and America, 1902; Prof. of same, 1905; sent again to Europe and America, 1922. Address: 60 Gotanda 5-chome, Shinagawaku, Tokyo.

Captain; Naval Affairs Propagation Dept., Navy; b. 1886 in Saitama-ken; s. of Kunihachi Sekine. Career: grad., Naval Academy, 1909, and Naval Staff Coll., 1921; Naval Attache to Legation, Brazil, 1925; Staff, Gen. Staff Office, 1928; Instructor, Naval Staff Coll., same year; Staff, Gen., Staff Office, 1931; present post since Oct., 1932. Address: c/o Naval Dept.

Coloratura Soprano; b. Mar., 1904 in Tokyo; d. of Yunosuke Seikiya, business man. Career: grad., Ochanomizu Girls' High School, 1922; studied music at Tokyo Academy of Music and under Prof. Salcholy; went to Europe and America, 1927 and 1931; received Diploma and granted title "Maestro", Bologna Univ., highest musical academy in Italy, 1929; often came on stage in Italy, taking chief rôles in "Madame Batterfly," "La Traviata," "Barber of Sevilla," "Rigoletto," "Lucia di Lammermoor"; passed Exam. at La Scara Theatre, 1931; her operatic performance in Hollywood proved great success. Address: c. o. Sakurakai, Shinanomachi, Yotsuyaku, Tokyo.
Chief, Personnel Office, State Council, Manchoukuo. Career: present post since 1932. Address: Hsinking.
Prop., Senda Shoten (traders); b. Aug., 1883; s. of Ichijuro Senda. Career: grad., Tokyo Higher Com. School; joined Mitsui Bussan Kaisha. Address: 11 Komagome-Akebonocho, Hongoku, Tokyo.

Dir., Inorganic Chemistry of Agrl. Products, South Manchuria Ry. Co.; b. May, 1887 in Hiroshima-ken; s. of Jumpei Sera. Career: grad., Agrl. Coll., Tokyo Imp. Univ., 1914; joined Sankyo Pharmaceutical Co.; Dir., Central Experimental Station, S. Manchuria Ry Co. Address: 86 Bunkadai, Dairen.

B. D.; Christian Minister; Dir., Japan Congregational Church; b. Aug., 1887 in Niigata-ken; s. of Tsurujiro Serino, landlord. Career: grad., Theological Dept., Doshisha Univ., 1913 and Union Theological Seminary, New York, 1919; studied at Columbia Univ., 1917–19; apptd. Minister, Naniwa Christian Church, Osaka; present post since 1919. Address: 10 Harada, Uchide, Hyogo-ken.

Author; Keizaigakushi (E. B.); b. May, 1897; s. of Tsuneharu Serisawa, religionist. Career: grad., 1st Higher School; Economics Dept., Tokyo Imp. Univ.; studied at Paris Univ., France for 3 years; Commr., Agr. & Forestry Dept.; Lecturer, Chuo Univ. Address: 52 Kotakimachi, Nakanoku, Tokyo.

D. L.; Sec., Swedish Legation, Tokyo; b. May, 1896 at Stockholm, Sweden; n. Swedish; s. of Christian Setterwall, Chief of Section, Royal Swedish State Library. Career: grad., Law Dept., Stockholm Univ.; entered diplomatic service, serving Swedish Legations, London, Riga, Revel, Rovno, Warsaw; Swedish Consulate-General, New York and Royal Foreign Office, Stockholm. Address: Swedish Legation, 63. Zaimokucho, Azabuku, Tokyo.
Sec. & Chief, Board of Audit, Manchoukuo. Career: present post since 1932. Address: Hsinking.

Ex-Pres., The Japan Times; b. 1871 in Ehime-ken; s. of Seimei Sheba, samurai. Career: studied at Aoyama Gakuin, Tokyo; went to Hawaii and entered business, 1891; started "Garden Island", bilanguage weekly, 1902; Publisher & Editor, "Hawaii Shimpo", 1907; also owned two other dailies, "Jiyu Shimbun" & "Kauai Shimpo"; attended Panama Exposition, San Francisco as Japan's Delegate; returned home upon death of his father, giving up domicile in Hawaii, 1916; again visited United States as Mem., Trade Commission, representing Tokyo Chamber of Com., 1918; joined Japan Times as Gen.-Mgr., 1920; later launched "Save the Mikasa" Movement; consummated same in 1923 with organization of "Save the Mikasa Assn."; retired from journalistic career, Dec., 1932; travelling in U.S., 1933–1934. Address: (Office) 508, Toyo Bldg., Kojimachiku, Tokyo.

Acting Pres., North Manchuria Ry.; b. 1874 in Chekiang Prov. Career: Foreign Vice-Minister, 1922; Foreign Mniister & Chairman, Custom Conf., 1925; Civil Affairs Minister, 1927; Mukden Foreign Adviser after Chang Tsuo-lin's death; Pres., North Chinese Ry., 1930; present post since 1932. Address: Harbin.

Baron; Kogakuhakushi (D. E.); Mem., House of Peers; Prof., Tokyo Imp. Univ.; Pres., Manchurian Chemical Ind. Co.; b. Mar., 1872 in Kanazawa City; s. of Baron Ban Shiba. Career: grad., Engrg. Dept., Tokyo Imp. Univ., and studied Marine Engrg. at P.-G. Course of same; Asst. Prof., 1894 and Prof., same, 1898; went to Europe to study Marine Engrg., 1902; attended British Engrg. Congress, Glasgow, 1902; Instructor, Naval Staff Coll.; Engr., Patent Bureau, 1906–1930; elected Mem., House of Peers, 1917; Adviser, South Manchuria Ry. Co. up to 1932; Press., Inst. for Aeronautics; Chief Dir., Imp. Navy Assn. Address: 16 Komagome-Akebonocho, Hongoku, Tokyo.

M. P.; Author; b. Aug., 1869 at Fukui City; s. of Yuzo Shiba. Career: grad., Cambridge Univ. and "Senka" Course of Litt. Coll., Tokyo Imp. Univ.; Prof., Takanawa Buddhism Univ.; Editor, Manchoho; Pres., Tokyo Taisei Shimbun; elected to Diet 3 times from Tokyo. Address: 166 Yoyogi Shibuyaku, Tokyo.

Mezzo-Soprano; b. Mar., 1895 in Tokyo; d. of Ryosaku Hanajima, business man. Career: completed Tokyo-fu Pref. 1st Girls' High School; grad., Vocal Dept., Tokyo Academy of Music; apptd. Prof., Toyo Music Sch.; Prof. Nippon Music Sch.; famous singer. Address: 49 Uchikoshi, Nakanoku, Tokyo.

Judge, Tokyo Local Court; b. Sept., 1898 in Osaka; s. of Mitsuhiko Shibata, business man. Career: grad., French Dept., Tokyo School of Foreign Languages; Law Coll., Kyoto Imp. Univ.; Official, Revenue Bureau, Finance Official and Sec., Social Welfare Bureau, Home Office; Sec., Japanese Delegation for Int'l Labour Bureau, Geneva; Prof. in charge, Kansai Franco-Japanese Inst. Address: 40 Sumiyoshicho, Nakanoku, Tokyo.

Mem., House of Peers; Ex-Chief Sec. of Cabinet; b. Nov., 1877; s. of Zenroku Sato, Shizuoka-ken and later adopted by Sahei Shibata. Career: grad., Law Coll., Tokyo Imp. Univ., 1904; Chief, Home Affairs Dept., Miyazaki-ken and Osaka-fu; Chief, Education Bureau of Chosen Govt.; Gov., Miye-ken, Fukuoka-ken and Aichi-ken; same, Osaka-fu, 1929. Address 2 Momozonocho, Nakanoku, Tokyo.
Dir., Ishikawajima Aircraft Co.; b. 1885 in Tokyo; s. of Kasuke Shibuya, business man. Career: grad., Engrg. Coll., Tokyo Imp. Univ., 1910. Address: 44 Takanawa-Minamicho, Shibaku, Tokyo.

Vice-Pres., Co-operative Union of Japan; Consulting Dir., Hypothec Bk. of Japan; b. June, 1865 in Matsue, Shimane-ken; s. of Hanzo Shidachi, of Matsue Clan. Career: grad., Tokyo Imp. Univ., 1889; became Mgr., Sumitomo Bk.; then Pres., Industrial Bk. of Japan; sent to Geneva as Japanese Delegate to World Econ. Conf., 1927. Address: 13 Iiguramachi-Rokuchome, Azabuku, Tokyo.

Baron; Mem., House of Peers; b. Aug., 1873; brother of Taira Shidehara. Career: grad., Law Coll., Tokyo Imp. Univ., 1895; Councillor, Embassies in America and England; Minister to Holland and Denmark; attended Washington Conf., 1921; Foreign Minister in Takaaki Kato Cabinet, 1924–27; same in Reijiro Wakatsuki Cabinet; same and Prime Minister, Pro Tem. in Yuko Hamaguchi Cabinet; nominated Mem., House of Peers, 1925. Address: 23 Kamifujimaecho, Komagome, Hongoku, Tokyo.

Bungakuhakushi (D. Litt.); Pres., Taihoku Imp. Univ.; b. Sept., 1870 in Osaka-fu; s. of Shinjiro Shidehara. Career: grad., Litt. Coll., Tokyo Imp. Univ., 1893; Prof., Kagoshima and Zoshikan Higher Schools; Principal, Yamanashi Pref. 1st Middle School; Prof., Tokyo Higher Normal School; School Inspector, Education Dept.; Prof., Tokyo Imp. Univ.; Dir., Hiroshima Higher Normal School; Dir., Bureau of Publications, Education Dept.; present post since 1928; sent abroad twice. Address: Official Residence, Tomitamachi, Taihoku, Taiwan.

Igakuhakushi (M. D.); b. Dec., 1870 in Sendai City; s. of Makoto Sato, samurai; adopted by Yoku Shiga, 1886. Career: grad., Med. Coll., Tokyo Imp. Univ., 1896; apptd. Commr., Quarantine Bureau, 1897; Dir., Infectious Diseases Inst.; studied in Germany, 1901–04; Dir., Kitasato Laboratory, 1914; Prof., Keio Univ.; Dir., Chosen Gov't. Hospital; Prof. and Dean of Med. Dept., Keijo Imp. Univ., 1926; Pres., same Univ., 1929–31. Address: 15 Aoyama-Tagakicho, Akasakaku, Tokyo.

Vice-Min., Foreign Office; b. 1887 in Oita-ken. Career: grad., Law Coll., Tokyo Imp. Univ.; Eleve Con., Germany; transferred to England, 1914; 3rd Emb. Sec., 1916; Con., Portland, 1918; Chief, 1st Section of Treaty Bureau, 1921; Sec., Aviation Bureau, Communication Office, same year; Chief, 2nd Section of Treaty Bureau, 1923; 1st Legation Sec., China, 1925; Emb. Councillor and Con.-Gen., Shanghai, 1930. Address: e/o Foreign Office, Tokyo.

Author; Dir., Russo-Japanese Trade News Agency; b. Apr., 1895 in Kumamoto-ken; s. of Yosaku Nishimura, business man. Career: studied Russian language at Tokyo School of Foreign Languages, etc.; Editor, Japan's Review; Editor, World Pamphlet News Agency; Sec., Russo-Japanese Arts Assn. Address: 126 Numabukuro-Minami-Nichome, Nakanoku, Tokyo.

Rear-Admiral; Non-Official Staff, Chosen Gov't.; b. Feb., 1875 in Hiroshima-ken; s. of Jitsuzo Shigemura, samurai. Career: grad., Naval Coll., 1893; Naval Engrg. School and Naval Staff Coll., 1896; sent to Germany and France by Naval Board of Command: Staff, Naval Construction Headquarters; Commr., Munitions Bureau; Chief, Fuel Dept.; present post since 1926. Address: 172 Koshi-do, Keijo, Chosen.

Manchoukuo Foreign Affairs Commissioner for North Manchuria; b. in Hupeh Prov. Career: grad., Chuo Univ., Tokyo; Charge d'Affaires to China Legation, Tokyo, 1923; Acting Councillor, Foreign Dept., 1924; Foriegn Affairs Commr. for Harbin, 1929; Councillor, Gov.'s Office, Kirin Prov., 1932. Address: Harbin.

Baron; Mem., House of Peers; Pres., Yasuda Life Ins. Co. and Teikoku Hemp Mfg. Co.; Auditor, Kyushu Elec. Power Co.; Dir., Yasuda Hozensha and Japan Industrial Club; b. Feb., 1876 in Kyoto; adopted-s. of Takahira Shijo. Career: gard., Law Coll., Tokyo Imp. Univ., 1904; apptd. Sec., Agrl. & Com. Dept.; Chief, Engrg. Section, Com. & Industry Bureau; Dir., Engrg. Bureau; Vice-Minister, Com. & Industry Dept.; elected Mem., House of Peers, 1932. Address: 36 Hongodori, Nakanoku, Tokyo.

Pres., Shimafuji & Co.; Bldg. Contracter; b. Jan., 1895 in Tokyo; s. of late Tokichi Shimada, contracter. Career: grad., Archtl. Dept., Engrg. Coll., Tokyo Imp. Univ., 1918; joined Mitsui Gomei Kaisha; succeeded his father's business. Address: 10 Miyamuracho, Azabuku, Tokyo.

Public Accountant; Chairman, Tokyo Public Accountant Assn.; b. Oct., 1886 in Tokyo; s. of Kijuro Shimada, Military Judge. Career: grad., Tokyo Higher Com. School; apptd. Dir., Musashi Seishoku Kaisha; Auditor, Hibiya Shoten K. K.; same, Hibiya Bank, Ltd. Address: 3 Sakurayamacho, Nakanoku, Tokyo.

Pres., Bank of Taiwan; b. Sept., 1885; s. of Hidekazu Shimada, Okayama-ken. Career: grad., Econ. Dept., Tokyo Imp. Univ., 1912; entered Finance Office; Supt., Tottori and Eitaibashi Tax Offices; Chief, Customs Tariff Dept., Taxation Supt. Offices, Nagoya and Tokyo; Dir., Bank of Taiwan, 1927. Address: 275 Chojamaru, Kami-Osaki, Osakimachi, Shinagawaku, Tokyo.

Rear-Admiral; Chief, 3rd Section, Naval Gen.-Staff; b. Sept., 1883 in Tokyo; s. of Takachika Shimada. Career: Attaché, Embassy in Italy during World War; Rear-Admiral, 1929; Chief Staff, 2nd Squadron; same, 1st Squadron; Dir., Naval Submarine School; Chief Staff, 3rd Squadron, during Shanghai Incident. Address: 120 Aoyama-Harajuku, Shibuyaku, Tokyo.

Mng.-Dir., Oriental Hotel, Ltd.; b. Jan., 1878 in Aichi-ken; s. of Shiro Shimada. Career: grad., Law Coll., Tokyo Imp. Univ., 1903; studied in America 4 years; joined Toyo Kisen Kaisha (Oriental Steamship Co.), 1905; promoted Mgr. of its Kobe Branch; present post since 1926. Address: Oriental Hotel, Kobe.

Prince; Captain (Navy); b. Oct., 1886 in Kagoshima; s. of late Prince Tadayoshi Shimazu, Feudal Lord of Satsuma. Career: grad., Naval Staff Coll.; apptd. Staff Officer, Naval General Staff; Instructor, Naval Staff Coll.; Naval Attaché in London; attended; Conference on Safety at Sea, London; London Naval Conference. Address: 234 Rokuchome, Gotanda, Shinagawaku, Tokyo.
Author of literary works; b. 1872 in Shinano; s. of Masaki Shimazaki, village headman. Carrer: grad., Union Coll. (Meiji Gakuin). Address: 33 Iigura-Katamachi, Azabuku, Tokyo.

M. P.; b. Jan., 1879 in Shiga-ken; s. of Hikojiro Shimizu, Osaka. Career: grad., Polit. Dept., Waseda Univ., 1902; joined Aikoku Life Ins. Co., 1904; elected to Diet 4 times since 1927; Dir. Seiyukai. Address: 84 Sakanmachi, Kamide, Otsu City.

Pres., Shimizu-Gumi, Ltd. (Builders, Constructors and Civil Engineers); Dir., Oki Elec. Co.; Acting Partner, Tokyo Iron Frame & Girder Mfg. Co.; b. Nov., 1867 in Tokyo; s. of Takanaga Ono; adopted by Mannosuke Shimizu. Career: grad., Engrg. Coll., Tokyo Imp. Univ., 1891; after graduation has engaged in adopted-father's business; went to Europe and America to inspect architecture, 1901. Address: 11 Sanchome, Surugadai, Kandaku, Tokyo.

Consul-Gen. at Hankow; b. Mar., 1879 in Okayama-ken; s. of Tazo Shimizu. Career: grad., Polit. Dept., Tokyo Semmon Gakko (now Waseda Univ.); sent to Vladivostok as Student of Foreign Office; 1898; Sec., Foreign Office, 1902; Vice-Consul, 1918; Consul, 1919; Consular Service at Chefoo, Chicago, Peiping, Cape Town, Neuchang, Changsha; Consul at Tsitsihar 1925–32; Present post since 1933. Address: Japanese Consulate-Gen., Hankow, China.
Civil Engineer, Builder & Contractor; b. Feb., 1901 in Tokyo; s. of Teikichi Shimizu and later adopted by Mannosuke Shimizu. Career: grad., Waseda Univ. Address: 41 Nakanegishi, Shitayaku, Tokyo.

Bungakuhakushi (D. Litt.); Prof., Tokyo Women's Higher Normal School; b. Mar., 1872 in Hiroshima; s. of late Susumu Tarao, and adopted by late Shuzo Shimoda. Career: grad., Litt. Coll., Tokyo Imp. Univ., 1896; sent abroad for study of Pedagogics, 1899–1902; present post since 1899; received degree, 1921. Address: 10 Komagome-Nishikatamachi, Hongoku, Tokyo.

Grand Chancellor, Imp. Orders; Dr. of Economics; b. Jan., 1885 in Tokyo; s. of late Dr. Kokichi Shimojo. Career: grad., Law Coll., Tokyo Imp. Univ.; Sec. of Cabinet; Councillor, Legislation Bureau; Dir., Cabinet Pension Bureau, Cabinet Statistical Bureau; then present post. Address: 26 Shimo-Rokubancho, Kojimachiku, Tokyo.

Hogakuhakushi (D. L.); Vice-Pres., Asahi Shinbun-sha; b. May, 1875 in Wakayama; s. of Fusajiro Shimomura, business man. Career: grad., Law Coll., Tokyo Imp. Univ., 1898; entered Communication Dept.; apptd. Dir., Savings Bureau; Civil Governor, Taiwan Gov't.; resigned same and entered present firm; taught Finance at Waseda, Chuo, Hosei Univs. and Tokyo Univ. of Com., 1898–1915. Address: Kurakuen, Nishinomiya, Hyogo-ken.

Hogakuhakushi (D. L.); Prof., Waseda Univ.; b. 1872 in Tokyo; s. of Joken Shinobu, Scholar of Chinese Classics. Career: entered diplomatic service; promoted Consul-General, and then Embassy Counsellor; but retired from same 1917. Address: 1321 Shimo-Ochiai, Yodobashiku, Tokyo.

Hogakuhakushi (D. L.); Chief Steward to Prince Yi; b. Oct., 1872 in Shizuoka-ken; s. of Jiroshichi Shinoda, landlord. Career: grad., Tokyo Imp. Univ., 1899; practised law, 1899; served as Adviser on Int'l Law to Nogi Army in Russo-Japanese War, 1904; engaged to settle Chientao Problem; Sec. to Residency-General of Chosen, 1909; Sec. Agrl., Com. and Industry Depts. of Chosen; Chief, Home Affairs Dept., Heian-Nando, Chosen; Non-Official Staff, Polit. Affairs Dept., Expreditionary Army to Vladivostok, 1919; Gov., Heian-Nando, 1919; Vice-Chief Steward to Prince Yi, 1923; went to Europe as Mem. to Prince Yi's Suite, 1927; present post since 1932. Address: 11 Wakagicho, Shibuyaku, Tokyo.

Pres., Hattori Trading Co.; Dir., Tokyo-Yokohama Elec. Ry. Co., Meguro-Kamata Elec. Ry. Co., Hattori Watch & Clock Co.; b. Mar. 1886; s. of Tetsujiro Suzuki, Gifu-ken; later adopted by Kuniharu Suzuki. Career: grad., Law Coll., Tokyo Imp. Univ., 1911. Address: 174 Kaminumabe, Denenchofu, Omoriku, Tokyo.

Pres., Sankyo Co.; b. Jan., 1877 in Yokohama; s. of Mataichi Shiohara, merchant. Career: grad., Yokohama Eiwa Gakko (Now extinct); has long been connected with following firms and social institutions: Sankyo Co.; Nitrogen Co.; Taiwan Pharmaceutical Co.; Brewery Co.; Takamine Corp., New York; Oriental Photo. Industry Co.; Asia Aluminium Co.; Kashiwagi Clinical Thermometer Co.; Sumitomo Aluminium Co.; Japan Bakelite Co.; Physical and Chemical Research Institute; Imp. Assn. for Promotion of Inventions; Tokyo Pharmaceutical Coll.; Chem. and Industrial Assn., etc. Address: 102 Hanezawacho, Shibuyaku, Tokyo.

Critic of Music; b. Aug., 1900 in Tokyo; s. of Tasuke Shiroiri, lawyer. Career: completed Tokyo-fu Pref. Middle School; grad., German Law Course, Waseda Univ., 1926; was on Editorial Staff, Yomiuri Shimbun, New Symphony Orchestra; Chief Editor, "The Music World"; Lecturer, Tokyo Music School; Executive Committee, "Concour de Musique"; Councillor, Tokyo Music Assn. Address: 1449 Kami-Igusa, Iogimachi, Suginamiku, Tokyo.

Kogakuhakushi (D. E.); M. I. N. A. (British); Councillor, Mitsubishi Shipbuilding & Engrg. Co.; b. Nov., 1867 in Okayama-ken; s. of Kumagoro Masayoshi, landlord. Career: grad., Naval Archtl. Dept., Tokyo Imp. Univ., 1890; joined Mitsubishi Kaisha, 1890; Engr., Nagasaki Works; Head, Kobe Works and then Nagasaki Works; Mng. Dir., Shipbuilding Dept., Mitsubishi Goshi Kaisha; Mng. Dir., Mitsubishi Shipbuilding & Engrg. Co.; present post since 1922. Address: 3 Maruyamacho, Koishikawaku, Tokyo.

1st Sec., Embassy in London; b. Apr., 1894 in Hyogo-ken; s. of Yosaburo Shiozaki. Career: grad., Tokyo Higher Com. School, 1918; passed Diplomatic & Consular Service Exam.; entered diplomatic service; attached to Consulate-Generals at Shanghai and San Francisco; Sec., Embassy in U. S., 1920; Commr., Treaty Bureau, Foreign Office, 1923; Sec., Legation in China, 1925; 1st Sec. of Embassy, Jan., 1932; attended League of Nations Assembly at Geneva, 1932. Address: Japanese Embassy, London, England.

Hogakuhakushi (D. L.); Dir., Waseda Univ.; Prof. and Chief, Political Economy Dept. of same Univ. and Prof., Waseda Semmon Gakko; Mem., Central Statistics Committee; Dir., Kyochokai; b. Oct., 1870 in Ibaraki-ken; s. of Masatsune Seki, samurai; adopted by Mototaka Shiozawa. Career: grad., Polit. Dept., Waseda Semmon Gakko, 1891; Prof., Waseda Univ.; studied in Germany and America; received degree, 1907; Pres., Waseda Univ., 1920; author of several books. Address: 726 Nishigaharamachi, Takinogawaku, Tokyo.
Chief, Gen. Affairs Div., Gen. Administrative Office, Hsing-an Prov. Manchoukuo; b. in Kagoshima-ken. Career: grad., Russo-Japanese Society Sch.; present post since 1932. Address: Hsinking.

Pres., Nippon Enamel Co., Gas Tube Sales Co., Kawasaki Fire Brick Co., Teikoku Artificial Fertilizer Co., China-Japan Colliery & Steamship Co., Central Iron Mfg. Co.; Vice-Pres., Nippon Steel Tube Co.; Mng. Dir., Tokyo Bay Reclamation Co.; Dir., Asano Family Co., etc.; b. July, 1867 in Fukushima-ken; adopted-s. of late Buhei Shiraishi. Career: grad., Law Coll., Tokyo Imp. Univ., 1892; entered Asano's firm; served chiefly in marine transportation business as Mgr. & Dir. of Toyo Kisen Kaisha, 1896–1912; founded Nippon Steel Tube Co., 1912, and engaged in steel mfg. business since. Address: 1 Kouncho, Mita, Shibaku, Tokyo.

Pres., To-a Dobun Kai; To-a Industry Co., b. July, 1870; brother of Saubu Shiraiwa, Okayama-ken. Career: grad., Nisshin Boeki Kenkyujo; established Daito Steamship Co.; Mng.-Dir., Nisshin Steamship Co. Address: 67 Aoyama-Minamicho-Rokuchome, Akasakaku, Tokyo.

Gov., Hyogo-ken; b. May, 1883 in Tokyo. Career: grad., Polit. Course, Tokyo Imp. Univ., 1908; served successively as Commr. of Shizuoka-ken, Yamanashi-ken; Dir. of Police Dept. of Yamanashi-ken, Yamagata-ken; Dir. of Home Affairs Dept. of Gifu-ken, Kyoto-fu and Tokyo-fu; and Gov., Gifu-ken, Ishikawa-ken, Toyama-ken, Saitama-ken, Shizuoka-ken, Hiroshima-ken; then transferred to present post. Address: Governor's Residence, Kobe.

Minister to Sweden; b. June, 1887; s. of Etsuzo Shiratori, Chiba-ken. Career: grad., Economics, Tokyo Imp. Univ., 1914; Head, Corr. Section; 1st Sec., Embassy, attended Naval Disarm. Conf. in Geneva; Chief, 2nd & 3rd Section, Information Bureau; Promoted to Dir. of same; Mem. of Comm. for Investigation of Cultural Works in China; Dir., Bureau of Intelligence, Foreign Office; present post since May, 1933. Address: Japanese Legation, Stockholm, Sweden.

Pres., Nitto Gramphone Co.; b. Aug., 1884 in Osaka; adopted-s. of late Zengoro Shirayama. Career: grad., Osaka Higher Com. Sch.; visited Europe, 1909; passed Exam. for Music Teacher for Middle Sch. Address: 3 Kawaramachi Itchome, Higashiku, Osaka.

Mem., House of Peers; Adviser, Seiyukai; b. Sept., 1869 at Matsuyama City; s. of Hisayasu Shoda. Career: grad., Law Coll., Tokyo Imp. Univ.; entered Finance Office; Chief, Finance Bureau; Vice-Minister of Finance in Yamamoto Cabinet; nominated Mem., House of Peers, 1914; Finance Minister in Terauchi Cabinet, 1916; Finance Minister in Kiyoura Cabinet, 1924; Education Minister in Tanaka Cabinet; went to Europe and America 3 times. Address: 45 Minamihiradaimachi, Shibuyaku, Tokyo.
Dir., Political Affairs Div., Hsing-an Prov. Career: present post since 1932. Address: Hsinking.
Dir., Land Bureau, Civil Affairs Dept., Manchoukuo. Career: present post since 1932. Address: Hsinking.

Exchange & Stock Broker; Prop., Toyu Senshobu & Toyu Shokenbu; b. June 1890 in Oita-ken; s. of Masuharu Shudo. Career: Dir., Shusui Real Estate Co.; Pres., Gohin Daiko Co.; Audtor, Dairen Money Exchange & Trust Co.; Pres. Oita-ken-jin kai of Dairen. Recreations: pictures, curio, golf, calligraphy. Address: (office) Okura Bldg., 18 Yamagatadori, Dairen. (home) 81 Sakuracho, Dairen.

Pianist; Prof., Tokyo Academy of Music, Ueno; b. May, 1885 in Kiev; n. Austrian. Career: grad., Coll. of Law, 1908; Academies of Music in Kiev and Vienna; studied piano under Prof. Feruccio Busoni; gave countless concerts in cities of European countries; taught at Academy of Music, Poland and at Vienna, for many years; present post since Apr., 1931; broadcasted over J.O.A.K., and J.O.B.K., several times. Address: 10 Hinokicho, Akasakaku, Tokyo.

M. P.; Dir., Saiseikai; Mem., Unemployment Prevention Committee; b. Aug., 1871 in Fukui-ken; s. of Ryohei Soeda, samurai. Career: grad., Law Coll., Tokyo Imp. Univ., 1898; Councillor, Hyogo-ken; Commr., Oita-ken, Kumamoto-ken, Shiga-ken and Yamanashi-ken; Gov., Saitama-ken and Yamagata-ken; Dir. of Home Affairs Bureau, Home Dept., 1917; sent to Diet 4 times; Councillor, Social Welfare Bureau. Address: 301 Shirokane-Sankocho, Shibaku, Tokyo.

Viscount; Mem., House of Peers; Dir., Nissho Marine & Fire Ins. Co.; Auditor, Bank of Taiwan, Nippon Dempo News Agency; Dir., Franco-Japannaise Societe; Int'l Committee of Kojunsha; b. July, 1870; s. of Sukemasa Soga. Career: studied in France; Captain (reserved); attended Paris Peace Conf. as Delegate of Nippon Dempo News Agency. Address: 148 Nishi-Okubo, Yodobashiku, Tokyo.

M. of Sc.; Mng.-Dir.; Meiji Sugar Mfg. Co.; same, Meiji Confectionery Co.; same, Sumatra Enterprising Co.; b. July, 1869 in Inuyama, Aichi-ken; s. of Ihori Tanaka, clansman. Career: grad., Tokyo Univ. of Tech.; Univ. of Michigan; apptd. Prof., Alma Mater; then Eng. Taiwan Govt.; founded Meiji Sugar Mfg. Co. in 1906, Meiji Confectionery Co. in 1916, Sumatra Enterprising Co. in 1918. Address: 52 Isaragocho, Shibaku, Tokyo.

n: Souza, Francisco Xavier da Silva e
t: Hon. Consul for Portugal, Kobe; Merchant; b. Jan., 1867 in Hongkong; n. Potuguese; s. of late A. J. Souza. Career: grad., Victoria Coll.; arrived in Kobe 1890 to join W. M. Strachan & Co.; left same to establish export business on his account, 1906; sent to India by Hosiery Mfrs. in Osaka to study and report on all requirement of Indian market for Japanese hosiery, 1907; joined as Mgr., Export Dept., Cornes & Co., Kobe, 1908–23; resigned same firm and went to Europe, America and India on business, 1925; Mgr., Kobe Office, Berrick & Co. from 1929 up to date; apptd. Hon. Consul for Portugal, 1919; apptd. Repr. in Japan for Macao Gov't. Bureau of Propaganda, 1924; founded Portugese Assn., 1920 and acted as Pres. for 3 consecutive years; represented Colony of Macao at funeral of eminent Portugese writer, late Capt. Wenceslau de Moraes, who died at Tokushima, July, 1929. Address: 17 Nakayamatedori-Nichome, Kobe.

American Consul at Tokyo; b. July, 1884 at Baltimore, Maryland; n. American; s. of C. Augustus E. Spamer, Attorney-at-law. Career: A. B.; A. M. (George Washington Univ., D. C.); LL. B. (Univ. of Maryland, Baltimore); Member of Maryland Bar; Printing and Publishing business, 1905–07; Educational Work in Government schools of Japan, 1907–10; Traveled in China, India, Egypt, Palestine and Europe, 1910–11; U. S. State Dept., April to June, 1916; Vice-Consul, Basel, Switzerland, 1916–17; U. S. Food Administration, 1917–19; U. S. Shipping Board, Apr. to Oct., 1919; American Consul at Yokohama, 1919; assigned to Medan, Sumatra, 1920; American Consul at Rotterdam, Holland, 1923; Amsterdam, 1924; Shanghai, 1929; present post since Jan., 1932. Address: 38 Motozonocho, Itchome, Kojimachiku, Tokyo.
—Lawyer; b. June, 1888 in Philadelphia, Penn., U. S.; n. American. Address: 45 Yamashitacho, Yokohama.

—M. D.; b. Sept., 1896 in Grossengottern, Germany; n. German; s. of Emil Stedefeld, Gutsbesitzer. Career: studied at Univs. of Freiburg, Kiel and Berlin; grad., Berlin Univ.; specialized in Ear, Nose, Throat and Eye diseases at Univ. of Berlin. Address: 67 Tansumachi, Azabuku, Tokyo.

—Mng.-Dir., K. K. L. Leybold Shokwan, Tokyo and Osaka; Vice-Chairman, Tokyo and Yokohama Foreign Board of Trade; merchant; b. Nov., 1886 in Liegnitz; n. German; s. of S. Steinfeld, banker. Career: grad., Johannis Gymnasium in Breslau; entered Simon, Evers & Co., Hamburg, 1905; later was despatched to Japan by same, and served for years as Sub.-Mgr. of its Kobe, Yokohama and Tokyo Offices; after World War, became Partner and Mng.-Dir. of present firm (successor to Mach. Dept. of Simon, Evers & Co.); also Sr. Mgr. of former firm, Hamburg. Address: 77 Sakuragaoka, Shibuyaku, Tokyo.

— American Vice-consul at Keijo, Chosen; b. Oct., 1892 in New York; n. American. Career: grad., American Coll.; U. S. Foreign Service since 1917. Address: American Consulate-General, 10 Teido, Keijo, Chosen.

— Hon. Consul-Gen. for Austria in Japan; Gen. Mgr. for Far Eats of Bohler Steel Works, Vienna (Austria); b. June, 1888 in Budapest; n. Austrian. Address: 6 Hinokicho, Akasakaku, Tokyo. Clubs: Deutsche Vereinigung, Tokyo; Ostasiatische Gesellschaft, Tokyo; Club Germania, Yokohama; German Club, Mukden.

—M. A.; B. Sc.; b. 1871 in Scotland; n. Scotch. Career: studied at Agrl. Coll. and Glasgow Univ.; Chemist and Agrl. Agent for Chilean Nitrate in Japan, 1907–31. Address: 6 of 450 Shirokane-Sankocho, Shibaku, Tokyo.

— American Consul, Tokyo; b. July, 1896 in Pomona, Illinois, U. S.; n. American; s. of late F. D. Sturgeon. Career: studied at Nebraska and Northwestern Univs.; entered American foreign service and assigned to American Embassy as Language Officer, 1920; apptd. Vice-Consul, Yokohama, 1922; assigned to Dairen, Manchoukuo, 1923; promoted Consul, 1925; assigned Consul, American Consulate-General, Tokyo, 1928. Address: American Consulate-General, Akasaka, Tokyo.

— Igakuhakushi (M. D.); Prof. Emeritus, Kanazawa Medical Coll.; b. Jan., 1872 in Yamagata-ken; s. of Tomiemon Sudo. Career: grad., Medical Coll., Tokyo Imp. Univ.; passed Exam. for Medical Practice; apptd. Asst., Alma Mater, 1894; Prof., 1905; received degree, 1911; sent to Germany for study, 1912; Prof., Kanazawa Med. School, same year; went to Europe, 1920; Prof., Kanazawa Med. Coll., 1922; Dean, same, 1924; again went to Europe, 1929; became Prof. Emeritus, 1932. Address: 1 of O-Ushizaka, Sakiuramura, Ishikawa-gun, Ishikawa-ken.

—Hogakuhakushi (D. L.); Prof., Tokyo Imp. Univ.; Dean, Law Coll., Tokyo Imp. Univ.; Councilor, Social Welfare Bureau; b. Nov., 1878 in Tokyo; s. of Ganseki Suehiro, judge. Career: grad., Law Coll., Tokyo Imp. Univ., 1912; apptd. Asst. Prof., then Prof. of same Univ.; received degree, 1920. Address: 124 Takehayacho, Koishikawauk, Tokyo.

— Hogakuhakushi (D. L.); Prof., Kyoto Imp. Univ.; Adviser, Kyoto Chamber of Com. & Industry; b. July, 1874 in Ehime-ken; s. of Shigeyasu Suehiro. Career: grad., Law Coll., Tokyo Imp. Univ., 1899 and P.-G. Course of same; studied in Europe, 1901; apptd. Asst. Prof., Kyoto Imp. Univ.; sent to America, 1913 and 1921. Address: 637 Sokokuji, Higashi-Monzencho, Karasumaru-Higashi-iru, Imadegawa, Kami-Kyoku, Kyoto.

— Vice-Admiral; Comdr.-in-Chief, Combined Fleet and 1st Squadron; b. 1881 in Saga-ken; s. of Sokuro Suetsugu. Career: grad., Naval Academy, 1899; Naval Staff Coll.; Aid-de-Camp, Naval Staff Academy; Staff, 1st Squadron; Chief, 1st Sec., Naval Gen. Staff; Comdr.-in-Chief, Submarine Squadron; Dir., Education Bureau, Naval Office; Vice-Chief, Naval Gen. Staff; Comdr.-in-Chief, 2nd Squadron; present post since Nov. 1933. Address: 895 Kamiogikubo, Yodobashiku, Tokyo.

—Mem., House of Peers; Lord-in-Waiting, Kinkei Hall; Chief Dir., Sendai Educational Inst.; b. Jan., 1869 in Miyagi-ken; s. of Michizane Sugawara. Career: grad., Law Coll., Tokyo Imp. Univ., 1895; Dir., Hakodate Revenue Supt. Bureau; Dir., Marugame and Kobe Revenue Supt. Bureaus; Councillor and Sec., Finance Office; Dir., Revenue Bureau, same Office; Vice-Minister, same Office; nominated Mem., House of Peers, 1916; Pres., Oriental Development Co., 1930–32. Address: 49 Kagomachi, Koishikawa, Tokyo.

—Hogakuhakushi (D. L.); Dir. Imp. Archives & Mausolea Bureau; b. Jan., 1873 in Okayama-ken; s. of Ryotaro Sugi. Career: grad., Law Coll., Tokyo Imp. Univ., 1900; was in service of Finance Office and Board of Audit. Address: 123 Kagomachi, Koishikawaku, Tokyo.
—Adviser, Land Bureau, Civil Affairs Dept., Manchoukuo. Career: present post since 1932. Address: Hsinking.

—Dir. & Mgr., Tokyo-fu Agrl. & Industrial Bank; b. July, 1887 in Hokkaido; s. of Katsuji Sugimoto, farmer; m. Masa, d. of Ryuzo Ogawa. Career: grad., Law Dept., Nihon Univ.; apptd. Sec. to Mgr., Elec. Light Dept., and Corr. Chief, Elec. Bureau, Tokyo Municipality; resigned same and went to British North Borneo, where he founded Borneo Plant Production Co.; returned home and apptd. Gen. Affairs Mgr., Tokyo-fu Agrl. & Industrial Bank; then promoted present post. Publications: “Recent China and Manchuria”, “Wondrous Fairy Tales”, “Datura Alba”, “On Real Estate Credit”, etc. Address: 185 Yoyogi-Sanya, Shibuyaku, Tokyo. Clubs: Elec. Club, Econ. Club.

— Auditor, Asahi Shimbun; b. July, 1872; s. of Shojiro Sugimura, samurai of Wakayama Clan. Career: studied Igirisu Horitsu Gakko and Senshin Gakuin; official, Embassy in U. S.; joined Asahi Shimbun, 1903. Address: 2210 Abiko, Abikomachi, Chiba-ken.

— Hogakuhakushi (D. L.); Minister on Waiting list; b. 1884 in Tokyo. Career: grad., Law Coll., Tokyo Imp. Univ., 1908; Attache, Emb. in France, 1916; 3rd Emb. Sec., 1918; Foreign Office Councillor, 1919; Chief, 2nd Section of Treaty Bureau, same year; Mem., Washington Conf., 1921; 1st Emb. Sec., France, 1923; Emb. Councillor, same year; Mem., 5th Gen. Meeting of League of Nations at Geneva, 1924; Dir., Japanese Bureau of League of Nations, 1926; returned home, 1933. Address: Foreign Office, Tokyo.

— Pres., Yamaichi Securities and Finance Co.; Mem., Tokyo Stock Exchange; Standing Committee, Tokyo Chamber of Com. & Industry; Auditor, Tokabu Daiko Co., Ltd.; b. Sept., 1870 in Hirosaki-shi; s. of Yoshinaga Sugino, samurai. Career: completed Banking Business Training School, Govt. Establishment; joined Bank of Japan, 1889; Asst. Mgr., Aichi Bank, 1896; Mgr., later Dir., Nagoya Bank; engaged in broker business in Tokyo since 1907; joined as Partner, Koike Goshi Kaisha, 1910; established Yamaichi Goshi Kaisha, 1917, succeeding to Koike Goshi Kaisha on its brilliant dissolution; present post since 1926. Address: 12 Mita, Meguroku, Tokyo.

— Lieut.-Gen.; Chief, Army Aviation Dept.; b. 1880 in Kokura City; s. of Tei Sugiyama. Career: grad., Mil. Academy, 1910; Chief, Mil. Affairs Section, War Dept., 1923–1925; went to Geneva for Disarmament Conf., League of Nations, 1926; Vice-Minister of War Dept., 1928; Comdr., 12th Div., 1932; present post since Mar., 1933. Address: Nakanomachi, Ichigaya, Ushigomeku, Tokyo.

— M. P.; Adviser, Rono-Taishuto; Pres., All Japan Farmers' Union; Dentist; b. Nov., 1885 in Osaka-fu. Career: grad., Osaka Agrl. School, 1903; Asst. Engr., Agrl. Society of Wakayama-ken; grad., Theological Dept., Tohoku Gakuin Coll., Sendai, 1909; preached Christianity in Fukushima-ken up to 1920; engaged in Farmer Movement with Toyohiko Kagawa; apptd. Chief, Central Executive Committee, Rodo-Nominto (Labor & Farmer Party); elected to Diet, 1932. Address: 63 Nishihorikawacho, Kitaku, Osaka.

— Hogakuhakushi (D. L.); Docteur Honoris Cansa de l'Université de Paris; Officier de la légion d'honneur; b. Jan., 1878 in Tokyo; s. of Kanzo Sugiyama, business man. Career: grad., Tokyo Imp. Univ.; sent to Europe for study, 1905–08 and 1926–27; Vice-Pres., Société Franco-Japonaise; Mng. Dir., Maison Franco-Japonaise; Mgr., Franco-Japanese Cultural Inst., Kyoto; many publications on Law. Address: 1 Sekiguchi-Komaicho, Koishikawaku, Tokyo.

— Pres., Sumida Bussan Co.; Pres., Oriental Coffee Co.; Pres., Nanyo Coffee Co.; b. 1882 in Hiroshima City; s. of Hatsuzo Sumida, farmer. Career: grad., Mid-Pacific Institute; established Sumita Shokai Co., 1898; Pres., Sumida Bussan Co., 1927; established Oriental Coffee Co., 1922; established Nanyo Coffee Co., 1926; rewarded by Nippon Sangyo Kyokai (Japan Industrial Society), 1927; rewarded by Hiroshima-ken Kaigai Kyokai (Over-sea Society), 1930. Address: 1429 Kinosaki, Mikagemachi, Mukogun, Hyogo-ken.

— Dir., Chosen Smokeless Coal Co. and Toyo Silk Mfg. Co.; Auditor, Chosen Raw Silk Co.; Mgr., Keijo Branch, Mitsui Bussan Kaisha; b. Jan., 1881 in Miye-ken; s. of Sadayuki Sumii. Career: joined Mitsui Bussan Kaisha, 1897, and served at its Branches at Osaka and Hongkong; Sub.-Mgr., Hongkong Branch. Address: 149 Asahimachi-Itchome, Keijo, Chosen.

— Nogakuhakushi (D. Agr.); Prof., Tokyo Agrl. Coll., and Dir., Educational Dept. of same; b. June, 1890 in Kumamoto-ken. Career: grad., Agrl. Coll., Tokyo Imp. Univ., 1913; Engineer, Taito Sugar Mfg. Co., 1915–18; Lecturer of same Univ., 1921–32. Address: 759 Kamimeguro, Meguroku, Tokyo.

— Baron; Pres., Sumitomo Goshi Kaisha; Dir., Besshi Mining Co., Sumitomo Bank, Sumitomo Warehouse Co., Sumitomo Trust Co., Sumitomo Life Ins. Co.; b. Feb., 1909 in Osaka; s. of late Baron Kichizaemon Sumitomo, business Man. Career: grad., Peers' School; studied at Kyoto Imp. Univ.; inherited family estate, 1926. Address: 1 of 1876 Tantakabayashi, Sumiyoshimura, Mukogun, Hyogo-ken.
—Dir., Ind. & Com. Bureau, Ind. Dept., Manchoukuo. Career: present post since 1932. Address: Hsinking.

—Gov., Heilungkiang Prov.; b. 1881 in Liaoyang-hsien, Mukden. Career: grad., Higher Normal Sch., Tokyo; Chief, Educ. Dept., Heilungkiang; Chief, Finance Dept., Kirin Prov.; Chief, Chang-tao, Heilungkiang; Mem., Govt. Committee & Chief, Construction Dept., Kirin, 1929; resigned post, 1931; Chief, Finance Dept., Kirin Govt.; Pres., Kirin Provincial Bank after Manchurian Trouble; Vice-Minister of Finance, 1932; present post since 1932. Address: Hsinking.
— Chief, Ind. Dept., Kirin Prov. Career: present post since 1932. Address: Kirin.
—Dir., Execution Bureau, Justice Dept., Manchoukuo; Lawyer. Career: studied Law in Japan; present post since 1932. Address: Hsinking.

—Mng.-Dir., Sino-Japanese Inst.; b. Oct., 1884 in Ehime-ken; s. of Mitsue Sunada, official. Career: grad., Com. Dept., To-a Dobun Shoin, China, 1906; Mgr., Tientsin Branch, Nippon Raw Cotton Co.; Pres., Japanese Chamber of Com., Tientsin, China. Address: 8 of 170 Harajuku, Sendagayamachi, Shibuyaku, Tokyo.

—M. P.; Lawyer; b. Sept., 1885 in Ehime-ken; s. of Shigeharu Sunada. Career: grad., Chuo Univ., 1904; elected to Diet 6 times; Vice-Minister, Agr. & Forestry Dept., 1931. Address: 582 Kita Senzokucho, Omori-ku, Tokyo.

—Captain; Chief, General Affairs Dept., Kure Naval Arsenal; b. Mar., 1887 in Tottori; s. of Yoshitake Sunagawa. Career: grad., Naval Academy; entered naval service. Address: Official residence B-1, Miyabara, Kure City.

— 1st Sec., Embassy at Constantinople; b. Sept., 1892 in Yamagata-ken; s. of late Shimpachiro Suwa. Career: grad., Law Coll., Tokyo Imp. Univ., 1917; passed Higher Civil Service Exam., same year; 2nd Sec., Legation at Hague, 1925; Consul at Medan, Sumatra, 1928; present post since 1932. Address: Japanese Embassy, Constantinople, Turkey.

—Adviser, Shakai Taishuto (Socialist Party); Chief Dir., Educ. Assn. for Laborer; b. Sept., 1885 in Miyagi-ken; s. of Masuji Suzuki. Career: grad., Law Coll., Tokyo Imp. Univ., 1909; joined Shueisha Printing Office; Corr., Asahi Shimbun; went to America to inspect int'l laborers' movement; attended Int'l Labor Conf. at Laborers' Delegate 4 times; elected to Diet from Osaka, 1928; present post since 1926. Address: 157 Sasukedori, Yuigahama, Kamakura, Kanagawa-ken.

—Journalist; Mng. News Editor, Tokyo Asahi Shimbun; b. Jan., 1890 in Chiba-ken; s. of Sukeyemon Suzuki, merchant. Career: grad., Tokyo School of Foreign Languages; Corr. of Asahi Shimbun during Versaille Peace Conf. and Washington Disarm. Conf., etc. Address: 470 Kami-Ochiai, Yodobashiku, Tokyo.

— Pres., Suzuki Shoten, Toshin Elec. Co., Showa Industry Co.; b. Feb., 1875 in Kanagawa-ken. Career: grad., Yokohama Com. School; established Suzuki Shoten jointly with his brother; went to Europe and America to inspect commerce and industry, 1925–26; again visited America partly on behalf of Foreign Office, 1931. Address: 83 Shimo-Osaki, Osakimachi, Shinagawaku, Tokyo.

—Grand Chamberlain; Privy Councillor; Admiral; b. Dec., 1867 in Osaka-fu; s. of late Yoshiaki Suzuki. Career: grad., Naval Academy, 1887; Naval Coll., 1896; apptd. Sub.-Lieut., 1889; fought in Sino-Japanese War as Captain, 6th Torpedo Boat; then Staff, Naval Affairs Bureau; Staff, Educ. Headquarters; Instructor, Naval Coll. and Military Academy; sent to Germany and apptd. Officer for bringing H. M. S. Kasuga home; fought in Russo-Japanese War as Comdr., Kasuga and 4th Destroyer Flotilla; Captain, H. M. S. Akashi, Soya; Principal, Naval Torpedo School; Captain, H. M. S. Shikishima, Tsukuba; Comdr., Maizuru Torpedo Flotilla and then 2nd Squadron; Dir., Personnel Affairs Bureau of Navy; Vice-Minister of Navy; Comdr., Training Squadron; Principal, Naval Academy; Comdr.-in-Chief, 2nd Squadron, 3rd Squadron, Kure Naval Station, 1st Squadron, Combined Fleet; nominated Supreme War Councillor; Chief, Naval General Staff. Address: 2 Ichibancho, Kojimachiku, Tokyo.

—Hogakuhakushi (D. L.); M. P.; Pres., Seiyukai; b. Oct., 1867 in Kanazawa; s. of Tomiemon Kawashima, and later adopted by Jiko Suzuki. Career: grad., Law Coll., Tokyo Imp. Univ., 1891; went to America and Europe to study legislation; Judge of Supreme Court; Pres., Tokyo District Court; Public Procurator, Supreme Court; Vice-Minister of Justice; Public Procurator-General; Justice Minister in Kiyoura Cabinet; Home Minister in Tanaka Cabinet; Justice Minister and later Home Minister in Inukai Cabinet; Mem., House of Peers. Address: 71 Sanbancho, Kojimachiku, Tokyo.

—Former Pres., Industrial Bank of Japan; b. June, 1866 in Hamamatsu; s. of Takizo Suzuki. Career: grad., Keio Univ., 1889; entered Yokohama Specie Bk., 1892; Sub.-Mgr., New York Branch of same, 1895; then Mgr., Tientsin, Peiping, Shanghai, Kobe Branches and Head Office, successively; Gen.-Mgr., 1914; Dir. & Gen.-Mgr., 1916; Vice-Pres., 1918; resigned, 1921; Pres., Int'l Trust Co., 1923; same, Bank of Chosen, 1925; same, Industrial Bk. of Japan, 1927; resigned, Sept., 1930. Address: 118 Hommuracho, Azabuku, Tokyo.

— Violinist; Head, Suzuki String Quartet; b. Oct., 1898 in Nagoya; s. of Masakichi Suzuki, mfr. of musical instruments. Career: completed Nagoya Com. School; studied violin under Madam Koko Ando; studied music under Profs. Karl Klinger and Georg Schumann, Hoch Schule, Germany, 1921–25; returned home once, but again went to Germany and studied under same musicians, 1926–28. Address: 26 of 176 Aoyama Harajuku, Shibuyaku, Tokyo.

—B. A. (Wabash Coll., 1906); Mgr., Finance Dept., Toho Elec. Power Co.; b. May, 1880 in Nagoya; s. of Saizo Suzuki, former editor and proprietor of local newspaper in Nagoya. Career: grad., Meiji Gakuin; Wabash Coll.; after 5 years stay in U. S., returned home; then managed father's paper for 2 years; entered Industrial Bank of Japan; served as Agent, London Branch of same, 1910–12; Sub-Mgr., Franco-Japanese Bank in Paris, 1912–18; returned home, 1918; since then has been connected with present firm. Address: 334 Oi-machi, Shinagawaku, Tokyo.

—General; Privy Councillor; Pres., Butokukai; b. Feb., 1865 in Niigata-ken; s. of Takatsugu Suzuki. Career: grad., Military Academy, 1891, and Military Coll., 1896; apptd. Staff, Gen. Staff Office; Sectional Chief, same; Instructor and Dir., Military Staff Coll.; Staff, Naval Board of Command; Comdr., Cavalry 3rd Brigade; Cavalry Inspector; Comdr., 4th and 5th Divisions; Comdr., Taiwan Army; Chief, Gen. Staff, 1926; sent to Europe, America and Siberia. Address: 606 Yoyogi-Hatsudaimachi, Shibuyaku, Tokyo.

—Dir., Army Press Bureau; b. 1894 in Chiba-ken. Career: grad., Mil. Academy, 1910 and Mil. Staff Coll., 1917; Attache, Gen. Staff Office, 1920; went to China, 1922; Comdr., 48th Regiment, 1926; to China again, 1927; Attache, Gen. Staff Office, same year; went to England, 1927; asst. Mil. Attache to Legation, China, same year; entered Mil. Affairs Bureau, Army, 1931; present post since Aug., 1933. Address: 5 Mitakecho, Sanya, Yoyogi, Shibuyaku, Tokyo.

—Dir., Kyodo Fire Ins. Co.; Auditor, Mitsukoshi, Ltd., Showa Fire Ins. Co., 1st Marine & Fire Ins. Co. and Toyo Printing Co.; b. Apr., 1862 in Nagano-ken; s. of Ryuzo Suzuki. Career: grad., Keio Univ.; Corr., Jiji Shimpo; Pres., Yokohama Boeki Shimbun; Dir., Oji Paper Mfg. Co.; Pres., Nippon Development Co.; elected to Diet 5 times, 1912–1932. Address: 2 Hirakawacho-Gochome, Kojimachiku, Tokyo.

—Nogakuhakushi (D. Agrl.); Prof., Biochemistry, Tokyo Imp. Univ. (since 1907); Research Mem., Inst. of Phys. and Chem. Research, Tokyo; Mem., Imp. Academy, Japan (since 1922); Mitglied, Deutschen Akademie der Natur Forscher (Halle); b. Apr., 1874 in Shizuoka-ken; s. of Shozo Suzuki, landowner. Career: grad., Faculty of Agrl., Tokyo Imp. Univ., 1896; apptd., Asst. Prof. of same, 1900; sent to Europe from Education Dept. to study Physiological Chemistry, 1901–06; returning home, apptd. Prof., Morioka Agrl. Coll., 1906; awarded with Imp. Academy Prize, for his discovery of Oryzanin (Vitamin B), 1921; succeeded in preparing synthetic Sake (wine), 1925; Tech. Adviser to Sankyo Co., South Manchuria Railway Co., etc. Address: 38 Udagawa, Shibuyaku, Tokyo.

— Hogakuhakushi (D. L.); Mem., Imp. Academy; Unattached Court Official, Household Dept.; Prof., Tokyo Imp. Univ.; b. Mar., 1874; s. of Kaichi Tachi, samurai. Career: grad., Law Coll., Tokyo Imp. Univ., 1897; studied Int'l Law in Daigakuin; studied Diplomatic History in Germany, France and England; Prof., Imp. Univ.; attended Paris Peace Conf. and Washington Conf. Address: 57 Gotanda 5-chome, Shinagawaku, Tokyo.

—Viscount; Pal. Councillor, Communications Dept.; Mem., House of Peers; b. Jan., 1880 in Tokyo; s. of Viscount Taneyasu Tachibana. Career: grad., Peers' School, 1904; apptd. Cavalry Lieut.; elected Mem., House of Peers several times since 1914; present post since June, 1932. Address: 2093 Sanno Nichome, Omoriku, Tokyo.

— Kogakuhakushi (D. E.); Mng. Dir. and Head, Engrg. Dept., Tokyo Elec. Light Co.; b. Apr., 1877 in Niigata-ken; s. of Zenzo Tachikawa, druggist. Career: grad., Engrg. Coll., Tokyo Imp. Univ.; joined Communications Dept.; fought in Russo-Japanese War; joined General Elec. Co., U. S.; Elec. Factory, Kobe Works, Mitsubishi Shipbuilding & Engrg., Co.; Mitsubishi Goshi Kaisha; Inawashiro Hydro-Elec. Power Co.; Tokyo Elec. Light Co. Address: 203 Kagomachi, Koishikawaku, Tokyo.

—M. P.; Pres., Dai Nippon News Agency; b. Apr., 1886 in Chiba; s. of Nenosuke Tada, landlord. Career: grad., Polit. Econ. Dept., Waseda Univ.; elected to Diet from Chiba-ken. Address: 10 Imairicho, Shibaku, Tokyo.

—Pres., Meiji Gakuin Coll.; b. Oct., 1869 in Saga-ken; s. of Setsuzo Tagawa, samurai. Career: grad., Polit. Dept., Tokyo Semmon Gakko, 1889; joined Yubin Hochi and Miyako Shimbun as Corr.; Official, Tokyo Municipality; Military Interpreter; Deputy Mayor of Tokyo; Councillor, Justice Dept.; elected to Diet 6 times since 1908; author of many books. Address: 25 Kobinata-Daimachi-Nichome, Koishikawaku, Tokyo.

— Dir., Kishimoto Shoten, Indo-Japanese Trading Co., Japan Steel Products Co., Marukugi Hanbaisho, Indian Iron & Steel Co.; Hon. Sec., Osaka Assn. for Liberty of Trading; b. Mar., 1883, Gumma Prefecture; s. of Sakusaburo Taguchi. Career: grad., Law Coll., Tokyo Imp. Univ., 1910; joined Editorial Staff, Kokumin Shimbun; toured Europe, America and British India on business 8 times since 1919. Address: 771, Uozaki-Yokoya, near Kobe.

—Mng. Dir., Asia Aluminium Co.; b. Sept., 1885 in Saitama-ken; s. of Hanshichi Taguchi. Career: grad., Yokohama Com. Sch.; Dir., Takamine Hozen Co., Sumitomo Aluminium Co., Japan Bakelight Co., Harley Davidson Motorcycle Sales Office. Address: 323 Gotenyama, Kitashinagawa, Shinagawaku, Tokyo.

—M. P.; b. Dec., 1879 in Oita-ken; s. of Giichi Tajima, landlord. Career: grad., Law Coll., Tokyo Imp. Univ.; Deputy Mayor, Tokyo City, 1923–24; Vice-Minister, Com. & Industry Dept., 1931. Address: 424 Juniso, Yodobashiku, Tokyo.

—Dir., and Mgr., Osaka Branch, Mitsui Bussan Kaisha; b. Feb., 1883 in Gumma-ken; s. of Bumpei Tajima, farmer. Career: grad., Tokyo Higher Com. School, 1905; joined Mitsui Bussan Kaisha, same year, and transferred to its New York Branch; apptd. Mgr., same Branch, 1921; elected Dir., 1930; apptd. Mgr., Osaka Branch, 1931. Address: 1 Koraibashi-Nichome, Higashiku, Osaka.

—Pres., Yokohama Com. Coll.; b. Dec. 1876 in Kumamoto-ken; s. of Eiji Tajiri, lawyer. Career: grad., Tokyo Univ. of Com. 1901; then completed Consular Service Graduate Course of same, 1903; Prof., Nagasaki Com. Coll., 1908–1920; Pres. of same, 1920–1923; present post since Dec., 1923. Address: Masaka, Isogocho, Isogoku, Yokohama.

—Pres., Takabane Shoten and Teikoku Brick Co.; Dir., Daikokuya Woolen Tailor and Japan Trades Assn.; b. July, 1867 in Aichi-ken; s. of late Sobei Takabane. Career: inherited family estate and father's name; Vice-Chairman, Kojimachi Ward Assembly; Mem., Tokyo Chamber of Com. & Industry. Address: 3 Kioicho, Kojimachiku, Tokyo.

— Pres., North Manchuria Mining Co.; Pres., Oriental Transportation & Trading Co.; Dir., Chuka Elec. Engrg. Works and Oriental Iron Steel Co.; b. Oct., 1880 in Fukui-ken; s. of Korenori Takagi, samurai. Career: studied at Niigata Com. School; grad., Tokyo Com. & Tech. Middle Sch.; joined Mitsui Bussan Kaisha and was sent to China; served as Military Interpreter in Boxer Uprising; on its conclusion again joined Mitsui and served at its Shanghai and Hankow Branches; resigned, 1911; Japanese Repr., Han-Yeh-Ping Iron & Coal Mining Co., 1911; founded Oriental Transportation & Trading Co., 1913. Address: 28 Minamicho, Takanawa, Shinagawaku, Tokyo.

—Prof., Tokyo Imp. Univ.; b. Dec., 1889 in Tokyo; s. of Baron Naibu Kanda and later adopted by mother's family. Career: grad., Law Coll., Tokyo Imp. Univ.; apptd. Asst.-Prof., Tokyo Imp. Univ., 1919; sent to America for study 4 years; travelled in Europe, 1923; Hepburn Prof. of American Constitution, History, and Diplomacy since 1924; served Executive Board of Japan Council of Institute of Pacific Relations since 1925. Address: 341 Seijo, Kinuta-mura, Tokyo-fu.

— Dir., Musashino Ry. Co.; Keizaigakushi (B. Econ.); b. Jan., 1903 in Tokyo-fu; s. of Gentaro Takahashi, landowner. Career: grad., Polit. Econ. Dept., Meiji Univ. Address: 265 Shimo-Hoya, Hoya-mura, Tokyo-fu.

—Kabuki Actor; b. 1880 in Tokyo; s. of Ichikawa Sadanji, 4th. Career: made debut, 1884; succeeded father's name, “Sadanji”, after father's death, 1906; visited Europe, same year; invited to Soviet for Kabuki Performances, 1928. Address: 19 Kitakogacho, Kanda, Tokyo.

— Chief, Social Section, Taiwan Gov't.; b. Feb., 1894 in Hiroshima-ken; s. of Shizundo Takahashi. Career: grad., Law Coll., Tokyo Imp. Univ., 1919; Official, Kagoshima-ken Pref. Office; Police Supt., Tottori-ken; same, Taiwan Gov't.; Procurator and Commr., Taihoku Pref.; Chief, Police Dept. of same; present post since 1932. Address: Sakumacho, Ichome, Taihoku City, Taiwan.

— Dir., Shoryu Bank, Yamashita Steamship Co.; Auditor, Mukden Hemp Mfg. Co.; Councillor, Yasuda Hozensha; b. June, 1882 in Sendai City; s. of Kagetsugu Takahashi, company director. Career: grad., Tokyo Kyokai Univ.; Mem., Maritime Affairs Board; Mng. Dir., Toyo Kisen Kaisha. Address: 17 of “Ha”-2 Yayoicho, Mukogaoka, Hongoku, Tokyo.

—M. P.; Rear-Admiral (reserve); b. Jan., 1879 in Iwate-ken; s. of Fukuya Takahashi, landowner. Career: grad., Naval Academy; apptd. Staff, Naval General Staff; Chief, Aviation Bureau, Naval Dept.; Captain, H. M. S. “Tama”; Head Instructer, Naval Academy; Dir., Naval Gunnery School; Comdr., 1st Torpedo Flottila; sent to Diet from Iwate-ken twice. Address: 121, Jiyugaoka, Himonya, Meguroku, Tokyo.

— Finance Minister; Adviser, Seiyukai Party; b. July, 1854 in Sendai City; s. of Koretada Takahashi, samurai. Career: sent to America by Shogunate; entered Education Dept. and served as Dir. of several schools; joined Bank of Japan and apptd. its Vice-Pres.; Pres., Yokohama Specie Bank; Pres., Bank of Japan; Finance Minister in Yamamoto and Hara Cabinets; Prime Minister; Pres., Seiyukai Party; ennobled, 1930 and nominated Mem., House of Peers; Agrl. & Com. Minister, Agr. & Forestry Minister and Com. & Industry Minister in Kato Cabinet; Adviser, Yasuda Hozensha; Finance Minister in Inukai Cabinet, 1931–32; present post since 1932. Address: 10 Omotemachi-Sanchome, Akasakaku, Tokyo.

— Pres., Teikoku Refrigerator Co. and Tokyo Warehouse Co.; Sr. Mng. Dir., Aioi Mujin K. K.; Dir., Nippon Dry-Ice Co., Ikegami Elec. Ry. Co., Hokkaido Ry. Co. and Hayashi Iron Works; Auditor, Nippon Fire Ins. Co., Toyo Can Mfg. Co., Kawasaki Ice Mfg. Co., Chiba Godo Bank and Toyo Bussan Kaisha; b. Sept., 1871 in Miyagi-ken; 3rd s. of Heizaburo Takahashi, samurai. Career: grad., 2nd Higher School and Fisheries Inst.; founded Iwate-ken Fishery School by order of Educational Authorities; after serving in official circles several years, apptd. Mng. Dir., Chiba-ken Agrl. & Industrial Bank; Mgr., Kobe Branch, Nippon Fire Ins. Co.; established Teikoku Refrigerator Co. Address: 2 of 532, Shimo-Meguro-Hatchome, Meguroku, Tokyo.

—Author; b. Sept., 1896 in Tokyo; s. of Jisaku Takahashi, business man. Career: grad., Tokyo Sch. of Foreign Languages and Tokyo Imp. Univ.; formerly Literary Staff of Tsukiji Little Theatre; Mem., Japanese Author Assn. Address: 14 Ueno-Hanazonocho, Shitayaku, Tokyo.

—Vice-Admiral; Comdr.-in-Chief, 2nd Squadron; b. Aug., 1882, in Tokyo. Career: Grad., Naval Academy, 1901; Comdr., H. M. S. Fuso; Comdr.-in-Chief, Combined Fleet; President, Naval Stuff Coll.; Vice-Chief, Navy Gen. Staff; present post since Nov. 1933. Address: 83 Imazato-cho, Shirokane, Shibaku, Tokyo.

—Architect; b. June, 1892 in Shiga-ken; s. of Yasukichi Takahashi, retired official. Career: grad., Tokyo Imp. Univ., 1916; apptd. Official Architect, Home Dept.; same, Imp. Household; Chief Architect, Tokyo Reconstruction Co. Address: 12 Hinokicho, Akasakaku, Tokyo.

—Dir., Nissho Co., Osaka; b. Mar., 1887 in Ehime-ken; s. of Sojiro Takahata, business man. Career: grad., Kobe Univ. of Com.; engaged in int'l trade as Mgr., London Branch of Suzuki-Shoten. Address: Okamoto, Mukogun, Hyogo-ken.

—Pres., Mannensha; b. Feb., 1857 in Tokushima; s. of Shinzo Takaki, samurai, Tokushima Clan. Career: studied at Chokyukan and Tokushima Branch School of Keio Univ.; joined Osaka Nippo-sha, 1879; shifted to Daito Nippo-sha, 1882; established Mannensha, 1890 and turned it into a corporation, 1920; apptd. Mgr., Osaka Christian Church, 1895; Dir., Japan Kumiai Christian Church, 1899; Mng. Dir., Maintenance Board, same. 1924. Address: Ashiya, Seidomura, Muko-gun, Hyogo-ken.

—Baron; Igakuhakushi (M. D.); Mem., House of Peers; b. Nov., 1875 in Tokyo; s. of Kanehiro Takaki, M. D., Mem., House of Peers. Career: grad., Peers' School, then studied physics in England, Germany and Austria for years; grad., Kings Coll. School and St. Thomas Hospital Medical Coll., London; served as Head Sergeon at St. Thomas Hospital, London; as Pres., Tokyo Hospital and Tokyo Charity Hospital; Head, Special Sch. of Tokyo Charity Hospital; sent to America to investigate medical education; elected to Mem., House of Peers; twice; became Pres., Japan and Kanto Rugby Union. Address: 13 Higashi-Toriizaka, Azabuku, Tokyo.

— Mng. Dir., Japan Tourist Bureau; b. Feb., 1886 in Miye-ken; s. of Jinnosuke Takaku. Career: grad., English Dept., Tokyo School of Foreign Languages, 1908; passed Higher Civil Service Exam., 1917; Penn. Univ., U. S., 1923; entered Ry. Dept.; apptd. Chief, Int'l Section, Transportation Bureau; joined present office, 1928; sent to Europe and America. Address: 130 Horinouchi, Wadaborimachi, Suginamiku, Tokyo.

— Mem., Nagoya Chamber of Com. & Industry; Prop., Shitei Shoten (Dealers in Fertilizer); High-Taxpayer; b. Nov., 1889; s. of late Teiichi Takamatsu, Aichi-ken. Career: grad., Law Coll., Tokyo Imp. Univ., 1915. Address: 3 Nayamachi-Itchome, Nakaku, Nagoya.

— Igakuhakushi (M. D.); Chief, Preventive Section, Sanitary Bureau, Home Office; b. Sept., 1884 in Ibaraki-ken; s. of Tohei Takano, landowner. Career: grad., Medical Coll., Tokyo Imp. Univ., 1909; became Staff, Infectious Diseases Institute; Mem., Kitazata Institute; Prof., Medical Coll., Keio Univ.; served Home Office; sent to Europe and America for study; received degree, 1918; present post since 1932. Address: 23 Minami-Teramachi, Yotsuyaku, Tokyo.

—Admiral; b. Apr., 1867 in Miyazaki-ken; s. of Saneaki Takarabe, samurai. Career: grad., Naval Academy, 1891, and Naval Staff Coll., 1893; apptd. Staff, Naval Board of Command; Comdr., H. M. S. Fuji; Staff, 1st Squadron; Vice-Minister of Navy; Comdr., 3rd Squadron and Ryojun Naval Port; Comdr., Saseho, Maizuru and Yokosuka Naval Stations; Supreme War Councillor; Navy Minister in T. Kato, Yamamoto, K. Kato, Wakatsuki and Hamaguchi Cabinets; attendede Naval Disarmament Conf., London, 1929. Address: 519 Shirokane-Sankocho, Shibaku, Tokyo.

— Igakuhakushi (M. D.); Physician; Pres., Toyonaika Hospital and Nankoin-Sanatorium; b. Aug., 1861 in Kyoto-fu; s. of Morimasa Masuyama, physician. Career: grad., Kyoto-fu Pref. Medical School and then Med. Dept., Tokyo Imp. Univ.; studied at Med. Dept., Berlin Univ.; Asst. Physician, Internal Dept., Med. Coll., Tokyo Imp. Univ., 1890–96; Lecturer, Internal Dept., Saiseigakusha Medical School, 1892–1902; representing Tokyo Medical and two other Societies, was sent to Hongkong to visit Dr. T. Aoyama who suffered from Pest, 1894; founded Toyonaika Hospital in Tokyo, 1896 and Nankoin-Sanatorium in Chigasaki, Kanagawa-ken, 1889; over both of which has been presided since. Address: 15 Kudan, 4-chome, Kojimachiku, Tokyo. Chigasakimachi, Kanagawa-ken.

— Stage Dancer; Instructor, Toyo Girls' Musical Academy, Nikaido's Gymnastic School, Shochiku Music and Ballet Dept., Shimbashi Geisha Girls' School; b. Sept., 1905 in Ishikawa-ken. Career: completed Ishikawa-ken Pref. 1st Girls' High School; grad., Tokyo Academy of Music; also Dance Course, Imperial Theater, Tokyo; studied at Tarasoff's and Arbacherry's Ballet Schools, Madame Noyes's Greek and Interpretative Dancing School, and Cembel's School in New York; stayed 3 years in Europe and America; gave several recitals in New York, once appearing at Aeorian Hall; made performance at Alhambra Theater, Paris, with Morgan dancers; appeared at Collicium Theater, London, with Lopoukowa and Idzikowski. Address: 868 Kashiwagi, Yodobashiku, Tokyo.
—Pres. Manchuria Daily News; Lieut.-Gen. (Reserve); b. Dec., 1869 in Kanazawa-shi; s. of late Bunkichi Takayagi. Career: grad., Military Academy and Military Coll. Address: 19 Hatsunecho, Dairen.

—Dir., Kansai Trust Co.; b. May, 1862 in Fukuoka-ken; s. of Kichiji Takayama, farmer. Career: grad., Tokyo Semmon Gakko (present Waseda Univ.); went to Europe and America to study Bourse System, 1886; Pres., Osaka Dojima Rice-Exchange; joined Mitsui; Dir., Kyodo Fire Ins. Co., 1906. Address: 12 Kita-Momotanicho, Minamiku, Osaka.

—Pres., Oriental Development Co.; b. July, 1867 in Ehime-ken; s. of Bumpei Takayama, samurai. Career: grad., Keio Univ., 1889; joined Mitsui Bank serving as Asst. Mgr. and Mgr., Hakodate, Miike, Nagasaki, Fukagawa and Otsu Branches; apptd. Dir., 1st Fire & Marine Ins. Co.; elected to Diet 6 times since 1908; Mng. Dir., Dai Nippon Sugar Mfg. Co.; Chairman, Board of Dirs., Teikoku Com. Bank; present post since 1932. Address: 23 Kasumicho, Tokyo.

—Prof., Law Coll., Tokyo Imp. Univ.; Dir., Pacific Problem Inquiry Committee; b. May, 1892 in Saitama-ken; s. of Kinzaemon Takayanagi. Career: grad., Law Coll., Tokyo Imp. Univ., 1912; apptd. Lecturer of same; went to Europe and America, 1915 and 1923; present post since 1920. Address: 253 Hisagi, Zushimachi, Kanagawa-ken.

—Bungakuhakushi (D. Litt.); Member de l'Institute international de Sociologie; Member of American Academy of Polit. & Social Science; b. Mar., 1871 in Niigata-ken; s. of Sadao Takebe. Career: grad., Tokyo Imp. Univ.; studied in Europe and America; Prof., Tokyo Imp. Univ.; Lecturer, Tokyo Univ. of Com.; same Tokyo Higher Normal School; same, Waseda Univ.; same, Military Coll.; same, Komazawa Univ., 1923–1928. Address: Yokogoemura, Nakakanbaragori, Niigata-ken.

—Kogakuhakushi (D. E.); b. Nov., 1872 in Fukuyama City, Hiroshima-ken; s. of Naoyuki Takeda, Chief Public Procurator. Career: grad., Tokyo Imp. Univ., 1887; apptd. Asst. Prof., Alma Mater, 1888; sent abroad for study of architecture, 1900; Prof., Kyoto Higher Tech. School, 1893; sent abroad to study Parl. bldg.; became Architect of Construction Bureau, Finance Dept.; Dir., Nagoya Higher Tech. School; Prof., Kyoto Imp. Univ.; Mem., National Monument & Treasure Preservation Committee; same, Kyoto City Town Planning Committee; same, Imp. Art Museum Designing Committee. Address: 4 Kamifusacho, Kamikyoku, Kyoto.

—Dir., Nippon Camphor Co.; Acting partner, Takeda & Co.; b. June, 1887 in Hyogo-ken; s. of Bunkichi Takeda. Career: grad., Kobe Higher Com. School; Graduate Course, Tokyo Higher Com. School. Address: 25 Kumochimachi Itchome, Fukiaiku, Kobe.

—Mng.-Dir., Iida Co. (Takashimaya); b. June, 1874 in Kyoto; s. of Inosuke Takeda, business man. Career: grad., Tokyo Higher Com. School; was in Europe for 15 years; visited Europe and America 4 times. Address: 18 Kasumicho, Azabuku, Tokyo.
—Mng.-Dir., Chobei Takeda & Co., Osaka; b. Aug., 1885 in Nara-ken; s. of Denjiro Takeda. Career: grad., Keio Univ. 1910; succeeded family estate, 1913. Address: 78 Kishinoshita, Ashiya, Hyogo-ken.

—A. M. (Columbia Univ.); Paymasteer Captain; Chief, 2nd Section, Gen. Affairs Dept., Naval Construction Headquarters; b. Apr., 1887 in Ibaragi-ken; s. Matsutaro Takei. Career: grad., Tokyo Univ. of Com., 1909; Columbia Univ., 1918; Attaché to Embassy in U. S.; Instructor, Naval Coll.; Head Instructor, Naval Paymasters' School; attached to Naval Construction Headquarters. Address: 416 Shimo-Ochiai, Yodobashiku, Tokyo.

— Adviser, Capital Construction Bureau, Manchoukuo; b. in Hyogo-ken. Career: grad., Civil Engrg. Coll., Kyoto Imp. Univ.; Prof., Kyoto Imp. Univ.; present post since 1933. Address: Hsinking. (Home Address) Kokuramachi, Kitashirakawa, Sa-kyo, Kyoto.

—Mem., House of Peers; Adviser, Tokyo Nichi-Nichi and Osaka Mainichi Shimbun; b. Oct., 1865 in Saitama-ken; s. of Senzaburo Kiyono; adopted by Tohei Takekoshi. Career: studied at Dojinsha and Keio Univ.; Corr., Jiji Shimpo, Osaka Kôron and Kokumin Shimbun; Editor, Sekai-no-Nippon, Monthly; apptd. Councillor and Sec., Education Dept., 1898; went to Europe, 1899, and France, where founded Franco-Japanese Assn., 1906; sent to Diet 5 times since 1902; apptd. Dir., Imp. Compiling Bureau, Household Dept. Address: 333 Arai-Yakushimachi, Nakanoku, Tokyo.

—Councillor, Embassy to America; b. Dec., 1884 in Saga City; s. of Tokitoshi Taketomi, Mem., House of Peers. Career: grad., Law Coll., Tokyo Imp. Univ., 1910; apptd. Diplomatic Probationer, Legation in Mexico; Sec. of Legation; Sec. and Commr., Foreign Office; Chief, 2nd Section, Com. Bureau; Sec., Agrl. & Com. Dept.; Sec. of Embassy; Consul-Gen. in France and America; Dir., Com. Bureau, Foreign Office 1927–32; Present post since 1933. Address Japanese Embassy, Washington, D. C.
—Dir., Gen. Affairs Bureau, Civil Dept., Manchoukuo. Career: present post since 1932. Address: Hsinking.

—Dir., Central Bank, Manchoukuo; b. 1881 in Yamaguchi-ken; adopted s. of Kojiro Takeyasu. Career: grad., German Law Coll., Tokyo Imp. Univ., 1905; entered Chosen Bank, same year; Chief, Financial Section, Chosen Bank; Chief, Gen. Affairs Section, Chosen Bank, Tokyo Branch; Mgr., Chosen Bank; present post since 1932. Address: Hsinking.

—Parl. Vice-Minister of Foreign Affairs; M. P.; b. Apr., 1884 in Aichi-ken; s. of Iwao Taki. Career: grad., Law Coll., Kyoto Imp. Univ., 1911; apptd. Lecturer, Kyoto Imp. Univ. and Kansai Univ.; elected to Diet 6 times since 1917; Councillor, Meiji Shrine Construction Bureau; Sec. to Home Minister; Sec. to Pres., Seiyu-Honto Party; Sec.-Gen., Seiyukai Party; present post since June, 1932. Address: 106 Kogaicho, Azabuku, Tokyo.

—Mng.-Dir., Kobe Exchange; Dir., Ujigawa Elec. Co.; Auditor, Osaka Fire & Marine Ins. Co., Nippon Menka K. K. etc.; Dir., Japan Economic League; Councillor, Hyogo-ken Industrial Assn.; Honorary Consul for Bolivia Republic; Councillor, Kobe Chamber of Com. & Industry; b. Dec., 1874 in Naraken. Career: grad., Osaka Higher Com. School; Pres., Kobe Chamber of Com. & Industry. Address: 1 Mizukidori 2-chome, Nakaku, Kobe.

—Lieut.-Gen. (Reserve.); b. Sept., 1878 in Shizuoka-ken; s. of Nobuo Tamon. Career: grad., Military Cadet School, 1898; Military Academy, 1899; Military Staff Coll., 1909; apptd. Instructor, Tactics Dept., Military Staff Coll.; Chief, Tamon's Party; Comdr., Infantry 2nd Regiment; Chief Staff, 4th Div.; Comdr., Infantry 6th Brigade; Head, 4th Dept., Gen. Staff Office; Sec., Military Academy; Pres. of same; Comdr., 2nd Div.; resigned post 1933. Address: c/o War Office, Tokyo.

— Pres., Nippon Steamship Co.; Pres., Tamura Gomei Kaisha; Dir., Oriental Hotel; Adviser, Kyodo Gyogyo K. K.; b. Jan., 1856; s. of Shozaburo Kuhara, business man, and later adopted by Ko Tamura. Career: inherited family estate, 1895. Address: Tenno, Hironomachi, Minatoku, Kobe.

—Dir., Kyodo Fishing Industry Co., Kobe Elec. Machinery Co., Asahi Marine Ins. Co., Dairen Central Real Estate Co.; Auditor, Nippon Kisen K. K.; Acting Partner, Tamura Gomei Kaisha; b. Feb., 1890 in Kyoto; s. of Junkichi Kishimoto; adopted by Ichiro Tamura, company director. Career: grad., Engrg. Coll., Tokyo Imp. Univ., 1914; made inspection tour to Europe and America. Address: Tenno, Hiranomachi, Minatoku, Kobe.

—Mem., House of Peers; Adviser, Kobe Chamber of Com. & Industry; Pres., Nikka Trust Co. and Nichibei Polished Rice & Milling Co.; Dir., Pacific Fire & Marine Ins. Co.; Pres., Kobe Exporters' Assn. and Kobe Japan-America Assn.; Prop., Tamura Trading Co.; b. Dec., 1863 in Osaka-fu; s. of Tahei Tamura. Career: studied in America; engaged in trade between Japan and Canada; opened store at Vancouver City; established Head Office at Kobe, and Branches at Osaka, Kyoto, Yokohama and Vancouver; apptd. Hon. Commr. for Canada Gov't.; elected to Diet from Kobe City, 1915; attended Int'l Labor Conf. Washington, 1919 as Capital Delegate; elected Mem., House of Peers. Address: 23 Sakaemachi-Rokuchome, Kobe.

— Ringakuhakushi (Dr. of Forestry); Mem., National Park Committee; Lecturer, Tokyo Imp. Univ., Non-Commissioned Staff of Home Office; b. Sept., 1890 in Okayama-ken; adopted-s. of Kisaku Tamura. Career: grad., Forestry Course, Agrl. Dept., Tokyo Imp. Univ., then P.-G. Course of same; apptd. Lecturer, Chiba-ken Pref. Horticultural School, 1917; same, Agrl. Dept., Tokyo Imp. Univ., 1919; Business Mgr., Hygienic Bureau, of Home Office, 1920, chiefly serving for research of Nat. Parks; went to Europe and America to study landscape architecture, 1923–24; apptd. Non-Commissioned Staff, Forestry Bureau, Agr. and Forestry Dept., 1924; Chief, Nat. Park Committee Meeting, 1931. Address: 225 Honmuracho, Azabuku, Tokyo.

—Dir., Dai Nippon Drug Mfg. Co.; Prop., Gohei Tanabe Shoten (mfgs., importers and exporters of chemicals & drugs); b. May, 1878 in Osaka; s. of late Gohei Tanabe. Career: inherited family estate, 1916. Address: 21 Doshumachi Sanchome, Higashiku, Osaka.

—Privy Councillor, Manchoukuo; b. 1878 in Yamanashi-ken; s. of Yoshinobu Tanabe. Career: grad., Law Coll., Tokyo Imp. Univ.; Chief, Administration Section, Yokohama Post-Office; Chief, Niigata Post-Office; Chief, Gen. Affairs Section, Osaka Communication Administrative Bureau, Communication Detp., 1911; studied Communication Works in France; Sec. and Councillor, Communication Dept., 1913; Councillor, Kwantung Govt., 1915; Gov., Osaka-fu, 1927; resigned post, 1928; present post since 1932. Address: Hsinking.

—M. P.; Adviser, Seiyukai; Pres., Niigata Jiji Shimbun-sha; Mng. Dir., Tateyama Elec. Power Co.; Dir., Nisshin Spinning Co. and Sagami Spinning Co.; b. Jan., 1874; s. of late Makichi Tanabe, Niigata-ken. Career: grad., Chuo Univ.; Mem., Niigata-ken Pref. Assembly; elected to Diet 7 times from Niigata-ken. Address: 8 Funamachi, Yotsuyaku, Tokyo.

—M. P.; Pres., Himegawa Elec. Power Co., Chuo Elec. Power Co.; Dir., Fujigawa Elec. Power Co. and Tokyo House; Sake Brewer; b. Mar., 1879; s. of Shichibei Tanabe, Yamanashi-ken. Career: grad., Kofu Middle School; elected to Diet 3 times. Address: Shichirimura, Higashiyamanashi-gun, Yamanashi-ken. (Tokyo home) 19 Kamimeguro I-chome, Meguroku, Tokyo.

—Dir., Mitsui Bussan Kaisha; Liaotung Steamship Co., Nippon Flour Mill Co., Sengokubara Real Estate Co.; Auditor, Chuo Univ.; b. July, 1874 in Fukui-ken; s. of late Kumakichi Tanaka, farmer. Career: grad., Tokyo Hogaku-in (present Chuo Univ.), 1891; joined Mitsui Bussan Kaisha, 1895; Sec., Head, various Sections of same; apptd. Dir., 1921. Address: 66 Hanezawa, Shibuyaku, Tokyo.

— Pres., Dai Nippon Artificial Fertilizer Co., Nippon Felt Co., Kyodo Pulp Co. and Godo Yushi Co.; Chairman, Board of Dirs., Osaka Alkali Land Co. and Nitto Ryuso Co., Vice-Pres., Karafuto Steamship Co. and Jomo Elec. Ry. Co.; Dir., Oji Paper Mfg. Co., Yashiro Paper Mfg. Co., Kumamoto Elec. Co., Oshima Steel Works, Asano Cement Co., Nippon Cement Co., Nippon Concrete Industry Co., Teikoku Artificial Fertilizer Co., Taiwan Fertilizer Co. and Nippon Eiga Gekijo, Ltd.; Auditor, Nippon Elec. Power Co., Tokyo-Wan Steamship Co. and Sino-Japanese Colliery & Steamship Co.; Councillor, Jinju Life Ins. Co.; b. Aug., 1863; s. of Shuzo Okawa; adopted by Ine Tanaka. Career: established Kanto Soda Co., 1896, and became its Mng. Dir.; participated in many business and built up present posts. Address: 36 Nezu-Miyanagacho, Hongoku, Tokyo.

—Pres., Kameoka Bk.; Pres., Kyoto Kosho Co. and Kyoto Textile Co.; Dir., Kyoto Stock Exchange; b. Jan., 1877 in Kyoto-fu; s. of Gentaro Tanaka, banker. Career: grad., Tokyo Univ. of Com., 1901; engaged in banking business for years. Address: Nishikoji-Agaru Shinmachidori, Nakakyoku, Kyoto.

Hogakuhakushi (D. L.); Pres., Waseda Univ.; Mem., Educational Council; b. Feb., 1876 in Nagano-ken; s. of Shunosuke Tanaka. Career: grad., Polit. Dept., Waseda Univ., 1896; then studied in Europe and America as student of Waseda Univ.; returning home, apptd. Prof. of same; also served Tokyo Nichi-Nichi and Tokyo Mainichi Shimbun as Editorial Staff and Chief Editor; received degree, 1910; apptd. present post, 1931. Address: 170 Bentencho, Ushigomeku, Tokyo.

Dir. & Mgr. of Kobe and Osaka Branches, Mitsubishi Warehouse Co.; b. May, 1886 in Tokyo-fu; s. of Ginzo Tanaka, samurai. Career: joined Mitsubishi Warehouse Co. Mgr., Osaka Branch of same; then Mgr., Kobe Branch; Mgr. of both branches in Kobe and Osaka since June, 1931; apptd. Dir. of same Jan. 1932. Address: 42 Shimoyamatedori-Hatchome, Kobe.
Dir., Finance Bureau, Finance Dept., Manchoukuo. Career: present post since 1932. Address: Hsinking.

M. P.; Pres., Municipal Assembly; Pres., Tanaka Saw Mill, Ltd.; b. Apr., 1877 in Gumma-ken; s. of Keizo Tanaka, landlord and Dir., Tokyo Housekeeping School. Career: completed Maebashi Middle School; studied at Doshisha Univ., Kyoto. Address: Miyashita-dori-Itchome, Asahigawa City.

Diplom für Versicherungs Verständige; Mem. Japanese Institue of Actuaries; Mng. Dir., Nippon Life Assurance Co.; b. Oct., 1881 in Tottori-ken; s. of late Masaharu Tanaka, Mayor of Tottori. Career: grad., Law Coll., Tokyo Imp. Univ., 1907; entered present firm, 1907; became Dir. of same, 1924; present post since 1928. Address: Nigawa, Ryogenmura, Mukogun, Hyogo-ken.

Ambassador on Waiting List; b. Jan., 1877 in Kyoto-fu; s. of Jinzaburo Tanaka. Career: grad., Consul Course, Tokyo Higher Com. School, 1898; Consul at Singapore, Hongkong and Seattle; Sec., Foreign Office; Chief, 1st and 2nd Section, Com. Bureau; Councillor of Embassy; Dir., Com. Bureau and Intelligence Bureau, Foreign Office; Pres., Japan Times; Ambassador to USSR, 1925-30; sent to Manchukuo, 1932. Address: 11 Konno, Shibuyaku, Tokyo.

M. P.; Councillor, Kyoto Municipal Assembly; Head, Kamitoba Credit Assn.; Head, Yodo River Water Facilities Assn.; Councillor, Minseito Party and Adviser of its Kyoto Branch; b. Feb., 1868 in Kyoto-fu; s. of late Yushiro Tanaka, farmer. Career: Kamioka Village Headman in Kyoto-fu since 1901; Mem., Councillor, Chairman, Kyoto-fu Pref. Assembly since 1894; elected to Diet 4 times from Kyoto-fu; recognised by Pref. Governor and Education Minister for merit of his service. Address: 128 Shimadacho, Kamitoba, Shimokyoku, Kyoto.

Mem., House of Peers; Rigakuhakushi (D. Sc.); Emeritus Prof., Tokyo Imp. Univ.; Pres., Nippon Romaji-Kai; b. Sept., 1856; s. of Inazo Tanakadate, samurai. Career: grad., Sc. Coll., Tokyo Daigaku, 1882; studied Elec. and Magnetism at Glasgow Univ. and Berlin Univ.; nominated Mem., House of Peers. Address: 144 Zoshigayamachi, Koishikawaku, Tokyo.

Councillor, Japanese Emb., Manchoukuo; b. Feb., 1889 in Kumamoto-ken; brother of Masaichi Tani, samurai. Career: grad., Law Coll., Tokyo Imp. Univ., 1913; apptd. Elève-Consul, Diplomatic Probationer and Sec. of Embassy; after long service in Europe, apptd. Councillor, Foreign Office and Sec. to Foreign Minister; Chief, 1st Section, Asia Bureau; Sec., Embassy in America, 1927; Dir., Asia Bureau, Foreign Office, 1930; present post since July, 1933. Address: c/o Japanese Embassy, Hsinking, Manchoukuo.

B. A.; M. A. (Harvard Univ.); b. June, 1884 in Miye-ken; 4th s. of late Bunshichi Tanikawa, banker. Career: grad., Univ. of Minnesota; Post Grad. Course, Harvard Univ.; Prof., Osaka Higher Com. School, 1911-18; Mng. Dir., Daito Marine & Fire Ins. Co.; present post since 1931. Address: 1107 Azekura, Sumiyoshimura, Mukogun, Hyogo-ken.

Vice-Admiral; Chief Paymaster, Kure Naval Station; b. Oct., 1883 in Fukuoka-ken; s. of Shikei Tannawa, physician. Career: grad., Tokyo Higher Com. School, 1905; served Navy since 1905. Address: 3 of Ko, Official residence, Kure Naval Station, Kure City.

Afghan Minister to Tokyo; b. 1897 in Haliul, Afghanistan; s. of M. Zanan Khan Tarzi. Career: grad., Habibia Coll.; diplomatic service for 15 yrs.; appointed Minister to Paris, 1927; present post since Sept., 1933. Address: Afghan Legation, 22 4-chome, Iigura, Azabuku, Tokyo.

Consul, Hsinking, Manchoukuo; b. May, 1896 in Tokyo; s. of Yoshinori Tashiro, M. D. Career: grad., Law Coll., Tokyo Imp. Univ., 1920; apptd. Diplomatic Probationer in Switzerland; Sec. of Embassy in Italy; Commr., Foreign Office, 1926; Mem., 1st Section, Asia Bureau; Consul at Tientsin, 1927, and Hsinking, 1929, present post since 1933. Address: Japanese Consulate-Gen. Hsinking, Manchoukuo.

B. S.; Ph. B.; Ph. D.; Pres., Tateishi Tr. Co., Ltd.; b. 1866 in Fukushima-ken; s. of Shigeiye Tateishi, samurai. Career: grad., Aoyama Gakuin; Univ. of Rochester, N. Y.; Univ. of Pensylvania, Pa.; Univ. of Hale, Germany; Staff, Kihenkai in Osaka Exhibition, 1893. Address: 30 Takanawa-Minamicho, Shibaku, Tokyo.

Lieut.-Gen.; Attaché, Gen. Staff Office; b. Oct., 1880 in Niigata-ken; s. of Shuhei Tatekawa. Career: grad., Military Staff Coll., 1909; Military Attaché in India; Sec. to War Minister; Committee, League of Nations; Comdr., Cavalry 5th Regiment; Sectional Chief, Gen. Staff Office; Military Attaché, Legation in China; Chief, 2nd Dept,. Gen. Staff Office, 1929; Chief, 1st Dept. of same, 1931; Military Repr., League of Nation's Assembly, July, 1932; present post since Mar., 1933. Address: 14 Oyamacho, Shibuyaku, Tokyo.

Chairman, Board of Dirs., Kainan Industry Co.; Mng. Dir., Kaigai Kogyo K. K.; Dir., Peru Raw Cotton Co. and South America Real Estate Co.; b. Mar., 1874 in Fukui-ken; s. of Seishin Tatsui. Career: grad., Univ. Course, Kyoto Bungaku-Ryo; studied at Sc. Coll., Tokyo Imp. Univ.; went to Austlaria and New Guinea; fought in Russo-Japanese War; joined Oriental Development Co. serving at its Chosen Office 10 years; Mng.-Dir., Toyo Kogyo Kaisha since 1917. Address: 653 Kitasenzokumachi, Omoriku, Tokyo.

Auditor, Hattori Watch & Clock Co.; b. Sept., 1856 in Tokyo-fu; s. of Yasubei Tatsui. Career: apptd. Sec. to Agrl. & Com. Minister; Dir. and Mgr., Tokyo Branch Office, Nipponsha; Chief Sec., then Dir., South Manchuria Ry. Co. up to 1921. Address: 57 Aoyama-Kitamachi-Rokuchome, Akasakaku, Tokyo.

Pres., Kobe Univ. of Com.; Adviser, Kobe Chamber of Com. & Industry; b. Mar., 1872; brother of Shuzaburo Tazaki, Nagasaki-ken. Career: grad., Tokyo Higher Com. School, 1901; went to America and Europe to study com. science, 1902; grad., Birmingham Univ., England, 1906; Prof., Nagasaki Higher Com. School; same, Kobe Higher Com. School, 1908; dispatched to America, 1914. Address: Takaha-Hirano, Rokkomura, Mukogun, Hyogo-ken.

Dir., 2nd Sec., Treaty Bureau, Foreign Office; b. Apr., 1892 in Tokyo-fu; s. of Kogoro Terajima, chief public procurator. Career: grad., Law Coll., Tokyo Imp. Univ., 1916; joined Mitsubishi Bank; apptd., Commr., Foreign Office, 1919; Sec., Embassy in France; Consul at Amoy, and Hankow; present post since 1932. Address: 2 Minami-Enokicho, Ushigomeku, Tokyo.

Kabuki Actor; Pres., Actors' Sch.; Mem., Rotary Club; b. 1885 in Tokyo; s. of Onoe Kikugoro, 5th. Career: appeared on stage with father from childhood; succeeded father's name, “Kikugoro”, after father's death, 1903; established Actors' Sch., 1930. Recreations: Shooting, Baseball. Religion: Konkonkyo. Address: 7 Shiba Park 11, Shibaku, Tokyo.

Vice-Admiral; Comdr., Training Squadron; b. Sept., 1882 in Wakayama-ken; s. of Yoshinari Terajima, samurai. Career: grad., Naval Academy, 1903, and Naval Staff Coll.; apptd. Staff, Naval Board of Command; same, 3rd Squadron; Naval Attaché, Embassy in France; Adjutant, Navy Dept.; Comdr., H. M. S. Yamashiro; Chief Staff, 2nd and 1st Mixed Fleet; Dir., Education Bureau, Navy Dept., 1930; went to Europe 4 times; Dir., Naval Affairs Bureau, 1932; present post since Aug., 1933. Address: 4 Aoyama-Takagicho-Jyunichome, Akasakaku, Tokyo.

Rigakuhakushi (D. Sc.); Prof. of Zoology; Dir. of Zool. Laboratory, Imp. Fisheries Institute, Tokyo; b. Sept., 1887 in Tokyo; s. of Hisashi Terao, former Prof. of Astronomy, Tokyo Imp. Univ. Career: grad., Science Dept., Tokyo Imp. Univ., 1912; apptd. present post, 1918; received Rockefeller Foundation Fellowship, 1926; went to U. S. on leave of absence to undertake biometrical study under Dr. Raymond Pearl at Institute for Biological Research, Johns Hopkins University for 1½ years. Address: 19 Obancho, Yotsuyaku, Tokyo.

Dir., Trade Bureau, Com. & Industry Dept.; b. Aug., 1890 in Chiba-ken; brother of Kochiku Onishi; adotped by Toru Terao. Career: grad., Law Coll., Tokyo Imp. Univ., 1915; entered Agrl. & Com. Dept.; Commr., Patent Bureau; Sec. to Agrl. & Com. Minister; Sec., Agrl. & Co. Dept.; same, Com. & Industry Dept.; Chief, trade Section, Com. Bureau; Commr., Special Industry Rationalization Bureau; present post since Jan., 1932. Address: 50 Obancho, Yotsuyaku, Tokyo.

Inspector, Kanto Branch, Canada Sun Life Ins. Co.; b. Feb., 1862 in Fukui; s. of Jihei Terao, samurai. Career: grad., Tokyo Higher Normal Sch.; Pres., Pref. Educ. Societies. Address: 541 Shimo-Meguro, Meguroku, Tokyo.
Gen. Mgr., Yamato Hotel; b. June, 1877; s. of Seimei Terasawa, samurai. Career: went to America to inspect hotel business; Dir., Namman Ryokan. Address: 52 Sakakimachi, Dairen.

Lawyer; Lecturer, Manchoukuo Law Coll.; Non-Official Staff, South Manchuria Ry. Co.; Legal Adviser, Chosen Bank, Manchuria Bank, South Manchuria Elec. Co., and Dairen Exchange & Trust Co.; b. 1888 in Nara-ken; s. of Fusakichi Terashima, farmer. Career: grad., Law Coll., Hosei Univ., Tokyo, 1911; Non-Official Staff, Tsingtao Army Commander-in-Chief's Hdqrs., 1922; opened Office in Dairen, 1924. Recreations: Reading, Utai (song). Address: Kirishima-cho, Dairen.

Count; Lieut.-Gen.; Comdr., 4th Division; b. Aug., 1879; s. of Count Seiki Terauchi, Ex-Prime Minister. Career: grad., Military Academy, 1900, and Military Staff Coll.; Instructor, Military Staff Coll.; Comdr., Imp. Guard Infantry 3rd Regiment; Chief Staff, Imp. Guard Division; Comdr., Infantry 19th Brigade; Chief-Staff, Chosen Army; Comdr., Independent Guard; sent to Germany, 1912; present post since 1932.
