Address: Official Residence, Otemae, Higashiku, Osaka. (Tokyo home) 606 Yoyogi-Hatsudaimachi, Shibuyaku, Tokyo.

Lyric Baritone; b. Apr., 1888 in Morioka City; s. of Tokutaro Terui, Supt. of Fish Market. Career: when young, went to America; educated music by Prof. Stone in Pasadena, Calif.; studied “Lieders” under Leech Sterner and Madame Rankin in New York, 1913-18; went to Paris and studied under Mlle. Pellion, 1918-19; returned home next year, and took active part in Kansai music circle for years; again visited Paris to study under Charles Pensera, French baritone, 1925-26; in recent years often gave vocal recitals in Tokyo. Address: 17 Showadori 1-chome, Nakanoku, Tokyo.

Mng.-Dir., Toshin Warehouse Co.; b. Sept., 1885 in Kyoto; s. of Tomonari Teshima. Career: grad., Tokyo Univ. of Com., 1906; joined and served Mitsui Bussan Kaisha, 1906-1924; Mitsui Gomei Kaisha, 1924-1931; became Mgr., Real Property Dept.; present post since Apr., 1931. Address: 28 Higashi Shinanomachi, Yotsuyaku, Tokyo.

M. D.; Physician and Surgeon; b. Feb., 1876 in Rome, Georgia, U. S.; n. American; s. of Rudolf Teusler. Career: received degree, Medical Coll. of Virginia, 1894; Asst. Prof., Pathology and Bacteriology, 1896-1900; Member Associated Press Staff in Japan, 1903-04; Physician to British Embassy, 1909-12; Comdr. American Red Cross Siberia, rank of Lieut.-Colonel, 1918-21; Member of American Embassy Staff, American Episcopal Mission; Dir., St. Barnabas' Hospital, Osaka since 1925; Dir., St. Luke's Int'l. Hospital since 1900. Address: 1 Akashicho, Tsukiji, Tokyo.

Minister of Communications; b. 1876 in Kaiping-hsien, Mukden. Career: grad., Waseda Univ., Tokyo; Chief, Foreign Office, Military Headquarters, Three Eastern Provices; Gov., Mukden Prov.; Took part in organization of Local Peace and Order Committee after death of Chang Tsuo-lin 1928; exerted in maintaining local peace at Manchuria Incident, and Chairman, North Eastern Communications Committee 1931; came to Japan 1932; present post since 1932. Address: Hsinking.

Manchoukuo Min., Tokyo; b. 1879 in Wu-hsien, Chekiang. Career: studied at St. John's Univ., Shanghai; published News Paper, Peiping; studied in England; attended Hague Conf. as Advocate-Gen.; Dir., Metropolitan Police Coll.; Mng.-Dir., Peiking-Suiyan Ry., 1916-1918; Mng.-Dir., Peiking-Hankow Ry., 1918-1919; Chief, Aviation Dept.; Associated Dir.-Gen., Lung-yen Iron Mining Com., 1919; Editor, Tientsin Daily, 1923-1924; Vice-Chairman, Financial Readjustment Commission, 1925-1926; Manchoukuo Special Envoy to League of Nations, 1932; present post since 1933. Address: 50 Sakurada-cho, Azabu-ku, Tokyo.

Count; Fleet-Admiral; b. Feb., 1847 in Kagoshima-ken; s. of Kichizaemon Togo, samurai. Career: sent to England for study, 1871; Comdr., H. M. S. Naniwa during Sino-Japanese War; Vice-Admiral and Comdr., Standing Squadron; Comdr., Maizuru Naval Station; Comdr., Saseho Naval Station; Chief, Naval Gen. Staff; Supreme War Councillor; during Russo-Japanese War, as Comdr. of Combined Fleet, defeated Russian Oriental Squadron off Port Arthur and wiped out 1st Oriental Squadron, moreover annihilated the Baltic Fleet at Tsushima Straits in 2-day desperate battle; conferred Grand Order, ennobled Count and made Fleet-Admiral, 1907; Pres., H. I. H. Crown Prince's Lecture-Hall. Address: 37 Kami-Rokubancho, Kojimachiku, Tokyo.

Nogakuhakushi (D. Agr.); Parl. Vice-Minister, Education Dept.; M. P.; b. Nov., 1881 in Kagoshima-ken; s. of Sanehiko Togo, samurai. Career: grad., Sapporo Agrl. Coll., 1905; studied at Berlin Univ.; entered Taiwan Gov't.; served 18 years and apptd. Dir., Industry Bureau; sent to America, Europe and South Seas; received degree, 1919; elected to Diet 4 times; present post since June, 1932. Address: 8 Kogaicho, Azabuku, Tokyo.

Baron; Mng. Dir., Japan Wireless Telegraph Co.; b. July, 1882 in Tokyo; s. of Vice-Admiral Masamichi Togo. Career: grad., Polit. Science Dept., Tokyo Imp. Univ.; Mem., House of Peers since 1911; Mem., Imp. Gov't. Tariff Committee. Address: 66 Minamicho-Nichome, Aoyama, Akasakaku, Tokyo.

Mem., Tokyo Stock Exchange; Prop., Tohyama Shoten; b. Jan., 1885 in Saitama-ken; s. of Chikazo Tohyama. Career: completed Keika Com. Sch.; engaged in present business since 1918; became Com. Councillor, Tokyo Stock Exchange, years ago; one of high taxpayers in Tokyo-fu. Address: 5 Sakamotocho, Nihonbashiku, Tokyo.

Viscount; Mem., House of Peers; Parl. Vice-Minister of War.; b. Feb., 1892 in Tokyo-fu; s. of Viscount Yoritomo Toki; adopted by Yoritoshi Toki. Career: studied at Sc. Coll., Tokyo Imp. Univ.; established Tokyo Provisions Co.; made inspection tour to Europe and America, 1921-23; Mem., House of Peers, 1922; Councillor, War Dept. in Inukai Cabinet, 1931; present post since June, 1932. Address: 38 Nagasumicho, Shibuyaku, Tokyo.

Former Mayor of Kyoto; b. Feb., 1875 in Wakayama-ken; s. of Tsunaemon Toki. Career: grad., Law Coll., Tokyo Imp. Univ., 1901; passed Exam. for Bench, 1898; Probationary Judge, 1898; admitted to Bar in Tokyo, 1899; passed Higher Civil Service Exam., 1899; entered Home Dept., 1901; apptd. Counsellor, Yamanashi-ken, 1903; sent to Europe and America, 1907-08; Chief, Home Affairs Dept., Osaka-fu; Governor, Kochi-ken and Ishikawa-ken; Gov.-General, Kwantung; Governor, Osaka-fu; Governor-General, Hokkaido; Mayor of Kyoto. Address: Toriimaemachi, Nanzenji, Kyoto.

M. P.; Adviser, Seiyukai; b. Dec., 1866 in Kagoshima-ken; s. of late Seisei Tokonami. Career: grad., Law Coll., Tokyo Imp. Univ., 1890; Sec., Finance Office; Councillor, Miyagi-ken; Gov., Yamagata-ken, Niigata-ken, etc.; Chief Prefectural Bureau; Vice-Minister of Home Office; Pres., Ry. Board; Home Minister in Hara Cabinet; same in Takahashi Cabinet; Pres., Seiyuhonto, 1923; made inspection tour to Europe and America. Address: 421, 1-chome, Nishiokubo, Yodobashiku, Tokyo.

Minister to Canada; Hogakushi (B. L.); b. Mar., 1884 in Tokyo; e. s. of Prince Iyesato Tokugawa. Career: grad., Peers' School; Polit. Dept., Tokyo Imp. Univ., 1909; passed Dept., Tokyo Imp. Univ., 1909; passed Diplomatic and Consular Service Exam.; Attaché, Embassy in London, 1910-13; Sec., Foreign Office, Tokyo, 1913-18; Priv. Sec. to Foreign Minister, 1914-15; 2nd Sec., Legation in Peking, 1918-19; 1st Sec. of same, 1919-21; 1st Sec., Embassy in London, 1921-25; Councillor of same, 1925; Consul-General, Australia and New Zealand, 1925-29; Member, Japanese Suite to H. R. H. Duke of Gloucester, during latter's visit to Japan on Garter Mission, May, 1929; present post since Oct., 1929. Address: Japanese Legation, Ottawa, Canada.

Prince (Cr., 1884); Mem., House of Peers; Pres., Board of Councillors, Peers' School; same, Peers Club; same, Japan Red Cross Society; b. July, 1863 in Tokyo; s. of late Lord Yoshiyori Tokugawa, and became heir to the last of Shoguns, 1908. Career: apptd. Governor, Shizuoka Clan, 1869, resigning from same, 1871; studied in England, 1877-1882; upon returning home, apptd. Lord-in-Waiting, Jako Hall; toured Europe and America for inspection, 1910; became Pres., Saiseikai (Imp. Gift Charitable Foundation); Delegate to Washington Disarmament Conference, 1921; attended Int'l Parl. Conf. in London and Int'l Red Cross Society Conf. in Brussels, 1930; Pres., House of Peers, 1903-33; Travelling abroad in 1933. Address: 330 Sendagaya Itchome, Shibuyaku, Tokyo.

Prince; Mem., House of Peers; Vice-Pres., Red Cross Society; b. Dec., 1886; s. of Marquis Tokuyasu Tokugawa. Career: attended Red Cross Society Assembly, Geneva, 1920. Address: 34 Sarugaku, Shibuyaku, Tokyo.

Marquis; Mem., House of Peers; b. Aug., 1892 in Tokyo; s. of late Marquis Yorimichi Tokugawa, Director of Imperial Bureau of Peerage. Career: grad., Peers' School; studied at Cambridge, 1913-16; travelled to Europe and America with Marchioness, 1921; returned home and took up management of Nanki Concert Hall and Musical Library, as he is greatly interested in Western music; devoted to propagation of musical taste as well as to its educational work; succeeded his father's undertakings; toured South Sea Islands, 1926-27; represented Japanese House of Peers at Int'l Parl. Conf. in London, 1929, and in Brussels, 1930, also at Int'l Parl. Union Conf. in London, 1930; Govt. Repr. to Int'l Congress of Concert in Paris, 1930; made extensive tour round South America, 1930-31; well-known as private diplomat and patron of music; at present Pres., Nanki Music Institute, Nanki Educational Society, Matsusaka Morality Society, Japan Genre Assn.; Vice-Pres., Polish-Japanese Society; Honorary Councillor Santa Cecillia in Rome; Mem., Int'l Musical Assn. and Kayokai Party. Address: 331 Kami-Osaki, Osakimachi, Shinagawaku, Tokyo.

Mem., House of Peers; Mem., Imp. Academy; Special Writer, Osaka Mainichi and Tokyo Nichi-Nichi; b. Jan., 1867 in Kumamoto-ken; s. of Ikkei Tokutomi, samurai. Career: studied at Doshisha Univ.; established Minyusha and published “Kokumin-no-Tomo”, monthly, 1889, and Kokumin Shimbun, daily, 1890; Councillor, Home Dept., 1897; went to Europe and visited L. Tolstoy; nominated Mem., House of Peers, 1911; resigned Kokumin Shimbun; went to China, 1931. Address: 2832 Sanno-Itchome, Omoriku, Tokyo.

Sr. Mng.-Dir., Konoshima Artificial Fertilizer Co.; Jr. Mng. Dir., Dai Nippon Artificial Fertilizer Co. and Godo Yushi K. K.; Auditor, Osaka Alkali Tochi K. K., etc.; b. Dec., 1880 in Aomori-ken; s. of Kinjiro Tomabechi. Career: grad., Applied Chemistry Course, Tokyo Higher Tech. Sch., 1903; joined Abe Paper Mfg. Co., same year; then Osaka Sulphate Soda Co., 1904; became Mgr., Dai Nippon Artificial Fertilizer Co., Jr. Mng. Dir. and Heda, General Affairs Dept. of same, 1931. Address: 4 Maruyama, Shibuyaku, Tokyo.

Baron; Hogakuhakushi (D. L.); Privy Councillor; Mem., Imp. Academy; Prof. Emeritus, Tokyo Imp. Univ.; Dir., Maison Franco-Japonaise and Hosei Univ.; b. Sept., 1858 in Kyoto; s. of Masatsune Tomii, samurai. Career: studied at Tokyo School of Foreign Languages; grad., Law Coll., Lyons Univ., France, 1882; Prof. and Dean, Law Coll., Tokyo Imp. Univ.; apptd. Privy Councillor, 1918; ennobled, 1926. Address: 71 Ichigaya-Yakuojimachi, Ushigomeku, Tokyo.

Hogakuhakushi (D. L.); Mem., House of Peers; Hon. Adviser, Meiji Univ.; b. Oct., 1856 in Tochigi-ken; s. of Toyoyoshi Tomiya, samurai. Career: grad., Law School, Foreign Office, 1884; studied in Europe, 1886; apptd. Judge, Tokyo District Court and Tokyo Appeal Court; Pres., Appellate Court and Supreme Court; Pres., Meiji Univ. Address: 12 Kitamachi, Ushigomeku, Tokyo.

Prof., Tokyo Univ. of Litt. & Sc.; Prof., Nippon Women's Univ.; Lecturer, Tokyo Imp. Univ.; b. Nov., 1876 in Fukuoka-ken; s. of Hayami Tomoeda. Career: grad., Litt. Coll., Tokyo Imp. Univ., 1901; went to England, 1904; apptd. Prof., 5th Higher School and Asst. Prof., Kyoto Imp. Univ.; studied in America, Germany and England, 1910; Prof., Tokyo Higher Normal School, 1914; Prof., Tokyo Imp. Univ., 1916; present post since 1929; Dir., Japanische-Deutsches Kulture-Institut. Address: 24 Komagome-Akebonocho, Hongoku, Tokyo.

Gov., Mukden Province; Minister of Civil Affaires; b. 1884 in Shenyang-hsien, Mukden. Career: studied in Military Academy, Tokyo; Staff Officer, Military Gov.'s Office, Heilungkiang 1920; Chief Staff, Military Gov.'s Office, and Acting Gov., Kirin 1923; Councillor, General's Office, Mukden 1926; Councillor, Public Peace Headquarters, Three Eastern Provs. after death of Chang Tsuo-lin 1928; Gov., Mukden Arsenal, 1927; Chairman and Mem., Govt. Committee, Liaoning Prov. 1930; Gov., Mukden Prov., 1931; present post since 1932. Address: Mukden.
Privy Councillor, Manchoukuo; b. 1861 in Szechwan Prov. Career: Prominent Business Man in Manchuria; present post since 1932. Address: Hsinking.

General; Chinese Min. to Tokyo; b. 1883 in Yingcheng, Hupei Province; n. Chinese. Career: entered Military Academy and 3rd Regiment, Tokyo, and completed Infantry Course, 1908; apptd. Prof., Military Coll. at Paoting-Fu; Vice-Minister of War, 1912; Vice-Chief of Gen. Staff, 1916; High Inspecting Commr. of Hupei and Hunan, 1923; Chairman of Anbui Provincial Gov't., 1927; Mem., National Go't. and Military Affairs Committee, 1924-26; Minister to Germany and Austria, 1930; Delegate to Disarmament Conf., League of Nations, and 10th and 11th Sessions, Assembly of League; Mem., Central Supervisory Committee; Chairman, Diplomatic Committee; present post since 1931; wrote and translated many books on military tactics. Address: Chinese Legation, Azabu, Tokyo.

Chief, Cultural Work Dept., Foreign Office; b. June, 1884 in Saga-ken; s. of Buntaro Tsubokami, samurai. Career: grad., Tokyo Higher Com. School, 1909; entered Foreign Office and served as Elève-Consul, Diplomatic Probationer, Consul-Gen., Sec. of Embassy; attached to Consulate-General in Tsitsihar, London and Hongkong; returned home, 1923, and apptd. Chief, 2nd and 3rd Sections, Asia Bureau; Chief, Financial Section, Foreign Minister's Secretariat; present post since 1929. Address: 14 Oyamamachi, Shibuyaku, Tokyo.

Prop., Katsugoro Tsuda Shoten (iron and steel marchants); Pres., Osaka Iron Works.; b. Sept., 1887; s. of Munekata Tsuda, Ehime-ken. Career: inherited family estate, 1921. Address: 8 Itachibori-Kitadori Rokuchome, Nishiku, Osaka.

Pres. and Dir., Kanegafuchi Spinning Co.; b. Mar., 1881 in Aichi-ken; s. of Yoshiroku Nishiyama, samurai, and later adopted by late Oto Tsuda. Career: grad., Law Dept., Keio Univ., 1907; upon grad. entered present firm; promoted persent post, 1930. Address: Hirata, Ashiya, Hyogo-ken.

Igakuhakushi (M. D.); Surgeon; b. Mar., 1886 in Fukui-ken. Career: grad., Medical Dep't., Kyoto Imp. Univ., 1911; Associate Prof., same Univ., 1913-26; Consulting Surgeon. Address: 52 Kumochicho-Nichome, Fukiaiku, Kobe.

Bungakuhakushi (D. Litt.); Dir., Tokyo Higher School; b. Sept., 1872 in Hyogo-ken; s. of Hideo Tsukahara. Career: grad., Tokyo Imp. Univ., 1902; studied at Leipzig, Berlin, and Columbia Univs., 1902-05; apptd. Prof., Hiroshima Higher Normal School; Inspector, Education Dept., 1905-25; Dir., Shizuoka Higher School, 1925-27; present post since 1927. Address: 881 Hatagaya, Haramachi, Shibuyaku, Tokyo.

Sec., Dept. of Foreign Affairs; b. June, 1896 in Kumamoto-ken; s. of Tooki Tsukamoto, official; married, 1931. Career: grad., Tokyo Higher Com. School; apptd. Sec. Foreign Office, 1921; Attaché Embassy in France, 1926; Sec., Embassy in Brazil, 1928; present post since 1930. Address: 438 Shimo-Totsuka, Yodobashiku, Tokyo.

Journalist; b. Apr., 1895 in Miye-ken. Career: grad., Post & Telegraph Coll., Tokyo, 1913; served Osaka Telegraph Office; then, Osaka Communication Bureau; Staff, Kokusai News Agency, 1920; same, Shimbun Rengo, 1926; Rengo's Repr. in Shanghai, 1927; same in Germany, 1929; Mgr., Osaka Office of Shimbun Rengo since 1931. Address: 733 Sakuragaoka, Minomomura, Osaka-fu.
D. D.; Minister; b. 1860 in Okayama-ken; s. of Kotoku Tsunashima, physician. Career: grad., Doshisha Univ. and Yale Divinity School; Christian Paster. Address: 1 Mita Tsunamachi, Shibaku. Tokyo.

Pres., Nagoya Bank; Dir., Toyo Warehouse Co.; Auditor, Central Trust Co.; Mem., Nagoya Chamber of Com. & Industry; b. Mar., 1863 in Aichi-ken; adopted-s. of Yasuzo Tsunekawa, landlord. Career: grad., Aichi-ken Normal School; joined Tsushima Bank, 1901, and later became its Dir.; when it was merged into Nagoya Bank, 1907, became Sub-Mgr. of same; gradually-promoted present post; once served as Pres., Nagoya Savings Bank and Auditor, Showa Bank. Address: 2 Enakacho Itchome, Nishiku, Nagoya.

Pres., Tokyo Mouselin-de-Laine Co.; Vice-Pres., Tokyo Chamber of Com. & Ind.; b. Sept., 1873 in Kanazawa; s. of Arinari Tsurumi, samurai, Kaga Clan. Career: grad., Law Coll., Tokyo Imp. Univ., 1899; Pres., Com. Museum, Agrl. & Com. Dept.; Dir., Yawata Iron Works; Dir., Fisheries Bureau, 1917; same, Forestry Bureau, 1918; Dir., Com. Affairs Bureau, 1920; apptd., Vice-Minister, Agrl. & Com. Dept., 1924; Chief Sec., Italian Int'l Exhibition; toured Europe, America and China; Special Committee Mem., Allied Powers Economic Conference during World War. Address: 12-4 Aoyama-Takagicho, Akasakaku, Tokyo.

Author; b. Jan., 1885 in Gumma-ken; s. of Yoshinori Tsurumi. Career: grad., Law Coll., Tokyo Imp. Univ., 1910; apptd. Sec. and Councillor, Ry. Dept.; sent to China, Europe and America; Chief, Gen. Affairs Section, Traffic Bureau, Ry. Dept.; canvassed through America on Anti-Japanese problems, 1924; went again to America, 1927; sent to Diet from Okayama-ken, 1928. Address: 50 Sakurada-cho, Azabuku, Tokyo.

Pres., Tsurutani Shokai; Auditor, Nippon Silk Fabric Co. and Shofu Industry Co.; b. June, 1868; s. of Tokuemon Nakagawa, and later adopted by Yoso Tsurutani. Career: went to America, 1888; Mem., Kobe Chamber of Com. & Industry. Address: 6 Yamamotodori-Shichome, Kobe.

Japanese Financial Commr., England, France and America; b. Jan., 1888 in Takamatsu City; s. of late Masami Tsushima. Career: grad., Law Coll., Tokyo Imp. Univ., 1912; Councillor, Finance Ministry; Sec. to Finance Minister; apptd. Financial Commr. Abroad, 1927; Attaché, Embassies in England, France and U. S.; Mem., Delegation to Chinese Tariff Special Conference, 1925; Mem., Delegation to VIII Gen. Meeting, League of Nations, Geneva, 1927; Delegate to Int'l Conf. for Abolition of Import & Export Prohibitions & Restrictions, Geneva, 1927 and 1928; Mem., Economic Consultative Committee, League of Nations, 1928; Mem., Delegation to London Naval Conf., 1930; Delegate to Reparation oCnf., at Lausanne, 1932. Address: (abroad) Japanese Financial Commn., 9 Bishopsgate, London, E. G. 2. (home) 62 Shimo-Nibancho, Kojimachiku, Tokyo.

Chief, 2nd Sec., Intelligence Bureau, Foreign Office; b. Nov., 1896 in Miye-ken; s. of Yaoju Tsutsui, M. D. Career: grad., German Law, Tokyo Imp. Univ., 1920; joined Mitsubishi Trading Co., same year; entered Foreign Office, 1921, serving at Embassy in Belgium; attended 5th & 6th Gen. Meeting, League of Nations at Geneva; present post since 1930. Address: 198 Shimo-Meguro, Meguroku, Tokyo.

Parl. Vice-Minister of Overseas Affairs Dept.; M. P.; b. Mar., 1889 in Shiga-ken; s. of Naojiro Tsutsumi. Career: grad., Polit. Dept., Waseda Univ.; sent to Diet 4 times since 1920; present post since June, 1932. Address: 405 Kami-Osaki, Shinagawaku, Tokyo.
Chief, Guard Corps, Chief Executive Office, Manchoukuo. Career: present post since 1932. Address: Hsinking.

Chief Sec., Heilungkiang Prov. Govt.; b. 1882 in Kirin Prov. Career: Sec., Heilungkiang Prov. Govt., 1929; Acting Chief Sec., Heilungkiang Prov. Govt., 1931; present post since 1932. Address: Tsitsihar.

Pres., The Silk, Ltd. (Toronto, Canada); Dir., Maruishi Trading Co. and Doshi Trading Co.; b. Feb., 1877 in Gumma-ken; s. of Jusaku Ubukata. Career: studied at Keio Univ.; engaged in silk trade for many years. Address: 10 Shirokane-Daimachi-Itchome, Shibaku, Tokyo.

Prof., Daito Bunka Gakuin; b. Apr., 1872 in Kumamoto-ken; s. of Kakuhei Uchibori. Career: grad., Tokyo Higher Normal School, 1898; apptd. Asst. Prof. of same; Instructor, Koto-Gakudo and Shihan-Gakudo, China, 1903-10; Dr., Normal Schools in Kanagawa-ken, Shizuoka-ken, Nagano-ken; Dir., S. Manchurian Middle School and Mukden Middle School, Mukden, 1917; Prof., Lushun Tech. Coll., and Principal, Lushun 2nd Middle School; present post since 1928. Address: 263 Okubo-Hyakuninmachi, Yodobashiku, Tokyo.

Japanese Consul, Tsitsihar, Manchoukuo; b. Aug., 1888 in Yamagata-ken; s. of late Koretaka Uchida, official. Career: passed Diplomatic and Consular Service Exam., 1920; apptd. Elève-Consul, Antwerp, Belgium, 1921; Japanese High Commisariat at Constantinople, 1922; Consul at Swatow, China, 1924-27; same at Mukden, 1927-29; same at Chefoo, 1929-32; present post since Aug., 1932. Address: Japanese Consulate, Tsitsihar, Manchoukuo.

Nogakuhakushi (Dr. Agr.); Mng. Dir., East Asia Industrial Co.; Auditor and Prof., Meiji Univ.; b. 1885 in Chiba-ken; s. of Heikichi Uchida, business man. Career: grad., Meiji Univ., 1908; joined Mitsui Bussan Kaisha; apptd. Gov't Com. Commr. to South China, 1914; Prof., Meiji Univ. since 1916; entered present firm, 1918. Address: 19 Tenjin, Nakanoku, Tokyo.

LL. D. (U. S.); Pres., Japan-Turkey Assn.; b. Jan., 1865 in Fukuoka-ken; s. of Jinzo Uchida, samurai of the Kokura Clan. Career: grad., Law Coll., Tokyo Imp. Univ., 1889; entered Foreign Office, and served at Shanghai, Seoul, New York as Vice-Consul and Consul-General; apptd. Minister Resident, Brazil, 1907; Minister, Sweden, Norway, Denmark, 1912-18; Ambassador, Turkey, 1921-23; resigned 1924. Address: 15 Nampeidai, Shibuyaku, Tokyo.

Nogakuhakushi (D. Agr.); Engr., Agr. & Forestry Dept.; Expert, Agrl. and Forestry; Lecturer, Agrl. Dept., Tokyo Imp. Univ.; Non-Commissioned Staff, Education Dept.; b. Dec., 1884 in Tokyo; s. of Yasubei Uchida, business man. Career: grad., 1st Higher School; Agrl. Dept., Tokyo Imp. Univ.; was Non-Commissioned Staff, Agrl. & Com. Dept.; sent to Pan-Pacific Educational Congress by Education Dept., 1927; sent abroad for study by Dept. of Agr. & Forestry; returning home, served Live-Stock Bureau of same; Councillor, Ornithological Society of Japan, etc. Address: 8 Aoba, Shibuyaku, Tokyo.
Prop., Furniture Shop; b. Feb., 1902 in Tokyo; s. of Torakichi Uchida, upholsterer. Career: grad., Tokyo City Com. School. Address: 80 Higashi-Morishitacho, Fukagawaku, Tokyo.

Count; Mem., House of Peers; Ex-Foreign Minister; b. Aug., 1865 in Kumamoto-ken; s. of Genshi Uchida, samurai. Career: grad., Law Coll., Tokyo Imp. Univ., 1887; Diplomatic Probationer at Washington, same year; Sec. to Agrl. & Com. Minister, 1890; Dir., Trade Bureau and Polit. Affairs Bureau; Sec.-Gen., Foreign Office; Minister to China; Ambassador to Austria and America; Foreign Minister in Saionji Cabinet; Ambassador to Russia; Foreign Minister in Hara Cabinet, 1918; Prime Minister protem., 1921; Foreign Minister in T. Kato Cabinet; Privy Councillor, 1925-29; Mem., House of Peers, 1926; Pres., South Manchuria Ry. Co., 1931; Foreign Minister, July, 1932 to Sept., 1933. Address: 350 Nishi-Okubo, Yodobashiku, Tokyo.

M. P.; Vice-Pres., Polit. Affairs Inquriy Committee; Lecturer, Waseda Univ.; b. Apr., 1877 in Miyagi-ken; s. of Sakutaro Uchigasaki. Career: grad., Litt. Coll., Tokyo Imp. Univ., 1901; studied at Oxford Univ., England, 1908; Prof., Waseda Univ.; made inspection tour to Europe, America and China, 1920; Dir., League of Nations Assn.; elected to Diet 3 times since 1924; Councillor, Home Dept., 1929. Address: 1470 Sugamo, Toshimaku, Tokyo.

Patent Attorney; b. Jan., 1868 in Yonezawa; s. of Genzo Uchimura. Career: upon grad., Tokyo Higher Polytechnic School (present Tokyo Engrg. Coll.), apptd. Examiner, Patent Office, 1890; Prof., Tokyo Suisan Koshujo (Fishery Inst.) up to 1906; Chief Engr., Teikoku Cold Storage Co., 1907; visited Europe and America for study; built cold-storages at principal places in Japan; retiring later from same, established Tokyo Patent & Trade Mark Agency Bureau; while then often apptd. Examiner of several Exhibitions; Lecturer, Waseda Univ.; Adviser, Civil Administrative Bureau, Saghalien; Residency-General, Korea; Officer, various societies and assns. Address: Sanno, Omoriku, Tokyo.

Consul-Gen. at Sao Paulo, Brazil; b. Feb., 1890 in Gumma-ken; s. of Iwakichi Uchiyama. Career: sent to Madrid as Student of Foreign Office, 1909; apptd. Chancelier, Legation in Spain; Sec., Legation in Poland; Sec. to Foreign Minister; Commr., Foreign Office; Sec., Embassy in Brazil; same, Legation in Spain and Embassies in Turkey and France; Consul at Buenos Ayres, Argentine, and Montevideo, Uruguay; present post since 1931. Address: Consulado Geral do Japao, Rua Lider o Porado 90, Sao Paulo, Brazil.

Consul at Seattle, U. S.; b. Jan., 1887 in Tokyo; s. of Zenzo Uchiyama, merchant. Career: grad., Yokohama Com. School; apptd. Chancelier, Foreign Office, 1907; Vice-Consul, Shanghai, 1919; Consul, Chefoo, 1921; same, Mukden, New York, Cuba and present place. Address: (office) Consulate of Japan, Central Bldg., Seattle.
Prop., Ueda Kabushiki-Ten; Mem., Tokyo Stock Exchange; b. Sept., 1891 in Tokyo; s. of Yosakichi Ueda, stock jobber. Career: grad., Osaka Com. School. Address: 21 Maruyamacho, Koishikawaku, Tokyo.

Dir., Elec. Bureau, Sapporo, Hokkaido; b. 1874 in Niigata-ken. Career: grad., Mech. Engrg. Coll., Tokyo Imp. Univ., 1900; Engr., Ry. Dept., Hokkaido; Chief, Traffic Section, Ry. Dept.; Ry. Supt.; took part in Construction of Meguro-Kamata Elec. Ry. and Tokyo-Yokohama Elec. Ry.; present post since 1927. Address: Elec. Bureau, Sapporo.

Major-Gen.; Dir., Ordnance Bureau, War Dept.; b. Apr., 1881 in Tokyo-fu; s. of Shigeru Uemura, samurai. Career: apptd. Artillery Sub-Lieut., 1902; grad., Engrg. Coll., Tokyo Imp. Univ., 1911; Commr., Aviation Headquarters; same, Military Technical Headquarters; Chief, Engrg. Dept., Ordnance Bureau; Commr., Com. & Industry Dept.; Chief, 1st Dept., Military Tech. Headquarters; went to Europe twice, 1915 and 1927; present post since 1930. Address: 183 Nishi-Okubo, Yodobashiku, Tokyo.

Chairman, Board of Directors, and Mag.-Dir., Asahi Shimbun-Sha; b. Oct., 1882 in Osaka; s. of Riichi Ueno, one of founders and shareholders of Asahi Shimbun. Career: grad., Law Coll., Tokyo Imp. Univ., 1907. Address: 5 Hiranomachi-Itchome, Higashiku, Osaka.

Honorary Vice-Consul for Jugoslavia; Pres., Ueyamayei's Japan Insect Powder Mfg. Co.; Dir., Kishiwada Cotton Spinning Co., Nankai Hydro-Elec. Co., Ueyama Trust Co., Osaka Traders' Assn.; b. Sept., 1889 in Wakayama; s. of Eiichiro Ueyama. Career: grad., Tokyo Higher Com. School; besides, Dir. of 6 other Societies and Assns. Address: Taishamura, Mukogun, Hyogo-ken.

General; Gov.-Gen., Chosen; b. June, 1868 in Okayama-ken; brother of Tonahachi Ugaki. Career: grad., Military Staff Coll.; Staff, Gen. Staff Office; Military Attaché to Germany; Chief, Military Affairs Dept., War Dept.; Comdr., Infantry 6th Regiment; Chief, 1st and Gen. Affairs Dept., Gen. Staff Office; Pres., Military Staff Coll.; Councillor, H. I. H. Crown Prince's Lecture Hall; Comdr., 10th Division; Vice-Minister of War; War Minister in Kiyorua, Kato and Wakatsuki Cabinet; Supreme War Councillor, 1927; War Minister, 1929-31; present post since 1931. Address: Official Residence, Waijodai, Keijo.

Sec. in Household of H. I. H. Prince Kanin; b. Mar., 1874 in Kumamoto; s. of Masato Ukita, paymaster major. Career: grad., Tokyo Higher Com. School; entered diplomatic and consular services, 1894 and retired, 1925; last position was Councillor of Embassy; Hon. Mem., Japan Society (London); Mem., Japan-British Society; Japan-Canada Assn., etc. Address: 20 Nagatacho-Nichome, Kojimachiku, Tokyo.

Pres., Ukon Trading Co., Nippon Marine Ins. Co., Nikkai Industrial Co.; b. Nov., 1889 in Fukui-ken; s. of late Gonzaemon Ukon. Career: upono grad., Econ. Dept., Keio Univ., 1914, entered business circle; high taxpayer in Fukui-ken. Address: 14, Kitadori-Gochome, Nishi-Nagahori, Nishiku, Osaka.

Lieut.-Gen.; Comdr., 20th Division; b. July, 1880 in Tokyo-fu; s. of Nobukazu Umezaki, samurai. Career: grad., Military Coll.; studied in Germany, 1914; apptd. Military Attaché, Legations in Sweden and Denmark; Comdr., Infantry 18th Regiment; Instructor, Military Staff Coll.; Pres., Cavalry School; Comdr., Cavalry 1st Brigade; Chief, Horse Supply Dept., 1930; Lieut.-Gen., 1931; present post since July, 1932. Address: Official Residence, Ryuzan, Keikido, Chosen. (Tokyo home) 531 Kami-Ochiai, Yodobashiku, Tokyo.

Viscount; Mem., House of Press; b. July, 1889 in Kyoto-fu; s. of late Viscount Sanemoro Umezono. Career: completed Kyoto Pref. 2nd Middle School; grad., Osaka Higher Com. School; Polit. Econ. Dept., Kyoto Imp. Univ.; apptd. Non-commissioned Staff, Shiga-ken; Dir., Kyoto Municipal Office; Lecturer, Kyoto Medical Coll. Address: 35 Naka-Kawaramachi, Simo-Kamo, Sakyoku, Kyoto.

Bungakuhakushi (D. Litt.); Prof., Tokyo Imp. Univ., Tokyo Univ. of Litt. & Science, Toyo Univ., Daito Bunka Gakuin; Dir., Japanese-German Cultural Inst., Toho Bunka Gakuin; Councillor, Tetsugaku-Kai, Toyo Kyokai; b. Nov., 1875 in Kumamoto-shi; s. of Jokuro Uno, samurai. Career: grad., 5th Higher School; Litt. Coll. and P.-G. Course, Tokyo Imp. Univ.; apptd. Prof., Tokyo Higher Normal School; Asst. Prof., Tokyo Imp. Univ.; sent to China and Germany for study 4 years. Address: 11 Takata-Oimatsucho, Koishikawaku, Tokyo.
Vice-Consul at Ichang, China; b. Sept., 1880 in Nagasaki-ken; s. of Takuma Fukabori. Career: grad., Toyo Kyokai. Address: Japanese Consulate, Ichang, China.

Adviser, State Council, Manchoukuo; b. May, 1869; brother of Shuntaro Usami, Yamagata-ken. Career: grad., Law Coll., Tokyo Imp. Univ., 1896; Gov., Toyama-ken; Councillor, Residency-General, Chosen; Chief, Public Works Bureau, Chosen Govt.; Gov., Tokyo-fu, 1921; Pres., Decoration Bureau, 1925; Chief, Resouress Bureau since 1927; Present post since 1932. Address: Hsinking.

Sec., Trade Bureau Foreign Office; b. Nov., 1893; s. of Kazutaro Usami, Nagano-ken. Career: grad., Law Coll., Tokyo Imp. Univ., 1918; entered Agrl. & Com. Dept.; Office, Foreign Office, 1920; attended General Assembly of League of Nations; Consul at Antung, China. Address: c. o. Foreign Office, Tokyo.

Chief, Home Dept., and Chief Sec., Privy Council of Chosen; b. Mar., 1883; s. of Jitsumitsu Ushijima, samurai of Kagoshima Clan. Career: grad., Law Coll., Tokyo Imp. Univ., 1910; Chief, Police Affairs Dept., Yamaguchi-ken, Kumamoto-ken and Hyogo-ken; Gov., Ibaragi-ken; Chief, Education Bureau, Chosen Govt. Address: Official Residence, Nishikomon, Keijo.

Mem. of House of Peers; Vice-Minister of Home Affairs; Mem., House of Peers; b. Aug., 1881 in Shimane-ken; brother of Tsunetaro Ushio. Career: grad., Law Coll., Tokyo Imp. Univ., 1907; Commr. and Sec., Home Office; Councillor, Household Dept.; Dir., Health Bureau and Local Bureau, Home Office; Vice-Minister, Home Affairs, 1928-1931; again Vice-Minister of same, 1932. Address: 1125 Nakanobumachi, Ebaraku, Tokyo.

Mayor of Tokyo; b. Apr., 1879 in Toyama-ken; s. of Tahei Ushizuka, landlord. Career: grad., Law Coll., Tokyo Imp. Univ., 1905; entered Communications Dept., same year; Sec., same; Sec. of Cabinet; nominated Chief, Statistics Bureau of Cabinet, 1916; Judge, Court of Administrative Litigation; Vice-Chief, National Census Bureau; Gov., Iwate-ken, Gumma-ken, Miyagi-ken; same, Tokyo-fu, 1929-31; Present post since May, 1933. Address: 19 Naka-Rokubancho, Kojimachiku, Tokyo.

Mng.-Dir., Teikoku Rayon K. K., Osaka; Auditor, Nippon Ringyo Kaisha; b. Dec., 1880 in Osaka; s. of Tameshichi Utsumi. Career: joined 34th Bank; then Central Laboratory, South Manchuria Ry. Co.; Dir. and Man., Naniwa Warehouse Co., etc. Address: 13 Tanaka-Asukaicho, Sakyoku, Kyoto.

Igakuhakushi (M.D.); Ex-Surgeon-Inspector-general. Career: grad., Medical Coll., Tokyo Imp. Univ., 1910; studied Treatment of infectious disease at hospital Komagome under Prof. Miyamoto; apptd. Surgeon-Sub-Lieut., 1st Class, 1910; Surgeon-Lieut., 1912; voyaged to China, Australia, New Zealand, South-Sea Islands; Surgeon-Lieut.-Comdr.; studied Internal Treatment at P.-G. Course, Tokyo Imp. Univ. under Prof. Inada, 1919-21; sent to Germany to study at Berlin Univ., Halle Univ., Kaiser Wilhelm's Institute, 1922-24; received degree, 1923; Surgeon-Comdr.; Surgeon-Inspector, 1926; Surgeon-Inspector-General, 1932-33. Address: 308 Nakameguro 2-chome, Meguroku, Tokyo.
Prop., Uyeda Shoten; Financier and Bond Broker; b. Dec., 1885 in Hyogo-ken; s. of late Sutezo Uyeda, village headman. Career: Sub-Mgr., Nagoya Bank. Address: Ashiya, Mukogun, Hyogo-ken.

Hogakuhakushi (D. L.); Prof., Tokyo Univ. of Com.; b. May, 1899 in Tokyo; s. of Akira Uyeda, samurai of Kishu Clan. Career: grad., Tokyo Univ. of Com., 1900; studied in England and Germany, 1905-08; apptd. Lecturer, Tokyo Univ. of Com., 1902; sent to Europe as Govt. Student, 1905; Prof., same Univ., 1919; Govt. Adviser at Int'l Labor Conf., Washington, 1919; Delegate to Int'l Econ. Conf., Geneva, 1927. Address: 9 Momozonocho, Nakanoku, Tokyo.

Vice-Speaker, Lower House; M. P.; Adviser, Seiyukai; b. May, 1877; s. of Shigetaro Uyehara, Nagano-ken. Career: grad., London Univ., 1910; Reporter, Saihoku Shimpo in America; Pres., Nichibei Shogyo-Sha, U. S.; Commr., English-Japanese Exhibition and Pacific World Exhibition, Panama; Lecturer, Tokyo Higher Tech. School; Prof., Meiji Univ. and Rikkyo Univ.; elected to Diet 6 times since 1917; Councillor, Communications Dept. and Foreign Office. Address: 12 Aoyama-Takagicho, Akasaka-ku, Tokyo.

Doctor of Forestry; Landscape Architect; b. Feb., 1889 in Tokyo; s. of late Yasuhei Uyehara. Career: grad., Tokyo Imp. Univ.; Non-Commissioned Staff, Chosen Govt.: same, Tokyo Municipality. Address: 1063 Shinkawa, Mitakamura, Kitatama-gun, Tokyo-fu.

(M. A.); Finnish Min., Tokyo; b. July, 1894 in Finland; s. of H. E. Wegelius, Dean. Career: entered Finnish Deplomatical Service 1919; Charge d'Affaires at Moscow, 1921; Sec. Legation at London 1921 1921-25; Finnish Rep. Secretariat of the League of Nations 1925; Sec. Legation at Bern 1926-28; in service at Ministry for Foreign Affairs at Helsinki 1928-33: as Chief, Bureau for League of Nations 1928-39, as Dir. Polit. & Com. Section 1930-31, as Sec.-General 1931-33; Charge d'Affaires in Rome 1929; Substitute Delegate, League of Nations Assembly 1925-28; Delegate, Int'l Labour Conference 1926; Delegate at several Int'l Conferences. Address: c/o Finnish Legation, 62, Tansumachi, Azabu-ku, Tokyo.

A. B., A. M.; b. Aug., 1891 in U. S. A. Career: Worked on various newspapers in U. S. A.; joined United Press in 1916 and served throughout United States and Latin America; came to the Far East as Gen. Mgr., 1925. Address: Nippon Dempo Tsushinsha, Tokyo.

Siamese Minister to Japan; b. Sept., 1884 in Bangkok; n. Siamese. Career: grad., Suan Kularb School, Bangkok; Military Coll., Siam and Germany; entered Diplomatic Service. Address: Siamese Legation, Tokyo.

Dir., Oriental Vacuum Industry Co.; b. July, 1897 in Osaka; s. of Takahide Wada, business Mgr. Career: studied at Economics Dept., Keio Univ.; succeeded family estate, 1919. Address: 29 Kiyohoricho, Higashiku, Osaka.

M. D.; D. D.; Missionary; b. Apr., 1863 in Columbus, Ill., U. S.; reared in Missouri; n. American; s. of Daniel Thomas Wainright, clergyman. Career: grad., Missouri Medical Coll., Washington Univ.; practiced medicine in Missouri, 1885-[?]8; came to Japan, 1888 under Board of Missions of Methodist Episcopal Church, South; taught English 2 years in Oita Middle School and organized Methodist Church at that place; Principal, Academic Dept., Kwansei Gakuin, 1890-1907; presiding Elder, St. Louis District in Missouri and Pastor, Univ. Methodist Church, 1907-1912; Gen. Sec., Christian Literature Society of Japan (Kyobun Kwan), 1912 to present; served as Acting Paster, Kobe Union Church, Hongkong Union Church, Tokyo Union Church; Mem. of numerous Christian Organizations; Executive Committee, Japan-America Society; Pres., Asiatic Society of Japan 1930-32. Address: 9 Aoyama Gakuin, Tokyo.

M. P.; Special Commr., Ry. Council; b. Jan., 1875; s. of Seikai Wakamiya, Tokyo-fu. Career: grad., Law Coll., Tokyo Imp. Univ., 1899; joined Communications Dept.; Vice-Minister of Communications, 1922; Dir., Aviation Bureau, 1923; elected to Diet 4 times since 1923. Address: 4 Omotemachi, Akasakaku, Tokyo.

M. A.; LL. B.; Consul-Gen. at Coucil; b. Jan., 1875; s. of Seikai Wakamiya, To-Keishichi Wakasugi. Career: grad., Tung Wen Coll., Shanghai, Univ. of Oregon and New York Univ.; Attaché to France; 3rd Embassy Sec.; Attended 1st & 10th Gen. Meeting, League of Nations; Consul at Los Angeles; 1st Embassy Sec., Eng. Address: Japanese Consulate-General, 22 Battery St., San Francisco, Calif., U. S.

Mem., House of Peers; Baron; Pres., Minseito; b. Feb., 1866 at Matsue City; s. of Senzaburo Okumura, samurai of Shimane-ken, and later adopted by Kei Wakatsuki. Career: grad., Law Coll., Tokyo Imp. Univ., 1892; joined Finance Office; Chief Revenue Officer of Ehime-ken, 1894; Sec. and Councillor, Finance Office; Judge, Court of Administrative Litigation and Chief, Revenue Bureau, Finance Office; Vice-Minister of Finance, 1906; Finance Minister in Katsura Cabinet, 1912; same in Okuma Cabinet, 1915; Home Minister in Momei Kato Cabinet and Premier after Kato's death; attended Naval Conference in London as Chief Delegate. Address: 129 Kamifujimaecho, Hongoku, Tokyo.

Rigakuhakushi (D. Sc.); Prof. Emeritus, Tokyo Imp. Univ.; b. Aug., 1867 in Gifu-ken; s. of Kan-ichiro Wakimizu. Career: grad., Coll. of Science, Tokyo Imp. Univ., 1893; Prof., Geology and Pedology, same Univ., 1896-1929; designated Prof. Emeritus, 1929. Address: 129 Kaminumabe, Higashi-Chofu, Omoriku, Tokyo.

A. B.; M. A.; B. D.; S. T. M.; Missionary; b. Aug., 1888 in New York City; n. American; s. of Dr. Oliver H. Walser, clergyman. Career: grad., Albany Academy, Union Coll., Union Theological Seminary, Columbia Univ.; Dir., "Open Door" Student Centre; Associate Sec., "Fellowship of Reconciliation in Japan". Address: 9 of 19-Go, Mita-Tsunamachi, Shibaku, Tokyo.
Dir., Revenue Supt. Bureau, Mukden Prov.; b. 1894 in Shangtung. Career: present post since 1932. Address: Mukden.

Vice-Minister of Defence; b. 1879 in Chengteh-hsien, Mukden. Career: grad., Mil. Academy, Japan; Teacher, Branch Sch., North Eastern Mil. Academy; Chief Staff, Nat. Defence Administrative Planning Office, 1930; exerted in meditation between Ma Chan-shan & Japanese Army as Representative of Ma; Acting Minister of Defence; present post since 1932. Address: Hsinking.

Dir., Central Bank, Manchoukuo; b. 1886 in Hyogo-ken. Career: grad., Kobe Com. Coll., 1907; joined Yokohama Specie Bank and served as Mgr. of Bombay & Dairen Branches; Mgr., Yokohama Specie Bank, 1930; present post since 1932. Address: Hsinking.

Prof., Nippon Women's Univ.; Dean, Girls' High School Attached to same; b. Jan., 1875 in Fukushima-ken; s. of Rinnai Watanabe, landlord. Career: grad., Higher Normal School; worked as journalist and teacher. Address: 267 Shimo-Hoya, Hoyamura, Kitatamagun, Tokyo-Fu.

General; Supreme War Councillor; Chief, Aviation Headquarters; b. Apr., 1871; s. of Takeemon Wada, Aichi-ken and later adopted by Shobei Watanabe. Career: grad., Military Academy, 1896 and Military Coll., 1903; Attaché, Embassy in Germany; Mem., General Staff Office and Adjutant to Marshal Yamagata; Attaché, Legation in Holland; Comdr., Infantry 29th Brigade; Chief, Military Coll.; Comdr., 7th Division; Comdr., Taiwan Army; Chief, Aviation Dept. Address: 336 Kamiogikubomachi, Suginamiku, Tokyo.

Lord-in-Waiting, Kinkei Hall; b. Jan., 1872 in Okayama-ken; s. of Tokuichiro Watanabe, soy brewer. Career: grad., Law Coll., Tokyo Imp. Univ., 1896; Councillor, Head, Internal Affairs Dept., Pref. Govt.; Chief, Pref. Bureau, Home Office; sent to Europe and America; Mayor of Yokohama, 1922; Pres., Oriental Development Co., 1925-28. Address: 552 Shimo-Ochiai Itchome, Yodobashiku, Tokyo.

Counsellor of Imp. Court and Master of Ceremonies; b. July, 1872 in Tokyo; s. of Naokatsu Matsudaira, feudal lord. Career: entered Imp. Household service early; once sent to Europe and America for study of ceremonies; visited America, Europe and England as Subordinate to Prince and Princess Higashi Fushimi, Prince and Princess Nashimoto, and late Prince Fushimi. Address: 9 Shitaya-Kayacho-Itchome, Shitayaku, Tokyo.

Former Editor, North China Standard; b. Mar., 1884 in Hiroshima-ken. Career: served at Honganji Temple, Kyoto; went to Peiping, and presided over "Junten-Jiho" and English daily North China Standard; travelled about 2 yrs. to Central Asia for exploration; Fellow, Royal Geographical Soc. (F. R. G. S.). Address: 35 Togo, Nakanoku, Tokyo.

Consul at Havana; b. July, 1883; s. of Jutaro Watanabe, Shizuoka-ken. Career: grad., Polit. Econ. Course, Waseda Univ., 1907; joined Foreign Office; Consul at New Orleans. Address: Legation of Japan, Calle 4 Entre 17 y 19, Vedado, Havana, Cuba.

Commr., Yokohama Chamber of Com. & Industry; Pres., Nippon Grindstone Co. and Watanabe Dozokukai; Dir., Watanabe Bank, Hotel New Grand; Auditor, Tokyo-Yokohama Elec. Ry. Co., Tokai Lead Pipe Co.; High-Taxpayer; b. July, 1887 in Yokohama City; s. of Fukusaburo Watanabe, banker. Career: grad., Law Coll., Tokyo Imp. Univ., 1914; went to America, 1916; Councillor, Kanagawa-ken Assembly. Address: 1 Motohamacho, Nakaku, Yokohama.

Major; Foreign Office Dept. Staff; Irr. Staff, Mukden Military Mission; b. July, 1887 in Tokyo. Career: grad., Military Academy; 2nd Lieut., 1906; Attache, 2nd Guard Regiment; despatched to London for Study, 1915-1916; transferred from War Office to Hdqrs., Siberian Expeditional Forces as Liaison Officer to Foreign Army Hdqrs., 1917; Liaison Officer, Foreign Contingents, Tientsin, 1921; retired 1925; present post since Mukden Incident; Spokesman, Gen. Honjo's Army Hdqrs. Address: 7 Hoicho, Mukden.

Prof., Tokyo Higher Normal School; Lecturer, Tokyo Univ. of Litt. & Sc.; b. Mar., 1873 in Hyogo-ken; s. of Naokata Watari. Career: grad., 1st Higher School; served as Lecturer, Middle School attached to Tokyo Higher Normal School, 1902; Lecturer, Tokyo Univ. of Com. and Nippon Univ. Address: 140 Haramachi, Koishikawa-ku, Tokyo.

Mng.-Dir., Tokyo Konoen K. K. (Tokyo Plant, Seed & Implement Co.); Vice-Pres. & Dir., Watase Dozoku K. K. (Watase Family Corporation, Ltd.); b. Feb., 1895 in Tokyo; s. of Torajiro Watase, business man. Career: grad., Tokyo Agrl. Univ., 1918; entered Chilean Nitrate Committee in Japan, 1921; apptd. its Asst. Delegate, 1929; Delegate, 1930; Dir., Chilean Nitrate Co., 1931-32; present post since 1926. Address: 31 Mitake, Shibuyaku, Tokyo.

Mgr., Nat. City Bank of New York, Tokyo; b. July, 1894 in Stillwater, Okla., U. S.; n. American; s. of Frank A. Waugh. Career: grad., Dartmouth Coll., 1915. Address: 1 Kami-Nibancho, Kojimachiku, Tokyo.

Dr. Phil.; b. Jan., 1879 in Köln, Germany; n. German. Career: grad., Univ. of Munich, 1909; apptd. Prof., German Language, Military Academy, Tokyo, 1922; same, Military Coll., Tokyo, 1929; Librarian, German East Asiatic Soc. Address: 714 Matsubara, Matsuzawamura, Setagayaku, Tokyo.
Chief, Educational Dept., Mukden Prov.; b. 1882. Career: present post since 1932. Address: Mukden.
Dr. Theol.; Missionary; Minister, German Church; b. Aug., 1901 in Mülhousen, Alsace; n. German. Address: 39 Kamitomizaka, Koishikawaku, Tokyo.

C. M. G.; British Consul-Gen., Osaka; b. Sept., 1884 in Newcastle-on-Tyne; n. British; s. of James White, merchant. Career: entered consular service, 1903; Vice-Consul, 1913; Consul, 1920; Consul-General, 1927. Address: British Consulate-General, Osaka.

Mng.-Dir., M. S. Wiersum & Co., Yokohama; Consul for Netherlands, Yokohama; b. 1878 in Kantens, Netherland; n. Dutch; s. of L. Wiersum. Career: grad., Hoogere Burger School, Groningen; business practice at Groningen and Hamburg 6 years; at Shanghai, Hankow and Yokohama, 1901-05; joined Messrs. Simon, Evers & Co., Yokohama, 1905; started business on his account, 1915. Address: M. S. Wiersum & Co., Ltd., 25 Yamashitacho, Yokohama.

Dir., Central Bank, Manchoukuo; b. 1877 in Liaoyang-hsien, Mukden. Career: grad., Peiping Mil. Supply Sch.; Dir., Tungfeng Revenue Supt. Bureau; Chief Sec.; Mukden Foreign Affaires Office; Dir., Mukden Forestry Bureau; Chief Sec., Agriculture and Commerce Dept., Mukden Prov.; Associated Dir., Three Prov. Bank; Mng.-Dir., same after Manchuria incident; present post since 1932. Address: Hsinking.

Dr. Phil.; Kammersänger; Bass Singer; Bass Singer; Prof., Imp. Academy of Music, Ueno; b. June, 1884 in Mühlhausen in Thüringen; n. German; s. of Franz Wucherpfennig, official. Career: grad., Univ. of Berlin, 1922; studied singing under Profs. R. von Milde and Moratti of Milano, Italy, 1912; sang 25 years in opera stages and concerts at Dessau, Nürnberg, Düsseldorf, Berlin, Karlsruhe, Frankfurt, Dresden, Cöln, Wiesbaden, Stuttgart, etc.; went to Norway, Hungary, South America and Italy for performance; kept private singing school in Karlsruhe, 1922-30; apptd. present post, Jan., 1932. Address: 1855 Nichome, Sanno, Omoriku, Tokyo.

Bungakuhakushi (D. Litt.); Prof., Taisho Univ.; Lecturer, Tokyo Imp. Univ.; b. Feb., 1879 in Fukushima-ken; s. of Tomeshichi, farmer. Career: grad., Tokyo Imp. Univ.; Chief, Tokyo Social Bureau, 1925-26; Asst. Prof., Tokyo Imp. Univ., 1924-25; sent to Europe and America, 1913-16 and 1922-23. Address: 365 Takinogawa, Takinogawaku, Tokyo.

Baron; Mem., House of Peers; b. July, 1883 in Tokyo; s. of late Hideichi Yabuki, Lieut.-Gen. Career: grad., Polit. Course, Tokyo Imp. Univ., 1908; joined Yokohama Specie Bank; then became Dir. of several firms; elected Mem., House of Peers; Parl. Vice-Minister of Foreign Affairs, Aug., 1925-July, 1927; Parl. Vice-Minister of Navy, July, 1929; Vice-Minister, Foreign Office, Apr.-Dec., 1931. Address: 46 Nampeidai, Shibuyaku, Tokyo.

Minister to Switzerland; b. Dec., 1879 in Shizuoka-ken; brother of Shusaku Yada. Career: grad., Law Coll., Tokyo Imp. Univ., 1906; Elève-Consul at Canton, Hankow and Tientsin; Diplomatic Probationer in China; Sec., Embassy in Italy; Consul-Gen. at San Francisco, London and Shanghai; apptd. present post, 1929; attended Gen. Disarmament Conf., Geneva, 1931. Address: Légation du Japon, 95 Thunstrosse, Berne, Suisse. (Tokyo home) 476 Yoyogi-Hatsudaimachi, Shibuyaku, Tokyo.

Hogakuhakushi (D. L.); Mem., Imperial Academy; Prof., Tokyo Imp. Univ.; Pres., Imp. Agrl. Soc.; Mng.-Dir., Gakushikai; Mem., Rice Problems Investigation Committee; b. July, 1870; s. of Hachizo Yahagi, Saitama-ken. Career: grad., Law Coll., Tokyo Imp. Univ., 1895; Asst. Prof., Tokyo Imp. Univ.; went to Germany, France and England to study economic science. Address: 562 Sendagaya, Shibuyaku, Tokyo.

Stage Dancer; b. Jan., 1907 in Tokyo; s. of late Takesaburô Yamada. Career: in early life, studied "No" dance, then shifted his study to new dance; travelled Europe and America for dance performances, 1926-29; returning home, founded Yamada Goro's Dance Studio. Address: Kaiyo Bldg., 2, Ginza Nishi-Rokuchome, Kyobashiku, Tokyo.

Vice-Pres., Dai Nippon Ice-Manufactory; Auditor, Tamamizu Sake Brewery Co., Marutomo, Kagoshima, Matsue, Aburatsu and Baizuru Ice-Manufactories; b. Mar., 1897 in Kyoto-fu; s. of Keisuke Yamada, mfr. and dealer in ice. Career: grad., Econ. Dept., Kyoto Imp. Univ., 1921; Pres., Ryumon Refrigeratory Co.; succeeded father's business and promoted to present post. Address: Tori Kajiicho, Kawaramachi, Kamikyoku, Kyoto.

Pres., Japan Symphony Assn.; Composer; Adviser, Takarazuka Opera, Columbia Gramaphone Co., etc.; b. June, 1886 in Tokyo; s. of Kenzo Yamada. Career: grad., Middle School Course, Kansei Gakuin, and Tokyo Academy of Music, Ueno; studied in Germany and grad., Composition Dept., Kaiser's Conservatoire, Berlin; conducted many orchestras in America; founded Philharmony Soc. and made many performances; composed numerous songs, orchestras, symphonies and operas; founded Music-Drama Assn. and Composers' Assn. Address: 19 Gobancho, Akasakaku, Tokyo.

Mng.-Dir., Shirokiya K. K.; b. Dec., 1885 in Yamaguchi-ken; 4th s. of Masanari Namiyama; adopted-s. of Ryuichi Yamada, Vice-Minister, War Officer. Career: grad., Military Academy, 1905; established Yamada Shokai, 1924; agent for Japan of Ford Motor Co.; founded Yamada Publishing Co.; present post since 1927. Address: 51 Rokubancho, Kojimachiku, Tokyo.

Hogakuhakushi (D. L.); Mem., Imp. Academy; Pres., Keijo Imp. Univ.; Hon. Prof., Tokyo Imp. Univ.; b. Nov., 1869 in Nara-ken; s. of Heizaburo Yamada. Career: grad., Law Coll., Tokyo Imp. Univ., 1896; took P.-G. Course in Int'l Law at same; studied in Europe and America, 1897; Prof., Law Coll., Tokyo Imp. Univ., 1901-1930; present post since 1931. Address: c/o Keijo Imp. Univ., Keijo.

Chairman, Board of Dirs., Shoko Glass Co.; Mng.-Dir., Asahi Glass Co.; b. Aug., 1870 in Kagoshima-ken; s. of Ariyasu Yamada. Career: apptd. Dir., Takachiho Brick Refinery. Address: 82 Aoyama-Minamicho-Rokuchome, Akasakaku, Tokyo.

Pres., Yokohama Engrg. Works; Dir., Daito Paints Co.; Auditor, Toyo Oxygen Co.; b. Aug., 1872 in Aichi-ken s. of Seiichi Adachi, samurai; adopted by Tosho Yamada, samurai. Career: grad., Engrg. Coll., Tokyo Imp. Univ., 1897; joined Yokohama Dockyard Co., and promoted to its Mng.-Dir.; established Yokohama Engrg. Works and became its Pres. Address: 39 Hommuracho, Yotsuyaku, Tokyo.

1st Emb. Sec. in Belgium; b. 1893 in Ibaragi-ken. Career: grad., Law Coll., Tokyo Imp. Univ.; Eleve Con., Hongkong, 1918; Attache in England, 1919; Mem., Paris Peace Treaty and 1st Gen. Meeting of League of Nations, 1920; 3rd Emb. Sec., 1921; 3rd Legation Sec., Sweden, 1922; Foreign Office Sec., 1924; Chief, 2nd Section of Europe & America Bureau, 1926; Mem., Naval Limitation Conf., Geneva, 1927; Mem., Naval Conf. at London, 1929. Address: c/o Japanese Embassy, Brussels, Belgium.

Mem., Yokohama Chamber of Com. & Ind.; Mng.-Dir., Kirin Beer K. K.; b. May, 1878 in Tokyo; s. of Kubei Kitagawa, and later adopted by Kura Yamagishi. Career: grad., Tokyo Higher Com. School, 1898; joined Mitsubishi Goshi Kaisha, same year; Mng.-Dir., Mitsubishi Shoji Kaisha, 1922-29; present post since 1929. Address: 146 Shirokane-Imazatocho, Shibaku, Tokyo.

M. P.; Mgr., Seiyukai Party; b. Jan., 1888 in Osaka; s. of Denzaburo Yamada. Career: grad., Law Coll., Tokyo Imp. Univ., 1915; studied at P.-G. Course, Kyoto Imp. Univ.; elected to Diet 5 times since 1920; Councillor, Finance Office, 1927-29; present post since 1932. Address: 6 Sakaedori-Nichome, Shibuyaku, Tokyo.

Ph. D.; Pres. & Mng.-Dir., Tokyo Elec. Co.; Dir., Daido Elec. Co., Daido Signal Co., Asahi Electrification Industry Co., 2nd Fuji Elec. Power Co. and Nippon Copper Works; b. Jan., 1874 in Tokyo; s. of Chozo Yamaguchi, dealer in tobacco. Career: grad., Johns Hopkins Univ., Baltimore, U. S., 1902; Vice-Chief, Mining Dept. then Mng.-Dir., Furukawa Gomei Kaisha; Mng.-Dir., Furukawa Elec. Industry Co., 1920; Dir., Tokyo Elec. Co., 1918; Mng.-Dir. and Vice-Pres. of same, 1921; present post since 1927. Address: 266 Minami-Shinagawa 5-chome, Shinagawaku, Tokyo.

Kogakuhakushi (D. E.); Prof., Applied Mechanics, Tokyo Imp. Univ.; Mem., Goetechnical Committee, Japanese Govt. Ry.; b. Mar., 1891 in Shizuoka-ken; s. of Kyujiro Yamaguti. Career: grad., Engrg. Coll., Tokyo Imp. Univ.; served as Engineer, Public Burough, 1914-16; Asst. Prof., Tokyo Imp. Univ., 1916-26; present post since 1926. Address: 1127 Daita, Setagayamachi, Setagayaku, Tokyo.

Consul-Gen., Vladivostok, USSR; b. Apr., 1872 in Aichi-ken; s. of Yazaemon Yamaguchi, farmer. Career: grad., Russian Language Course, Tokyo School of Foreign Languages; apptd. Infantry Sub-Lieut., 1895; Eléve Interpreter, Foreign Office, 1900; Chancelier of same, 1907; Vice-Consul, 1917; Consul, 1919; present post since 1927. Address: Japanese Consulate-General, Vladivostok, USSR.

Mng.-Dir., Shigisan Elec. Ry. Co.; b. Feb., 1896 in Osaka; s. of Kamekichi Yamaguchi. Career: grad., Law Dept., Kansai Univ.; Dir., Osaka Sennichimae Land Co.; Mng.-Dir., Nippon Cable Car Co., Shigisan Cable Car Co. Address: 35 Dogashibacho, Tennojiku, Osaka.

Pres., Sumatra Development Co.; Dir., Borneo Gum Co.; Auditor, Nankai Bleaching Powder Co.; b. Dec., 1878 in Tokyo; s. of Junkichi Yamaji, business man. Career: Dir., Nanyo Cultivation Assn.; Mng.-Dir., Tokyo Riding Club; Adviser, Kanto Student Riding Assn. Address: 5 Rokubancho, Kojimachiku, Tokyo.

Author; Chief Editor, daily "Japan"; Lecturer, Rissho Univ.; b. Mar., 1879 in Osaka; s. of Sojiro Yamakawa, samurai. Career: chiefly studied by himself; taught by Chigaku Tanaka; once became clerk, and journalist. Address: 617 Inamuragasaki, Kamakura, Kanagawa-ken.

Hogakuhakushi (D. L.); Mem., House of Peers; b. Dec., 1873 in Nagasaki-ken; s. of Kagenori Yamakawa, samurai. Career: grad., Law Coll., and P.-G. Course, Tokyo Imp. Univ., 1898; apptd. Councillor, Navy Dept., 1899; Interpreter of same, 1900; Dir., Ry. Dept.; Prof., Naval Staff Coll.; attended 2nd World Peace Conf., Hague, 1907 and Peace Conf. in France, 1919; Dir., Special Peace Treaty Bureau; Dir., Treaty Bureau, Foreign Office, 1920; Dir., Legislation Bureau, 1925-27; nominated Mem., House of Peers, 1926; attended London Conf., 1929. Address: Oyamamachi, Shibuyaku, Tokyo.

M. P.; Adviser, Seiyukai Party; b. Oct., 1867 in Fukui City; s. of Takeo Yamamoto. Career: when young joined Mitsui Bussan Kaisha and promoted its Mng. Dir.; Dir. of many firms; resigned Mitsui Bussan Kaisha, 1914; elected to Diet 5 times since 1920; Chairman, Executive Committee, Seiyukai; Pres., South Manchuria Ry. Co. Address: 43 Shinsakamachi, Akasakaku, Tokyo.

Dir., Nisshin Spinning Co.; b. Nov., 1884 in Hyogo-ken; s. of Sadashichi Miki, and later adopted by Motosaburo Yamamoto. Career: grad., Law Coll., Tokyo Imp. Univ., 1911; joined present firm, 1912. Recreations: literary arts, fine arts. Address: 11 Kitamachi, Ushigomo-ku, Tokyo.

Hogakuhakushi (D. L.); Dean, Economic Coll., Kyoto Imp. Univ.; Prof., Economics, Kyoto Imp. Univ.; b. Jan., 1874 in Miyeken; s. of Shohei Yamamoto. Career: studied at Doshisha Univ., Kyoto Imp. Univ., Columbia and Wisconsin Univs. (U. S.), Halle and Berlin Univs. (Germany). Address: 1 of 31 Koyama-Shimofusacho, Kami-Kyoku, Kyoto.

Dir., Communication Bureau, Chosen Govt. Gen.; b. 1886 in Hyogo-ken. Career: grad., Law Coll., Tokyo Imp. Univ., 1910; Administrative Office, Gunma-ken; Sec., Legislative Bureau; Head, 1st Section, Legislative Bureau; present post since 1928. Recreations: hores-riding, tennis, utai (song). Address: Yamato-cho, Keijo, Chosen.

Mng.-Dir., Japan Beer & Mineral Springs Co.; Pres., Yamatame Glass Mfg. Co.; b. Apr., 1893 in Osaka; s. of Tamezo Yamamoto, glass mfr. Career: stduied science and mathematics under Prof. Franklin; went to U. S., 1917; Mng.-Dir., Japan Bottle Mfg. Co. which inc. to present firm, 1921. Address: Yorikicho, Kitaku, Osaka.

Baron; Home Minister; Mem., House of Peers, Adviser, Minseito; b. Mar., 1856; s. of Kaku Yamamoto, samurai of Bungo Clan. Career: studied at Keio Univ. and Mitsubishi Com. School; Mgr., Nippon Yusen Kaisha; Business Mgr., Bank of Japan; Dir., Yokohama Specie Bank; Pres., Bank of Japan; same, Hypothec Bank of Japan; Finance Minister in 3rd Saionji Cabinet; Com. & Agrl. Minister in Yamamoto Cabinet and Hara Cabinet; nominated Mem., House of Peers. Address: 38 Kami-nibancho, Kojimachiku, Tokyo. (Official Residence) 1 Soto-Sakuradamachi, Kojimachiku, Tokyo.

Dr. et Bonarum Artium Magister (Leipzig Univ.); M. P.; Adviser, Seiyukai; b. Jan., 1870 in Niigata-ken; s. of Katsura Yamamoto, physician; Career: grad., Economics and Science of Agr., Halle and Leipzig Univs., Germany; conferred Dr. Ph. degree, from same; returning home, apptd. Prof., 2nd Higher School; resigned, 1897; joined Hypothec Bank of Japan as Chief, Appraisement Section; elected to Diet 8 times; leader of Seiyukai party; apptd. twice Minister of Agr. & Forestry in both Tanaka Cabinet and Inukai's; Pres., Taiwan Seito Kaisha and Dir. of several other business firms. Address: 2658 Kamimeguro, Meguroku, Tokyo.

Pres., Hakushinsha, Bun-undo; Rep. Dir., Dai Nippon Pencil Mfg. Co.; Chairman, Board of Directors, Tokyo Shokai and Photo Chemical Laboratory; Auditor, Nippon Chemical Industry Co., Meiji Confectionery Co., Tokiwa Elec. Co., Oriental Photo Industry Co. and Nippon Art Paper Co.; b. Sept., 1872 in Nagaoka City; s. of Risaku Yamamoto. Career: founded Hakushisha, 1897; made inspection tour to Europe and America, 1910. Address: 21 Kita-Kogacho, Surugadai, Kandaku, Tokyo.

Lieut.-General; Comdr., 16th Division; b. Dec., 1875 in Shimane-ken; s. of Sainosuke Yamamoto, samurai. Career: apptd. Comdr., 18th Division; Dir., Toyama Military School; Present post since 1930. Address: Tayamachi, Fukakusa, Fushimiku, Kyoto.

Territorial Comdr., Salvation Army, Japan; b. Aug., 1872 in Okayama-ken; s. of Sahachi Yamamuro, landowner. Career: studied at Doshisha Univ.; in 1895 entered Salvation Army, to which has devoted his whole life; commencing as Lieut., has now reached highest rank in S. A.; served as Corps Commanding Officer; Training School Principal; Editor, Chief Sec. for Japan; present post since 1926; travelled extensively in Europe and America; Mem., High Council of Salvation Army; noted preacher and teacher of Christianity. Address: (office) 5 Hitotsubashidori, Kandaku, Tokyo.

Mng.-Dir. Mitsubishi Bank; b. Oct., 1880 in Kumamoto-ken; s. of Soi Yamamuro. Career: grad., Law Coll., Tokyo Imp. Univ., 1907; studied in Europe and America; upon returning home, joined Mitsubishi Goshi Kaisha; after having served as Vice-Chief, Bank Dept. of same, Business Mgr., London Branch Mgr., Dir., Osaka Branch Mgr., appointed present post, 1929; once served as Special Mem., Osaka Chamber of Com. & Ind. Publications: "Japan's Money Market", etc. Address: 10 Mukoyama, Shibuyaku, Tokyo.

Mem., Tokyo Stock Exchange; b. Aug., 1888 in Tokyo; s. of Genbei Kimura, and later adopted by Seibei Yamanaka. Career: grad., Chuo Com. School. Address: (office) 7 Edobashi Itchome, Nihonbashiku, Tokyo.

Vice-Pres., Taiwan Elec. Power Co.; b. Apr., 1883; s. of Han Yamanaka, samurai of Hikone Clan; later adopted by Harue Yamanaka. Career: grad., Law Coll., Tokyo Imp. Univ., 1908; joined Bank of Japan; Mgr., London Branch of same; then present post. Address: (Tokyo home) 12 Yanaka-Shimizucho, Shitayaku, Tokyo.

Vice-Pres., Central Bank of Manchoukuo; b. Jan., 1872 in Okayama-ken; s. of Genshiro Yamanari. Career: grad., Tokyo Higher Commercial Sch.; entered business; Pres., Toyo Sugar Mfg. Co.; Chairman of Board, Shinko Land Co.; present post since 1932. Address: Hsinking, Manchoukuo.

Admiral; b. July, 1877 in Miyagi-ken; s. of Bunnoshin Yamanashi, samurai. Career: grad., Naval Coll., 1898; Instructor, Naval Staff Coll.; Staff, Naval Board of Command; Comdr., H. M. S. Katori; Chief, 1st Section, Naval Affairs Bureau, Navy Dept.; Chief Staff-Officer, Yokosuka Naval Station; Chief, Yokosuka Naval Arsenal; Headquarters Chief, Naval Construction Dept.; Vice-Minister of Navy, 1928; Staff, Naval Board of Command, 1930; Comdr., Saseho Naval Station; same, Kure Naval Station. Address: care Navy Office, Tokyo.

Auditor, Toyo Cotton Spinning Co.; A. M. S. T.; b. June, 1876 in Otsu, Shiga-ken; adopted-s. of late Takeo Yamanobe, Pres. of above firm. Career: grad., Textile Dept., Municipal School of Technology, Manchester, England; served present firm since 25 years ago; authority on cotton spinning industry business in Japan; succeeded father's estate, 1920. Address: 19 Dogashibacho, Tennojiku, Osaka.

Lord-in-Waiting, Kinkei Hall; Mem., Ry. Council; b. Nov., 1866 in Kagoshima-ken; s. of Jishu Yamanouchi. Career: grad., Law Coll., Tokyo Imp. Univ., 1890; entered official service; attended World Sexual Diseases Prevention Conf. at Brussels, 1899; returning home next year, apptd. Governor, Aomori-ken; Dir., Ry. Bureau, Communications Dept.; Dir., Ry. Board; Gov., Hokkaido; Chief Sec. of Cabinet; nominated Mem., House of Peers, 1914; Ry. Minister in Yamamoto Cabinet, 1923; Privy Councillor, 1932-1933. Address: 33 Fujimicho, Azabuku, Tokyo.

Retired Lieut.-Gen.; Adviser, South Manchuria Ry. Co., b. Aug., 1876 in Kyoto-fu; s. of Kakudo Yamanouchi; adopted by Masaaki Yamanouchi. Career: grad., Military Coll., 1897, Military Artillery School and Engrg. Coll., Tokyo Imp. Univ.; apptd. Instructor, Military Coll.; Adjutant, Field Telegraph Dept., Imp. Headquarters; Instructor, Artillery School; Commr., Gen. Staff Office; Mem., Military Tech. Headquarters; Sectional Chief, Military Ordinance Bureau; Chief, 2nd Dept., Military Tech. Headquarters; Chief, Military Fortification Headquarters; apptd. present post, Aug., 1932. Address: 34 Hikawamachi, Nakanoku, Tokyo.

Hogakuhakushi (D. L.); Mem., House of Peers; Pres., Nihon Univ.; former Gov., Kwantung Govt.; b. Apr., 1876; s. of Tsuruji Kosaka and later adopted by Toyo Yamaoka. Career: grad., Nippon Horitsu Gakko, 1899; Judge, Tokyo District Court; studied criminal action law in Germany; Councillor, Justice Dept.; Chief, Bureau of Penal Affairs; same, Police Bureau, Home Office; nomiated Mem., House of Peers; Pres., Nihon Univ.; received degree, 1919. Address: 20 Shinsen, Shibuyaku, Tokyo.

Major-General; Dir., Military Affairs Bureau; Sec.-Gen., Supreme War Council; b. Nov., 1882 in Kochi-ken; s. of Jukichi Yamaoka. Career: apptd. Instructor, Military Staff Coll.; Comdr., Student Corps, Military Coll.; Comdr., Infantry 22nd Regiment; Chief, 2nd Section, Board of Military Instruction; Comdr., Infantry 1st Brigade; Major-Gen., 1931; present post since 1932. Address: 436 Kashiwagi, Yodobashiku, Tokyo.

Consul at Manchouli, Manchoukuo; b. Feb., 1880 in Kochi-ken; s. of late Keikichi Yamasaki. Career: grad., Dobun Shoin; Consul at Chientao, Newchang, Tsitsihar, Kalgan. Address: Japanese Consulate, Manchouli, Manchoukuo.

Rear-Admiral; Chief, Gen. Affairs Sec., Naval Construction Dept., Navy Office b. Sept., 1883; s. of Keisuke Yamashita, Shinto priest. Career: grad., Naval Coll., Naval Gunnery School, Naval Submarine School, and Naval Staff Coll; present post since 1933. Address: c.o. Kanseihonbu, Tokyo.

M. P.; Founder and Principal, Tokyo Com. & Tech. School; b. Feb., 1872 in Kagawa-ken; s. of Jugoro Yamashita, farmer. Career: studied at Jinseisha School, Kyoto; sent to Diet from Kagawa-ken 4 times; apptd. Councillor, Dept. of Education; granted Blue Ribbon Medal for his service. Address: 2 Yayoicho, Mukogaoka, Hongoku, Tokyo.

Kogakushi; Architect and Engr.; b. Apr., 1888 in Yamagata-ken; s. of Shinriki Yamashita, educator. Career: grad., Archit. Dept., Tokyo Imp. Univ., 1912; served Mitsubishi Real Estate Dept., 1912-23; Lecturer, Archit. Dept., Tokyo Imp. Univ. since 1920 up to date; as Chief Archit., Shibaura Engrg. Works, engaged in erection of their New Plants at Tsurumi, Yokohama, 1923-25; Lecturer, Akita Mining Coll., 1925-27; Chief Archit., Mitsui Gomei Kaisha, 1925-29; opened Archit. & Engrg. Office, 1929. Address: 141 Otsuka-Sakashitamachi, Koishikawaku, Tokyo.

Minister to Argentine; b. Jan., 1880 in Shizuoka-ken; s. of Kazuyasu Aida, samurai. Career: grad., Law Coll., Tokyo Imp. Univ., 1906; apptd. Elève-Consul, Diplomatic Probationer, Sec. of Legation and served at Canton, Spain, France, America and Argentine; Sec., Foreign Office and Agrl. & Com. Dept.; Chief, Gen. Affairs Section, Treaty Bureau; Chief, 3rd Section, Europe & America Bureau; Councillor, Embassies in USSR and Brazil; present post since 1928. Address: Legacion Del Japan, Calle Reconquista 134, Buenos Aires, La Argentina.

M. E. (Cornell Univ.); Mng.-Dir., Enoshima Elec. Ry. Co.; b. Apr., 1872 in Nara; brother of Chikayuki Yamazaki, educater. Career: grad., Elec. Dept., Tokyo Imp. Univ., 1897; grad., P.-G. Course, Cornell Univ., America, 1902; Dir. and Chief Engr., Keihin Elec. Ry. Co., Katsuragawa Hydro-Elec. Co., etc.; Vice-Pres., Elec. Assn. Address: 116 Honmuracho, Azabuku, Tokyo.

M. P.; Chairman, Polit. Affairs Inquiry Committee, Seiyukai; b. June, 1880 in Tokyo; s. of Motoyoshi Yamazaki, samurai. Career: grad., Law Coll., Kyoto Imp. Univ., 1906; apptd. Official and Councillor, Taiwan Gov't.; Sec. and Councillor, Education Dept.; Dir., Common Education Bureau, Education Dept.; Parl. Vice-Minister of Education; elected to Diet 4 times. Address: 2570 Nishi-Sugamo-Nichome, Toshimaku, Tokyo.

Lieut.-General; Vice-Minister of War; b. Oct., 1879 in Nagasaki-ken; s. of Tomotaro Kusunoki; adopted by Shizuko Yanagawa. Career: grad., Military Coll.; fought in Russo-Japanese War; grad., Military Staff Coll.; Instructor, Military Cavalry School; Comdr., Cavalry 20th Regiment; Sectional Chief, Gen. Staff Office; Comdr., Cavalry 1st Brigade; Dir., Cavalry School; present post since 1930. Address: (Official Residence) 13 Gobancho, Kojimachiku, Tokyo.

Bungakushi (B. A.); Guest Staff, Osaka Mainichi Shinbun; b. Mar., 1889 in Tokyo; s. of Naoyoshi Yanagi, Rear-Admiral, Mem., House of Peers. Career: grad., Philosophical Dept., Litt. Coll., Tokyo Imp. Univ.; became Lecturer and Prof. in Toyo and Meiji, Doshisha and Harvard Univs. Address: 26 Hisakata-cho, Koishikawaku, Tokyo.

Pres., 1st Fire & Marine Ins. Co.; Auditor, Mitsukoshi, Ltd., Niko Co. and Daini Fuji Elec. Power Co., Ltd.; b. Sept., 1862 in Nagano-ken; s. of Yasoki Yanagi. Career: grad., Keio Univ., 1889; joined Jiji Shimpo, same year; joined Tomioka Silk Manufactory, 1894; Mng.-Dir., Maebashi Spinning Works, Ltd., same year; Mgr., Shinmachi Spinning Works, 1895; joined Mitsui Bank, 1899; Mgr. of its Branches at Shimonoseki, Hiroshima and Nagasaki; Chief, Real Estate Dept. of same bank, 1909; established 1st Fire & Marine Ins. Co., Ltd. and became its Mng.-Dir., 1917; then promoted to present post. Address: 37 Honmuracho, Azabuku, Tokyo.

Ex.-Pres., Chugai Shogyo Shimpo; Mem., Int'l Tourist Committee; Councillor, Kyochokai; Dir., Japan Radio Corporation and Japan Press Assn.; b. Aug., 1875 in Fukuyama City; s. of Takeo Yanagida, samurai. Career: grad., Econ. Dept., Senshu Univ., 1894, and Law Dept., Chuo Univ., 1896; joined Chugai Shogyo Shimposha; Mgr. Econ. Dept.; Chief Editor, Dir., then Mng.-Dir. of same; Pres., 1926-1933. Address: 1 of 16 Nijukkimachi, Ushigomeku, Tokyo.

Motorcar Importer; b. Jan., 1883 in Nagano-ken; s. of Mojuro Yanagida. Career: grad., Econ. Dept., Senshu Univ.; Mem., Tokyo City Assembly; Mem., Nihonbashi Ward Assembly; Pres., Tokyo Motorcar Assn. Address: 1 Gofukubashi Nichome, Nihonbashiku, Tokyo.

Count; Mem., House of Peers; Mem., Special Commission of Public Health and Hygiene; Hon. Mem., Royal Statistical Society (London); Pres., Yanagisawa Statistical Institute; b. Dec., 1870; s. of Komei Yanagisawa, landlord of Kurokawa Clan, and later adopted by Yasukata Yanagisawa. Career: grad., Univ. Course of Peers' School; studied at Berlin Univ., Strassburg Univ. and Wien Univ.; Lecturer, Waseda Univ.; attended Int'l Statistical Conference in Rome and Warsaw; Pres., Tokyo City Assembly. Address: 8 Tamachi, Shibaku, Tokyo.

Envoy Extroadinary and Minister Plenipotentiary to Chile; b. 1884 in Fukuoka-ken. Career: grad., Law Coll., Tokyo Imp. Univ.; Attache, Emb. in England, 1914; Foreign Office Sec., 1916; Attache, 1st Section of Political Affairs Bureau, 1920; Mem., 1st Gen. Meeting of League of Nations, same year; 2nd Legation Sec., China, 1921; 1st Emb. Sec., Belgium, 1924; Consul.-Gen., Canton, 1928; Sec. Govt. Gen., Taiwan, same year; 1st Legation Sec., China, 1930; Emb. Councillor, China 1930; present post since 1933. Address: c/o Japanese Legation, Santiago, Chile.

M. P.; Acting Partner, Shokozan Clay Co.; b. Jan., 1886 in Kagawa-ken; s. of Mataji Yano. Career: grad., Meiji Univ., 1907; passed Higher Civil Service Exam.; Police Supt., Kagawa-ken, District Headman of Kagawa-ken, entered business. Address: 5 Mita, Meguroku, Tokyo.

Pres., 1st Mutual Life Ins. Co.; Pres., 1st Mutual Savings Bank; Dir., Seimei Hoken Shoken K. K.; b. Dec., 1865 in Okayama-ken; s. of San-eki Yano. Career: grad., Med. Dept., 3rd Higher School, 1889; apptd. Physician, Nippon Life Ins. Co.; made inspection tour to Europe and America, 1895-97; Commr., Ins. Dept., Agrl. & Com. Dept.; Examiner, Statistics Bureau of Cabinet, 1900; established 1st Mutual Life Ins. Co., 1902, and became its Pres. Address: 126 Den-en-Chofu, Omoriku, Tokyo.

M. A. (Columbia Univ.); Pres., Hikone Coll. of Com.; b. July, 1886 in Kochi-ken; s. of Seikichiro Yano, business man. Career: grad., Yamaguchi Coll. of Com. and Columbia Univ.; Prof., Yamaguchi Coll. of Com.; School-Inspector, taking charge of com. education at Education Dept. Address: 26 Konki, Hikone, Shiga-ken.

Pres., Yasaka Shoji K. K.; b. May, 1885 in Saga-ken; s. of Eisuke Hara, and later adopted by Tomoki Yasaka. Career: entered business early; for years engaged in Russo-Japanese trade; received silver cup for merit of his service in Russo-Japanese War; visited U. S. for inspection, 1922. Address: 24 Shoto, Shibuyaku, Tokyo.

Lecturer, Tokyo Higher Polytechnical School; b. Sept., 1901 in Tokyo; s. of late Zenzaburo Yasuda, business man; Mem., House of Peers. Career: grad., Western Arts Course, Tokyo Academy of Fine Arts; sent to France as Student of Education, 1929; many of his paintings accepted in Imp. Arts Exhibitions. Address: 1 Iidamachi-Sanchome, Kojimachiku, Tokyo.

b. Aug., 1875; s. of late Naoichi Yasuda, landlord. Career: grad., Law Coll., Tokyo Imp. Univ., 1903; joined Bank of Japan; Asst. to Auditor, London Agent of same; served Mgr. of its Branches at Nagoya, Kyoto and Moji; Chief, National Treasury Bureau; Vice-Pres., Industrial Bank of Japan, 1928-30. Address: 274 Chojamaru, Kamiosaki, Tokyo.

Pres., Tokyo Higher Polytechnical School; b. Nov., 1874; s. of Gunzo Teramoto and later adopted by Gihei Yasuda. Career: grad., Training School for Teachers attached to Tokyo Higher Tech. School; Prof., Tokyo Higher Tech. School; same, Tokyo Academy of Fine Arts; went to Austria-Hungary to study design. Address: 1073 Nakanobu-Yashikishita, Ebaraku, Tokyo.

Prof., Tokyo School of Foreign Languages; b. Sept., 1876 in Shimane-ken; s. of Toshio Yasugi, samurai. Career: grad., Litt. Coll., Tokyo Imp. Univ., 1900; studied in Russia; returning home became Prof., Tokyo School of Foreign Languages to date; inspected through Russia with late Count Shimpei Goto, 1927. Address: 19 Kasumicho, Azabuku, Tokyo.

B. A. (Cambridge); b. Oct., 1859 in Fukuoka-ken; s. of Ichiro Yasuhiro. Career: grad., Keio Univ.; studied at Central Inst., Hongkong, 1888; studied Chinese at Peking and law at Cambridge Univ.; Sec. of Cabinet; Councillor, Legislation Bureau; Sec. to Home Minister; Dir., Common Educational Affairs Bureau, Education Dept.; Chief Sec. of Cabinet; Sec.-Gen., Agrl. & Com. Dept.; Dir., Legislation Bureau and Pension Bureau; nominated Mem., House of Peers, 1899; Privy Councillor, 1926; Pres., South Manchuria Ry. Co., 1924-28. Address: 34 Naka-Rokubancho, Kojimachiku, Tokyo.

Baron; Hon. Pres., Moji Club; Pres., Kyushu Steel Works; b. Apr., 1849; s. of Shoeki Tokunaga and later adopted by Okaemon Yasukawa. Career: studied at Keio Univ.; engaged in coal-mining and sales business; established Meiji Senmon Gakko at his own expense; elected to Diet from Fukuoka City; nominated Mem., House of Peers. Address: 1072 Nakabaru, Tobata City, Fukuoka-ken.

B. S.; Pres., Yasukawa Elec. Works; Pres., Meiji Mining Co., etc.; b. Sept., 1877 in Fukuoka-ken; s. of Baron Keiichiro Yasukawa, business man. Career: studied at Keio Univ.; grad., Univ. of Pennsylvania, Phila.; high taxpayer in Fukuoka-ken; conferred Blue Ribbon Medal, 1927. Address: Tobata Nakahara, Fukuoka-ken.

Mng.-Dir., Mitsui Bussan Kaisha; Dir., Toa Kogyo K. K., Shibaura Engrg. Works, Nippon Elec. Co. and Toyo Raw Cotton Co.; Dir., Mitsui Gomei Kaisha; b. Apr., 1870 in Kyoto-fu; s. of Tarosuke Yasukawa. Career: grad., Osaka Higher Com. School, 1889; joined Mitsui Bussan Kaisha, and served as Mgr., Branches at Kobe, Tientsin and Dairen; Business Mgr., Tokyo Head Office; Mng.-Dir., of same, 1918; Dir., Mitsui Gomei Kaisha, 1932. Address: 55 Sekiguchi-Daimachi, Koishikawaku, Tokyo.
M. P.; Retired Vice-Admiral; b. Dec., 1880 in Iwate-ken; s. of Kiichiro Yasumi, official. Career: grad., Naval Staff Coll. Address: 48 Kitamachi, Takanawa, Shibaku, Tokyo.

Minister to Siam; b. Apr., 1882 in Yamaguchi-ken; s. of Kihachi Yatabe. Career: grad., Tokyo Higher Com. School, 1907; entered Foreign Service, 1908; Sec., Foreign Office, 1919-24; 1st Sec., Embassy in U. S., 1924-26; Consul-General, Tsingtao, 1926-28; present post since 1928. Address: Japanese Legation, Bangkok, Siam.

M. P.; Parl. Vice-Minister of Justice; b. Dec., 1879; s. of Jinroku Yatsunami, Oita-ken. Career: grad., Law Coll., Tokyo Imp. Univ., 1909; opened Law Office; Sec. to Communication Minister, 1915; elected to Diet 4 times; Councillor, Justice Dept.; Chairman, Executive Committee of Minseito; present post since May, 1932. Address: 1 Kasumicho, Azabuku, Tokyo.

Chairman, Board of Directors, Sumitomo Bank; Councillor, Bank of Japan; b. Sept., 1872 in Kagoshima-ken; s. of Ki Yatsushiro, samurai. Career: grad., Law Coll., Tokyo Imp. Univ., 1896; occupied many posts in Nippon Yusen Kaisha, including headship of its London Branch; joined Sumitomo Bank, Gen. Business Mgr., then promoted to present posts; Dir., Sumitomo Goshi Kaisha, Sumitomo Trust Co., Sumitomo Warehouse Co., Sumitomo Life Ins. Co., Osaka North Harbor Co.; Auditor, Sumitomo Colliery Co., Sumitomo Fertilizer Works, Sumitomo Besshi Mine, Sumitomo Steel-Tube & Copper Works; Vice-Pres., Hawaii Int'l Trust Co.; Mem., Special Industry Investigation Committee; Councillor, Bank of Japan; Mem., Special Monetary Circulation System Investigation Committee; Chairman, Osaka Clearing House; Mem. of Committee, Councillor Osaka Chamber of Com. & Industry. Address: Sumiyoshimura, Mukogun, Hyogo-ken.

Mayor of Mukden; Chief, Inspection Bureau, Manchoukuo Hsiehhohui; b. 1896 in Kinhsien, Mukden. Career: grad., Tokyo Imp. Univ.; Non-Official Staff, South Manchuria Ry., 1926; Mem., Dairen Municipal Assembly, 1928; Councillor, Mukden Provincial Office, 1931; present post since 1932. Address: Mukden.
Gov., Southern Sub-Province, Hsing-an Prov. Manchoukuo. Career: present post since 1932. Address: Gov.'s Office, South Sub-Province, Hing-an Prov., Manchoukuo.

Chief, 2nd Section, Cultural Work Bureau, Foreign Office; b. Mar., 1884 in Fukui-ken; s. of Kanshiro Yedo. Career: grad., History Dept., Tokyo Imp. Univ.; entered Foreign Office, 1918; Vice-Consul at Tientsin, 1912-21; same at San Francisco, 1922; Consul at Kiukiang, China, 1922-24; same at Tsingtao, 1925-27; Liverpool, 1927-30; Vancouvor, 1930-31; present post since 1931. Address: 28 Kamejimacho I-chome, Nihonbashiku, Tokyo.

Embassy Com. Councillor at Shanghai; b. April, 1876 in Hiroshima-ken; s. of Mototaro Yokotake. Career: grad., Tokyo Com. Coll. 1899; joined Mitsui Bussan Kaisha; served its branches at Singapore, Sourabaya, London, Lyons, Shanghai; apptd. Com. Attaché of Legation, 1922; Com. Councillor of Embassy, 1927. Address: Japanese Com. Councillor's Office, 149 Szechuan Road, Shanghai.

Gov. of Kanagawa-ken; b. Jan., 1884 in Akita-ken; s. of Yuki Yokoyama, samurai. Career: grad., Law Coll., Tokyo Imp. Univ., 1909; apptd. Sec., Engrg. Bureau; Gov., Hiroshima-ken and Ishikawa-ken; Dir. Police Bureau, 1928; Gov., Kyoto-fu, 1931; same, Kanagawa-ken, 1932. Address: Official Residence, 18 Momijigaokamachi-Itchome, Nakaku, Yokohama.

Vice-Admiral; Chief, Saseho Naval Station; b. in Iwate-ken. Career: Naval Attache, Embassy in Russia; Chief, 3rd Section, Navy Office; Chief, 1st Despatched Squadron; Chief, Chinkai Naval Port; Chief, 3rd Squadron; Attached, Naval General Staff; present post since Nov., 1933. Address: Saseho Naval Station, Nagasaki-ken.

Pres., Mitsui Trust Co.; Dir., Mitsui Gomei Kaisha; same, Mitsui Bank; Special Mem., Tokyo Chamber of Com. & Industry; Pres., Trust Assn.; b. Feb., 1876 in Tokyo; s. of Takezo Wada, samurai; adopted by Tozaburo Wada. Career: grad., Aoyama Gakuin Coll.; studied in America 8 years; joined Nippon Ry. Co.; joined Mitsui Bank as Mgr., Branches at Osaka and Yokohama; Mng. Dir. of same, 1909. Address: Aoyama-Minamicho-Rokuchome, Akasakaku, Tokyo.

Mng.-Dir., Kyodo Trust Co.; b. May, 1776 in Saga-ken; s. of Asakichi Yoshida, farmer. Career: grad., Law Coll., Tokyo Imp. Univ.; Commr., Revenue Superintending Office; Chief of same; Chief, Custom House; Sec., Home Office; Commr., Imp. Forest Bureau; Chief, Bureau of Imp. Supplies; Chief, Communications Office, Taiwan Govt.; then present post. Address: 162 Kaimori, Ashiya, Mukogun, Hyogo-ken.

Bungakuhakushi (D. Litt.); Prof., Tokyo Imp. Univ.; b. Feb., 1874; s. of Eijiro Yoshida, Yamagata-ken. Career: grad., Litt. Coll., Tokyo Imp. Univ., 1900; P.-G. Course of same; went to Germany and France for study of moral science; Prof., Tokyo Higher Normal School and Tokyo Higher Normal School for Women; attended World Conference at Mons City, Belgium. Address: 110 Hakusan-Gotenyama, Koishikawaku, Tokyo.

Civil Engr., Imp. Japanese Navy; Chief, Naval Civil Engrg. Bureau, Navy Dept.; b. Mar., 1884 in Kyoto. Career: grad., Civil Engrg. Dept., Sapporo Agrl. Coll.; upon grad. served Navy, taking charge of civil engineering work; gradually promoted to present post; sent to Europe and America for study, 1914-15. Address: Naval Official Residence, Inaokacho, Yokosuka.

Lawyer; Auditor, Omi Ry. Co.; Dir., Kansai Univ.; b. Mar., 1878 in Ishikawa-ken; s. of Sozaemon Yoshida, landlord. Career: grad., Law Dept., Kansai Univ. and Nippon Univ.; began to practice law, 1907; Mem., Osaka Prefectural Assembly; Pres., Osaka Bar Assn. Address: 5 Hiranomachi-Nichome, Higashiku, Osaka.

Envoy Extroadinary and Minister Plenipatentiary in Waiting list; b. Sept., 1878; s. of Tsuna Takeuchi, M. P. and later adopted by Kenzo Yoshida. Career: grad., Law Coll., Tokyo Imp. Univ., 1906; 3rd Sec., Embassy in Italy; Sec., Chosen Govt.; 2nd Sec., Embassy in America; attended Peace Conference; 1st Sec., Embassy in England; Consul-General at Tientsin; same at Mukden; Minister to Sweden; Vice-Minister of Foreign Affairs, 1928; Ambassador to Italy 1930-1932. Address: c/o Foreign Office.
Auditor, Bank of Japan; b. July, 1886; s. of Kajiro Yoshida, Osaka. Career: grad., P.-G. Course of Tokyo Higher Com. School; joined present firm. Address: 498 Kugaharacho, Omoriku, Tokyo.
Dir., Chiba Godo Bank; b. Nov., 1878 in Tokyo; s. of Tanjibei Yoshida. Career: grad., Keio Univ.; Dir., Sobu Bank and Tokiwa Savings Bank. Address: 29 Nishi-Edogawacho, Koishikawaku, Tokyo.

Physician; M. D.; Mem., Taihokushu Conf.; Mem., Taiwan Central Sanitation Committee; b. 1875 in Hyogo-ken; s. of Shigeru Yoshida, physician. Career: grad., Special Physical Course, Medical Coll., Kyoto Imp. Univ., 1899; studied Bacteriology in Ishigami Labratory, Osaka; Sea-Port Quarantine Physician; Taiwan Govt. Gen., 1901; Asst. Prof., Medical Coll., Taiwan, 1905; studied in Germany, 1907; Prof., Medical Coll., Taiwan, 1910; Chief Physician & Vice-Pres., Red Cross Society Hospital, Taiwan Branch, same year; rewarded by Taiwan Educational Society, 1922; Est., Yoshida Hospital in Taihoku, same year. Recreations: Reading, Paintings. Address: Tsukiji-machi, Taihoku.

M. P.; Chairman, Fukuoka-ken Pref. Assembly; b. Dec., 1888 in Fukuoka-ken; s. of Tomojiro Yoshida. Career: grad., Polit. Econ. Dept., Waseda Univ.; apptd. Dir., Kyushu Dental Coll.; Polit. Dept. Mgr., Fukuoka Nichi-Nichi Shimbun; then became Pres. of same. Address: Gennanso, Jigyo-Kawabatadori, Fukuoka.

Retired General; b. Dec., 1873; s. of Nobuyuki Yoshida, samurai of Kagoshima Clan. Career: grad., Military Academy, 1895; Adjutant, War Office and Sec. to War Minister; Head, Tech. Administration Dept.; Mem., Tech. Committee; dispatched to Germany, England and America, 1918. Address: 1248 Shimo-Ochiai, Yodobashiku, Tokyo.

Trader; b. June, 1883 in Yokohama; s. of Toyokichi Yoshida, trader. Career: grad., Yokohama Com. School; established Owariya and Okabe Shokai; Dir., Yokohama Motorcar Co. and Japan Asphaltum Industrial Co. Address: 67 Mita, Meguroku, Tokyo.

Dir., and Head, Service Dept., Teikoku Nokai (Agrl. Assn.); b. May, 1878 in Ibaragi-ken; s. of Eisuke Yoshioka, educator. Career: grad., Law Coll., Tokyo Imp. Univ., 1906; passed Higher Civil Service Exam.; Resident Official in London, 1912; Gov., Tainan-shu, Taiwan; Chief, Monopoly Bureau, Taiwan Govt.; Gov., Taihokushu. Address: 990 Shizen-en, Nakameguro-Sanchome, Meguroku, Tokyo.

M. P.; Adviser, Seiyukai; b. Sept., 1865 in Chiba-ken; s. of Shonosuke Yoshiue.
