Career: Pres., Hokkai Times, Hokkaido Jiji, Osaka Shimpo and Chuo Shimbun; elected to Diet 8 times since 1904; Councillor, Foreign Office; inspected Chilean Colonization System; Parl. Vice-Minister of Com. & Industry in Tanaka Cabinet, 1927; apptd. Adviser of Seiyukai Party, 1932. Address: 42 Miyamuracho, Azabuku, Tokyo.

Mem., House of Peers; b. Jan., 1874 in Niigata-ken; s. of Joro Yoshizawa, banker. Career: grad., Litt. Course, Tokyo Imp. Univ., 1899; passed Diplomatic Service Exam.; apptd. Attaché, Foreign Office; Dir., Polit. Affairs Bureau; same, Asiatic Bureau; 1st Sec., Embassy in England; Minister to China; Ambassador to France; Foreign Minister in Inukai Cabinet, Jan.-May, 1932; nominated Mem., House of Peers, July, same year. Address: 22 Kasumicho, Azabuku, Tokyo.

C. B.; 2nd Sec., Chinese Legation at Tokyo; b. July, 1891 in Hopei Province, China; n. Chinese; s. of Y. T. Young. Career: studied at Law Course, Pei-Yang Univ., Tientsin and grad., Com. Dept., Meiji Univ., Tokyo; apptd. Prof., Tientsin Law Coll.; passed Diplomatic Exam., 1921; served in Foreign Office, and apptd. Attaché, Chinese Legation, Tokyo, 1924; 3rd Sec., 1927; present post since 1932. Address: Chinese Legation, Azabu, Tokyo.

Commander, Mukden Province Guards; b. 1882 in Taian-hsien, Mukden Prov. Career: Comdr., Chang Tsuo-lin's Guards; Chief, Aide-de-Camp of Chang 1927; War Councillor, Commander-in-chief's Office, North Eastern Frontier Defence Army; Took part in establishing Manchoukuo after Manchurian Incident; present post since 1932. Address: Mukden.
Dir., Mukden High Court. Career: present post since 1932. Address: Mukden.

Dir., Capital Construction Bureau, Manchoukuo; Chief, Propaganda Office, Manchoukuo Hsiehhohui. Career: Chief Sec., Gov.'s Office, Mukden Prov., and Chief, Propaganda Office, Manchoukuo Hsiehhohui, 1932; present post since 1933. Address: Mukden.
Chief, Pin-chiang Revenue Supt. Office. Career: present post since 1932. Address: c/o Pin-chiang Revenue Supt. Office.

Privy Councillor, Manchoukuo; b. 1870 in Liaoyang-hsien, Mukden Prov. Career: Dir., Liaoyang General Police Bureau after Russo-Japanese War; Chief Sec. to Chang Tsuo-lin, 1916; Heilunkiang Mil. Gov.'s Sec. Chief, 1922; Vice-Pres., North Eastern Local Peace Federation after Chang's death; Councillor, Office of Commander-in-Chief, North Eastern Frontier Defence Army, 1929; Chairman, Local Peace Committee during Manchuria Incident; Supreme Adviser, Mukden Prov., 1931; exerted in Manchoukuo Foundation Movement, 1931; present post since 1932. Address: Hsinking.

Imp. Household Minister; b. 1874 in Yamaguchi-ken; s. of Koan Yuasa. Career: grad., Polit. Coll., Tokyo Imp. Univ., 1898; Councillor, Shiga-ken; Dir., Prefectural Bureau, Home Dept., 1912; Gov., Shizuoka-ken, 1914; Dir., Police Bureau Home Dept., 1915; Mem., House of Peers; Metropolitan Police Chief; Vice-Minister of Home Dept.; Civil Govr. Chosen Govt.; resigned Mem., House of Peers; Pres., Board of Audit, 1929; present post since Feb., 1933. Address: 6 Nakamachi, Ushigomeku, Tokyo.

Barrister at Law; Attorney; b. Apr., 1899 in Matsue, Shimane-ken; s. of Toyotaro Yuasa, lawyer. Career: grad., Tokyo Imp. Univ., 1923; then studied at Inner Temple, London; Univ. of Grenoble, France; Univ. of Vienna, Austria; North Western Univ., Chicago. Address: 42 Kitahama Nichome, Higashiku, Osaka.
Chief, Gen. Affairs Office, Capital Construction Bureau, Manchoukuo; b. in Yamagata-ken. Career: grad., Polit. Coll., Tokyo Imp. Univ.; present post since 1932. Address: Hsinking.

Pres., Industrial Bank of Japan; Dir., Japan Industrial Club; b. May, 1882 in Yamagata-ken; s. of Yaemon Yuki. Career: grad., Law Coll., Tokyo Imp. Univ., 1903; joined Bank of Japan; served at its Branches at London, Osaka, Kyoto and Nagoya; Mng. Dir., Yasuda Hozensha; Vice-Pres., Yasuda Bank; Dir., Mitsui Trust Co., Nippon Yusen Kaisha, Nippon Elec. Co. and Nippon Wireless Telegraph Co., apptd. present post, 1930. Address: 61 Nagasakacho, Azabuku, Tokyo.

Pres., Central Bank of Manchoukuo; b. 1875 in Shulan-hsien. Career: Chief, Liaoshen-Tao, Mukden Prov., same Kirin Prov. Office after Manchurian Incident; present post since establishment of firm, 1932. Address: Hsinking, Manchoukuo.

Acting Consul at Rangoon, Burma; b. 1894 in Tottori City; s. of late Rinzo Yutani. Career: grad., Administration Dept., Official Training Coll., Communications Office; Chancellor, Consulate at Shanghai, Chicago, London, Bombay; then present post. Address: Japanese Consulate, Rangoon, Burma.

Pres., Int'l Corr. Assn.; Pres., Herald of Asia, and Middle School Text-Book Publishing Co.; b. Dec., 1862 in Tottori-ken; s. of Yasugoro Zumoto. Career: grad., Sapporo Agrl. Coll., 1884; Corr., Japan Mail; Sec. of Ito Cabinet; started Japan Times, 1897, and became Prop. and Editor of same up to 1914; elected M. P., 1917; went abroad several times; established Keijo Press. in Chosen, 1906; elected to Diet, 1917. Address: 118 Honmuracho, Azabuku, Tokyo.

I. M. The Crown Prince of Japan during H. I. H.'s visit to England, 1921. Address: 22 Rosary Gardens, London S. W. 7; care Army & Navy Club, London S. W. 1, England.

Address: 10. Saint Swithin's Lane, London E. C. 4, England.

Address: 57 Iverna Court, Kensington, London L. W. 8, England.
